question_english: In a mango market, at ₹40 the quantity demanded is 38 kg and supplied is 6 kg; at ₹100, both are 12 kg; at ₹150, demanded is 8 kg and supplied is 43 kg. Identify the equilibrium and the outcome at the other prices.

question_english: What is the difference between excess demand and excess supply?
question_hinglish: Excess demand aur excess supply mein kya fark hai?
answer_english: Excess demand, or a shortage, occurs at a price below equilibrium, when quantity demanded is more than quantity supplied (Qs < Qd). Excess supply, or a surplus, occurs at a price above equilibrium, when quantity supplied is more than quantity demanded (Qs > Qd). At equilibrium, there is neither.

question_english: Does market equilibrium exist in the real world? Explain with the example of face masks.
question_hinglish: Kya real world mein market equilibrium hota hai? Face masks ke example se samjhao.
answer_english: In theory, equilibrium is where demand and supply intersect, but real markets are dynamic. Technology, wages, interest rates, wars, pandemics, weather and disasters keep changing demand and supply, so the market is always adjusting to a new equilibrium. During COVID-19 in 2020, mask demand surged, supply could not catch up and prices rose; suppliers then adjusted and prices fell, returning to pre-pandemic levels after the pandemic.
answer_hinglish: Theory mein equilibrium woh point hai jahan demand aur supply milte hain, par asli markets badalte rehte hain. Technology, wages, interest rates, yuddh, mahamaari, mausam aur aapdaayein demand aur supply badalti rehti hain, isliye market hamesha naye equilibrium ki taraf adjust hota hai. 2020 mein COVID-19 ke dauraan masks ki demand achanak badhi, supply turant nahi badh payi aur daam badhe; phir suppliers ne adjust kiya, daam gire, aur mahamaari ke baad pehle jaise ho gaye.
ncert_context: In theory, equilibrium is an intersection point between demand and supply. But in the real world, markets are dynamic. Changes in technology, wages, interest rates, as well as wars, political events, pandemics, weather and natural disasters alter demand and supply. Therefore, equilibrium in the real world is never stable; the market is always adjusting to a new equilibrium. During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, demand for face masks surged, supply could not catch up immediately, and prices rose. Over time, suppliers adjusted and prices fell; after the pandemic, prices reduced to pre-pandemic levels.

question_english: How do hotel tariffs show that markets are dynamic?
question_hinglish: Hotel tariffs kaise dikhate hain ki markets dynamic hote hain?
answer_english: Hotels change room prices with demand, season and events. A Goa hotel may charge ₹1,500 on an off-season weekday, ₹8,000 on a tourist-season weekend and ₹25,000 on New Year's Eve. If a group cancels, it may cut tariffs by 40 per cent overnight to fill rooms. Prices depend on booking speed, nearby hotels' tariffs, local events, weather forecasts, days left before arrival and past trends.
answer_hinglish: Hotels demand, season aur events ke hisaab se room ke daam badalte hain. Goa ka ek hotel off-season weekday pe ₹1,500, tourist season ke weekend pe ₹8,000 aur New Year's Eve pe ₹25,000 le sakta hai. Agar koi group cancel kare, toh rooms bharne ke liye raaton-raat 40 percent daam ghata sakta hai. Daam booking ki speed, aas-paas ke hotels ke daam, local events, mausam ke forecast, aane mein bache din aur pichhle trends pe nirbhar karte hain.

question_english: During online festival sales, many products are sold at very low prices. Why do sellers do this, and who benefits?
question_hinglish: Online festival sales mein kai products bahut kam daam pe bikte hain. Sellers aisa kyun karte hain, aur fayda kise hota hai?
answer_english: Sellers lower prices to clear excess supply and attract buyers; by the law of demand, a lower price raises quantity demanded. Consumers who postponed purchases expecting discounts now buy, so sellers sell larger quantities and move stock. Consumers benefit from lower prices, and sellers benefit from higher sales volume and revenue as the market adjusts towards a new equilibrium.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the difference between a price ceiling and a price floor? Give examples.
question_hinglish: Price ceiling aur price floor mein kya fark hai? Examples do.
answer_english: A price ceiling is a maximum price a seller can charge, such as maximum prices set for essential medicines to prevent overcharging. A price floor is a limit on how low a price can be, such as the minimum wage that ensures workers earn enough; to be effective, a price floor must be set above the market equilibrium price.
answer_hinglish: Price ceiling woh maximum daam hai jo seller le sakta hai, jaise zaroori dawaiyon pe zyada vasooli rokne ke liye maximum price. Price floor yeh tay karta hai ki daam kitna neeche ja sakta hai, jaise minimum wage jo workers ko kaafi kamaai ensure karta hai; asar daalne ke liye price floor market equilibrium price se upar hona chahiye.
ncert_context: The government regulates unfair practices to protect consumers, workers and producers. It sets maximum prices (price ceiling) for essential goods like medicines to prevent overcharging. Similarly, it sets a minimum wage to ensure workers earn enough; this lower limit is known as the price floor. Price ceiling: an imposed price control setting the maximum amount a seller can charge. Price floor: an imposed limit on how low a price can be; for it to be effective, it must be set above the market equilibrium price.

question_english: What is a monopoly, and why does the government regulate it?
question_hinglish: Monopoly kya hai, aur sarkar ise regulate kyun karti hai?
answer_english: A monopoly is a market structure with a single seller or producer controlling the entire supply of a unique product or service with no close substitutes, giving it significant power to set prices and output. It harms consumer welfare by charging higher prices, providing poorer quality and restricting supply, so the government regulates it by keeping prices and quantity supplied in check.
answer_hinglish: Monopoly aisa market structure hai jisme ek hi seller ya producer kisi unique product ya service ki poori supply control karta hai jiska koi kareebi vikalp nahi, isliye use daam aur output tay karne ki badi taakat milti hai. Yeh zyada daam lekar, kharab quality dekar aur supply rok kar consumers ko nuksaan pahunchata hai, isliye sarkar daam aur supply ko control mein rakh kar ise regulate karti hai.
ncert_context: Sometimes a single or a few sellers dominate the market; they can charge higher prices and supply less than a competitive market would. This form of monopoly would be detrimental to consumer welfare as it may charge higher prices, provide poorer quality and restrict supply. The government regulates such practices by keeping prices and quantity supplied in check. Monopoly: a market structure with a single seller or producer controlling the entire supply of a unique product or service, facing no close substitutes, allowing significant power to set prices and output.

question_english: What is the difference between hoarding and black marketing?

question_english: What are the limitations of excessive government intervention in markets?
question_hinglish: Market mein sarkar ke zyada dakhal ki kya seemayein hain?
answer_english: Excessive intervention can cause price distortions and reduce producer incentives, as when prices fixed below market levels lead to reduced production and shortages. It creates compliance burdens through many regulations, licences and permits that hurt small businesses and ease of doing business. It also discourages innovation and entrepreneurship, reducing long-term productivity.
answer_hinglish: Zyada dakhal se daam bigad sakte hain aur producers ki prerna ghat sakti hai, jaise market se kam daam fix karne pe production ghat-ta hai aur kami hoti hai. Bahut saare niyam, licences aur permits compliance ka bojh badhate hain, jo chhote businesses aur ease of doing business ko nuksaan pahunchate hain. Yeh innovation aur entrepreneurship ko bhi rokta hai, jisse long-term productivity ghat-ti hai.
ncert_context: Government regulations are required when markets are inefficient, but excessive intervention can have adverse effects. a) Price distortions and reduced producer incentives: prices fixed below market levels may reduce motivation to supply, causing shortages. b) Compliance burdens: extensive regulations, licences, permits and compliance procedures hurt businesses, especially small enterprises, and hamper ease of doing business. c) Discourages innovation and entrepreneurship: heavy regulation and price controls reduce incentives to invest in new ideas or better technology, reducing long-term productivity.

question_english: If market forces set the price of wheat at ₹30 per kg but the government fixes a maximum price of ₹20 per kg, how much less does a farmer get per kg, and per 100 kg? What might happen?
question_hinglish: Agar market forces wheat ka daam ₹30 per kg tay karein par sarkar ₹20 per kg maximum price fix kare, toh kisan ko per kg aur 100 kg pe kitna kam milega? Kya ho sakta hai?
answer_english: Per kg, the farmer gets ₹30 − ₹20 = ₹10 less. For 100 kg, the loss is 100 × ₹10 = ₹1,000. With lower returns, farmers may lose motivation to supply and stop investing in better seeds, irrigation or technology, leading to reduced production and shortages.
answer_hinglish: Per kg kisan ko ₹30 − ₹20 = ₹10 kam milte hain. 100 kg pe nuksaan 100 × ₹10 = ₹1,000 hai. Kam kamaai se kisan supply karne ki prerna kho sakte hain aur behtar beej, irrigation ya technology mein invest karna band kar sakte hain, jisse production ghatega aur kami hogi.
ncert_context: When the government fixes prices below market levels, producers may lose motivation to supply goods or services. For instance, if the government sets a maximum price for wheat at ₹20 per kg while market forces set it at ₹30 per kg, farmers receive less than they would in a free market. This may lead to reduced production and shortages. Farmers won't invest in better seeds, irrigation or technology if they cannot earn adequate returns.

question_english: What is meant by 'ease of doing business', and how can regulation affect it?
question_hinglish: 'Ease of doing business' ka kya matlab hai, aur regulation ise kaise prabhavit karta hai?

question_english: If the government sets a maximum sale price for an essential vaccine below the market-driven price, what is likely to happen? (a) Surplus (b) Shortage (c) No effect (d) Fall in demand

question_english: In what way does Sorrieu's print depict a utopian vision?
question_hinglish: Sorrieu ka print kis tarah utopian vision dikhata hai?
answer_english: A utopian vision is a society so ideal it is unlikely to exist. Sorrieu imagined a world of democratic and social republics in which all peoples, grouped as nations, peacefully honour Liberty while absolutism lies shattered and heaven blesses their fraternity. In 1848 many of these nations, such as Germany, did not even exist as united states, so the image showed an ideal rather than reality.
answer_hinglish: Utopian vision aisi aadarsh society hai jo shayad kabhi na ho. Sorrieu ne democratic aur social republics ki duniya socha jisme sab log, nations mein bante hue, shanti se Liberty ka samman karte hain, absolutism toota pada hai aur swarg unke bhaichaare ko aashirwad deta hai. 1848 mein Germany jaise kai nations ek desh ke roop mein the hi nahi, isliye yeh tasveer sachchai nahi, ek aadarsh thi.

question_english: According to Ernst Renan, what makes a nation?
question_hinglish: Ernst Renan ke hisaab se nation kya banata hai?
answer_english: In his 1882 lecture 'What is a Nation?', Renan rejected the idea that a nation is formed by common language, race, religion or territory. For him, a nation is the culmination of a long past of endeavours, sacrifice and devotion: common glories in the past, a common will in the present, and the wish to perform great deeds together. A nation is a large-scale solidarity whose existence is a 'daily plebiscite', and nations guarantee liberty.
answer_hinglish: 1882 ke apne lecture 'What is a Nation?' mein Renan ne yeh maanne se inkaar kiya ki nation common bhasha, race, dharm ya territory se banta hai. Unke liye nation mehnat, tyaag aur samarpan ke lambe ateet ka nateeja hai: ateet ki saajhi shaan, vartamaan mein saajhi ichchha, aur milkar bade kaam karne ki chahat. Nation ek bade paimaane ki ekjutta hai jiska astitva 'roz ka plebiscite' hai, aur nations azaadi ki guarantee hain.
ncert_context: In a lecture at the University of Sorbonne in 1882, French philosopher Ernst Renan criticised the notion that a nation is formed by a common language, race, religion or territory: 'A nation is the culmination of a long past of endeavours, sacrifice and devotion… To have common glories in the past, to have a common will in the present, to have performed great deeds together, to wish to perform still more, these are the essential conditions of being a people. A nation is therefore a large-scale solidarity… Its existence is a daily plebiscite… Their existence is a guarantee of liberty.'

question_english: What steps did the French revolutionaries take to create a sense of collective identity among the French people?
question_hinglish: French revolutionaries ne French logon mein saamuhik pehchaan banane ke liye kya kadam uthaye?
answer_english: They promoted the ideas of la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen); replaced the royal standard with a new tricolour flag; renamed the elected Estates General the National Assembly; composed new hymns, took oaths and commemorated martyrs in the nation's name; set up a centralised administration with uniform laws; abolished internal customs duties and adopted uniform weights and measures; and made Parisian French the common language, discouraging regional dialects.
answer_hinglish: Unhone la patrie (fatherland) aur le citoyen (citizen) ke ideas failaye; royal jhande ki jagah naya tricolour laaye; chuni gayi Estates General ka naam National Assembly rakha; nation ke naam pe naye geet, shapath aur shaheedon ki yaad manayi; uniform kanoon wala centralised administration banaya; andar ke customs duties khatam karke ek jaise naap-tol apnaye; aur regional boliyon ki jagah Paris wali French ko common bhasha banaya.
ncert_context: The French revolutionaries introduced measures to create collective identity. The ideas of la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen) emphasised a united community with equal rights under a constitution. A new tricolour flag replaced the royal standard. The Estates General was elected by active citizens and renamed the National Assembly. New hymns were composed, oaths taken and martyrs commemorated. A centralised administrative system formulated uniform laws. Internal customs duties were abolished and a uniform system of weights and measures adopted. Regional dialects were discouraged and French as spoken in Paris became the common language.

question_english: How did the French Revolution spread the idea of nationalism outside France?
question_hinglish: French Revolution ne France ke bahar nationalism ka idea kaise failaya?
answer_english: The revolutionaries declared that the French nation's mission was to liberate the peoples of Europe from despotism and help them become nations. When news of events in France reached European cities, students and educated middle classes set up Jacobin clubs, whose campaigns prepared the way for French armies moving into Holland, Belgium, Switzerland and much of Italy in the 1790s. With the revolutionary wars, French armies carried nationalism abroad.
answer_hinglish: Revolutionaries ne kaha ki French nation ka mission Europe ke logon ko tanashahi se azaad karke unhe nations banane mein madad karna hai. France ki khabar Europe ke shehron mein pahunchne pe students aur padhe-likhe middle class ne Jacobin clubs banaye, jinke campaigns ne 1790s mein Holland, Belgium, Switzerland aur Italy ke bade hisse mein ghusne wali French armies ka raasta banaya. Revolutionary wars ke saath French armies nationalism ko bahar le gayi.
ncert_context: The revolutionaries declared that it was the mission and destiny of the French nation to liberate the peoples of Europe from despotism, in other words to help other peoples of Europe to become nations. When news of events in France reached different cities of Europe, students and other members of the educated middle classes began setting up Jacobin clubs. Their activities and campaigns prepared the way for French armies which moved into Holland, Belgium, Switzerland and much of Italy in the 1790s. With the outbreak of the revolutionary wars, the French armies began to carry the idea of nationalism abroad.

question_english: What was the Napoleonic Code of 1804, and what did it change?
question_hinglish: 1804 ka Napoleonic Code kya tha, aur isne kya badla?
answer_english: The Civil Code of 1804, known as the Napoleonic Code, did away with all privileges based on birth, established equality before the law and secured the right to property. It was exported to regions under French control. Although Napoleon destroyed democracy in France by returning to monarchy, this code incorporated revolutionary principles to make administration more rational and efficient.

question_english: What changes did Napoleon introduce to make administration more efficient in the territories he ruled?
question_hinglish: Napoleon ne apne shaasit ilaakon mein administration ko efficient banane ke liye kya badlav kiye?

question_hinglish: Jeete gaye ilaakon mein French rule ke liye shuruaati josh dushmani mein kyun badal gaya?
answer_english: In places like Holland, Switzerland, Brussels, Mainz, Milan and Warsaw, French armies were first welcomed as harbingers of liberty. question_hinglish: Habsburg Empire political ekta ki bhavna kyun nahi bana paaya?

question_english: Describe the aristocracy and peasantry of early nineteenth-century Europe.
question_hinglish: Unnees-vi sadi ki shuruaat ke Europe ki aristocracy aur kisaanon ka varnan karo.
answer_english: The landed aristocracy was the dominant class socially and politically. Its members shared a common lifestyle across regions, owned country estates and town-houses, spoke French in diplomacy and high society, and were linked by marriage, but they were numerically small. The majority were peasants: in the west, land was farmed by tenants and small owners, while in Eastern and Central Europe vast estates were cultivated by serfs.
answer_hinglish: Zameendaar aristocracy social aur political roop se sabse haavi class thi. Iske log regions ke paar ek jaisa jeevan jeete, gaon mein estates aur shehar mein ghar rakhte, diplomacy aur high society mein French bolte, aur shaadi se jude hote the, par sankhya mein kam the. Zyadatar log kisaan the: west mein zameen tenants aur chhote maalik jot-te the, jabki Eastern aur Central Europe mein bade estates serfs jot-te the.

The majority of the population was the peasantry. To the west, land was farmed by tenants and small owners, while in Eastern and Central Europe vast estates were cultivated by serfs.

question_english: Which new social groups emerged with industrialisation, and among whom did ideas of national unity become popular?
question_hinglish: Industrialisation se kaun se naye social groups bane, aur national unity ke ideas kinme popular hue?
answer_english: Industrialisation began in England in the second half of the eighteenth century and in France and the German states in the nineteenth. It created a working class and middle classes of industrialists, businessmen and professionals. Ideas of national unity, following the abolition of aristocratic privileges, gained popularity among the educated, liberal middle classes.
answer_hinglish: Industrialisation England mein eighteenth century ke doosre half mein aur France aur German states mein nineteenth century mein shuru hua. Isse working class aur industrialists, businessmen aur professionals wali middle classes bani. Aristocratic vishesh adhikaar khatam karke national unity ke ideas padhe-likhe, liberal middle classes mein popular hue.
ncert_context: In Western and parts of Central Europe, industrial production and trade led to the growth of towns and commercial classes. Industrialisation began in England in the second half of the eighteenth century, but in France and parts of the German states only during the nineteenth century. New social groups came into being: a working-class population, and middle classes made up of industrialists, businessmen and professionals. It was among the educated, liberal middle classes that ideas of national unity following the abolition of aristocratic privileges gained popularity.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What did liberalism stand for in nineteenth-century Europe?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century Europe mein liberalism kis cheez ka samarthak tha?
answer_english: Liberalism, from the Latin liber meaning free, stood for individual freedom and equality before the law. Politically it meant government by consent, an end to autocracy and clerical privileges, a constitution and representative government through parliament, and the inviolability of private property. Economically it meant freedom of markets and abolition of state restrictions on the movement of goods and capital.
answer_hinglish: Liberalism, jo Latin liber yaani 'azaad' se bana, vyakti ki azaadi aur kanoon ke saamne barabari ka samarthak tha. Politically iska matlab tha sahmati se sarkar, tanashahi aur church ke vishesh adhikaar ka ant, constitution aur parliament se representative sarkar, aur private property ki surakshit. Economically iska matlab tha markets ki azaadi aur saamaan aur capital ki aavajahi pe sarkari rokon ka khatma.
ncert_context: Ideas of national unity were closely allied to liberalism. The term derives from the Latin root liber, meaning free. For the new middle classes, liberalism stood for freedom for the individual and equality of all before the law. Politically, it emphasised government by consent. Since the French Revolution, liberalism stood for the end of autocracy and clerical privileges, a constitution and representative government through parliament. Liberals stressed the inviolability of private property. Economically, liberalism stood for freedom of markets and abolition of state-imposed restrictions on movement of goods and capital.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Did liberal 'equality before the law' mean universal suffrage? Explain.
question_hinglish: Kya liberal 'kanoon ke saamne barabari' ka matlab universal suffrage tha? Samjhao.
answer_english: No. In revolutionary France, the first experiment in liberal democracy, the right to vote and be elected was given only to property-owning men; men without property and all women were excluded. Only briefly under the Jacobins did all adult males vote. The Napoleonic Code returned to limited suffrage and reduced women to the status of minors under fathers and husbands, so women and non-propertied men organised movements for equal political rights.
answer_hinglish: Nahi. Revolutionary France mein, jo liberal democracy ka pehla prayog tha, vote dene aur chune jaane ka haq sirf property wale purushon ko mila; bina property ke purush aur saari mahilayein bahar the. Sirf Jacobins ke time thodi der sab adult purush vote de paaye. Napoleonic Code ne phir seemit suffrage laaya aur mahilaon ko pita aur pati ke under minor jaisa bana diya, isliye mahilaon aur bina property wale purushon ne barabar political adhikaaron ke liye andolan kiye.
ncert_context: Equality before the law did not necessarily stand for universal suffrage. In revolutionary France, the first political experiment in liberal democracy, the right to vote and get elected was granted exclusively to property-owning men. Men without property and all women were excluded. Only for a brief period under the Jacobins did all adult males enjoy suffrage. The Napoleonic Code went back to limited suffrage and reduced women to the status of a minor, subject to the authority of fathers and husbands. Women and non-propertied men organised opposition movements demanding equal political rights.

question_english: A merchant travelling from Hamburg to Nuremberg in 1833 passed 11 customs barriers, paying about 5 per cent duty at each. If he paid duty on goods worth 1,000 units at each barrier (ignoring compounding), how much duty would he pay in total?
question_hinglish: 1833 mein Hamburg se Nuremberg jaane wala ek vyapaari 11 customs barriers se guzra, har ek pe lagbhag 5 percent duty dekar. Agar woh har barrier pe 1,000 units ke saamaan pe duty de (compounding chhod kar), toh kul kitni duty dega?
answer_english: Duty per barrier = 5% of 1,000 = 50 units. Total duty = 11 × 50 = 550 units, more than half the value of the goods. Such barriers were seen by commercial classes as obstacles to economic exchange and growth.

question_english: What was the zollverein, and how did it help German unification?
question_hinglish: Zollverein kya tha, aur isne German unification mein kaise madad ki?
answer_english: The zollverein was a customs union formed in 1834 at the initiative of Prussia and joined by most German states. question_english: What political ends did Friedrich List hope to achieve through the zollverein?
question_hinglish: Friedrich List zollverein se kaun se political lakshya paana chahte the?
answer_english: Friedrich List, an economics professor at Tübingen, wrote in 1834 that the zollverein aimed to bind the Germans economically into a nation, strengthening it materially by protecting its interests externally and stimulating internal productivity. He hoped it would awaken national sentiment by fusing individual and provincial interests, believing a free economic system was the only way to create national feeling.
answer_hinglish: Tübingen ke economics professor Friedrich List ne 1834 mein likha ki zollverein ka lakshya Germans ko economically ek nation mein baandhna hai, jisse bahar unke interests ki raksha aur andar productivity badhakar nation mazboot ho. Unhe ummeed thi ki yeh vyakti aur province ke interests ko milakar national bhavna jagayega, kyunki unke hisaab se free economic system hi national feeling paida kar sakta tha.
ncert_context: Economists began to think in terms of the national economy. Friedrich List, Professor of Economics at the University of Tübingen, wrote in 1834: 'The aim of the zollverein is to bind the Germans economically into a nation. It will strengthen the nation materially as much by protecting its interests externally as by stimulating its internal productivity. It ought to awaken and raise national sentiment through a fusion of individual and provincial interests. The German people have realised that a free economic system is the only means to engender national feeling.'

question_english: What did conservatives believe after 1815?
question_hinglish: 1815 ke baad conservatives kya maante the?
answer_english: Conservatism stressed tradition, established institutions and customs, and preferred gradual development to quick change. question_english: What was the Treaty of Vienna of 1815, and what changes did it make?
question_hinglish: 1815 ki Treaty of Vienna kya thi, aur isne kya badlav kiye?

question_english: Who was Giuseppe Mazzini, and what were his ideas?
question_hinglish: Giuseppe Mazzini kaun the, aur unke kya vichaar the?
answer_english: Mazzini, born in Genoa in 1805, was an Italian revolutionary and member of the secret society Carbonari. Exiled in 1831 at 26 for attempting a revolution in Liguria, he founded Young Italy in Marseilles and Young Europe in Berne. He believed God intended nations to be the natural units of mankind, so Italy had to be forged into a single unified republic. His opposition to monarchy frightened conservatives; Metternich called him 'the most dangerous enemy of our social order'.

Liguria mein revolution ki koshish ke liye 1831 mein 26 saal ki umar mein unhe exile kiya gaya, aur unhone Marseilles mein Young Italy aur Berne mein Young Europe banaye. Woh maante the ki Bhagwan ne nations ko insaanon ki natural units banaya hai, isliye Italy ko ek united republic banana zaroori tha. Monarchy ke unke virodh se conservatives darte the; Metternich ne unhe 'humare social order ka sabse khatarnaak dushman' kaha.

question_english: Why did the Greek war of independence mobilise nationalist feeling across Europe?
question_hinglish: Greek war of independence ne poore Europe mein nationalist bhavna kyun jagayi?
answer_english: Greece had been part of the Ottoman Empire since the fifteenth century, and its struggle for independence began in 1821. Greek nationalists got support from Greeks in exile and from West Europeans who admired ancient Greek culture. Poets and artists praised Greece as the cradle of European civilisation and mobilised opinion against a Muslim empire; Lord Byron raised funds, went to fight and died of fever in 1824. The Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 recognised Greece as independent.

question_hinglish: Romanticism kya tha, aur isne nationalism mein kaise yogdaan diya?
answer_english: Romanticism was a cultural movement whose artists and poets criticised the glorification of reason and science and focused on emotions, intuition and mystical feelings. They tried to create a sense of shared collective heritage and common cultural past as the basis of a nation. Herder claimed true German culture lay among the common people (das volk), and the national spirit (volksgeist) was popularised through folk songs, poetry and dances.
answer_hinglish: Romanticism ek cultural movement tha jiske kalakaar aur kavi reason aur science ki tareef ki aalochana karke bhavnaon, intuition aur rahasyamay ehsaason pe dhyaan dete the. Unhone nation ke aadhaar ke roop mein saajhi virasat aur common saanskritik ateet ki bhavna banane ki koshish ki. Herder ne kaha ki asli German sanskriti aam logon (das volk) mein hai, aur national spirit (volksgeist) lok geeton, kavita aur nritya se failaya gaya.

question_english: How were music and language used to keep Polish nationalism alive?
question_hinglish: Polish nationalism ko zinda rakhne ke liye music aur bhasha ka kaise use hua?
answer_english: Poland was partitioned by Russia, Prussia and Austria at the end of the eighteenth century, but national feelings survived through music and language. Karol Kurpinski's operas turned folk dances like the polonaise and mazurka into nationalist symbols. After Russia imposed Russian in schools and crushed the 1831 rebellion, the clergy used Polish in Church gatherings and religious instruction; many priests were jailed or sent to Siberia, and Polish became a symbol of struggle against Russian dominance.
answer_hinglish: Eighteenth century ke ant mein Russia, Prussia aur Austria ne Poland ko baant liya, par national bhavna music aur bhasha se bachi rahi. Karol Kurpinski ke operas ne polonaise aur mazurka jaise lok nritya ko nationalist prateek bana diya. Russia ne schools mein Russian thopi aur 1831 ka vidroh kuchla, toh clergy ne Church ki sabhaon aur dharmik shiksha mein Polish use ki; kai paadriyon ko jail ya Siberia bheja gaya, aur Polish Russian dabdabe ke khilaaf sangharsh ka prateek ban gayi.
ncert_context: Poland had been partitioned at the end of the eighteenth century by Russia, Prussia and Austria. question_english: How did the Grimm brothers contribute to German nation-building?
question_hinglish: Grimm brothers ne German nation-building mein kaise yogdaan diya?
answer_english: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm spent six years travelling village to village collecting folktales handed down through generations, publishing their first collection in 1812. They were active in liberal politics, especially for press freedom, and published a 33-volume German dictionary. Seeing French domination as a threat to German culture, they believed the folktales expressed a pure German spirit and saw collecting them and developing the language as part of creating a German national identity.
answer_hinglish: Jacob aur Wilhelm Grimm ne chhe saal gaon-gaon ghoom kar peedhiyon se chali aa rahi lok kathayein ikatthi ki aur 1812 mein pehla sangrah chhapa. Woh liberal politics, khaas kar press ki azaadi, mein active the aur unhone German bhasha ka 33-volume dictionary chhapa. French dabdabe ko German sanskriti ke liye khatra maan kar woh lok kathaon ko shuddh German aatma ki abhivyakti maante the, aur unhe ikattha karne aur bhasha vikasit karne ko German national identity banane ka hissa samajhte the.
ncert_context: The brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, born in Hanau in 1785 and 1786, developed an interest in collecting old folktales. They spent six years travelling from village to village, writing down fairy tales handed down through generations. In 1812 they published their first collection. Both became active in liberal politics, especially the movement for freedom of the press, and published a 33-volume dictionary of the German language. They saw French domination as a threat to German culture and believed the folktales were expressions of a pure German spirit, part of the effort to oppose French domination and create a German national identity.

question_english: What economic hardships in the 1830s and 1840s led to revolts in Europe?
question_hinglish: 1830s aur 1840s ki kaun si economic mushkilon se Europe mein vidroh hue?
answer_english: Population grew enormously, so job seekers outnumbered jobs, and rural migrants crowded into city slums. Small producers faced stiff competition from cheap machine-made English imports, especially in textiles. Where aristocracy still ruled, peasants struggled under feudal dues. Rising food prices or bad harvests caused widespread pauperism; in 1848, food shortages and unemployment brought Parisians onto the streets, forcing Louis Philippe to flee.
answer_hinglish: Aabaadi bahut badhi, isliye naukri dhundhne wale naukriyon se zyada ho gaye, aur gaon se aaye log shehar ki bheed wali bastiyon mein rehne lage. Chhote producers ko, khaas kar kapde mein, England ke saste machine-made maal se kada mukabla mila. Jahan aristocracy ka raaj tha wahan kisaan feudal dues ke bojh tale the. Khaane ke badhte daam ya kharab fasal se gareebi faili; 1848 mein khaane ki kami aur berozgaari se Paris ke log sadkon pe aaye aur Louis Philippe ko bhaagna pada.
ncert_context: The 1830s were years of great economic hardship in Europe. The first half of the nineteenth century saw an enormous increase in population. In most countries there were more seekers of jobs than employment. Rural populations migrated to cities to live in overcrowded slums. Small producers faced stiff competition from cheap machine-made goods from England, especially in textiles. Where aristocracy still enjoyed power, peasants struggled under feudal dues. The rise of food prices or a bad harvest led to widespread pauperism. In 1848, food shortages and widespread unemployment brought the population of Paris out on the roads, and Louis Philippe was forced to flee.

question_english: What caused the Silesian weavers' uprising of 1845?
question_hinglish: 1845 ke Silesian weavers ke vidroh ka kaaran kya tha?
answer_english: In Silesia, cotton weaving was the main occupation and workers lived in extreme misery. Contractors who supplied raw material and ordered finished textiles took advantage of their desperate need for jobs and drastically reduced payments. On 4 June, weavers marched to their contractor's mansion demanding higher wages; when treated with scorn, some smashed the house and plundered cloth. The contractor returned with the army, and eleven weavers were shot.
answer_hinglish: Silesia mein cotton weaving mukhya rozgaar tha aur mazdoor bahut gareebi mein the. Kachcha maal dene aur taiyaar kapde ka order dene wale contractors ne unki naukri ki majboori ka fayda uthakar bhugtaan bahut ghata diya. 4 June ko weavers zyada mazdoori maangne contractor ke mahal tak gaye; tiraskaar milne pe kuch ne ghar tod-phod kiya aur kapda loota. Contractor sena lekar laut-aaya, aur gyaarah weavers ko goli maar di gayi.
ncert_context: In 1845, weavers in Silesia had led a revolt against contractors who supplied them raw material and gave them orders for finished textiles but drastically reduced their payments. Journalist Wilhelm Wolff wrote that cotton weaving was the most widespread occupation and the misery of workers was extreme; contractors took advantage of the desperate need for jobs to reduce prices. On 4 June, weavers marched to the contractor's mansion demanding higher wages, were treated with scorn, smashed windowpanes and furniture and plundered cloth. The contractor returned with the army, and eleven weavers were shot.

question_english: What was the Frankfurt parliament, and why did it fail?
question_hinglish: Frankfurt parliament kya thi, aur yeh fail kyun hui?
answer_english: Middle-class political associations in the German regions voted for an all-German National Assembly. On 18 May 1848, 831 elected representatives took their places in the Frankfurt parliament in the Church of St Paul and drafted a constitution for a German nation headed by a monarchy subject to parliament. King Friedrich Wilhelm IV of Prussia rejected the crown and joined other monarchs against the assembly. The middle-class parliament also resisted workers' and artisans' demands and lost their support, and troops finally forced it to disband.
answer_hinglish: German regions ke middle-class sangathanon ne ek all-German National Assembly ke liye vote kiya. 18 May 1848 ko 831 chune representatives Church of St Paul mein Frankfurt parliament mein baithe aur ek aise German nation ka constitution banaya jiska head parliament ke under monarchy ho. Prussia ke raja Friedrich Wilhelm IV ne taj thukra diya aur doosre raajaon ke saath assembly ka virodh kiya. Middle-class parliament ne workers aur artisans ki maangein bhi nahi maani aur unka saath kho diya, aur aakhir mein sena ne use bhang karwa diya.

question_english: What was the role of women in the liberal and nationalist movements of 1848?
question_hinglish: 1848 ke liberal aur nationalist andolanon mein mahilaon ka kya role tha?
answer_english: Large numbers of women had participated actively in the liberal movement: they formed political associations, founded newspapers and joined meetings and demonstrations. Extending political rights to women remained controversial within the liberal movement.

Mahilaon ko political haq dena liberal andolan mein vivaadit raha.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the process of Italian unification.
question_hinglish: Italian unification ki process batao.
answer_english: Mazzini's revolutionary uprisings of 1831 and 1848 failed, so Sardinia-Piedmont under King Victor Emmanuel II took up unification through war. Chief Minister Cavour engineered an alliance with France, and Sardinia-Piedmont defeated Austria in 1859. In 1860 Garibaldi's armed volunteers marched into South Italy and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, winning peasant support to drive out the Spanish rulers. In 1861 Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of united Italy.
answer_hinglish: Mazzini ke 1831 aur 1848 ke vidroh fail hue, isliye King Victor Emmanuel II ke under Sardinia-Piedmont ne yuddh se unification ka zimma liya. Chief Minister Cavour ne France ke saath alliance banaya, aur 1859 mein Sardinia-Piedmont ne Austria ko haraya. 1860 mein Garibaldi ke hathiyaarband volunteers South Italy aur Kingdom of the Two Sicilies mein ghuse aur kisaanon ka saath lekar Spanish shaasakon ko bhagaya. 1861 mein Victor Emmanuel II ko united Italy ka raja ghoshit kiya gaya.
ncert_context: In the 1830s Mazzini sought a unitary Italian Republic and formed Young Italy. The failure of uprisings in 1831 and 1848 meant the mantle fell on Sardinia-Piedmont under King Victor Emmanuel II to unify the Italian states through war. Chief Minister Cavour, through a diplomatic alliance with France, helped Sardinia-Piedmont defeat Austrian forces in 1859. Armed volunteers under Giuseppe Garibaldi joined. In 1860 they marched into South Italy and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies and won the support of local peasants to drive out the Spanish rulers. In 1861 Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of united Italy.

question_english: What does the 'La Talia' story reveal about Italian unification?
question_hinglish: 'La Talia' wali kahani Italian unification ke baare mein kya batati hai?

question_english: How was the history of nationalism in Britain unlike the rest of Europe?
question_hinglish: Britain mein nationalism ka itihaas baaki Europe se kaise alag tha?
answer_english: In Britain, the nation-state did not result from a sudden revolution but from a long-drawn-out process. Before the eighteenth century there was no British nation; people identified as English, Welsh, Scot or Irish. As England grew in wealth and power, the English parliament, which had seized power from the monarchy in 1688, became the instrument to forge a nation-state with England at its centre, extending English influence over the other nations of the islands.

Jaise-jaise England daulat aur taakat mein badha, 1688 mein monarchy se power lene wali English parliament woh zariya bani jisse England ko kendra mein rakh kar nation-state bana aur English prabhav baaki nations pe faila.
ncert_context: The model of the nation-state, some scholars argue, is Great Britain. In Britain the formation of the nation-state was not the result of a sudden upheaval or revolution but of a long-drawn-out process. There was no British nation prior to the eighteenth century. The primary identities of the people of the British Isles were ethnic ones such as English, Welsh, Scot or Irish. As the English nation grew in wealth and power, it extended its influence over the other nations. The English parliament, which had seized power from the monarchy in 1688, was the instrument through which a nation-state with England at its centre came to be forged.

question_english: How did the Act of Union of 1707 affect Scotland?
question_hinglish: 1707 ke Act of Union ne Scotland ko kaise prabhavit kiya?
answer_english: The Act of Union between England and Scotland formed the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain', which in effect let England impose its influence on Scotland. The British parliament was dominated by English members, and Scotland's distinctive culture and political institutions were systematically suppressed. Catholic Highland clans faced terrible repression; Highlanders were forbidden to speak Gaelic or wear their national dress, and many were forcibly driven from their homeland.
answer_hinglish: England aur Scotland ke beech Act of Union se 'United Kingdom of Great Britain' bana, jisse asal mein England ne Scotland pe apna prabhav thopa. British parliament mein English members haavi rahe, aur Scotland ki alag sanskriti aur political sansthaon ko vyavasthit tareeke se dabaya gaya. Highlands ke Catholic clans pe bhayanak dabaav hua; Highlanders ko Gaelic bolne ya apni national poshaak pehenne se roka gaya, aur kai logon ko zabardasti unke ghar se nikala gaya.
ncert_context: The Act of Union (1707) between England and Scotland that resulted in the formation of the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain' meant that England was able to impose its influence on Scotland. The British parliament was henceforth dominated by its English members. Scotland's distinctive culture and political institutions were systematically suppressed. The Catholic clans of the Scottish Highlands suffered terrible repression whenever they asserted their independence. The Scottish Highlanders were forbidden to speak their Gaelic language or wear their national dress, and large numbers were forcibly driven out of their homeland.

question_english: What is the meaning of the symbols used in the allegory of Germania?

question_english: Why did nationalist tensions emerge in the Balkans?
question_hinglish: Balkans mein nationalist tanaav kyun paida hua?
answer_english: The Balkans, a region of geographical and ethnic variation whose inhabitants were broadly called Slavs, was largely under the Ottoman Empire. Romantic nationalism and the Ottoman Empire's disintegration made it explosive. Balkan peoples used history to claim lost independence, the Balkan states were jealous of each other and wanted more territory, and big powers, Russia, Germany, England and Austro-Hungary, competed to control the region. This led to a series of wars and finally the First World War.
answer_hinglish: Balkans, jahan bhaugolik aur ethnic vividhata thi aur log Slavs kehlate the, zyadatar Ottoman Empire ke under tha. Romantic nationalism aur Ottoman Empire ke bikharne ne ise vishphotak bana diya. Balkan log itihaas ka hawala dekar khoi azaadi maangte the, Balkan states ek-doosre se jalte aur zyada ilaaka chahte the, aur Russia, Germany, England aur Austro-Hungary jaisi badi powers ilaake pe control ke liye ladti thi. Isse kai yuddh hue aur aakhir mein First World War.
ncert_context: The most serious source of nationalist tension after 1871 was the Balkans, a region of geographical and ethnic variation comprising modern-day Romania, Bulgaria, Albania, Greece, Macedonia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Slovenia, Serbia and Montenegro, whose inhabitants were broadly known as Slavs. A large part was under the Ottoman Empire. Romantic nationalism and the disintegration of the Ottoman Empire made the region explosive. Balkan peoples used history to claim they had once been independent. question_english: How did European nationalism influence anti-imperial movements in colonies?
question_hinglish: European nationalism ne colonies ke anti-imperial andolanon ko kaise prabhavit kiya?

question_english: Choose three examples to show the contribution of culture to the growth of nationalism in Europe.
question_hinglish: Europe mein nationalism ke vikaas mein sanskriti ke yogdaan ke teen examples do.
answer_english: First, Romantics like Herder held that the national spirit (volksgeist) lay in folk songs, poetry and dances of the common people. Second, the Grimm brothers collected German folktales and compiled a German dictionary to oppose French domination and build German identity. Third, in partitioned Poland, Kurpinski's operas made the polonaise and mazurka national symbols, and the clergy's use of Polish became a symbol of resistance to Russia.
answer_hinglish: Pehla, Herder jaise Romantics maante the ki national aatma (volksgeist) aam logon ke lok geeton, kavita aur nritya mein hai. Doosra, Grimm brothers ne French dabdabe ka virodh karne aur German pehchaan banane ke liye German lok kathayein ikatthi ki aur German dictionary banaya. Teesra, bate hue Poland mein Kurpinski ke operas ne polonaise aur mazurka ko national prateek banaya, aur clergy ka Polish use karna Russia ke khilaaf virodh ka prateek bana.
ncert_context: Culture played an important role in creating the idea of the nation. Romantic philosopher Herder claimed true German culture lay among the common people, das volk, and the spirit of the nation (volksgeist) was popularised through folk songs, poetry and dances. The Grimm brothers collected folktales and published a German dictionary as part of the effort to oppose French domination and create a German national identity. In Poland, Karol Kurpinski turned folk dances like the polonaise and mazurka into nationalist symbols, and the use of Polish became a symbol of the struggle against Russian dominance.

question_english: Why is the growth of nationalism in the colonies linked to anti-colonial movements?
question_hinglish: Colonies mein nationalism ka vikaas anti-colonial andolanon se kyun juda hai?
answer_english: In India and many other colonies, people began discovering their unity in the process of struggling against colonialism. The shared sense of being oppressed under colonial rule became a bond that tied many different groups together. However, each class and group felt colonialism differently, so their ideas of freedom were not always the same, and the Congress under Gandhi tried to forge them into one movement.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the First World War create a new economic and political situation in India?
question_hinglish: First World War ne India mein nayi economic aur political sthiti kaise banayi?
answer_english: The war caused a huge rise in defence expenditure, financed by war loans and higher taxes: customs duties were raised and income tax introduced. Prices doubled between 1913 and 1918, causing extreme hardship. Forced recruitment of soldiers from villages caused widespread anger. Crop failures in 1918-19 and 1920-21 led to acute food shortages, and with an influenza epidemic, 12 to 13 million people died according to the 1921 census.

Gaon se zabardasti sainikon ki bharti se gussa faila. 1918-19 aur 1920-21 mein fasal kharab hone se khaane ki bhaari kami hui, aur influenza mahamaari ke saath 1921 census ke hisaab se 12 se 13 million log mare.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is meant by the idea of satyagraha?
question_hinglish: Satyagraha ke idea ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english: Satyagraha emphasised the power of truth and the need to search for truth. It held that if the cause was true and the struggle against injustice, physical force was unnecessary to fight the oppressor. Without seeking vengeance or being aggressive, a satyagrahi could win through non-violence by appealing to the oppressor's conscience, persuading people to see the truth rather than forcing it on them.
answer_hinglish: Satyagraha satya ki taakat aur satya ki khoj pe zor deta tha. Iske hisaab se agar kaaran sachcha ho aur ladai anyay ke khilaaf ho, toh atyaachaari se ladne ke liye shaaririk bal ki zaroorat nahi. Badla liye bina ya aakramak hue bina satyagrahi ahinsa se, atyaachaari ki antaraatma ko jagakar jeet sakta hai, logon ko satya zabardasti thopne ki jagah samjha kar.
ncert_context: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India in January 1915 from South Africa, where he had fought the racist regime with a novel method of mass agitation, satyagraha. The idea of satyagraha emphasised the power of truth and the need to search for truth. If the cause was true and the struggle against injustice, physical force was not necessary to fight the oppressor. Without seeking vengeance or being aggressive, a satyagrahi could win through non-violence by appealing to the conscience of the oppressor. People had to be persuaded to see the truth instead of being forced. Gandhi believed this dharma of non-violence could unite all Indians.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What did Gandhi mean when he said satyagraha is active resistance and not passive resistance?
question_hinglish: Gandhi ka kya matlab tha jab unhone kaha ki satyagraha passive nahi, active resistance hai?
answer_english: Gandhi said passive resistance is called the weapon of the weak, but satyagraha can be used only by the strong and calls for intense activity. It is not physical force: a satyagrahi does not inflict pain or seek the adversary's destruction and bears no ill-will. It is pure soul-force based on truth and love, and non-violence is the supreme dharma.
answer_hinglish: Gandhi ne kaha ki passive resistance ko kamzoron ka hathiyaar kaha jaata hai, par satyagraha sirf taakatwar use kar sakte hain aur isme bahut zyada sakriyata chahiye. Yeh shaaririk bal nahi hai: satyagrahi dushman ko dard nahi deta, uska vinaash nahi chahta aur man mein koi bair nahi rakhta. Yeh satya aur prem pe tiki shuddh aatma-shakti hai, aur ahinsa sabse bada dharma hai.
ncert_context: Gandhi wrote: 'It is said of passive resistance that it is the weapon of the weak, but the power which is the subject of this article can be used only by the strong. This power is not passive resistance; indeed it calls for intense activity. The movement in South Africa was not passive but active… Satyagraha is not physical force. A satyagrahi does not inflict pain on the adversary; he does not seek his destruction… In the use of satyagraha, there is no ill-will whatever. Satyagraha is pure soul-force. Truth is the very substance of the soul… Nonviolence is the supreme dharma.'

question_english: Which satyagraha movements did Gandhi organise after returning to India?
question_hinglish: India laut-ne ke baad Gandhi ne kaun se satyagraha andolan chalaye?
answer_english: In 1917 Gandhi went to Champaran in Bihar to inspire peasants against the oppressive plantation system. In 1918 he organised a satyagraha among cotton mill workers in Ahmedabad. Also in 1918, he supported peasants of Kheda district in Gujarat, who, hit by crop failure and plague, could not pay revenue and demanded relaxation of revenue collection.

ncert_context: After arriving in India, Mahatma Gandhi successfully organised satyagraha movements in various places. Affected by crop failure and a plague epidemic, the peasants of Kheda could not pay the revenue and were demanding that revenue collection be relaxed.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why were Indians outraged by the Rowlatt Act?
question_hinglish: Indians Rowlatt Act se naraz kyun the?
answer_english: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was hurriedly passed through the Imperial Legislative Council despite the united opposition of the Indian members. It gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years. Gandhi launched a nationwide non-violent satyagraha against it, starting with a hartal on 6 April.
answer_hinglish: 1919 ka Rowlatt Act Indian members ke ek-jut virodh ke bawajood Imperial Legislative Council mein jaldi-jaldi pass kiya gaya. Isne sarkar ko political gatividhiyan dabaane ki bahut badi taakat di aur political qaidiyon ko bina mukadme ke do saal tak band rakhne ki ijaazat di. Gandhi ne iske khilaaf 6 April ki hartal se shuru hone wala desh-vyapi ahinsak satyagraha chalaya.
ncert_context: In 1919 Gandhiji decided to launch a nationwide satyagraha against the proposed Rowlatt Act (1919). This Act had been hurriedly passed through the Imperial Legislative Council despite the united opposition of the Indian members. It gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities, and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years. Mahatma Gandhi wanted non-violent civil disobedience against such unjust laws, which would start with a hartal on 6 April.

question_english: What happened at Jallianwalla Bagh on 13 April 1919?
question_hinglish: 13 April 1919 ko Jallianwalla Bagh mein kya hua?
answer_english: A large crowd gathered in the enclosed ground of Jallianwalla Bagh; some came to protest the government's repressive measures, others to attend the annual Baisakhi fair, and many villagers were unaware of martial law. General Dyer entered, blocked the exit points and opened fire, killing hundreds. He later declared his object was to 'produce a moral effect', creating terror and awe in the minds of satyagrahis.

General Dyer ne andar aakar nikalne ke raaste band kiye aur bheed pe goli chalwayi, jisse saikdon log mare. Baad mein usne kaha ki uska maqsad 'moral effect' paida karna, yaani satyagrahiyon ke mann mein dar aur khauf bithana tha.

question_english: How did the government respond to protests after the Jallianwalla Bagh massacre?
question_hinglish: Jallianwalla Bagh hatyakaand ke baad virodh pe sarkar ne kaise react kiya?

Hinsa failte dekh Gandhi ne andolan rok diya.

question_english: Why did Gandhi take up the Khilafat issue?
question_hinglish: Gandhi ne Khilafat ka mudda kyun uthaya?
answer_english: The Rowlatt satyagraha was largely limited to cities, and Gandhi wanted a broader movement, which he felt needed Hindus and Muslims to come closer. After the First World War, Ottoman Turkey was defeated and a harsh treaty was rumoured against the Ottoman emperor, the Khalifa. A Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919, and leaders like Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali discussed united action with Gandhi, who saw it as a chance to bring Muslims into a unified national movement.

March 1919 mein Bombay mein Khilafat Committee bani, aur Muhammad Ali aur Shaukat Ali jaise leaders ne Gandhi se ek-jut andolan ki baat ki, jise Gandhi ne Muslims ko national andolan mein laane ka mauka maana.

question_english: What did Gandhi argue in Hind Swaraj, and how was non-cooperation to unfold?
question_hinglish: Hind Swaraj mein Gandhi ne kya kaha, aur non-cooperation kaise aage badhna tha?
answer_english: In Hind Swaraj (1909), Gandhi argued that British rule was established and survived only with Indians' cooperation; if Indians refused to cooperate, British rule would collapse within a year and swaraj would come. He proposed that non-cooperation unfold in stages, beginning with surrender of government titles and boycott of civil services, army, police, courts, legislative councils, schools and foreign goods, and, if the government used repression, a full civil disobedience campaign.

Unhone kaha ki non-cooperation charanon mein chale, sarkari titles lautane aur civil services, sena, police, courts, legislative councils, schools aur videshi saamaan ke boycott se shuru ho, aur agar sarkar dabaav kare toh poora civil disobedience campaign chalaya jaaye.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the middle class participate in the Non-Cooperation Movement in towns?
question_hinglish: Shehron mein middle class ne Non-Cooperation Movement mein kaise hissa liya?
answer_english: The movement began with middle-class participation in cities in January 1921. Thousands of students left government schools and colleges, headmasters and teachers resigned, and lawyers gave up practice. Council elections were boycotted in most provinces except Madras, where the non-Brahman Justice Party contested to gain power usually held by Brahmans.
answer_hinglish: Andolan January 1921 mein shehron mein middle class ki bhagidaari se shuru hua. Hazaaron students ne sarkari schools aur colleges chhode, headmasters aur teachers ne istifa diya, aur vakeelon ne vakalat chhodi. Madras ko chhod kar zyadatar provinces mein council elections ka boycott hua; Madras mein non-Brahman Justice Party ne woh power paane ke liye chunaav lada jo aksar sirf Brahmans ke paas hoti thi.
ncert_context: The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January 1921. The movement started with middle-class participation in the cities. Thousands of students left government-controlled schools and colleges, headmasters and teachers resigned, and lawyers gave up their legal practices. The council elections were boycotted in most provinces except Madras, where the Justice Party, the party of the non-Brahmans, felt that entering the council was one way of gaining some power, something that usually only Brahmans had access to.

question_english: The value of imported foreign cloth fell from Rs 102 crore to Rs 57 crore between 1921 and 1922. What was the fall in value, and by roughly what percentage?
question_hinglish: 1921 aur 1922 ke beech videshi kapde ke import ki keemat Rs 102 crore se Rs 57 crore ho gayi. Keemat kitni giri, aur lagbhag kitne percent?

question_english: Why did the Non-Cooperation Movement in the cities gradually slow down?
question_hinglish: Shehron mein Non-Cooperation Movement dheere-dheere dheema kyun pada?
answer_english: Khadi cloth was often more expensive than mass-produced mill cloth, and poor people could not afford it, so they could not boycott mill cloth for long. Boycotting British institutions also required alternative Indian institutions, which were slow to come up. So students and teachers began trickling back to government schools and lawyers returned to government courts.
answer_hinglish: Khadi aksar mill ke kapde se mehngi thi aur gareeb use khareed nahi sakte the, isliye woh lambe samay tak mill ke kapde ka boycott nahi kar sakte the. British sansthaon ke boycott ke liye Indian vikalp chahiye the, jo dheere bane. Isliye students aur teachers dheere-dheere sarkari schools mein laut-ne lage aur vakeel sarkari courts mein waapas kaam karne lage.
ncert_context: As the boycott spread, production of Indian textile mills and handlooms went up. But the movement in the cities gradually slowed down for a variety of reasons. Khadi cloth was often more expensive than mass-produced mill cloth and poor people could not afford to buy it. How then could they boycott mill cloth for too long? The boycott of British institutions posed a problem: alternative Indian institutions had to be set up for use in place of British ones, and these were slow to come up. So students and teachers began trickling back to government schools and lawyers joined back work in government courts.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What were the grievances and demands of the Awadh peasant movement?
question_hinglish: Awadh ke kisaan andolan ki shikaayatein aur maangein kya thi?
answer_english: Led by Baba Ramchandra, a sanyasi who had been an indentured labourer in Fiji, Awadh peasants opposed talukdars and landlords who demanded exorbitant rents and many cesses. Peasants had to do begar on landlords' farms without payment and, as tenants, had no security of tenure and were regularly evicted. They demanded reduction of revenue, abolition of begar and social boycott of oppressive landlords, organising nai-dhobi bandhs to deny landlords even barbers and washermen.
answer_hinglish: Fiji mein indentured labourer reh chuke sanyasi Baba Ramchandra ke netritva mein Awadh ke kisaan talukdaron aur zameendaaron ke khilaaf the jo bahut zyada lagaan aur kai cess maangte the. Kisaanon ko zameendaaron ke kheton pe bina mazdoori begar karni padti thi aur tenants hone se unhe zameen ki koi suraksha nahi thi, unhe baar-baar bedakhal kiya jaata tha. Unhone lagaan kam karne, begar khatam karne aur atyaachaari zameendaaron ke samajik boycott ki maang ki, aur nai-dhobi bandh karke zameendaaron ko naai aur dhobi ki sevaon se bhi vanchit kiya.
ncert_context: In Awadh, peasants were led by Baba Ramchandra, a sanyasi who had earlier been to Fiji as an indentured labourer. The movement was against talukdars and landlords who demanded exorbitantly high rents and a variety of other cesses. Peasants had to do begar and work at landlords' farms without any payment. As tenants they had no security of tenure, being regularly evicted so that they could acquire no right over the leased land. The movement demanded reduction of revenue, abolition of begar, and social boycott of oppressive landlords. In many places nai-dhobi bandhs were organised by panchayats to deprive landlords of the services of barbers and washermen.

question_english: Why was the Congress leadership unhappy with the way the Awadh peasant movement developed?
question_hinglish: Awadh ka kisaan andolan jis tarah badha, usse Congress leadership naraz kyun thi?

question_english: Why did the hill people of the Gudem Hills revolt in the early 1920s?
question_hinglish: 1920s ki shuruaat mein Gudem Hills ke pahadi logon ne vidroh kyun kiya?
answer_english: In the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh, as in other forest regions, the colonial government closed large forest areas, stopping people from grazing cattle and collecting fuelwood and fruits. This hurt their livelihoods and denied their traditional rights. When the government also forced them to do begar for road building, they revolted in a militant guerrilla movement.
answer_hinglish: Andhra Pradesh ke Gudem Hills mein, doosre jungle ilaakon ki tarah, colonial sarkar ne jungle ke bade hisse band kar diye, jisse log maveshi charaa nahi sakte the aur lakdi aur phal nahi le sakte the. Isse unki rozi aur paramparik adhikaar chhine. Jab sarkar ne sadak banane ke liye zabardasti begar bhi karwayi, toh unhone ugr guerrilla andolan ke roop mein vidroh kiya.

Their livelihoods were affected and they felt their traditional rights were being denied. When the government began forcing them to contribute begar for road building, the hill people revolted.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Who was Alluri Sitaram Raju, and how did he combine Gandhian ideas with armed struggle?
question_hinglish: Alluri Sitaram Raju kaun the, aur unhone Gandhian ideas ko hathiyaarband sangharsh ke saath kaise joda?
answer_english: Alluri Sitaram Raju led the Gudem rebels. He claimed special powers like correct astrological predictions, healing and surviving bullets, and the rebels saw him as an incarnation of God. He praised Gandhi, said he was inspired by Non-Cooperation, and persuaded people to wear khadi and give up drinking, but he insisted India could be liberated only by force. The rebels attacked police stations and fought guerrilla warfare; Raju was captured and executed in 1924 and became a folk hero.
answer_hinglish: Alluri Sitaram Raju ne Gudem vidrohiyon ka netritva kiya. Woh sahi jyotish bhavishyavaani, ilaaj karne aur goli se bachne jaisi khaas shaktiyon ka daava karte the, aur vidrohi unhe Bhagwan ka avatar maante the. Unhone Gandhi ki tareef ki, kaha ki woh Non-Cooperation se prerit hain, aur logon ko khadi pehenne aur sharaab chhodne ko kaha, par saath hi kaha ki India sirf bal se azaad ho sakta hai. Vidrohiyon ne police stations pe hamle kiye aur guerrilla yuddh lada; Raju 1924 mein pakde gaye aur faansi di gayi, aur lok-nayak ban gaye.
ncert_context: The person who came to lead the Gudem hill people was Alluri Sitaram Raju. He claimed he could make correct astrological predictions, heal people and survive even bullet shots. The rebels proclaimed that he was an incarnation of God. Raju talked of the greatness of Mahatma Gandhi, said he was inspired by the Non-Cooperation Movement, and persuaded people to wear khadi and give up drinking. But he asserted that India could be liberated only by the use of force, not non-violence. The Gudem rebels attacked police stations, attempted to kill British officials and carried on guerrilla warfare. Raju was captured and executed in 1924, and over time became a folk hero.

question_english: What did swaraj mean to plantation workers in Assam?
question_hinglish: Assam ke plantation mazdooron ke liye swaraj ka kya matlab tha?
answer_english: For Assam plantation workers, freedom meant the right to move freely in and out of the confined tea gardens and to keep a link with their home villages. Under the Inland Emigration Act of 1859, they could not leave without permission, which was rarely given. Hearing of Non-Cooperation, thousands defied the authorities and headed home, believing Gandhi Raj was coming and everyone would get land. Stranded by a railway and steamer strike, they were caught by police and brutally beaten.
answer_hinglish: Assam ke plantation mazdooron ke liye azaadi ka matlab tha band chaay bagaanon se aazaadi se aana-jaana aur apne gaon se rishta banaye rakhna. 1859 ke Inland Emigration Act ke under woh bina ijaazat bahar nahi ja sakte the, jo shayad hi milti thi. Non-Cooperation ki khabar sun kar hazaaron mazdoor adhikaariyon ki baat na maan kar ghar ki taraf chal pade, yeh sochkar ki Gandhi Raj aa raha hai aur sabko zameen milegi. Railway aur steamer hadtaal mein phans kar woh police ke haath pade aur bahut peete gaye.
ncert_context: For plantation workers in Assam, freedom meant the right to move freely in and out of the confined space in which they were enclosed, and retaining a link with the village from which they had come. When they heard of the Non-Cooperation Movement, thousands of workers defied the authorities, left the plantations and headed home, believing Gandhi Raj was coming and everyone would be given land. Stranded on the way by a railway and steamer strike, they were caught by the police and brutally beaten up.

question_english: What did Jawaharlal Nehru's experience near Rae Bareli in January 1921 show about non-violence?
question_hinglish: January 1921 mein Rae Bareli ke paas Jawaharlal Nehru ke anubhav ne ahinsa ke baare mein kya dikhaya?
answer_english: On 6 January 1921, police fired at peasants near Rae Bareli and stopped Nehru from going to the spot. Agitated, Nehru addressed the gathered peasants and later wrote that for a moment his blood was up and non-violence almost forgotten, but thinking of Gandhi and seeing the calm peasants, he spoke humbly on non-violence, admitting he needed the lesson more than they did, and the peasants dispersed peacefully.
answer_hinglish: 6 January 1921 ko Rae Bareli ke paas police ne kisaanon pe goli chalayi aur Nehru ko wahan jaane se roka. question_english: List the different social groups that joined the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1921.
question_hinglish: 1921 ke Non-Cooperation Movement mein shaamil hue alag social groups ki list banao.
answer_english: The movement drew in the urban middle class (students, teachers, headmasters and lawyers), merchants and traders who refused to deal in foreign goods, peasants in Awadh led by Baba Ramchandra, tribal people in the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh led by Alluri Sitaram Raju, and plantation workers in Assam. Har group apni ummeedon ke saath juda.
ncert_context: Various social groups participated in the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement, each with its own aspiration. subject: Social Science
question_english: What debates arose within the Congress after the Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn?
question_hinglish: Non-Cooperation Movement waapas lene ke baad Congress mein kya bahas hui?
answer_english: Some leaders, tired of mass struggles, wanted to contest elections to the provincial councils set up by the Government of India Act of 1919, to oppose British policies from within, argue for reform and show the councils were not truly democratic. C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress for this. But younger leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose pressed for more radical mass agitation and full independence.
answer_hinglish: Kuch leaders, jo bade andolanon se thak chuke the, Government of India Act 1919 se bani provincial councils ke elections ladna chahte the, taaki andar se British policies ka virodh karein, sudhaar ki maang karein aur dikhayein ki councils sach mein democratic nahi hain. Iske liye C. R. Das aur Motilal Nehru ne Congress ke andar Swaraj Party banayi. Par Jawaharlal Nehru aur Subhas Chandra Bose jaise young leaders zyada ugr jan-andolan aur poori azaadi chahte the.

Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress to argue for a return to council politics. subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the worldwide economic depression affect Indian peasants in the late 1920s?
question_hinglish: Late 1920s mein worldwide economic depression ne Indian kisaanon ko kaise prabhavit kiya?
answer_english: Agricultural prices began to fall from 1926 and collapsed after 1930. As demand for agricultural goods fell and exports declined, peasants found it difficult to sell their harvests and pay their revenue, so by 1930 the countryside was in turmoil.
answer_hinglish: Kheti ke daam 1926 se girne lage aur 1930 ke baad dhah gaye. Kheti ke saamaan ki demand aur export ghatne se kisaanon ko fasal bechna aur lagaan dena mushkil ho gaya, isliye 1930 tak gaon mein uthal-puthal mach gayi.

question_english: How did the demand for Purna Swaraj come about?
question_hinglish: Purna Swaraj ki maang kaise aayi?
answer_english: To win over Indians, Viceroy Lord Irwin announced in October 1929 a vague offer of 'dominion status' in an unspecified future and a Round Table Conference. This did not satisfy the Congress; radicals led by Nehru and Bose grew assertive while moderates lost influence. In December 1929, under Nehru's presidency, the Lahore Congress formalised the demand for 'Purna Swaraj' and declared 26 January 1930 as Independence Day, when people would pledge to struggle for complete independence.

December 1929 mein Nehru ki adhyakshata mein Lahore Congress ne 'Purna Swaraj' ki maang ko aupchaarik roop diya aur 26 January 1930 ko Independence Day ghoshit kiya, jab log poori azaadi ke liye ladne ki shapath lenge.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What did the Independence Day Pledge of 26 January 1930 declare?
question_hinglish: 26 January 1930 ki Independence Day Pledge mein kya ghoshana thi?
answer_english: The pledge declared that Indians, like any people, have the inalienable right to freedom, to enjoy the fruits of their toil and the necessities of life. If a government deprives people of these rights and oppresses them, they have the right to alter or abolish it. Since British rule had deprived Indians of freedom and ruined India economically, politically, culturally and spiritually, India must sever the British connection and attain Purna Swaraj.
answer_hinglish: Pledge mein kaha gaya ki Indians ko, kisi bhi janta ki tarah, azaadi, apni mehnat ka phal aur zaroori cheezon ka atoot haq hai. Agar koi sarkar logon ko in haqon se vanchit kare aur dabaaye, toh logon ko use badalne ya khatam karne ka haq hai. Kyunki British raaj ne Indians ki azaadi chheeni aur India ko economically, politically, culturally aur spiritually barbaad kiya, isliye India ko British rishta todkar Purna Swaraj paana chahiye.
ncert_context: The Independence Day Pledge, 26 January 1930: 'We believe that it is the inalienable right of the Indian people, as of any other people, to have freedom and to enjoy the fruits of their toil and have the necessities of life… if any government deprives a people of these rights and oppresses them, the people have a further right to alter it or to abolish it. The British Government in India has not only deprived the Indian people of their freedom but has based itself on the exploitation of the masses, and has ruined India economically, politically, culturally, and spiritually. We believe, therefore, that India must sever the British connection and attain Purna Swaraj or Complete Independence.'

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did Gandhi choose salt as a symbol to unite the nation?
question_hinglish: Gandhi ne desh ko jodne ke liye namak ko prateek kyun chuna?
answer_english: The Independence Day celebrations of 1930 attracted little attention, so Gandhi needed to connect the abstract idea of freedom to everyday life. On 31 January 1930 he sent Viceroy Irwin eleven demands covering all classes, from industrialists to peasants. The most stirring was abolishing the salt tax: salt was consumed by rich and poor alike and was an essential food, so the tax and government monopoly over salt production revealed the most oppressive face of British rule.

Sabse prerak maang namak tax hatane ki thi: namak ameer-gareeb sab khaate the aur yeh zaroori khaana tha, isliye namak pe tax aur iske utpaadan pe sarkari monopoly British raaj ka sabse atyaachaari chehra dikhata tha.
ncert_context: The Independence Day celebrations attracted very little attention, so Gandhi had to relate the abstract idea of freedom to concrete issues of everyday life. He found in salt a powerful symbol that could unite the nation. The most stirring was the demand to abolish the salt tax. Salt was consumed by the rich and the poor alike and was one of the most essential items of food. The tax on salt and the government monopoly over its production, Gandhi declared, revealed the most oppressive face of British rule.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the Salt March.
question_hinglish: Salt March ka varnan karo.
answer_english: Gandhi's letter to Irwin was an ultimatum: if the demands were not met by 11 March, the Congress would launch civil disobedience. Irwin refused to negotiate, so Gandhi began the salt march with 78 trusted volunteers, walking over 240 miles from Sabarmati ashram to the coastal town of Dandi in 24 days, about 10 miles a day. Thousands heard him along the way. On 6 April he reached Dandi and ceremonially broke the law by making salt from boiled sea water, beginning the Civil Disobedience Movement.
answer_hinglish: Gandhi ka Irwin ko patra ek ultimatum tha: agar 11 March tak maangein na maani gayi toh Congress civil disobedience shuru karegi. Irwin ne baat nahi ki, toh Gandhi 78 bharosemand volunteers ke saath Sabarmati ashram se Dandi tak 240 mile se zyada, 24 din mein, lagbhag 10 mile roz chale. Raaste mein hazaaron log unhe sunne aaye. 6 April ko Dandi pahunch kar unhone samudr ka paani ubaal kar namak banaya aur kanoon toda, jisse Civil Disobedience Movement shuru hua.
ncert_context: Gandhi's letter was an ultimatum: if the demands were not fulfilled by 11 March, the Congress would launch a civil disobedience campaign. Irwin was unwilling to negotiate. So Gandhi started his famous salt march accompanied by 78 trusted volunteers. The march was over 240 miles, from Gandhiji's ashram in Sabarmati to the Gujarati coastal town of Dandi. The volunteers walked for 24 days, about 10 miles a day. Thousands came to hear him wherever he stopped, and he urged them to peacefully defy the British. On 6 April he reached Dandi and ceremonially violated the law, manufacturing salt by boiling sea water. This marked the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

question_english: How was the Civil Disobedience Movement different from the Non-Cooperation Movement?
question_hinglish: Civil Disobedience Movement Non-Cooperation Movement se kaise alag tha?
answer_english: In the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1921-22, people were asked only to refuse cooperation with the British. subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the government respond as the Civil Disobedience Movement spread in 1930?
question_hinglish: 1930 mein Civil Disobedience Movement failne pe sarkar ne kaise react kiya?
answer_english: The government began arresting Congress leaders, leading to violent clashes. When Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a devout disciple of Gandhi, was arrested in April 1930, crowds in Peshawar faced armoured cars and police firing and many were killed. When Gandhi was arrested a month later, workers in Sholapur attacked police posts, municipal buildings, courts and railway stations. The government responded with brutal repression: peaceful satyagrahis, women and children were beaten and about 100,000 people were arrested.
answer_hinglish: Sarkar ne Congress leaders ko giraftaar karna shuru kiya, jisse hinsak takraav hue. April 1930 mein Gandhi ke bhakt shishya Abdul Ghaffar Khan ki giraftaari pe Peshawar mein bheed ne armoured cars aur police firing ka saamna kiya aur kai log mare. Ek mahine baad Gandhi ki giraftaari pe Sholapur ke mazdooron ne police chowkiyon, municipal imaaraton, courts aur railway stations pe hamle kiye. Sarkar ne kroor dabaav kiya: shaant satyagrahiyon, mahilaon aur bachchon ko peeta gaya aur lagbhag 100,000 log giraftaar hue.
ncert_context: Worried by the developments, the colonial government began arresting Congress leaders one by one, leading to violent clashes. A frightened government responded with brutal repression. Peaceful satyagrahis were attacked, women and children beaten, and about 100,000 people arrested.
