question_english: What was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, and what happened afterwards?
question_hinglish: Gandhi-Irwin Pact kya tha, aur uske baad kya hua?
answer_english: Facing brutal repression, Gandhi called off the movement and signed a pact with Irwin on 5 March 1931. Gandhi agreed to attend a Round Table Conference in London (the Congress had boycotted the first), and the government agreed to release political prisoners. In December 1931 Gandhi went to London but negotiations broke down. Back in India, he found a new cycle of repression, with Ghaffar Khan and Nehru jailed and the Congress declared illegal, so he relaunched Civil Disobedience, which lost momentum by 1934.
answer_hinglish: Kroor dabaav ke beech Gandhi ne andolan roka aur 5 March 1931 ko Irwin ke saath samjhauta kiya. Gandhi London mein Round Table Conference mein jaane ko maane (Congress ne pehli conference ka boycott kiya tha), aur sarkar political qaidiyon ko chhodne pe maani. December 1931 mein Gandhi London gaye par baatcheet toot gayi. Waapas aakar unhone dekha ki naya dabaav shuru ho gaya hai, Ghaffar Khan aur Nehru jail mein the aur Congress ko gair-kanooni ghoshit kar diya gaya tha, isliye unhone Civil Disobedience phir shuru kiya, jo 1934 tak dheema pad gaya.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did rich peasants join the Civil Disobedience Movement, and why were they disappointed?
question_hinglish: Ameer kisaan Civil Disobedience Movement mein kyun jude, aur woh niraash kyun hue?
answer_english: Rich peasant communities like the Patidars of Gujarat and the Jats of Uttar Pradesh grew commercial crops and were hard hit by the trade depression and falling prices. Losing cash income, they could not pay revenue, and the government refused to reduce it, so they enthusiastically supported the movement; for them swaraj meant a struggle against high revenues. They were deeply disappointed when it was called off in 1931 without revenue revision, and many refused to rejoin in 1932.

question_english: Why was the relationship between poor peasants and the Congress uncertain?
question_hinglish: Gareeb kisaanon aur Congress ka rishta anishchit kyun raha?
answer_english: Poorer peasants were often small tenants renting land from landlords. As the Depression shrank their cash incomes, they could not pay rent and wanted unpaid rent remitted, joining radical movements often led by Socialists and Communists. Fearing it would upset rich peasants and landlords, the Congress was unwilling to support 'no rent' campaigns in most places, so its relationship with poor peasants remained uncertain.

question_english: Why did Indian business classes support the Civil Disobedience Movement, and why did their enthusiasm decline?
question_hinglish: Indian business classes ne Civil Disobedience Movement ka saath kyun diya, aur unka josh kyun ghata?
answer_english: Indian merchants and industrialists, who had grown powerful through wartime profits, opposed colonial policies restricting business and wanted protection against foreign imports and a rupee-sterling exchange ratio that discouraged imports. They formed the Indian Industrial and Commercial Congress (1920) and FICCI (1927), and leaders like Purshottamdas Thakurdas and G. D. Birla gave financial help and refused to trade imported goods. After the Round Table Conference failed, they feared militant activities, prolonged business disruption and growing socialism among young Congress members.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did industrial workers participate in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
question_hinglish: Industrial mazdooron ne Civil Disobedience Movement mein kaise hissa liya?
answer_english: Industrial workers did not participate in large numbers, except in the Nagpur region, and stayed aloof as industrialists came closer to the Congress. Some selectively adopted Gandhian ideas like boycotting foreign goods in their own movements against low wages and poor conditions: railway workers struck in 1930, dockworkers in 1932, and Chotanagpur tin mine workers wore Gandhi caps in rallies in 1930. The Congress was reluctant to include workers' demands, fearing it would alienate industrialists.
answer_hinglish: Nagpur region ko chhod kar industrial mazdoor badi sankhya mein shaamil nahi hue, aur industrialists ke Congress ke kareeb aane se door rahe. Kuch ne kam mazdoori aur kharab haalaat ke khilaaf apne andolanon mein videshi saamaan ke boycott jaise Gandhian ideas apnaye: 1930 mein railway mazdooron aur 1932 mein dock mazdooron ne hadtaal ki, aur 1930 mein Chotanagpur ki tin khadaanon ke mazdooron ne Gandhi topi pehen kar rallies ki. Congress industrialists ke naraz hone ke dar se mazdooron ki maangein shaamil karne se hichki.
ncert_context: The industrial working classes did not participate in the Civil Disobedience Movement in large numbers, except in the Nagpur region. As the industrialists came closer to the Congress, workers stayed aloof. But the Congress was reluctant to include workers' demands, feeling this would alienate industrialists and divide the anti-imperial forces.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the role of women in the Civil Disobedience Movement, and did it change how their position was seen?
question_hinglish: Civil Disobedience Movement mein mahilaon ka kya role tha, aur kya isse unki sthiti ko dekhne ka nazariya badla?
answer_english: Women participated on a large scale: thousands came to hear Gandhi during the salt march, joined protest marches, made salt, picketed foreign cloth and liquor shops, and many went to jail. In towns they came from high-caste families and in villages from rich peasant households, and they saw service to the nation as a sacred duty. But this did not radically change their position: Gandhi believed women's duty was home and family, and the Congress long kept them out of positions of authority, wanting only their symbolic presence.
answer_hinglish: Mahilaon ne badi sankhya mein hissa liya: salt march mein hazaaron Gandhi ko sunne aayi, juloos mein shaamil hui, namak banaya, videshi kapde aur sharaab ki dukaanon pe picketing ki, aur kai jail gayi. Shehron mein woh oonchi jaati ke parivaaron se aur gaon mein ameer kisaan gharon se thi, aur desh seva ko pavitra kartavya maanne lagi. Par isse unki sthiti mein bada badlav nahi aaya: Gandhi maante the ki mahilaon ka kartavya ghar-parivaar hai, aur Congress ne lambe samay tak unhe adhikaar ke padon se door rakha, sirf unki prateekaatmak maujoodgi chahi.
ncert_context: Another important feature of the Civil Disobedience Movement was the large-scale participation of women. During the salt march, thousands of women came out to listen to Gandhi. They participated in protest marches, manufactured salt, and picketed foreign cloth and liquor shops. Many went to jail. In urban areas these women were from high-caste families; in rural areas from rich peasant households. They began to see service to the nation as a sacred duty. Yet this did not necessarily mean any radical change in how women's position was visualised. Gandhi was convinced women's duty was to look after home and hearth. For a long time the Congress was reluctant to allow women to hold any position of authority, keen only on their symbolic presence.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did Gandhi try to address untouchability?
question_hinglish: Gandhi ne chhua-chhoot ko door karne ki koshish kaise ki?
answer_english: Gandhi declared that swaraj would not come for a hundred years if untouchability was not eliminated. question_english: What was the Poona Pact of 1932?
question_hinglish: 1932 ka Poona Pact kya tha?
answer_english: Dr B. R. Ambedkar, who organised dalits into the Depressed Classes Association in 1930, demanded separate electorates for dalits at the second Round Table Conference, clashing with Gandhi. When the British conceded the demand, Gandhi began a fast unto death, believing separate electorates would slow dalits' integration into society. Ambedkar accepted Gandhi's position, resulting in the Poona Pact of September 1932, which gave the Depressed Classes (later Scheduled Castes) reserved seats in provincial and central councils, voted in by the general electorate.
answer_hinglish: 1930 mein dalits ko Depressed Classes Association mein sangathit karne wale Dr B. R. Ambedkar ne second Round Table Conference mein dalits ke liye separate electorate maangi aur Gandhi se unka matbhed hua. British ne maang maan li toh Gandhi ne aamaran anshan shuru kiya, yeh maante hue ki separate electorate dalits ke society mein ghulne-milne ko dheema karega. Ambedkar ne Gandhi ki baat maani aur September 1932 mein Poona Pact hua, jisne Depressed Classes (baad mein Scheduled Castes) ko provincial aur central councils mein reserved seats di, par unhe general electorate chunta.

question_english: Why were some Muslim political organisations lukewarm towards the Civil Disobedience Movement?
question_hinglish: Kuch Muslim political sangathan Civil Disobedience Movement ke prati thande kyun the?
answer_english: After the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement declined, many Muslims felt alienated from the Congress, which from the mid-1920s was more visibly associated with Hindu religious nationalist groups like the Hindu Mahasabha. ncert_context: After the decline of the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement, a large section of Muslims felt alienated from the Congress. subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the Quit India Movement?
question_hinglish: Quit India Movement kya tha?
answer_english: The failure of the Cripps Mission and the effects of World War II caused widespread discontent, leading Gandhi to demand complete British withdrawal. The Congress Working Committee passed the 'Quit India' resolution at Wardha on 14 July 1942, and the All India Congress Committee endorsed it in Bombay on 8 August 1942, when Gandhi gave his 'Do or Die' speech. It became a mass movement of students, workers and peasants, with leaders like Jayprakash Narayan, Aruna Asaf Ali, Ram Manohar Lohia and women like Matangini Hazra, Kanaklata Barua and Rama Devi. The British took over a year to suppress it.
answer_hinglish: Cripps Mission ki naakaami aur World War II ke asar se bahut asantosh faila, aur Gandhi ne British ki poori vaapsi ki maang ki. Congress Working Committee ne 14 July 1942 ko Wardha mein 'Quit India' resolution pass kiya, aur 8 August 1942 ko Bombay mein All India Congress Committee ne ise maana, jab Gandhi ne 'Do or Die' speech di. Yeh students, mazdooron aur kisaanon ka jan-andolan bana, jisme Jayprakash Narayan, Aruna Asaf Ali, Ram Manohar Lohia aur Matangini Hazra, Kanaklata Barua aur Rama Devi jaisi mahilayein shaamil thi. British ko ise dabaane mein ek saal se zyada laga.

The British took more than a year to suppress it.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the image of Bharat Mata develop as a symbol of the nation?
question_hinglish: Bharat Mata ki chhavi nation ke prateek ke roop mein kaise vikasit hui?
answer_english: In the twentieth century, India's identity came to be visually associated with Bharat Mata. The image was first created by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, who wrote 'Vande Mataram' in the 1870s as a hymn to the motherland; it was later included in his novel Anandamath and widely sung during the Swadeshi movement. Moved by Swadeshi, Abanindranath Tagore painted Bharat Mata as a calm, composed, divine and spiritual ascetic. The image later took many forms in popular prints, and devotion to it came to be seen as evidence of nationalism.
answer_hinglish: Twentieth century mein India ki pehchaan Bharat Mata ki chhavi se judi. Yeh chhavi pehli baar Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay ne banayi, jinhone 1870s mein maatribhoomi ki stuti mein 'Vande Mataram' likha; baad mein yeh unke upanyaas Anandamath mein aaya aur Swadeshi andolan mein khoob gaaya gaya. Swadeshi se prerit Abanindranath Tagore ne Bharat Mata ko shaant, sthir, divya aur aadhyatmik tapasvini ke roop mein chitrit kiya. Baad mein popular prints mein iske kai roop bane, aur iske prati bhakti nationalism ka saboot maani jaane lagi.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the revival of Indian folklore help build nationalism?
question_hinglish: Indian lok-kathaon ke punarjeevan ne nationalism banane mein kaise madad ki?
answer_english: In the late nineteenth century, nationalists recorded folk tales sung by bards and toured villages to gather folk songs and legends, believing they showed true traditional culture damaged by outside forces and that preserving them would restore pride in the past. In Bengal, Rabindranath Tagore collected ballads, nursery rhymes and myths and led the folk revival. In Madras, Natesa Sastri published a four-volume collection of Tamil folk tales, The Folklore of Southern India, calling folklore national literature.
answer_hinglish: Late nineteenth century mein nationalists ne bhaaton ki gaayi lok kathayein likhi aur gaon ghoom kar lok geet aur kahaniyan ikatthi ki, yeh maante hue ki inme bahari taakaton se bigdi asli paramparik sanskriti hai aur inhe bachana ateet pe garv waapas laayega. Bengal mein Rabindranath Tagore ne gaathayein, bachchon ki kavitayein aur mithak ikatthe karke lok punarjeevan ki aguaai ki. Madras mein Natesa Sastri ne Tamil lok kathaon ka chaar-volume sangrah The Folklore of Southern India chhapa aur lok-sahitya ko national literature kaha.
ncert_context: Ideas of nationalism also developed through a movement to revive Indian folklore. In late-nineteenth-century India, nationalists began recording folk tales sung by bards and toured villages to gather folk songs and legends. These tales, they believed, gave a true picture of traditional culture corrupted by outside forces. Preserving them was essential to discover national identity and restore pride in the past. In Bengal, Rabindranath Tagore collected ballads, nursery rhymes and myths, and led the folk revival. In Madras, Natesa Sastri published a massive four-volume collection of Tamil folk tales, The Folklore of Southern India. He believed folklore was national literature, 'the most trustworthy manifestation of people's real thoughts and characteristics'.

question_english: Compare the Swadeshi flag of Bengal with Gandhi's Swaraj flag of 1921.
question_hinglish: Bengal ke Swadeshi jhande ko Gandhi ke 1921 ke Swaraj jhande se compare karo.
answer_english: The Swadeshi movement flag was a red, green and yellow tricolour with eight lotuses representing the eight provinces of British India and a crescent moon representing Hindus and Muslims. Gandhi's Swaraj flag of 1921 was a red, green and white tricolour with a spinning wheel in the centre, representing the Gandhian ideal of self-help. Carrying such flags during marches became a symbol of defiance.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did unity within the national movement often break down?
question_hinglish: National andolan ke andar ekta aksar kyun toot jaati thi?
answer_english: Anger against colonial rule brought diverse groups into a common struggle, and the Congress under Gandhi tried to channel grievances into organised movements. But each group participated with its own aspirations, so freedom meant different things to different people. The Congress kept trying to ensure one group's demands did not alienate another, which is why unity often broke down, and high points of nationalist unity were followed by phases of disunity, producing a nation with many voices.
answer_hinglish: Colonial raaj ke khilaaf gusse ne vividh groups ko ek sangharsh mein joda, aur Gandhi ke under Congress ne shikaayaton ko sangathit andolanon mein badalne ki koshish ki. Par har group apni ummeedon ke saath juda, isliye azaadi ka matlab har kisi ke liye alag tha. Congress koshish karti rahi ki ek group ki maang doosre ko naraz na kare, isi wajah se ekta aksar toot-ti thi, aur ekta ke oonche daur ke baad phoot ke daur aate the, jisse kai awaazon wala nation ban raha tha.
ncert_context: A growing anger against the colonial government brought various groups and classes into a common struggle in the first half of the twentieth century. The Congress under Gandhi tried to channel people's grievances into organised movements. But diverse groups participated with varied aspirations and expectations. As their grievances were wide-ranging, freedom from colonial rule meant different things to different people. The Congress continuously attempted to resolve differences and ensure that the demands of one group did not alienate another. This is precisely why the unity within the movement often broke down. High points of nationalist unity were followed by phases of disunity and inner conflict. What was emerging was a nation with many voices wanting freedom from colonial rule.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why do historians say that the making of the global world has a long history?
question_hinglish: Historians kyun kehte hain ki global world banne ka itihaas lamba hai?
answer_english: Although globalisation is often linked to the last 50 years, human societies have become steadily more interlinked throughout history. Travellers, traders, priests and pilgrims travelled vast distances for knowledge, opportunity or spiritual fulfilment, or to escape persecution, carrying goods, money, values, skills, ideas, inventions and even germs. As early as 3000 BCE, coastal trade linked the Indus valley with West Asia, and Maldivian cowries reached China and East Africa.
answer_hinglish: Globalisation ko aksar pichhle 50 saal se joda jaata hai, par poore itihaas mein insaani samaaj lagaataar jude hain. Answer the question in English using only the given context.

Although globalisation is often linked to the last 50 years, human societies have become steadily more interlinked throughout history. Travellers, traders, priests and pilgrims travelled vast distances for knowledge, opportunity or spiritual fulfilment, or to escape persecution, carrying goods, money, values, skills, ideas, inventions and even germs. As early as 3000 BCE, coastal trade linked the Indus valley with West Asia, and Maldivian cowries reached China and East Africa.

question_english: Give examples of how food shows long-distance cultural exchange in the pre-modern world.
question_hinglish: Pre-modern duniya mein khaana lambi doori ke saanskritik lena-dena ko kaise dikhata hai, examples do.
answer_english: It is believed noodles travelled west from China to become spaghetti, or that Arab traders took pasta to fifth-century Sicily; similar foods existed in India and Japan, so the true origin may never be known. Also, common foods like potatoes, soya, groundnuts, maize, tomatoes, chillies and sweet potatoes came from the American Indians and reached Europe and Asia only after Columbus reached the Americas about five centuries ago.
answer_hinglish: Maana jaata hai ki noodles China se pashchim jaakar spaghetti bane, ya Arab vyapaari pasta ko fifth century ke Sicily le gaye; India aur Japan mein bhi aise khaane the, isliye asli shuruaat shayad kabhi pata na chale. Saath hi aalu, soya, moongfali, makka, tamatar, mirch aur shakarkand jaise aam khaane American Indians se aaye aur lagbhag paanch sadi pehle Columbus ke America pahunchne ke baad hi Europe aur Asia pahunche.
ncert_context: Food offers many examples of long-distance cultural exchange. Traders and travellers introduced new crops to the lands they travelled. Many of our common foods such as potatoes, soya, groundnuts, maize, tomatoes, chillies and sweet potatoes were not known to our ancestors until about five centuries ago. They were introduced in Europe and Asia after Christopher Columbus accidentally discovered the Americas, and came from America's original inhabitants, the American Indians.

question_english: How did the global transfer of disease help in the colonisation of the Americas?
question_hinglish: Pre-modern duniya mein bimaariyon ke failne ne America ke colonisation mein kaise madad ki?
answer_english: The most powerful weapon of the Spanish conquerors was not a military one but germs such as smallpox that they carried. Because of their long isolation, America's original inhabitants had no immunity to these European diseases. Smallpox spread deep into the continent, even ahead of Europeans, killing and decimating whole communities and paving the way for conquest. Unlike guns, which could be captured and turned against invaders, diseases could not be used against the mostly immune conquerors.
answer_hinglish: Spanish vijetaon ka sabse taakatwar hathiyaar koi military hathiyaar nahi, balki unke saath aaye smallpox jaise keetanu the. Lambe samay tak alag rehne se America ke mool nivaasiyon mein in European bimaariyon ke khilaaf immunity nahi thi. Smallpox Europeans se bhi aage mahadweep ke andar tak faila aur poore samudaay khatam kar diye, jisse vijay aasaan hui. Bandookon ko chheen kar hamlaawaron ke khilaaf use kiya ja sakta tha, par bimaariyon ko nahi, kyunki vijeta zyadatar immune the.

question_english: What are the three types of flows within international economic exchange?
question_hinglish: International economic lena-dena mein teen tarah ke flows kaun se hain?
answer_english: Economists identify three flows: the flow of trade, which in the nineteenth century was largely trade in goods like cloth or wheat; the flow of labour, or migration of people in search of employment; and the movement of capital for short-term or long-term investments over long distances. These flows were closely interwoven, though labour migration was often more restricted than goods or capital flows.
answer_hinglish: Economists teen flows maante hain: trade ka flow, jo nineteenth century mein zyadatar kapde ya gehun jaise saamaan ka vyapaar tha; labour ka flow, yaani rozgaar ki talaash mein logon ka pravaas; aur capital ki aavajahi, yaani lambi doori pe short-term ya long-term nivesh. Yeh flows aapas mein gahre jude the, par labour migration aksar saamaan ya capital se zyada seemit tha.
ncert_context: Economists identify three types of movement or flows within international economic exchanges. The first is the flow of trade, which in the nineteenth century referred largely to trade in goods (e.g., cloth or wheat). The second is the flow of labour, the migration of people in search of employment. The third is the movement of capital for short-term or long-term investments over long distances. All three flows were closely interwoven and affected people's lives more deeply than ever before. Labour migration was often more restricted than goods or capital flows.

question_english: What were the Corn Laws, and what were the effects of their abolition?
question_hinglish: Corn Laws kya the, aur unhe khatam karne ka kya asar hua?
answer_english: Population growth and expanding cities raised Britain's demand for food grains and pushed up prices, and under pressure from landed groups the government restricted corn imports through the Corn Laws. Unhappy with high food prices, industrialists and urban dwellers forced their abolition. Afterwards, food could be imported more cheaply than it could be produced in Britain, so British agriculture could not compete; vast lands were left uncultivated and thousands lost work, flocking to cities or migrating overseas.
answer_hinglish: Badhti aabaadi aur faile shehron se Britain mein anaaj ki demand aur daam badhe, aur zameendaar groups ke dabaav mein sarkar ne Corn Laws se makke ka import roka. Mehnge khaane se naraz industrialists aur shehri logon ne in kanoonon ko khatam karwaya. Iske baad khaana Britain mein ugaane se sasta import hone laga, isliye British kheti mukabla nahi kar paayi; bahut zameen khaali chhooti aur hazaaron logon ki naukri gayi, jo shehron mein gaye ya videsh chale gaye.
ncert_context: Population growth from the late eighteenth century increased demand for food grains in Britain. Vast areas of land were left uncultivated, and thousands were thrown out of work. They flocked to the cities or migrated overseas.

question_english: How did Britain's decision to import food lead to increased migration to America and Australia?
question_hinglish: Britain ke khaana import karne ke faisle se America aur Australia ki taraf pravaas kaise badha?
answer_english: As food prices fell after the Corn Laws were abolished, consumption rose, and faster industrial growth raised incomes and food imports. To meet British demand, lands were cleared in Eastern Europe, Russia, America and Australia. This needed railways to link farms to ports, new harbours and settlements, all requiring capital and labour. Capital flowed from London, and labour shortages in America and Australia drew migrants: nearly 50 million people emigrated from Europe there in the nineteenth century.
answer_hinglish: Corn Laws khatam hone se khaana sasta hua, khapat badhi, aur tez industrial growth se aamdani aur food imports badhe. British demand poori karne ke liye Eastern Europe, Russia, America aur Australia mein zameen saaf ki gayi. Iske liye kheton ko ports se jodne wali railways, naye bandargaah aur bastiyan chahiye thi, jinke liye capital aur labour lage. Capital London se aaya, aur America aur Australia mein mazdooron ki kami ne pravaasiyon ko kheecha: nineteenth century mein lagbhag 50 million log Europe se wahan gaye.
ncert_context: As food prices fell, consumption in Britain rose. Faster industrial growth led to higher incomes and more food imports. Around the world, in Eastern Europe, Russia, America and Australia, lands were cleared and food production expanded to meet British demand. Railways were needed to link agricultural regions to ports, new harbours built and people settled on the lands. All these activities required capital and labour. Capital flowed from financial centres such as London. The demand for labour where it was short, as in America and Australia, led to more migration. Nearly 50 million people emigrated from Europe to America and Australia in the nineteenth century. Worldwide some 150 million left their homes.

question_english: How had a global agricultural economy taken shape by 1890?
question_hinglish: 1890 tak ek global agricultural economy kaise ban gayi thi?
answer_english: By 1890, food no longer came from a nearby village but from thousands of miles away. It was grown not by a peasant on his own land but by a possibly recently arrived agricultural worker on a large farm that a generation earlier had been forest. It was transported by railways built for that purpose and by ships increasingly manned by low-paid workers from southern Europe, Asia, Africa and the Caribbean, with complex changes in labour, capital, ecology and technology.
answer_hinglish: 1890 tak khaana paas ke gaon se nahi, hazaaron mile door se aane laga. Ise apni zameen jot-ne wala kisaan nahi, balki shayad haal hi mein aaya khetihar mazdoor ek bade farm pe ugaata tha jo ek peedhi pehle jungle tha. Ise isi kaam ke liye bani railways aur southern Europe, Asia, Africa aur Caribbean ke kam mazdoori wale mazdooron se chalne wale jahazon se laaya jaata tha, aur labour, capital, paryavaran aur technology mein kai badlav aaye.
ncert_context: By 1890, a global agricultural economy had taken shape, accompanied by complex changes in labour movement patterns, capital flows, ecologies and technology. Food no longer came from a nearby village or town, but from thousands of miles away. It was not grown by a peasant tilling his own land, but by an agricultural worker, perhaps recently arrived, working on a large farm that only a generation ago had most likely been a forest. It was transported by railway, built for that very purpose, and by ships increasingly manned by low-paid workers from southern Europe, Asia, Africa and the Caribbean.

question_english: How did refrigerated ships change the meat trade and diets in Europe?
question_hinglish: Refrigerated jahazon ne Europe mein meat vyapaar aur khaan-paan ko kaise badla?
answer_english: Till the 1870s, animals were shipped live from America to Europe, taking up ship space, and many died, fell ill or lost weight, making meat an expensive luxury beyond the reach of the poor. Refrigerated ships allowed animals to be slaughtered in America, Australia or New Zealand and shipped as frozen meat, reducing shipping costs and meat prices. Many poor Europeans could now add meat, butter and eggs to bread and potatoes, and better living conditions promoted social peace at home and support for imperialism abroad.
answer_hinglish: 1870s tak jaanwar America se Europe zinda bheje jaate the, jo jahaz ki jagah lete the, aur kai mar jaate, beemar padte ya wazan kho dete, isliye meat gareebon ki pahunch se bahar mehnga shauk tha. Refrigerated jahazon se jaanwaron ko America, Australia ya New Zealand mein hi kaat kar jamaya hua meat bheja jaane laga, jisse shipping kharch aur meat ke daam ghate. Kai gareeb Europeans roti aur aalu ke saath meat, makkhan aur ande khaane lage, aur behtar jeevan se desh mein shanti aur bahar imperialism ke liye samarthan badha.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did Europeans face a labour shortage in Africa, and how did they force Africans into wage work?
question_hinglish: Africa mein Europeans ko mazdooron ki kami kyun hui, aur unhone Africans ko wage work mein kaise dhakela?
answer_english: Africa had abundant land and a small population, and land and livestock sustained livelihoods, with few consumer goods to buy, so people rarely worked for wages. Europeans wanting plantations and mines faced a shortage of wage labour. They imposed heavy taxes payable only through wage work, changed inheritance laws so only one family member inherited land, pushing others into the labour market, and confined mineworkers in compounds.
answer_hinglish: Africa mein zameen bahut aur aabaadi kam thi, zameen aur maveshi se guzaara hota tha aur khareedne layak saamaan kam tha, isliye log shayad hi mazdoori karte the. Plantations aur khadaanein chaahne wale Europeans ko mazdoor nahi mile. Unhone bhaari tax lagaye jo sirf mazdoori se chukaaye ja sakte the, virasat ke kanoon badle taaki parivaar ka sirf ek sadasya zameen paaye aur baaki mazdoori mein jaayein, aur khadaan mazdooron ko ahaaton mein band rakha.
ncert_context: Historically, Africa had abundant land and a relatively small population. For centuries, land and livestock sustained African livelihoods and people rarely worked for a wage. There were few consumer goods that wages could buy. Europeans came to Africa hoping to establish plantations and mines, but faced a shortage of labour willing to work for wages. Employers used many methods to recruit and retain labour. Heavy taxes were imposed which could be paid only by working for wages. Inheritance laws were changed so that only one member of a family was allowed to inherit land, pushing the others into the labour market. Mineworkers were confined in compounds and not allowed to move about freely.

question_english: What is indentured labour?
question_hinglish: Indentured labour kya hai?
answer_english: An indentured labourer is a bonded labourer under contract to work for an employer for a specific amount of time, to pay off his passage to a new country or home. Indian indentured labourers were hired under contracts promising return travel to India after five years' work on the employer's plantation.

Indian indentured mazdooron ko aise contracts pe rakha jaata tha jo maalik ke plantation pe paanch saal kaam ke baad India waapsi ka vaada karte the.

question_english: Why did people from certain Indian regions migrate as indentured labourers, and where did they go?
question_hinglish: Kuch Indian ilaakon ke log indentured mazdoor bankar kyun gaye, aur kahan gaye?
answer_english: Most came from eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, central India and the dry districts of Tamil Nadu, where in the mid-nineteenth century cottage industries declined, land rents rose and lands were cleared for mines and plantations. Unable to pay rents and deeply indebted, the poor migrated for work. Main destinations were the Caribbean islands (Trinidad, Guyana, Surinam), Mauritius and Fiji; Tamil migrants went to Ceylon and Malaya, and workers were recruited for Assam's tea plantations.
answer_hinglish: Zyadatar log eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, central India aur Tamil Nadu ke sookhe districts se the, jahan mid-nineteenth century mein kutir udyog ghate, lagaan badha aur khadaanon aur plantations ke liye zameen saaf hui. Lagaan na de paane aur karz mein doobne se gareeb kaam ki talaash mein gaye. Mukhya thikaane Caribbean dweep (Trinidad, Guyana, Surinam), Mauritius aur Fiji the; Tamil pravaasi Ceylon aur Malaya gaye, aur Assam ke chaay bagaanon ke liye bhi bharti hui.

question_english: Why has nineteenth-century indenture been described as a 'new system of slavery'?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century ke indenture ko 'gulaami ka naya system' kyun kaha gaya?
answer_english: Recruiting agents, paid a small commission, gave false information about destinations, travel, the nature of work and living conditions, often not even telling migrants about the long sea voyage, and sometimes forcibly abducted unwilling migrants. On plantations, living and working conditions were harsh and workers had few legal rights. Ram Narain Tewary's testimony from Demerara describes bruised hands, jail for missing work, heavy tasks and wage deductions.
answer_hinglish: Chhota commission paane wale agents thikaanon, yaatra, kaam aur rehne ki haalat ke baare mein jhoothi jaankari dete, aksar lambi samudri yaatra ka bhi nahi batate, aur kabhi na chaahne walon ko zabardasti utha le jaate. Plantations pe rehne aur kaam ki haalat kathor thi aur mazdooron ke kanooni adhikaar kam the. Demerara se Ram Narain Tewary ki gawaahi chhile haathon, kaam na kar paane pe jail, bhaari kaam aur mazdoori mein katautiyon ka zikr karti hai.
ncert_context: Recruitment was done by agents engaged by employers and paid a small commission. Agents tempted migrants with false information about destinations, modes of travel, the nature of the work, and living and working conditions. Often migrants were not told they were to embark on a long sea voyage. Sometimes agents forcibly abducted less willing migrants. Nineteenth-century indenture has been described as a 'new system of slavery'. On arrival, labourers found living and working conditions harsh, with few legal rights. Ram Narain Tewary, who spent ten years on Demerara, testified that he bruised his hands, was jailed for 14 days for missing work, tasks were extremely heavy and wages were deducted.

question_english: How did indentured workers develop new forms of cultural expression?
question_hinglish: Indentured mazdooron ne saanskritik abhivyakti ke naye roop kaise banaye?
answer_english: Many workers blended old and new cultural forms. In Trinidad, the annual Muharram procession became a riotous carnival called 'Hosay' (for Imam Hussain) joined by workers of all races and religions. The protest religion of Rastafarianism, made famous by Bob Marley, is said to reflect links with Indian migrants, and 'chutney music' in Trinidad and Guyana expresses the post-indenture experience. Such fusion is part of the making of the global world.
answer_hinglish: Kai mazdooron ne purane aur naye saanskritik roop milaaye. Trinidad mein saalana Muharram juloos 'Hosay' (Imam Hussain ke liye) naam ke masti bhare carnival mein badal gaya jisme har nasl aur dharm ke mazdoor shaamil hue. Bob Marley se mashhoor virodh-dharm Rastafarianism mein Indian pravaasiyon se rishta dikhta hai, aur Trinidad aur Guyana ka 'chutney music' indenture ke baad ke anubhav ko dikhata hai. Aisa mel global world banne ka hissa hai.
ncert_context: Workers discovered their own ways of surviving. Many escaped into the wilds, facing severe punishment if caught. Others developed new forms of individual and collective self-expression, blending different cultural forms, old and new. In Trinidad the annual Muharram procession was transformed into a riotous carnival called 'Hosay' (for Imam Hussain) in which workers of all races and religions joined. The protest religion of Rastafarianism (made famous by Jamaican reggae star Bob Marley) is said to reflect links with Indian migrants to the Caribbean. 'Chutney music', popular in Trinidad and Guyana, is another creative expression of the post-indenture experience. These forms of cultural fusion are part of the making of the global world.

question_english: What role did Indian bankers and traders play abroad in the nineteenth century?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century mein videsh mein Indian bankers aur vyapaariyon ki kya bhoomika thi?
answer_english: Groups like the Shikaripuri Shroffs and Nattukottai Chettiars financed export agriculture in Central and Southeast Asia with their own funds or loans from European banks, had sophisticated systems to transfer money over long distances, and developed indigenous corporate forms. Indian traders and moneylenders followed Europeans into Africa, while Hyderabadi Sindhi traders went beyond European colonies, setting up emporia at busy ports from the 1860s to sell curios to growing numbers of tourists.
answer_hinglish: Shikaripuri Shroffs aur Nattukottai Chettiars jaise groups ne apne paise ya European banks se udhaar lekar Central aur Southeast Asia mein export kheti ko paisa diya, lambi doori pe paisa bhejne ka unnat system rakha, aur desi corporate dhaanche banaye. Indian vyapaari aur saahookar Europeans ke peeche Africa gaye, jabki Hyderabadi Sindhi vyapaari European colonies se aage gaye aur 1860s se vyast bandargaahon pe dukaanein kholkar badhte paryatakon ko curios beche.

The Shikaripuri Shroffs and Nattukottai Chettiars were among the bankers and traders who financed export agriculture in Central and Southeast Asia, using their own funds or those borrowed from European banks. Indian traders and moneylenders followed European colonisers into Africa. Hyderabadi Sindhi traders ventured beyond European colonies; from the 1860s they established flourishing emporia at busy ports worldwide, selling curios to tourists.

question_english: How did India's exports change during the nineteenth century?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century mein India ke exports kaise badle?
answer_english: Fine Indian cottons were historically exported to Europe, but Britain imposed tariffs on cloth imports to protect its industry, and Indian textiles faced stiff competition elsewhere. The share of cotton textiles in India's exports fell from about 30 per cent around 1800 to 15 per cent by 1815 and below 3 per cent by the 1870s. Meanwhile raw material exports rose: raw cotton's share rose from 5 to 35 per cent between 1812 and 1871, indigo was important, and opium to China became for a while India's largest export.
answer_hinglish: Pehle India ka mahin cotton Europe jaata tha, par Britain ne apne udyog ko bachane ke liye kapde ke import pe tariff lagaye aur Indian kapdon ko doosri jagah kada mukabla mila. India ke exports mein cotton textiles ka hissa 1800 ke aas-paas 30 percent se 1815 tak 15 percent aur 1870s tak 3 percent se neeche aa gaya. Wahin kachche maal ka export badha: 1812 se 1871 ke beech raw cotton ka hissa 5 se 35 percent hua, indigo important raha, aur China ko afeem kuch samay India ka sabse bada export bani.
ncert_context: Historically, fine Indian cottons were exported to Europe. With industrialisation, British industrialists pressured the government to restrict cotton imports; tariffs were imposed and Indian textiles faced stiff competition. The share of cotton textiles in exports from India fell from some 30 per cent around 1800 to 15 per cent by 1815, and below 3 per cent by the 1870s. Exports of raw materials increased: between 1812 and 1871, the share of raw cotton exports rose from 5 per cent to 35 per cent. Indigo was another important export. Opium shipments to China grew rapidly from the 1820s to become for a while India's single largest export; Britain used the earnings to finance its tea imports from China.

question_english: How did India help Britain through the multilateral settlement system?
question_hinglish: Multilateral settlement system ke through India ne Britain ki madad kaise ki?
answer_english: British manufactures flooded India, and the value of British exports to India was much higher than British imports from India, giving Britain a trade surplus with India. Britain used this surplus to balance its trade deficits with countries from which it imported more than it sold. This multilateral settlement system lets one country's deficit with another be settled by its surplus with a third. The surplus also paid 'home charges': British officials' remittances, interest on India's external debt and pensions of British officials.
answer_hinglish: British saamaan Indian market mein bhar gaya, aur Britain ka India ko export India se import se kaafi zyada tha, jisse Britain ka India ke saath trade surplus bana. Britain ne is surplus se un deshon ke saath apna trade deficit poora kiya jinse woh bechne se zyada khareedta tha. Multilateral settlement system mein ek desh ka doosre se deficit teesre desh ke saath surplus se poora hota hai. Is surplus se 'home charges' bhi chukaye gaye: British officials ka ghar bheja paisa, India ke videshi karz ka byaaj aur British officials ki pension.
ncert_context: Over the nineteenth century, British manufactures flooded the Indian market. The value of British exports to India was much higher than the value of British imports from India, so Britain had a 'trade surplus' with India. Britain used this surplus to balance its trade deficits with other countries from which it was importing more than it was selling to. This is how a multilateral settlement system works: it allows one country's deficit with another to be settled by its surplus with a third country. India thus played a crucial role in the world economy. Britain's trade surplus in India also paid the 'home charges': private remittances by British officials and traders, interest payments on India's external debt, and pensions of British officials in India.

question_english: What is a tariff?
question_hinglish: Tariff kya hai?

Tariffs were imposed on cloth imports into Britain, and the inflow of fine Indian cotton began to decline.

question_english: How did the First World War turn the US from a debtor into a creditor?
question_hinglish: First World War ne US ko debtor se creditor kaise banaya?
answer_english: The war snapped economic links between major powers fighting each other. To pay for it, Britain borrowed large sums from US banks and the US public. So at the war's end, the US and its citizens owned more overseas assets than foreigners owned in the US, transforming it from an international debtor into an international creditor.

question_english: Why did Britain face a prolonged economic crisis after the First World War?
question_hinglish: First World War ke baad Britain ko lamba economic sankat kyun jhelna pada?
answer_english: While Britain was preoccupied with war, industries developed in India and Japan, so Britain struggled to regain its Indian market and compete with Japan. It had borrowed heavily from the US and was burdened with external debt. When the war boom ended, production contracted and unemployment rose, and the government cut war spending, causing huge job losses: in 1921 one in every five British workers was out of work.
answer_hinglish: Jab Britain yuddh mein laga tha, India aur Japan mein udyog viksit hue, isliye Britain ko Indian market waapas paane aur Japan se mukabla karne mein mushkil hui. Usne US se bhaari udhaar liya tha aur videshi karz mein dooba tha. War boom khatam hone pe production ghata aur berozgaari badhi, aur sarkar ne yuddh kharch kaata, jisse bahut naukriyan gayi: 1921 mein har paanch British mazdooron mein se ek berozgaar tha.
ncert_context: Britain, the world's leading economy pre-war, faced a prolonged crisis. While Britain was preoccupied with war, industries had developed in India and Japan. After the war Britain found it difficult to recapture its position in the Indian market and to compete with Japan. To finance war expenditure Britain had borrowed liberally from the US, leaving it burdened with huge external debts. The war had led to an economic boom; when it ended, production contracted and unemployment increased. The government reduced bloated war expenditures. These developments led to huge job losses: in 1921 one in every five British workers was out of work.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did Henry Ford introduce mass production, and how did it affect workers?
question_hinglish: Henry Ford ne mass production kaise shuru kiya, aur isse mazdooron pe kya asar hua?
answer_english: Henry Ford adapted the assembly line of a Chicago slaughterhouse to his Detroit car plant. Workers repeated a single task mechanically at a pace set by the conveyor belt, unable to delay, take breaks or chat, so cars came off the line at three-minute intervals; the T-Model Ford was the first mass-produced car. Unable to cope, workers quit in large numbers, so Ford doubled the daily wage to $5 in January 1914, banned trade unions, and recovered the cost by repeatedly speeding up the line.
answer_hinglish: Henry Ford ne Chicago ke kasaaikhaane ki assembly line ko apne Detroit car plant mein apnaya. Mazdoor conveyor belt ki raftaar pe ek hi kaam baar-baar mashini tareeke se karte, na ruk sakte, na aaraam kar sakte, na baat kar sakte, isliye har teen minute mein car nikalti; T-Model Ford pehli mass-produced car thi. Dabaav na jhel paane se mazdoor badi sankhya mein naukri chhodne lage, toh Ford ne January 1914 mein roz ki mazdoori dugni karke $5 ki, trade unions pe rok lagayi, aur line ki raftaar baar-baar badha kar kharch waapas nikaala.
ncert_context: A pioneer of mass production was Henry Ford. He adapted the assembly line of a Chicago slaughterhouse to his car plant in Detroit. The assembly line forced workers to repeat a single task mechanically and continuously at a pace dictated by the conveyor belt. No worker could delay, take a break or have a friendly word with a workmate. Ford's cars came off the line at three-minute intervals. The T-Model Ford was the world's first mass-produced car. Workers unable to cope quit in large numbers. Ford doubled the daily wage to $5 in January 1914 and banned trade unions. He recovered the high wage by repeatedly speeding up the production line, calling it his 'best cost-cutting decision'.

question_english: What were the causes of the Great Depression?
question_hinglish: Great Depression ke kaaran kya the?
answer_english: First, agricultural overproduction: as prices fell, farmers produced even more to maintain income, worsening the glut and pushing prices further down, so produce rotted unsold. Second, many countries financed investment through US loans; at the first sign of trouble US lenders panicked, and overseas loans fell from over $1 billion in early 1928 to a quarter of that a year later, causing bank failures in Europe, currency collapses like the pound sterling, and deeper slumps in Latin America. The US also doubled import duties, hurting world trade.
answer_hinglish: Pehla, kheti ka zyada utpaadan: daam girne pe kisaanon ne aamdani bachane ke liye aur zyada ugaaya, jisse bharmaar badhi aur daam aur gire, aur fasal bina bike sad gayi. Doosra, kai deshon ne US ke karz se nivesh kiya tha; mushkil ke pehle sanket pe US lenders ghabra gaye, aur videshi karz 1928 ki shuruaat ke $1 billion se zyada se ek saal baad chauthai reh gaya, jisse Europe mein banks doobe, pound sterling jaisi currencies giri aur Latin America mein mandi badhi. US ne import duty dugni ki, jisse world trade ko chot lagi.
ncert_context: The depression was caused by several factors. First, agricultural overproduction remained a problem, worsened by falling prices. As agricultural incomes declined, farmers expanded production to maintain income, worsening the glut and pushing prices down further. Farm produce rotted for lack of buyers. Second, in the mid-1920s many countries financed investments through loans from the US. US lenders panicked at the first sign of trouble. In the first half of 1928, US overseas loans amounted to over $1 billion; a year later it was one quarter of that. In Europe this led to failure of major banks and collapse of currencies such as the pound sterling; in Latin America it intensified the slump in agricultural and raw material prices. The US doubled import duties, a severe blow to world trade.

question_english: How did the Great Depression affect the United States?
question_hinglish: Great Depression ne United States ko kaise prabhavit kiya?
answer_english: The US was the industrial country most severely hit. Banks slashed domestic lending and called back loans; farms could not sell harvests and businesses collapsed. subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the impact of the Great Depression on the Indian economy?
question_hinglish: Great Depression ka Indian economy pe kya asar hua?
answer_english: India's exports and imports nearly halved between 1928 and 1934, and wheat prices fell by 50 per cent. Peasants suffered more than urban dwellers, since the colonial government refused to reduce revenue demands. Bengal's jute growers saw raw jute prices crash over 60 per cent as gunny exports collapsed. Peasants used savings, mortgaged land and sold jewellery, so India exported gold, which helped Britain's recovery but not peasants. Urban fixed-income groups were better off as prices fell, and tariff protection boosted industrial investment.
answer_hinglish: 1928 se 1934 ke beech India ke exports aur imports lagbhag aadhe ho gaye, aur gehun ke daam 50 percent gire. Kisaanon ko shehri logon se zyada nuksaan hua, kyunki colonial sarkar ne lagaan kam nahi kiya. Gunny bags ka export girne se Bengal ke jute kisaanon ke kachche jute ke daam 60 percent se zyada gire. Kisaanon ne bachat khatam ki, zameen girvi rakhi aur gehne beche, isliye India ne sona export kiya, jisse Britain ko fayda hua par kisaanon ko nahi. Shehar ke fixed aamdani wale log daam girne se behtar haalat mein the, aur tariff suraksha se industrial nivesh badha.
ncert_context: The depression immediately affected Indian trade. India's exports and imports nearly halved between 1928 and 1934. Between 1928 and 1934, wheat prices in India fell by 50 per cent. Peasants suffered more than urban dwellers. Though agricultural prices fell sharply, the colonial government refused to reduce revenue demands. Bengal jute producers grew raw jute processed into gunny bags; as gunny exports collapsed, the price of raw jute crashed more than 60 per cent. Peasants used up savings, mortgaged lands and sold jewellery, and India became an exporter of gold. Keynes thought Indian gold exports promoted global recovery; they helped Britain's recovery but did little for peasants. Those with fixed incomes in towns were better off. Industrial investment grew as the government extended tariff protection.

question_english: How was the Second World War different in its human cost, and what shaped post-war reconstruction?
question_hinglish: Second World War insaani nuksaan mein kaise alag tha, aur yuddh ke baad ke punarnirmaan ko kisne aakar diya?
answer_english: The Second World War, fought for six years between the Axis (Nazi Germany, Japan, Italy) and the Allies (Britain, France, Soviet Union, US), killed at least 60 million people, about 3 per cent of the 1939 world population. Unlike earlier wars, most deaths occurred outside battlefields, and more civilians than soldiers died. Reconstruction was shaped by the US emerging as the dominant Western power and by the Soviet Union's dominance after transforming into a world power.
answer_hinglish: Axis (Nazi Germany, Japan, Italy) aur Allies (Britain, France, Soviet Union, US) ke beech chhe saal chale Second World War mein kam se kam 60 million log mare, jo 1939 ki duniya ki aabaadi ka lagbhag 3 percent tha. Pehle ke yuddhon se alag, zyadatar maut yuddh-kshetra ke bahar hui aur sainikon se zyada aam log mare. Punarnirmaan ko US ke Western duniya ki sabse badi taakat banne aur world power bane Soviet Union ke dabdabe ne aakar diya.
ncert_context: The Second World War was fought between the Axis powers (mainly Nazi Germany, Japan and Italy) and the Allies (Britain, France, the Soviet Union and the US) for six years. At least 60 million people, about 3 per cent of the world's 1939 population, are believed to have been killed. Unlike earlier wars, most deaths took place outside the battlefields; many more civilians than soldiers died. Vast parts of Europe and Asia were devastated. Two crucial influences shaped post-war reconstruction: the US's emergence as the dominant economic, political and military power in the Western world, and the dominance of the Soviet Union, which had transformed itself from a backward agricultural country into a world power.

question_english: What two lessons did economists and politicians learn from the inter-war economic experience?
question_hinglish: Inter-war economic anubhav se economists aur politicians ne kaun se do sabak seekhe?
answer_english: First, an industrial society based on mass production cannot be sustained without mass consumption, which needs high and stable incomes and therefore steady full employment; since markets alone cannot guarantee this, governments must intervene to minimise fluctuations in price, output and employment. Second, full employment could be achieved only if governments had power to control flows of goods, capital and labour with the outside world.
answer_hinglish: Pehla, mass production pe tiki industrial society mass consumption ke bina nahi chal sakti, jiske liye oonchi aur sthir aamdani aur isliye lagaataar poora rozgaar chahiye; akele markets yeh guarantee nahi kar sakte, isliye sarkar ko daam, utpaadan aur rozgaar ke utaar-chadhaav kam karne ke liye dakhal dena hoga. Doosra, poora rozgaar tabhi mil sakta hai jab sarkar ke paas bahar ke saath saamaan, capital aur labour ke flow ko control karne ki taakat ho.
ncert_context: Economists and politicians drew two key lessons from inter-war experiences. First, an industrial society based on mass production cannot be sustained without mass consumption. To ensure mass consumption, high and stable incomes were needed, which required steady, full employment. Markets alone could not guarantee full employment, so governments would have to step in to minimise fluctuations of price, output and employment. The second lesson related to a country's economic links with the outside world: the goal of full employment could only be achieved if governments had power to control flows of goods, capital and labour.

question_english: What is meant by the Bretton Woods Agreement?
question_hinglish: Bretton Woods Agreement ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english: The framework of the post-war international economic system, aimed at preserving economic stability and full employment in the industrial world, was agreed at the UN Monetary and Financial Conference at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, in July 1944. It set up the IMF to deal with members' external surpluses and deficits and the World Bank to finance post-war reconstruction. The system used fixed exchange rates: currencies were pegged to the dollar, and the dollar was anchored to gold at $35 per ounce.
answer_hinglish: Industrial duniya mein economic sthirta aur poora rozgaar banaye rakhne wale post-war international economic system ka dhaancha July 1944 mein Bretton Woods, New Hampshire mein UN Monetary and Financial Conference mein tay hua. Isne members ke bahari surplus aur deficit sambhalne ke liye IMF aur yuddh ke baad punarnirmaan ke liye World Bank banaya. System fixed exchange rates pe tha: currencies dollar se judi thi, aur dollar sone se $35 per ounce pe bandha tha.
ncert_context: The main aim of the post-war international economic system was to preserve economic stability and full employment in the industrial world. Its framework was agreed at the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference held in July 1944 at Bretton Woods in New Hampshire, USA. It established the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to deal with external surpluses and deficits of member nations, and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank) to finance post-war reconstruction. These are called the Bretton Woods twins. The Bretton Woods system was based on fixed exchange rates: national currencies were pegged to the dollar, and the dollar was anchored to gold at $35 per ounce.

question_hinglish: IMF aur World Bank mein decision-making kiske haath mein hai?

question_english: Why were the Bretton Woods institutions unsuitable for newly independent countries?
question_hinglish: Bretton Woods sansthayein naye azaad deshon ke liye sahi kyun nahi thi?
answer_english: After the war, most colonies in Asia and Africa became independent but were burdened by poverty and lack of resources from long colonial rule. The IMF and World Bank were designed for industrial countries' financial needs and not equipped to handle poverty and underdevelopment. From the late 1950s they shifted attention to developing countries, so ironically former colonies came under guidance of agencies dominated by former colonial powers, which still controlled resources like minerals and land.
answer_hinglish: Yuddh ke baad Asia aur Africa ki zyadatar colonies azaad hui par lambe colonial raaj se gareebi aur sansaadhanon ki kami mein doobi thi. IMF aur World Bank industrial deshon ki financial zarooraton ke liye bane the aur gareebi aur pichhdepan se nipatne ke layak nahi the. Late 1950s se unhone developing deshon pe dhyaan diya, isliye vidambana yeh hui ki purani colonies un sansthaon ki salah pe chalne lagi jinpe purani colonial powers haavi thi, jo ab bhi khanij aur zameen jaise sansaadhan control karti thi.
ncert_context: After the Second World War, most colonies in Asia and Africa emerged as independent nations over two decades. They were overburdened by poverty and lack of resources, and handicapped by long colonial rule. The IMF and World Bank were designed to meet the financial needs of industrial countries and were not equipped to cope with poverty and lack of development in former colonies. As Europe and Japan rebuilt, they grew less dependent on these institutions, so from the late 1950s the Bretton Woods institutions shifted attention to developing countries. Ironically, newly independent countries came under the guidance of agencies dominated by former colonial powers, which still controlled vital resources such as minerals and land.

question_english: What was the G-77, and how was it a reaction to the Bretton Woods twins?
question_hinglish: G-77 kya tha, aur yeh Bretton Woods twins ki pratikriya kaise tha?
answer_english: Most developing countries did not benefit from the fast growth of Western economies in the 1950s and 1960s, and they were guided by IMF and World Bank agencies dominated by former colonial powers, while large foreign corporations exploited their resources cheaply. So they organised as the Group of 77 to demand a new international economic order (NIEO): real control over their natural resources, more development assistance, fairer prices for raw materials and better access for their manufactured goods in developed markets.
answer_hinglish: Zyadatar developing deshon ko 1950s aur 1960s mein Western economies ke tez vikaas ka fayda nahi mila, aur woh purani colonial powers ke dabdabe wale IMF aur World Bank ki salah pe chalte the, jabki badi videshi companies unke sansaadhan saste mein loot-ti thi. Isliye unhone Group of 77 banakar new international economic order (NIEO) ki maang ki: apne prakritik sansaadhanon pe asli control, zyada vikaas sahayata, kachche maal ke uchit daam aur developed markets mein unke saamaan ki behtar pahunch.
ncert_context: Former colonial powers still controlled vital resources such as minerals and land in many former colonies. Large corporations of powerful countries like the US often secured rights to exploit developing countries' natural resources very cheaply. Most developing countries did not benefit from the fast growth of Western economies in the 1950s and 1960s. Therefore they organised themselves as a group, the Group of 77 (G-77), to demand a new international economic order (NIEO). By the NIEO they meant a system that would give them real control over their natural resources, more development assistance, fairer prices for raw materials, and better access for their manufactured goods in developed countries' markets.

question_english: How did the international financial system change from the mid-1970s?

question_english: Give two examples from history showing the impact of technology on food availability.
question_hinglish: Itihaas se do examples do jo dikhayein ki technology ne khaane ki uplabdhta ko kaise prabhavit kiya.
answer_english: First, refrigerated ships allowed animals to be slaughtered in America, Australia or New Zealand and shipped as frozen meat, lowering meat prices so Europe's poor could add meat, butter and eggs to their diet. Second, railways, larger ships and new harbours linked newly cleared farmlands in Eastern Europe, Russia, America and Australia to ports, bringing food cheaply to Britain from thousands of miles away.
answer_hinglish: Pehla, refrigerated jahazon se jaanwaron ko America, Australia ya New Zealand mein kaat kar jamaya hua meat bheja gaya, jisse meat sasta hua aur Europe ke gareeb meat, makkhan aur ande khaane lage. Doosra, railways, bade jahazon aur naye bandargaahon ne Eastern Europe, Russia, America aur Australia ke naye kheton ko ports se joda, jisse hazaaron mile door se khaana saste mein Britain pahuncha.
ncert_context: Refrigerated ships enabled the transport of perishable foods over long distances. Animals were slaughtered at the starting point—in America, Australia or New Zealand—and transported to Europe as frozen meat, lowering meat prices; the poor in Europe could add meat, butter and eggs to their diet. Around the world lands were cleared to meet British food demand; railways were needed to link agricultural regions to ports, and new harbours built. Faster railways, lighter wagons and larger ships helped move food more cheaply and quickly from faraway farms to final markets.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Give one example each of the flow of trade, labour and capital involving India in the nineteenth century.
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century mein India se jude trade, labour aur capital ke flow ka ek-ek example do.
answer_english: Trade: India exported raw cotton, indigo and opium, whose share rose as cotton textile exports fell, while British manufactures flooded India. Labour: Indian indentured workers from eastern UP, Bihar, central India and Tamil Nadu migrated to the Caribbean, Mauritius, Fiji, Ceylon and Malaya. Capital: Shikaripuri Shroffs and Nattukottai Chettiars financed export agriculture in Central and Southeast Asia.
answer_hinglish: Trade: India ne raw cotton, indigo aur afeem export ki, jinka hissa cotton kapdon ka export girne ke saath badha, jabki British saamaan India mein bhar gaya. Labour: eastern UP, Bihar, central India aur Tamil Nadu ke Indian indentured mazdoor Caribbean, Mauritius, Fiji, Ceylon aur Malaya gaye. Capital: Shikaripuri Shroffs aur Nattukottai Chettiars ne Central aur Southeast Asia mein export kheti ko paisa diya.
ncert_context: Economists identify three flows: trade, labour and capital. India's exports of raw cotton rose from 5 to 35 per cent of exports between 1812 and 1871, and opium to China became for a while its largest export, while British manufactures flooded India. Indian indentured workers from eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, central India and Tamil Nadu went to the Caribbean, Mauritius, Fiji, Ceylon and Malaya. The Shikaripuri Shroffs and Nattukottai Chettiars financed export agriculture in Central and Southeast Asia.

question_english: What did the images 'Dawn of the Century' and 'Two Magicians' convey about industrialisation?
question_hinglish: 'Dawn of the Century' aur 'Two Magicians' tasveeron ne industrialisation ke baare mein kya sandesh diya?
answer_english: E.T. Paull's 1900 music book cover showed a goddess-like angel of progress carrying the new century's flag on a winged wheel of time, with railways, cameras, machines, printing presses and factories behind her. A trade magazine image contrasted Aladdin, representing the East and the past, with a modern mechanic, representing the West and modernity, who builds bridges, ships and towers. Both glorified machines and gave a triumphant account of industrialisation as a story of progress.
answer_hinglish: E.T. Paull ki 1900 ki music book ke cover pe ek devi jaisi pragati ki angel nayi sadi ka jhanda liye samay ke pankh wale pahiye pe baithi thi, aur peeche railway, camera, machines, printing press aur factory the. Ek trade magazine ki tasveer mein Aladdin, jo East aur ateet ka prateek tha, ko ek modern mechanic se compare kiya gaya, jo West aur modernity ka prateek tha aur pul, jahaz aur towers banata tha. Dono ne machines ki tareef ki aur industrialisation ko pragati ki jeet wali kahani ki tarah dikhaya.
ncert_context: In 1900, music publisher E.T. Paull produced a music book whose cover announced the 'Dawn of the Century'. At the centre is a goddess-like figure, the angel of progress, bearing the flag of the new century, perched on a wheel with wings symbolising time. Behind her are signs of progress: railway, camera, machines, printing press and factory. A trade magazine picture showed two magicians: Aladdin from the Orient, who built a palace with his magic lamp, and the modern mechanic, who with modern tools builds bridges, ships, towers and high-rise buildings. Aladdin represents the East and the past, the mechanic the West and modernity. These images offer a triumphant account of the modern world.

messages.content:
Context:
In 1900, music publisher E.T. Paull produced a music book whose cover announced the 'Dawn of the Century'. At the centre is a goddess-like figure, the angel of progress, bearing the flag of the new century, perched on a wheel with wings symbolising time. Behind her are signs of progress: railway, camera, machines, printing press and factory. A trade magazine picture showed two magicians: Aladdin from the Orient, who built a palace with his magic lamp, and the modern mechanic, who with modern tools builds bridges, ships, towers and high-rise buildings. Aladdin represents the East and the past, the mechanic the West and modernity. These images offer a triumphant account of the modern world.

Question:
'Dawn of the Century' aur 'Two Magicians' tasveeron ne industrialisation ke baare mein kya sandesh diya?

Intent Type: explain_concept
Answer the question in Hinglish using only the given context.

E.T. Paull ki 1900 ki music book ke cover pe ek devi jaisi pragati ki angel nayi sadi ka jhanda liye samay ke pankh wale pahiye pe baithi thi, aur peeche railway, camera, machines, printing press aur factory the. Ek trade magazine ki tasveer mein Aladdin, jo East aur ateet ka prateek tha, ko ek modern mechanic se compare kiya gaya, jo West aur modernity ka prateek tha aur pul, jahaz aur towers banata tha. Dono ne machines ki tareef ki aur industrialisation ko pragati ki jeet wali kahani ki tarah dikhaya.

question_hinglish: 'Orient' shabd ka kya matlab hai?

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is meant by proto-industrialisation?
question_hinglish: Proto-industrialisation ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english: Proto-industrialisation refers to the phase of large-scale industrial production for an international market that existed before factories, in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Town merchants supplied money to peasants and artisans in the countryside and persuaded them to produce for international markets. It was controlled by merchants, with goods produced by many producers working within their family farms, not in factories.
answer_hinglish: Proto-industrialisation seventeenth aur eighteenth century ka woh daur hai jab factories se pehle international market ke liye bade paimaane pe industrial utpaadan hota tha. Shehar ke vyapaari gaon ke kisaanon aur kaarigaron ko paisa dekar unse international market ke liye saamaan banwate the. Yeh vyapaariyon ke control mein tha, aur saamaan factories mein nahi, balki parivaar ke kheton pe kaam karne wale bahut saare utpaadak banate the.
ncert_context: Even before factories began to dot the landscape in England and Europe, there was large-scale industrial production for an international market, not based on factories. Many historians refer to this phase as proto-industrialisation (proto: indicating the first or early form of something). In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, merchants from towns in Europe began moving to the countryside, supplying money to peasants and artisans and persuading them to produce for an international market. This system was part of a network of commercial exchanges, controlled by merchants, and goods were produced by a vast number of producers working within their family farms, not in factories.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did merchants from European towns begin employing peasants and artisans in the villages in the seventeenth century?
question_hinglish: Seventeenth century mein European shehron ke vyapaari gaon ke kisaanon aur kaarigaron se kaam kyun karwane lage?
answer_english: With expanding world trade and colonies, demand for goods grew, but merchants could not expand production in towns because urban crafts and trade guilds were powerful. Guilds trained craftspeople, controlled production, regulated competition and prices, and restricted entry of new people, and rulers granted them monopoly rights over specific products. So it was difficult for new merchants to set up business in towns, and they turned to the countryside.
answer_hinglish: World trade aur colonies ke vistaar se saamaan ki demand badhi, par vyapaari shehron mein utpaadan nahi badha sakte the kyunki wahan crafts aur trade guilds taakatwar the. Guilds kaarigaron ko train karte, utpaadan control karte, mukabla aur daam niyantrit karte aur naye logon ko aane se rokte the, aur raajaon ne unhe khaas cheezon pe monopoly di thi. Isliye naye vyapaariyon ke liye shehar mein business karna mushkil tha, aur woh gaon ki taraf mude.
ncert_context: With the expansion of world trade and acquisition of colonies, demand for goods grew. But merchants could not expand production within towns because urban crafts and trade guilds were powerful. These were associations of producers that trained craftspeople, maintained control over production, regulated competition and prices, and restricted the entry of new people into the trade. Rulers granted guilds the monopoly right to produce and trade in specific products. It was therefore difficult for new merchants to set up business in towns. So they turned to the countryside.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did poor peasant households eagerly agree to work for merchants?
question_hinglish: Gareeb kisaan parivaar vyapaariyon ke liye kaam karne ko utsuk kyun hue?
answer_english: Open fields were disappearing and commons were being enclosed, so cottagers and poor peasants who had depended on common lands for firewood, berries, vegetables, hay and straw needed new income. Their tiny plots could not employ all household members. Working for merchants let them stay in the countryside, keep cultivating their plots, supplement their shrinking farm income and make fuller use of family labour.
answer_hinglish: Khule khet khatam ho rahe the aur common zameen gheri ja rahi thi, isliye lakdi, ber, sabzi, ghaas aur bhoose ke liye common zameen pe nirbhar gareeb kisaanon ko nayi aamdani chahiye thi. Unki chhoti zameen pe parivaar ke sab logon ko kaam nahi milta tha. Vyapaariyon ke liye kaam karke woh gaon mein reh sakte the, apni zameen jot sakte the, ghatti kheti ki aamdani badha sakte the aur parivaar ki mehnat ka poora use kar sakte the.
ncert_context: This was a time when open fields were disappearing and commons were being enclosed. Cottagers and poor peasants who had depended on common lands for firewood, berries, vegetables, hay and straw had to look for alternative income. Many had tiny plots of land which could not provide work for all household members. So when merchants offered advances to produce goods, peasant households eagerly agreed. By working for the merchants, they could remain in the countryside and continue to cultivate their small plots. Income from proto-industrial production supplemented their shrinking income from cultivation and allowed a fuller use of family labour.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe how the merchant clothier organised cloth production in England under proto-industrialisation.
question_hinglish: Proto-industrialisation mein England ke merchant clothier ne kapde ka utpaadan kaise sangathit kiya, batao.
answer_english: The merchant clothier, based in a town, bought wool from a wool stapler and carried it to spinners. The spun yarn passed in stages to weavers, fullers and dyers, mostly working in the countryside. Finishing was done in London, which became a finishing centre, before export merchants sold the cloth internationally. Each merchant employed 20 to 25 workers at every stage, so each clothier controlled hundreds of workers.
answer_hinglish: Shehar mein rehne wala merchant clothier wool stapler se oon khareed kar kaatne walon tak le jaata tha. Kaata hua dhaaga charanon mein bunkaron, fullers aur rangrezon tak jaata tha, jo zyadatar gaon mein kaam karte the. Finishing London mein hoti thi, jo finishing centre ban gaya, aur phir export vyapaari kapda international market mein bechte the. Har charan mein har vyapaari 20 se 25 mazdoor rakhta tha, isliye har clothier saikdon mazdooron ko control karta tha.
ncert_context: Within this system a close relationship developed between town and countryside. Merchants were based in towns but the work was done mostly in the countryside. A merchant clothier in England purchased wool from a wool stapler and carried it to the spinners; the yarn was taken in subsequent stages to weavers, fullers and then dyers. The finishing was done in London before the export merchant sold the cloth in the international market. London came to be known as a finishing centre. At each stage 20 to 25 workers were employed by each merchant, so each clothier was controlling hundreds of workers.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Who were the stapler and the fuller, and what is carding?
question_hinglish: Stapler aur fuller kaun the, aur carding kya hai?
answer_english: A stapler is a person who 'staples' or sorts wool according to its fibre. A fuller is a person who 'fulls', or gathers, cloth by pleating. Carding is the process in which fibres such as cotton or wool are prepared before spinning.
answer_hinglish: Stapler woh vyakti hai jo oon ko uske resho ke hisaab se chhaant-ta hai. Fuller woh vyakti hai jo kapde ko plate bana kar ikattha karta hai. Carding woh process hai jisme cotton ya oon jaise reshe kataai se pehle taiyaar kiye jaate hain.

question_english: Which were the most dynamic industries in Britain's industrialisation, and how did leadership shift?
question_hinglish: Britain ke industrialisation mein sabse gatisheel udyog kaun se the, aur netritva kaise badla?
answer_english: Cotton and metals were the most dynamic industries. Cotton led the first phase of industrialisation up to the 1840s. After that, iron and steel led the way, as railway expansion in England from the 1840s and in the colonies from the 1860s rapidly raised demand. By 1873 Britain was exporting iron and steel worth about £77 million, double the value of its cotton exports.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why do historians say that industrialisation in Britain was not rapid or limited to factories?
question_hinglish: Historians kyun kehte hain ki Britain ka industrialisation na tez tha na sirf factories tak seemit?
answer_english: New industries could not easily displace traditional ones: even at the end of the nineteenth century, less than 20 per cent of the workforce was in technologically advanced sectors, and much textile output came from domestic units. Traditional industries like food processing, building, pottery, glass, tanning and furniture grew through small innovations. Technology spread slowly because it was expensive, broke down and was costly to repair, so the typical mid-nineteenth-century worker was a traditional craftsperson and labourer, not a machine operator.
answer_hinglish: Naye udyog purane udyogon ko aasaani se hata nahi paaye: nineteenth century ke ant tak bhi 20 percent se kam mazdoor unnat technology wale sectors mein the, aur kapde ka bada hissa gharelu ikaiyon mein banta tha. Food processing, nirmaan, mitti ke bartan, kaanch, chamda aur furniture jaise paramparik udyog chhote innovations se badhe. Technology dheere faili kyunki woh mehngi thi, kharab hoti thi aur marammat mehngi thi, isliye mid-nineteenth century ka aam mazdoor machine operator nahi, paramparik kaarigar aur mazdoor tha.

question_english: How does the history of the steam engine show that new technology spread slowly?
question_hinglish: Steam engine ka itihaas kaise dikhata hai ki nayi technology dheere faili?
answer_english: James Watt improved Newcomen's steam engine and patented it in 1781, and his friend Mathew Boulton manufactured it, but for years he found no buyers. At the start of the nineteenth century there were no more than 321 steam engines in all of England: 80 in cotton, nine in wool and the rest in mining, canal works and iron works. Other industries did not use them till much later, showing that even powerful technology was slow to be accepted.
