subject: Social Science
question_english: What was life like for workers in nineteenth-century Britain?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century Britain mein mazdooron ki zindagi kaisi thi?
answer_english: Getting a job depended on networks of friends and kin; those without connections waited weeks, sleeping under bridges, in Night Refuges or in Poor Law Casual Wards. Seasonal work meant long periods without employment, and odd jobs were hard to find. Wages rose a little, but rising prices during the Napoleonic War cut real wages, and income depended on days of work. About 10 per cent of the urban population was extremely poor even in good times, and in slumps like the 1830s unemployment rose to 35 to 75 per cent.
answer_hinglish: Naukri dosto aur rishtedaaron ke network pe nirbhar thi; bina jaan-pehchaan wale hafton intezaar karte, pulon ke neeche, Night Refuges ya Poor Law ke Casual Wards mein sote. Mausami kaam ka matlab tha lambe samay berozgaari, aur chhote-mote kaam milna mushkil tha. Mazdoori thodi badhi, par Napoleonic War mein badhte daamon ne asli kamaai ghatayi, aur aamdani kaam ke dinon pe nirbhar thi. Achhe samay mein bhi shehar ki lagbhag 10 percent aabaadi bahut gareeb thi, aur 1830s jaisi mandi mein berozgaari 35 se 75 percent tak pahunchi.
ncert_context: Getting a job depended on networks of friendship and kin. Many jobseekers waited weeks, spending nights under bridges or in night shelters, Night Refuges set up by private individuals, or Casual Wards maintained by the Poor Law authorities. Seasonality meant prolonged periods without work. Wages increased somewhat in the early nineteenth century, but when prices rose sharply during the Napoleonic War, the real value of earnings fell. Income depended on the period of employment. At the best of times till the mid-nineteenth century, about 10 per cent of the urban population were extremely poor. In slumps like the 1830s, unemployment went up to between 35 and 75 per cent in different regions.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why do average wage figures tell us little about the welfare of nineteenth-century workers?
question_hinglish: Average mazdoori ke aankde nineteenth century ke mazdooron ki bhalaai ke baare mein kam kyun batate hain?
answer_english: Average wages hide variations between trades and fluctuations from year to year. Real wages could fall even when money wages rose; for example, during the Napoleonic War, prices rose sharply so the same wages bought fewer things. Workers' income also depended on the number of days of work, and seasonal or slump-related unemployment meant long periods without earnings.
answer_hinglish: Average mazdoori alag-alag kaamon ke fark aur saal-dar-saal utaar-chadhaav ko chhupa deti hai. Paise ki mazdoori badhne pe bhi asli mazdoori gir sakti thi; jaise Napoleonic War mein daam tezi se badhe, toh utni hi mazdoori mein kam saamaan aata tha. Aamdani kaam ke dinon pe bhi nirbhar thi, aur mausami ya mandi ki berozgaari ka matlab tha lambe samay bina kamaai.
ncert_context: Wages increased somewhat in the early nineteenth century. But they tell us little about the welfare of workers. The average figures hide the variations between trades and the fluctuations from year to year. When prices rose sharply during the prolonged Napoleonic War, the real value of what workers earned fell significantly, since the same wages could buy fewer things. Moreover, income depended not on the wage rate alone; the number of days of work determined the average daily income of workers.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did women workers in Britain attack the Spinning Jenny?
question_hinglish: Britain mein mahila mazdooron ne Spinning Jenny pe hamla kyun kiya?
answer_english: The Spinning Jenny, devised by James Hargreaves in 1764, let one worker turn a single wheel to work several spindles and spin many threads at once, speeding up spinning and reducing the need for labour. Women who survived by hand spinning in the woollen industry feared unemployment and lost work to these machines, so they attacked them, and the conflict over the jenny continued for a long time.
answer_hinglish: 1764 mein James Hargreaves ki banayi Spinning Jenny se ek mazdoor ek pahiya ghuma kar kai takliyan chala ke ek saath kai dhaage kaat sakta tha, jisse kataai tez hui aur mazdooron ki zaroorat ghati. Oon udyog mein haath se kaat kar guzaara karne wali mahilayein berozgaari se dari aur in machines ki wajah se unka kaam chhina, isliye unhone in pe hamla kiya, aur yeh sangharsh lambe samay tak chala.
ncert_context: The fear of unemployment made workers hostile to the introduction of new technology. When the Spinning Jenny was introduced in the woollen industry, women who survived on hand spinning began attacking the new machines. This conflict continued for a long time. Spinning Jenny: devised by James Hargreaves in 1764, this machine speeded up the spinning process and reduced labour demand. subject: Social Science
question_english: How was the pre-colonial export trade in Indian textiles organised?
question_hinglish: Pre-colonial daur mein Indian kapdon ka export vyapaar kaise sangathit tha?
answer_english: Before machine industries, Indian silk and cotton dominated the international textile market. Armenian and Persian merchants carried goods from Punjab to Afghanistan, Persia and Central Asia by camel. Sea trade operated through Surat (linked to Gulf and Red Sea ports), Masulipatam and Hoogly (linked to Southeast Asia). Supply merchants gave advances to weavers and carried cloth to ports, where export merchants' brokers negotiated prices. Indian merchants and bankers financed production and supplied exporters.

Supply merchants bunkaron ko advance dekar kapda bandargaah tak laate, jahan export vyapaariyon ke dalaal daam tay karte. Indian vyapaari aur bankers utpaadan ko paisa dete aur exporters ko maal dete the.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did the port of Surat decline by the end of the eighteenth century?
question_hinglish: Eighteenth century ke ant tak Surat bandargaah ka patan kyun hua?
answer_english: By the 1750s, the network controlled by Indian merchants was breaking down as European companies gained power, first securing concessions from local courts and then monopoly trading rights. Old ports like Surat and Hoogly, through which local merchants operated, declined: exports fell, credit dried up and local bankers went bankrupt. Trade through Surat fell from Rs 16 million in the late seventeenth century to Rs 3 million by the 1740s, while Bombay and Calcutta grew under European control.
answer_hinglish: 1750s tak Indian vyapaariyon ka network toot raha tha kyunki European companies taakatwar ho rahi thi, pehle local darbaaron se riyaayatein lekar aur phir vyapaar ka monopoly paakar. Local vyapaariyon wale purane bandargaah Surat aur Hoogly ghate: export gire, udhaar sookh gaya aur local bankers diwaaliya hue. Surat se vyapaar seventeenth century ke ant ke Rs 16 million se 1740s tak Rs 3 million reh gaya, jabki European control mein Bombay aur Calcutta badhe.
ncert_context: By the 1750s the network controlled by Indian merchants was breaking down. subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the East India Company procure regular supplies of cotton and silk textiles from Indian weavers?
question_hinglish: East India Company ne Indian bunkaron se cotton aur resham ke kapdon ki niyamit supply kaise haasil ki?
answer_english: After gaining political power in Bengal and Carnatic in the 1760s and 1770s, the Company asserted a monopoly to eliminate competition, control costs and ensure regular supply. First, it removed existing traders and brokers and appointed paid servants called gomasthas to supervise weavers, collect supplies and check quality. Second, it stopped Company weavers from dealing with other buyers through advances: weavers who took loans for raw material had to hand their cloth only to the gomastha.
answer_hinglish: 1760s aur 1770s mein Bengal aur Carnatic mein political taakat paane ke baad Company ne mukabla khatam karne, laagat control karne aur niyamit supply ke liye monopoly jamayi. Pehle, usne purane vyapaariyon aur dalaalon ko hataya aur bunkaron ki nigraani, maal ikattha karne aur quality jaanchne ke liye vetanbhogi gomasthas rakhe. Doosre, advance system se Company ke bunkaron ko doosre khareedaaron se lena-dena karne se roka: kachche maal ke liye karz lene wale bunkar sirf gomastha ko hi kapda de sakte the.
ncert_context: Before establishing political power in Bengal and Carnatic in the 1760s and 1770s, the Company found it hard to ensure regular supplies; French, Dutch, Portuguese and local traders competed for cloth. Once it established political power, it asserted a monopoly right to trade and developed a system to eliminate competition, control costs and ensure regular supplies. First, it tried to eliminate existing traders and brokers and establish direct control over the weaver, appointing a paid servant called the gomastha to supervise weavers, collect supplies and examine quality. Second, it prevented Company weavers from dealing with other buyers through the system of advances: weavers given loans to purchase raw material had to hand over their cloth to the gomastha.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did clashes break out between weavers and gomasthas?
question_hinglish: Bunkaron aur gomasthas ke beech takraav kyun hue?
answer_english: Earlier supply merchants often lived in the weaving villages and had close relations with weavers, helping them in crises. The new gomasthas were outsiders with no long-term link to the village; they acted arrogantly, marched in with sepoys and peons, and punished, beat and flogged weavers for delays. Weavers lost the space to bargain or sell to other buyers, received miserably low prices, and were tied to the Company by loans.
answer_hinglish: Pehle ke supply merchants aksar bunkar gaon mein hi rehte the aur bunkaron se kareebi rishta rakhte, mushkil mein madad karte the. Naye gomasthas bahari log the jinka gaon se koi lamba rishta nahi tha; woh ghamand se pesh aate, sepoys aur peons ke saath gaon mein ghuste, aur deri pe bunkaron ko maarte-peet-te aur kode lagaate. Bunkaron se mol-bhaav aur doosre khareedaaron ko bechne ki azaadi chhin gayi, unhe bahut kam daam milta, aur karz ne unhe Company se baandh diya.

question_english: Why did Indian textile exports decline in the nineteenth century?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century mein Indian kapde ka export kyun ghata?
answer_english: In 1772 Company official Henry Patullo claimed demand for Indian textiles could never fall, but as English cotton industries grew, industrialists pressured the government to impose import duties on cotton textiles so Manchester goods faced no competition in Britain. They also persuaded the Company to sell British manufactures in India. So piece-goods fell from 33 per cent of India's exports in 1811-12 to no more than 3 per cent by 1850-51.

question_english: What problems did Indian cotton weavers face in the nineteenth century?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century mein Indian cotton bunkaron ko kaun si mushkilein jhelni padi?
answer_english: Weavers faced two problems at once: their export market collapsed and their local market shrank, glutted with cheap machine-made Manchester imports, which rose from virtually nothing to over 31 per cent of import value by 1850 and over 50 per cent by the 1870s. In the 1860s, the American Civil War made Britain buy Indian raw cotton, so its price shot up and weavers were starved of supplies. By the late nineteenth century, Indian factories also flooded the market with machine goods.

Nineteenth century ke ant tak Indian factories ne bhi machine ka maal market mein bhar diya.
ncert_context: At the end of the eighteenth century there had been virtually no import of cotton piece-goods into India. By 1850 cotton piece-goods constituted over 31 per cent of the value of Indian imports; by the 1870s over 50 per cent. Weavers faced two problems: their export market collapsed and the local market shrank, glutted with Manchester imports produced cheaply by machines. By the 1860s, when the American Civil War cut off US cotton supplies, Britain turned to India. As raw cotton exports increased, the price of raw cotton shot up and weavers were starved of supplies and forced to buy at exorbitant prices. By the end of the nineteenth century, factories in India began flooding the market with machine-goods.

question_english: What do the reports on Jahanabad, Behar and the Koshtis show about Indian weaving in the nineteenth century?
question_hinglish: Jahanabad, Behar aur Koshtis ki reports nineteenth century ki Indian bunaai ke baare mein kya batati hain?
answer_english: The Commissioner of Patna reported that brisk cloth manufacture at Jahanabad had entirely ceased and was very limited at Behar because local products could not compete with cheap, durable Manchester goods. The 1872 Census of the Central Provinces said the Koshtis, weavers of fine cloth, could not compete with showy Manchester goods and had emigrated in large numbers, chiefly to Berar, to work as day labourers. Both show decline and desolation in weaving regions.

Central Provinces ke 1872 Census ne kaha ki mahin kapda bunne wale Koshtis chamakdaar Manchester maal se mukabla na kar paane se badi sankhya mein, khaas kar Berar, dihaadi mazdoor bankar chale gaye. question_english: How did colonial control limit Indian businessmen, and what role did European Managing Agencies play?
question_hinglish: Colonial control ne Indian businessmen ko kaise seemit kiya, aur European Managing Agencies ki kya bhoomika thi?
answer_english: As colonial control tightened, Indian merchants were barred from trading with Europe in manufactured goods, had to export mostly raw materials like raw cotton, opium, wheat and indigo, and were edged out of shipping. Indians were not allowed into European chambers of commerce.

question_english: Where did workers for Indian factories come from?
question_hinglish: Indian factories ke mazdoor kahan se aate the?
answer_english: Factory workers rose from 584,000 in 1901 to over 2,436,000 by 1946. In most industrial regions, workers came from surrounding districts: peasants and artisans who found no work in villages. Over 50 per cent of Bombay's cotton mill workers in 1911 came from neighbouring Ratnagiri, and Kanpur's mills drew workers from villages in Kanpur district. Workers moved between village and city, returning for harvests and festivals, and over time travelled great distances, such as from the United Provinces to Bombay's textile mills and Calcutta's jute mills.

Mazdoor gaon aur shehar ke beech aate-jaate, fasal aur tyohaar pe ghar laut-te, aur samay ke saath door tak jaane lage, jaise United Provinces se Bombay ki textile mills aur Calcutta ki jute mills.

question_english: Why did early Indian cotton mills produce yarn rather than cloth?
question_hinglish: Shuruaati Indian cotton mills kapde ki jagah dhaaga kyun banati thi?
answer_english: European Managing Agencies invested mainly in export products like tea and coffee plantations, mining, indigo and jute. When Indian businessmen set up industries in the late nineteenth century, they avoided competing with Manchester goods in India. Since yarn was not an important British import (only superior yarn was imported), early Indian mills produced coarse cotton yarn, which was used by Indian handloom weavers or exported to China.

Kyunki dhaaga British import ka bada hissa nahi tha (sirf badhiya dhaaga aata tha), shuruaati Indian mills ne mota cotton dhaaga banaya, jo Indian handloom bunkar use karte the ya China export hota tha.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What changes in the early twentieth century made Indian industrialists shift from yarn to cloth production?
question_hinglish: Twentieth century ki shuruaat mein kin badlavon ne Indian industrialists ko dhaage se kapde ki taraf mode?
answer_english: As the swadeshi movement grew, nationalists mobilised people to boycott foreign cloth, and industrial groups pressured the government for tariff protection and concessions. From 1906, Indian yarn exports to China declined as Chinese and Japanese mills flooded the Chinese market. So Indian industrialists shifted from yarn to cloth, and cotton piece-goods production doubled between 1900 and 1912.
answer_hinglish: Swadeshi andolan badhne pe nationalists ne logon ko videshi kapde ke boycott ke liye ekjut kiya, aur industrial groups ne sarkar pe tariff suraksha aur riyaayaton ke liye dabaav daala. 1906 se China ko Indian dhaage ka export ghata kyunki Chinese aur Japanese mills ka maal Chinese market mein bhar gaya. Isliye Indian industrialists dhaage se kapde ki taraf mude, aur 1900 se 1912 ke beech cotton piece-goods ka utpaadan dugna hua.
ncert_context: By the first decade of the twentieth century a series of changes affected industrialisation. As the swadeshi movement gathered momentum, nationalists mobilised people to boycott foreign cloth. Industrial groups organised to protect their interests, pressuring the government to increase tariff protection and grant concessions. From 1906, the export of Indian yarn to China declined since produce from Chinese and Japanese mills flooded the Chinese market. So industrialists in India began shifting from yarn to cloth production. Cotton piece-goods production in India doubled between 1900 and 1912.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did industrial production in India increase during the First World War?
question_hinglish: First World War ke dauraan India mein industrial utpaadan kyun badha?
answer_english: With British mills busy with war production for the army, Manchester imports into India declined, giving Indian mills a vast home market. As the war continued, Indian factories were called on to supply war needs: jute bags, cloth for uniforms, tents, leather boots, horse and mule saddles and more. New factories were set up, old ones ran multiple shifts, and workers worked longer hours, so production boomed. After the war, Manchester never regained its position in India.
answer_hinglish: British mills sena ke liye yuddh ka maal banane mein lagi thi, isliye India mein Manchester ka import ghata aur Indian mills ko bada gharelu market mila. Yuddh lamba khinchne pe Indian factories se jute ke bore, vardi ka kapda, tambu, chamde ke joote, ghode aur khacchar ki kaathiyan jaisi cheezein maangi gayi. Nayi factories bani, purani kai shifts mein chali aur mazdooron ne zyada ghante kaam kiya, isliye utpaadan bahut badha. Yuddh ke baad Manchester India mein apni jagah kabhi waapas nahi le paaya.
ncert_context: Till the First World War, industrial growth was slow. The war created a dramatically new situation. With British mills busy with war production to meet the needs of the army, Manchester imports into India declined. Indian mills had a vast home market to supply. As the war prolonged, Indian factories were called upon to supply war needs: jute bags, cloth for army uniforms, tents and leather boots, horse and mule saddles and many other items. New factories were set up and old ones ran multiple shifts. Many new workers were employed and everyone worked longer hours. Industrial production boomed. After the war, Manchester could never recapture its old position in the Indian market, and local industrialists captured the home market.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did handloom production expand in the twentieth century despite competition from mills?
question_hinglish: Mills ke mukable ke bawajood twentieth century mein handloom utpaadan kaise badha?
answer_english: Cheap machine thread wiped out hand spinning, but weavers survived, and handloom cloth production almost trebled between 1900 and 1940. This was partly due to technology: weavers adopted looms with a fly shuttle, which raised productivity, sped up production and reduced labour demand. By 1941 over 35 per cent of handlooms had fly shuttles, rising to 70 to 80 per cent in Travancore, Madras, Mysore, Cochin and Bengal, along with other small innovations.

Iski ek wajah technology thi: bunkaron ne fly shuttle wale karghe apnaye, jisse utpaadakta badhi, kaam tez hua aur mazdooron ki zaroorat ghati. 1941 tak 35 percent se zyada handlooms mein fly shuttle tha, aur Travancore, Madras, Mysore, Cochin aur Bengal mein yeh 70 se 80 percent tha, saath mein aur chhote innovations bhi the.
ncert_context: In some instances, handicrafts production actually expanded in the twentieth century. While cheap machine-made thread wiped out spinning in the nineteenth century, weavers survived. In the twentieth century, handloom cloth production expanded steadily, almost trebling between 1900 and 1940. This was partly because of technological changes. Craftspeople adopt new technology if it improves production without pushing up costs. subject: Social Science
question_english: Why were some weavers better able than others to survive competition from mills?
question_hinglish: Kuch bunkar mills ke mukable mein doosron se behtar kyun tike rahe?
answer_english: Weavers of coarse cloth sold to the poor, whose demand fluctuated violently; in bad harvests and famines the rural poor could not buy cloth. Demand for finer varieties bought by the well-to-do was more stable, so famines did not affect sales of Banarasi or Baluchari saris. Mills also could not imitate specialised weaves like saris with woven borders or the famous lungis and handkerchiefs of Madras.
answer_hinglish: Mota kapda bunne wale gareebon ko bechte the, jinki demand bahut badalti thi; kharab fasal aur akaal mein gaon ke gareeb kapda nahi khareed paate the. Ameeron ke khareede mahin kapdon ki demand zyada sthir thi, isliye akaal ka Banarasi ya Baluchari saris ki bikri pe asar nahi pada. Mills khaas bunaai bhi nakal nahi kar sakti thi, jaise buni hui border wali saris ya Madras ki mashhoor lungis aur rumaal.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did Manchester industrialists use labels to sell cloth in India?
question_hinglish: Manchester ke industrialists ne India mein kapda bechne ke liye labels ka kaise use kiya?
answer_english: Manchester industrialists put labels on cloth bundles to make the place of manufacture and company name familiar to buyers and to mark quality; seeing 'MADE IN MANCHESTER' in bold was meant to give buyers confidence. Labels were also illustrated, often with Indian gods and goddesses like Krishna or Saraswati, as if divine approval backed the goods, and to make foreign products seem familiar to Indians.
answer_hinglish: Manchester ke industrialists kapde ke bandalon pe labels lagaate taaki banne ki jagah aur company ka naam khareedaaron ko yaad rahe aur quality ka nishaan bane; bade aksharon mein 'MADE IN MANCHESTER' dekh kar khareedaar ko bharosa ho. Labels pe aksar Krishna ya Saraswati jaise Indian devi-devtaon ki tasveerein hoti, mano maal ko divya manzoori mili ho, aur videshi maal Indians ko apna sa lage.
ncert_context: When Manchester industrialists began selling cloth in India, they put labels on the cloth bundles. The label made the place of manufacture and the company's name familiar to the buyer, and was a mark of quality. When buyers saw 'MADE IN MANCHESTER' in bold on the label, they were expected to feel confident about buying the cloth. Labels also carried images and were often beautifully illustrated. Images of Indian gods and goddesses regularly appeared, as if the association with gods gave divine approval to the goods. The image of Krishna or Saraswati was also intended to make the manufacture from a foreign land appear familiar to Indian people.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why were calendars an effective way to advertise products in late nineteenth-century India?
question_hinglish: Late nineteenth century India mein calendars products ke prachaar ka asardaar tareeka kyun the?
answer_english: Unlike newspapers and magazines, calendars were used even by people who could not read. They hung in tea shops and poor people's homes as well as offices and middle-class apartments, so people saw the advertisements day after day all year. They used images of gods, and figures of emperors and nawabs, suggesting that if you respected royalty you should respect the product.
answer_hinglish: Newspapers aur magazines ke ulat, calendars anpadh log bhi use karte the. Yeh chaay ki dukaanon aur gareebon ke gharon se lekar offices aur middle-class gharon tak lagte the, isliye log saal bhar roz advertisement dekhte the. Inme devtaon ki tasveerein aur samraaton aur nawabon ki chhaviyan hoti, jo sandesh deti ki agar tum raajsi vyakti ka samman karte ho toh is product ka bhi karo.
ncert_context: By the late nineteenth century, manufacturers were printing calendars to popularise their products. Unlike newspapers and magazines, calendars were used even by people who could not read. They were hung in tea shops and poor people's homes as much as in offices and middle-class apartments, and those who hung calendars saw the advertisements day after day through the year. Figures of gods were used to sell products. Figures of important personages, emperors and nawabs, also adorned advertisements and calendars, the message being: if you respect the royal figure, then respect this product.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Having studied the history of industrialisation, how would you view the images 'Dawn of the Century' and 'Two Magicians'?
question_hinglish: Industrialisation ka itihaas padhne ke baad tum 'Dawn of the Century' aur 'Two Magicians' tasveeron ko kaise dekhoge?
answer_english: These images present industrialisation as a triumphant story of machines and progress, with the West as modern and the East as backward. But history shows technology spread slowly, hand labour and small workshops remained central in Britain, colonial rule shaped and limited Indian industry, and workers suffered unemployment and hardship. So the images give a one-sided, glorified picture that ignores hand technology and the human cost of industrialisation.
answer_hinglish: Yeh tasveerein industrialisation ko machines aur pragati ki jeet ki kahani ki tarah dikhati hain, jisme West modern aur East pichhda hai. Par itihaas batata hai ki technology dheere faili, Britain mein haath ki mehnat aur chhote workshops kendra mein rahe, colonial raaj ne Indian udyog ko aakar diya aur roka, aur mazdooron ne berozgaari aur takleef jheli. Isliye yeh tasveerein ek-tarfa, badha-chadha kar pesh ki gayi chhavi hain jo haath ki technology aur insaani keemat ko nazarandaaz karti hain.
ncert_context: These images offer a triumphant account of the modern world associated with rapid technological change, machines, factories, railways and steamships; Aladdin represents the East and the past, the mechanic the West and modernity. Yet technological changes occurred slowly; the typical mid-nineteenth-century worker was a traditional craftsperson; colonial rule conditioned Indian industrialisation; workers faced unemployment and poverty. The age of industries meant major technological changes and a new labour force, but hand technology and small-scale production remained an important part of the industrial landscape.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did print technology develop in China?
question_hinglish: China mein print technology kaise viksit hui?
answer_english: The earliest print technology was a system of hand printing developed in China, Japan and Korea. From 594 CE, Chinese books were printed by rubbing paper, also invented there, against inked woodblocks; since both sides of the thin sheet could not be printed, the 'accordion book' was folded and stitched at the side. The imperial state was long the major producer, printing textbooks for civil service examinations. In the late nineteenth century, Western mechanical presses were imported and Shanghai became the hub of the new print culture.
answer_hinglish: Sabse pehli print technology China, Japan aur Korea mein haath se chhaapne ka system thi. 594 CE se China mein kitabein syaahi lage woodblocks pe kaagaz, jo wahin bana tha, ragad kar chhaapi jaati thi; patle kaagaz ke dono taraf chhapaai nahi ho sakti thi, isliye 'accordion book' ko mod kar side se silaa jaata tha. Lambe samay tak imperial state sabse bada chhaapne wala tha, jo civil service exams ki kitabein chhaapta tha. Late nineteenth century mein Western mechanical presses aaye aur Shanghai nayi print sanskriti ka kendra bana.
ncert_context: The earliest kind of print technology was developed in China, Japan and Korea, a system of hand printing. From 594 onwards, books in China were printed by rubbing paper, also invented there, against the inked surface of woodblocks. As both sides of the thin, porous sheet could not be printed, the traditional Chinese 'accordion book' was folded and stitched at the side. Skilled craftsmen could duplicate the beauty of calligraphy. The imperial state in China was for a long time the major producer of printed material, printing textbooks for civil service examinations in vast numbers. Western printing techniques and mechanical presses were imported in the late nineteenth century, and Shanghai became the hub of the new print culture.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the uses of print diversify in seventeenth-century China?
question_hinglish: Seventeenth century China mein print ke upyog kaise badhe?
answer_english: As urban culture bloomed, print was no longer used only by scholar-officials. Merchants used print in everyday life to collect trade information, and reading became a leisure activity. The new readers preferred fiction, poetry, autobiographies, literary anthologies and romantic plays. Rich women began reading, and many women published poetry and plays, including wives of scholar-officials, while courtesans wrote about their lives.
answer_hinglish: Shehri sanskriti ke failne se print sirf scholar-officials tak seemit nahi raha. Vyapaari vyapaar ki jaankari ke liye roz print use karne lage, aur padhna manoranjan ka zariya ban gaya. Naye paathak kahaniyan, kavita, aatmakathayein, sahitya sangrah aur romantic naatak pasand karte the. Ameer mahilayein padhne lagi, aur kai mahilaon ne kavita aur naatak chhape, jaise scholar-officials ki patniyan, aur courtesans ne apni zindagi ke baare mein likha.
ncert_context: From the sixteenth century, the number of examination candidates rose, increasing the volume of print. By the seventeenth century, as urban culture bloomed in China, the uses of print diversified. Print was no longer used just by scholar-officials. Merchants used print in their everyday life as they collected trade information. Reading increasingly became a leisure activity. The new readership preferred fictional narratives, poetry, autobiographies, anthologies of literary masterpieces and romantic plays. Rich women began to read, and many women began publishing their poetry and plays. Wives of scholar-officials published their works and courtesans wrote about their lives.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did print culture develop in Japan?
question_hinglish: Japan mein print sanskriti kaise viksit hui?
answer_english: Buddhist missionaries from China introduced hand printing into Japan around 768-770 CE. The oldest Japanese book, printed in 868 CE, is the Buddhist Diamond Sutra with six sheets of text and woodcut illustrations. Pictures were printed on textiles, playing cards and paper money, and in medieval Japan books were cheap and abundant. In late-eighteenth-century Edo (Tokyo), illustrated collections depicted elegant urban culture, and libraries and bookstores were full of hand-printed books on women, music, calculations, tea ceremony, flower arrangement, etiquette, cooking and famous places.

question_english: Who was Kitagawa Utamaro, and what was ukiyo art?
question_hinglish: Kitagawa Utamaro kaun the, aur ukiyo kala kya thi?
answer_english: Kitagawa Utamaro, born in Edo in 1753, was known for ukiyo, 'pictures of the floating world', which depicted ordinary, especially urban, human experiences. His prints travelled to the US and Europe and influenced artists like Manet, Monet and Van Gogh. Publishers commissioned artists' outlines, and woodblock carvers carved blocks from them, destroying the original drawing so that only prints survived.

Unke prints US aur Europe tak gaye aur Manet, Monet aur Van Gogh jaise kalakaaron ko prabhavit kiya. Publishers kalakaaron se rekhachitra banwate, aur woodblock kaarigar unse block taraashte, jisme asli chitra nasht ho jaata aur sirf prints bachte.

question_english: What are the Tripitaka Koreana and the Jikji?
question_hinglish: Tripitaka Koreana aur Jikji kya hain?
answer_english: The Tripitaka Koreana is a mid-thirteenth-century Korean collection of Buddhist scriptures engraved on about 80,000 woodblocks, inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register in 2007. The Jikji, printed in the late fourteenth century, is among the world's oldest books printed with movable metal type; it contains the essentials of Zen Buddhism and mentions about 150 monks of India, China and Korea, and was inscribed on the register in 2001.
answer_hinglish: Tripitaka Koreana mid-thirteenth century ka Korean Buddhist granthon ka sangrah hai jo lagbhag 80,000 woodblocks pe khuda hai, aur 2007 mein UNESCO Memory of the World Register mein shaamil hua. Late fourteenth century mein chhapi Jikji duniya ki sabse purani movable metal type se chhapi kitabon mein se hai; isme Zen Buddhism ki mool baatein aur India, China aur Korea ke lagbhag 150 bhikshuon ka zikr hai, aur yeh 2001 mein register mein shaamil hui.

It contains the essential features of Zen Buddhism and mentions about 150 monks of India, China and Korea. It was printed in the late 14th century. Its second volume is in the National Library of France. It was inscribed on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register in 2001.

question_english: Why did woodblock printing come to Europe only after 1295?
question_hinglish: Woodblock printing Europe mein 1295 ke baad hi kyun aayi?
answer_english: Chinese paper had reached Europe via the silk route in the eleventh century, making manuscripts possible, but woodblock printing technology was known only in China. In 1295, Marco Polo returned to Italy after many years exploring China and brought back knowledge of woodblock printing. Italians then began producing books with woodblocks, and the technology spread across Europe.

Phir Italians woodblocks se kitabein banane lage aur technology poore Europe mein faili.

China already had the technology of woodblock printing, and Marco Polo brought this knowledge back with him. question_english: Why could handwritten manuscripts not meet the growing demand for books in Europe?
question_hinglish: Europe mein haath ki likhi pothiyan kitabon ki badhti demand kyun poori nahi kar paayi?
answer_english: As demand for books grew, booksellers exported books and held book fairs, and scribes were increasingly employed by booksellers, sometimes over 50 for one bookseller. But copying was expensive, laborious and time-consuming, and manuscripts were fragile, awkward to handle and hard to carry or read, so their circulation stayed limited. This created the need for quicker, cheaper reproduction through a new print technology.
answer_hinglish: Kitabon ki demand badhne pe booksellers ne export kiya aur book fairs lage, aur scribes booksellers ke liye kaam karne lage, kabhi ek bookseller ke liye 50 se zyada. Par nakal karna mehnga, mehnati aur samay lene wala tha, aur pothiyan naazuk, sambhalne mein mushkil aur le jaane ya padhne mein kathin thi, isliye unka prasaar seemit raha. Isse nayi print technology se tez aur sasti chhapaai ki zaroorat bani.
ncert_context: As demand for books increased, booksellers began exporting books and book fairs were held. Scribes were no longer solely employed by wealthy patrons but increasingly by booksellers; more than 50 scribes often worked for one bookseller. But the production of handwritten manuscripts could not satisfy the ever-increasing demand. Copying was an expensive, laborious and time-consuming business. Manuscripts were fragile, awkward to handle, and could not be carried around or read easily. Their circulation remained limited. There was a great need for even quicker and cheaper reproduction of texts, possible only with a new print technology.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did Gutenberg develop the printing press?
question_hinglish: Gutenberg ne printing press kaise banaya?
answer_english: Johann Gutenberg, son of a merchant who grew up on an agricultural estate, had seen wine and olive presses as a child, became a master goldsmith, and learnt to make lead moulds for trinkets. Drawing on this, he adapted existing technology: the olive press became the model for the printing press, and moulds were used to cast metal types for letters. He developed the first-known press at Strasbourg in the 1430s and perfected the system by 1448; his first printed book was the Bible, about 180 copies in three years.
answer_hinglish: Vyapaari ke bete Johann Gutenberg ne bachpan mein ek bade khet pe sharaab aur jaitoon ke press dekhe, phir sunaar bane aur gehnon ke liye seese ke saanche banana seekha. Isi gyaan se unhone maujood technology ko badla: jaitoon ka press printing press ka model bana, aur saanchon se aksharon ke metal type dhaale gaye. Unhone 1430s mein Strasbourg mein pehla jaana-maana press banaya aur 1448 tak system poora kiya; unki pehli chhapi kitaab Bible thi, teen saal mein lagbhag 180 copies.
ncert_context: The breakthrough occurred at Strasbourg, Germany, where Johann Gutenberg developed the first-known printing press in the 1430s. Gutenberg was the son of a merchant and grew up on a large agricultural estate, where he saw wine and olive presses. He learnt to polish stones, became a master goldsmith, and acquired the expertise to create lead moulds for making trinkets. Drawing on this knowledge, he adapted existing technology. The olive press provided the model for the printing press, and moulds were used for casting metal types for the letters of the alphabet. By 1448, Gutenberg perfected the system. The first book he printed was the Bible. About 180 copies were printed and it took three years.

The olive press provided the model for the printing press, and moulds were used for casting metal types for the letters of the alphabet. By 1448, Gutenberg perfected the system. The first book he printed was the Bible. About 180 copies were printed and it took three years.

question_english: What are a platen, a compositor, a galley and vellum?
question_hinglish: Platen, compositor, galley aur vellum kya hain?
answer_english: A platen is a board pressed onto the back of the paper in letterpress printing to get the impression from the type, once wooden and later steel. Vellum jaanwar ki khaal se bana charmapatra hai, jis pe mehngi haath ki likhi luxury kitabein banti thi.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the print revolution create a new reading public?
question_hinglish: Print revolution ne naya reading public kaise banaya?
answer_english: Printing reduced the cost, time and labour of producing books and allowed multiple copies, so books reached an ever-growing readership. Earlier, reading was restricted to elites, and common people lived in an oral culture, hearing sacred texts, ballads and folk tales. Now a reading public emerged alongside the hearing public. Since literacy was low, printers published illustrated ballads and folk tales that were sung and recited in villages and taverns, so oral and reading cultures intermingled.
answer_hinglish: Printing ne kitabein banane ki laagat, samay aur mehnat ghatayi aur kai copies sambhav ki, isliye kitabein badhte paathakon tak pahunchi. Pehle padhna elites tak seemit tha, aur aam log maukhik sanskriti mein rehte the, pavitra granth, gaathayein aur lok kathayein sunte the. Ab sunne wale public ke saath padhne wala public bana. Kyunki saakshrata kam thi, printers ne chitron wali gaathayein aur lok kathayein chhapi jo gaon aur sharaab-khaanon mein gaayi aur sunaayi jaati thi, isliye maukhik aur padhne ki sanskriti ghul-mil gayi.
ncert_context: With the printing press, a new reading public emerged. Printing reduced the cost of books; time and labour came down, and multiple copies were produced easily. Earlier, reading was restricted to elites. Common people lived in an oral culture, hearing sacred texts, ballads and folk tales. If earlier there was a hearing public, now a reading public came into being. But literacy rates in most European countries were very low till the twentieth century. So printers published popular ballads and folk tales, profusely illustrated, which were sung and recited at gatherings in villages and taverns. Oral culture entered print and printed material was orally transmitted. The hearing public and reading public intermingled.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did some people fear that print could lead to the growth of dissenting ideas?
question_hinglish: Kuch log kyun dar-te the ki print se asahmati wale vichaar badhenge?
answer_english: Print allowed wide circulation of ideas, so even those who disagreed with established authorities could print and spread their views and move people to action. Religious authorities, monarchs, writers and artists feared that without control over what was printed and read, rebellious and irreligious thoughts would spread and the authority of 'valuable' literature would be destroyed. Erasmus complained that printers filled the world with stupid, slanderous, irreligious and seditious books.
answer_hinglish: Print se vichaar door tak fail sakte the, isliye sthapit adhikaariyon se asahmat log bhi apne vichaar chhaap kar faila sakte the aur logon ko kaam ke liye prerit kar sakte the. Dharmik adhikaari, raaja, lekhak aur kalakaar dar-te the ki agar chhapne aur padhne pe control na ho toh vidrohi aur adharmik vichaar failenge aur 'keemti' sahitya ka adhikaar khatam hoga. Erasmus ne shikaayat ki ki printers duniya ko bewakoof, nindak, adharmik aur rajdroh wali kitabon se bhar rahe hain.

question_english: Why did the Roman Catholic Church begin keeping an Index of Prohibited Books from the mid-sixteenth century?
question_hinglish: Roman Catholic Church ne mid-sixteenth century se Index of Prohibited Books kyun rakhna shuru kiya?
answer_english: Print and popular religious literature encouraged individual interpretations of faith, even among little-educated working people. For example, Menocchio, a sixteenth-century Italian miller, read locally available books, reinterpreted the Bible and formed views of God and Creation that enraged the Church; during the inquisition against heretical ideas he was hauled up twice and executed. Troubled by such questioning of faith, the Church imposed severe controls on publishers and booksellers and kept an Index of Prohibited Books from 1558.
answer_hinglish: Print aur lokpriya dharmik sahitya ne kam padhe-likhe mazdooron mein bhi aastha ki apni vyakhya ko badhava diya. Jaise sixteenth century ke Italian chakki-waale Menocchio ne local kitabein padh kar Bible ki nayi vyakhya ki aur Bhagwan aur srishti pe aise vichaar banaye jinse Church naraz hua; heretical vichaaron ke khilaaf inquisition mein unhe do baar pakda gaya aur maut di gayi. Aise sawaalon se pareshaan Church ne publishers aur booksellers pe kade niyantran lagaye aur 1558 se Index of Prohibited Books rakhna shuru kiya.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the 'reading mania' in seventeenth and eighteenth-century Europe?
question_hinglish: Seventeenth aur eighteenth century Europe ka 'reading mania' kya tha?
answer_english: Literacy rose as churches set up village schools for peasants and artisans; by the late eighteenth century some parts of Europe had 60 to 80 per cent literacy, creating a reading mania. Pedlars carried little books to villages: almanacs, ballads, folk tales and entertainment reading. England had penny chapbooks sold by chapmen, and France had the cheap 'Bibliotheque Bleue' in blue covers, plus romances and histories. From the early eighteenth century, periodicals combined current affairs and entertainment, and works of Newton, Paine, Voltaire and Rousseau reached wider readers.
answer_hinglish: Churches ke gaon mein kisaanon aur kaarigaron ke liye schools kholne se saakshrata badhi; eighteenth century ke ant tak Europe ke kuch hisson mein 60 se 80 percent saakshrata thi, jisse padhne ka junoon paida hua. Pheriwale gaon mein chhoti kitabein le jaate: almanac, gaathayein, lok kathayein aur manoranjan ki cheezein. England mein chapmen penny chapbooks bechte, aur France mein neele cover wali sasti 'Bibliotheque Bleue', romances aur histories thi. Early eighteenth century se patrikaon ne khabar aur manoranjan joda, aur Newton, Paine, Voltaire aur Rousseau ke lekh zyada paathakon tak pahunche.
ncert_context: Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries literacy rates went up. Churches set up schools in villages for peasants and artisans. By the end of the eighteenth century, in some parts of Europe literacy rates were 60 to 80 per cent. There was a virtual reading mania. Booksellers employed pedlars who roamed villages carrying little books: almanacs, ballads, folktales and entertainment. In England, penny chapbooks were carried by pedlars called chapmen and sold for a penny. In France were the 'Bibliotheque Bleue', low-priced books on poor paper bound in cheap blue covers, and romances and 'histories'. The periodical press developed from the early eighteenth century, combining current affairs with entertainment. Writings of Isaac Newton, Thomas Paine, Voltaire and Rousseau were widely printed and read.

question_english: Why did some people in eighteenth-century Europe think print culture would bring enlightenment and end despotism?
question_hinglish: Eighteenth century Europe mein kuch log kyun maante the ki print culture gyaan laayegi aur tanashahi khatam karegi?

question_english: What does publisher James Lackington's 1791 diary entry show about reading among the poor?
question_hinglish: Publisher James Lackington ki 1791 ki diary gareebon mein padhne ke baare mein kya dikhati hai?
answer_english: Lackington noted that book sales had increased prodigiously in twenty years. Poor farmers and country people who earlier spent winter evenings telling stories of witches and ghosts now listened to their children read tales and romances, and people going to town were asked to bring back books like Peregrine Pickle's Adventure and The History of Joseph Andrews. It shows reading spreading even among poor rural people.
answer_hinglish: Lackington ne likha ki bees saal mein kitabon ki bikri bahut badhi. Gareeb kisaan aur gaon ke log, jo pehle sardiyon ki shaam chudailon aur bhooton ki kahaniyan sunaate the, ab apne bachchon se kahaniyan aur romances sunte, aur shehar jaane walon ko Peregrine Pickle's Adventure aur The History of Joseph Andrews jaisi kitabein laane ko kaha jaata. Isse pata chalta hai ki padhna gareeb gaon waalon tak bhi fail raha tha.

question_english: Why do some historians think print culture created the basis for the French Revolution?
question_hinglish: Kuch historians kyun maante hain ki print culture ne French Revolution ki neev rakhi?
answer_english: Three arguments are usually given. First, print popularised Enlightenment thinkers like Voltaire and Rousseau, who criticised tradition, superstition and despotism, demanded rule of reason, and attacked the Church's sacred authority and the state's despotic power. Second, print created a culture of dialogue and debate in which values and institutions were re-evaluated, giving rise to ideas of social revolution. Third, by the 1780s, literature and cartoons mocking royalty circulated underground, building hostility to the monarchy.
answer_hinglish: Aksar teen tark diye jaate hain. Pehla, print ne Voltaire aur Rousseau jaise Enlightenment vichaarakon ko popular banaya, jinhone parampara, andhvishwaas aur tanashahi ki aalochana ki, tark ke raaj ki maang ki, aur Church ke pavitra adhikaar aur state ki tanashahi pe hamla kiya. Doosra, print ne bahas aur samvaad ki sanskriti banayi jisme mulya aur sansthayein dobara parkhi gayi aur samajik kranti ke vichaar bane. Teesra, 1780s tak raajgharaane ka mazaak udaane wala sahitya aur cartoons chupke se faile, jisse monarchy ke khilaaf nafrat bani.
ncert_context: Many historians argue that print culture created conditions for the French Revolution. Three arguments are put forward. First: print popularised the ideas of Enlightenment thinkers, whose writings criticised tradition, superstition and despotism, argued for the rule of reason, and attacked the sacred authority of the Church and the despotic power of the state. The writings of Voltaire and Rousseau were read widely. Second: print created a new culture of dialogue and debate; all values, norms and institutions were re-evaluated, and new ideas of social revolution came into being. Third: by the 1780s there was an outpouring of literature that mocked the royalty and criticised their morality. Cartoons suggested the monarchy was absorbed in pleasures while common people suffered. This literature circulated underground and led to hostile sentiments against the monarchy.

question_english: Did print directly shape people's minds before the French Revolution?
question_hinglish: Kya French Revolution se pehle print ne seedhe logon ke mann ko aakar diya?
answer_english: Not directly. Print certainly helped spread ideas, but people did not read just one kind of literature: alongside Voltaire and Rousseau, they were exposed to monarchical and Church propaganda. They accepted some ideas, rejected others and interpreted things their own way. So print did not directly shape their minds, but it opened up the possibility of thinking differently.
answer_hinglish: Seedhe nahi. Print ne vichaar failane mein madad zaroor ki, par log ek hi tarah ka sahitya nahi padhte the: Voltaire aur Rousseau ke saath unhe monarchy aur Church ka prachaar bhi milta tha. Woh kuch vichaar maante, kuch thukraate aur apne tareeke se samajhte the. Isliye print ne mann ko seedhe nahi badla, par alag tarah sochne ki sambhavna kholi.

question_english: How did children become an important category of readers in the nineteenth century?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century mein bachche paathakon ki important shreni kaise bane?
answer_english: As primary education became compulsory from the late nineteenth century, children became important readers and school textbook production became critical for publishers. A children's press was set up in France in 1857, publishing new works and old fairy and folk tales. The Grimm Brothers' 1812 collection of peasant folk tales was edited to remove anything unsuitable for children or vulgar to elites, so print recorded old tales but also changed them.

question_english: How did workers become readers and writers in nineteenth-century England?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century England mein mazdoor paathak aur lekhak kaise bane?

After the working day was gradually shortened from the mid-nineteenth century, workers had time for self-improvement and wrote political tracts and autobiographies in large numbers. Thomas Wood, a Yorkshire mechanic, rented old newspapers and read them by firelight because he could not afford candles.

question_english: What innovations in printing technology took place in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth aur early twentieth century mein printing technology mein kya innovations hue?
answer_english: By the late eighteenth century presses were made of metal. By the mid-nineteenth century, Richard M. Hoe of New York perfected the power-driven cylindrical press, printing 8,000 sheets per hour and useful for newspapers. In the late nineteenth century the offset press could print up to six colours at once. From the early twentieth century, electric presses sped up printing, along with better paper feeding, better plates, automatic paper reels and photoelectric colour register controls.

Late nineteenth century mein offset press aaya jo ek saath chhe rang chhaap sakta tha. Early twentieth century se bijli ke press ne chhapaai tez ki, saath mein kaagaz daalne ke behtar tareeke, behtar plates, automatic paper reels aur colour register ke photoelectric controls aaye.

question_english: How did printing begin in India?
question_hinglish: India mein printing kaise shuru hui?
answer_english: The printing press first came to Goa with Portuguese missionaries in the mid-sixteenth century; Jesuit priests learnt Konkani and printed tracts, and by 1674 about 50 books were printed in Konkani and Kanara. Catholic priests printed the first Tamil book in 1579 at Cochin and the first Malayalam book in 1713. By 1710 Dutch Protestant missionaries had printed 32 Tamil texts. The English press grew late, though the East India Company imported presses from the late seventeenth century.

Catholic paadriyon ne 1579 mein Cochin mein pehli Tamil kitaab aur 1713 mein pehli Malayalam kitaab chhapi. 1710 tak Dutch Protestant missionaries ne 32 Tamil texts chhape. English press der se badha, halaanki East India Company late seventeenth century se presses mangwaane lagi thi.

question_english: Who was James Augustus Hickey, and why did Warren Hastings persecute him?
question_hinglish: James Augustus Hickey kaun the, aur Warren Hastings ne unhe kyun sataaya?
answer_english: From 1780, James Augustus Hickey edited the Bengal Gazette, a weekly calling itself 'a commercial paper open to all, but influenced by none', so English printing in India began as private enterprise independent of colonial influence. Hickey published many advertisements, including on the import and sale of slaves, and gossip about the Company's senior officials. Enraged, Governor-General Warren Hastings persecuted him and encouraged officially sanctioned newspapers to counter information damaging the government's image.
answer_hinglish: 1780 se James Augustus Hickey ne Bengal Gazette edit kiya, ek saaptahik jo khud ko 'sabke liye khula, par kisi se prabhavit nahi' commercial paper kehta tha, isliye India mein English printing colonial prabhav se azaad private udyam ke roop mein shuru hui. Hickey ne bahut advertisements chhape, gulaamon ke import aur bikri wale bhi, aur Company ke bade adhikaariyon ke baare mein gossip. Naraz hokar Governor-General Warren Hastings ne unhe sataaya aur sarkar ki chhavi bigaadne wali jaankari ka jawab dene ke liye sarkari manzoori wale akhbaar badhaye.
ncert_context: From 1780, James Augustus Hickey began to edit the Bengal Gazette, a weekly magazine that described itself as 'a commercial paper open to all, but influenced by none'. So it was private English enterprise, proud of its independence from colonial influence, that began English printing in India. Hickey published a lot of advertisements, including those relating to the import and sale of slaves. But he also published a lot of gossip about the Company's senior officials in India. Enraged by this, Governor-General Warren Hastings persecuted Hickey, and encouraged the publication of officially sanctioned newspapers that could counter the flow of information damaging the image of the colonial government.

question_english: How did print shape religious reform debates in nineteenth-century India?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century India mein print ne dharmik sudhaar ki bahas ko kaise aakar diya?
answer_english: From the early nineteenth century, intense debates on religion were carried out in public and in print. Printed tracts and newspapers spread new ideas and shaped the debate, letting a wider public participate. Reformers and Hindu orthodoxy clashed over widow immolation, monotheism, Brahmanical priesthood and idolatry, printing ideas in everyday spoken language. Rammohun Roy published the Sambad Kaumudi from 1821, and the orthodoxy commissioned the Samachar Chandrika to oppose him.
answer_hinglish: Early nineteenth century se dharm pe tez bahas public aur print mein hui. Chhape tracts aur akhbaaron ne naye vichaar failaye aur bahas ko roop diya, jisse bada public hissa le saka. Sudhaarak aur Hindu kattarpanthi sati, ekeshvarvaad, Brahmin purohitvaad aur moorti pooja pe takraaye, aur vichaar aam boli mein chhape gaye. Rammohun Roy ne 1821 se Sambad Kaumudi nikaala, aur kattarpanthiyon ne unke virodh mein Samachar Chandrika nikalwaya.
ncert_context: From the early nineteenth century, there were intense debates around religious issues, carried out in public and in print. Printed tracts and newspapers not only spread new ideas but shaped the nature of the debate. A wider public could participate and express their views. There were intense controversies between social and religious reformers and the Hindu orthodoxy over widow immolation, monotheism, Brahmanical priesthood and idolatry. In Bengal, tracts and newspapers proliferated. To reach a wider audience, ideas were printed in the everyday, spoken language of ordinary people. Rammohun Roy published the Sambad Kaumudi from 1821 and the Hindu orthodoxy commissioned the Samachar Chandrika to oppose his opinions.

question_english: How did print encourage the reading of religious texts among Hindus and connect communities?
question_hinglish: Print ne Hinduon mein dharmik granth padhne ko kaise badhaya aur samudaayon ko kaise joda?
answer_english: Print encouraged reading Hindu religious texts, especially in vernaculars. The first printed edition of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas came out from Calcutta in 1810, cheap lithographic editions flooded north Indian markets by the mid-nineteenth century, and from the 1880s the Naval Kishore Press in Lucknow and Shri Venkateshwar Press in Bombay published many vernacular religious texts. Portable texts could be read anywhere or read aloud to illiterate groups. Newspapers also carried news across regions, creating pan-Indian identities.
answer_hinglish: Print ne Hindu dharmik granth, khaas kar local bhashaon mein, padhne ko badhava diya. Chhote granth kahin bhi padhe ya anpadh logon ko sunaaye ja sakte the. Akhbaaron ne bhi ilaakon ke beech khabrein pahunchaa kar pan-Indian pehchaan banayi.

question_english: What new forms of publication and visual culture emerged in India with print?
question_hinglish: Print ke saath India mein prakaashan aur drishya sanskriti ke kaun se naye roop aaye?
answer_english: As more people could read, they wanted their own lives and feelings reflected, so the novel, from Europe, acquired Indian forms, along with lyrics, short stories and essays on social and political matters. By the late nineteenth century a new visual culture emerged: painters like Raja Ravi Varma produced images for mass circulation, wood engravers worked for print shops, and cheap prints and calendars decorated even poor homes. From the 1870s, caricatures and cartoons in journals commented on social and political issues.
answer_hinglish: Zyada log padhne lage toh woh apni zindagi aur bhavnayein padhna chahte the, isliye Europe se aaye upanyaas ne Indian roop liya, saath mein geet, kahaniyan aur social-political nibandh aaye. Late nineteenth century tak nayi drishya sanskriti bani: Raja Ravi Varma jaise chitrakaaron ne bade paimaane pe chitra banaye, lakdi ke kaarigar print shops mein kaam karne lage, aur saste prints aur calendars gareebon ke ghar bhi sajaane lage. 1870s se patrikaon mein caricatures aur cartoons social aur political muddon pe tippani karne lage.
ncert_context: Printing created an appetite for new kinds of writing. As more people could read, they wanted their own lives, experiences and emotions reflected. The novel, developed in Europe, soon acquired distinctively Indian forms. Other new forms entered reading: lyrics, short stories, essays about social and political matters. By the end of the nineteenth century, a new visual culture took shape. Painters like Raja Ravi Varma produced images for mass circulation. Poor wood engravers set up shop near letterpresses. Cheap prints and calendars could be bought even by the poor. By the 1870s, caricatures and cartoons were published in journals, some ridiculing educated Indians' fascination with Western tastes, others expressing fear of social change; there were imperial caricatures lampooning nationalists and nationalist cartoons criticising imperial rule.

question_english: What did the spread of print culture in nineteenth-century India mean for women?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century India mein print sanskriti ke failne ka mahilaon ke liye kya matlab tha?
answer_english: Women's reading increased greatly in middle-class homes as liberal husbands and fathers educated them at home and later sent them to women's schools, and journals carried women's writings, arguments for their education and home-study syllabi. Conservative families resisted, but some women defied them: Rashsundari Debi learnt to read secretly in her kitchen and wrote Amar Jiban (1876), the first full-length Bengali autobiography. Kailashbashini Debi, Tarabai Shinde and Pandita Ramabai wrote about women's oppression and widows' miserable lives.
answer_hinglish: Middle-class gharon mein mahilaon ka padhna bahut badha, kyunki liberal pati aur pita unhe ghar pe padhate aur baad mein mahila schools bhejte, aur patrikayein mahilaon ke lekh, unki shiksha ke tark aur ghar pe padhai ka syllabus chhaapti. Kattar parivaaron ne virodh kiya, par kuch mahilaon ne bagaavat ki: Rashsundari Debi ne rasoi mein chupke se padhna seekha aur Amar Jiban (1876) likhi, jo Bengali ki pehli poori aatmakatha thi. Kailashbashini Debi, Tarabai Shinde aur Pandita Ramabai ne mahilaon ke shoshan aur vidhvaon ki dukhi zindagi pe likha.
ncert_context: Women's reading increased enormously in middle-class homes. Liberal husbands and fathers educated women at home and sent them to schools set up after the mid-nineteenth century. Journals carried writings by women, explained why women should be educated and provided syllabi for home-based schooling. Conservative Hindus believed a literate girl would be widowed and Muslims feared educated women would be corrupted by Urdu romances. In East Bengal, Rashsundari Debi, a young married girl in an orthodox household, learnt to read in the secrecy of her kitchen and wrote her autobiography Amar Jiban, published in 1876, the first full-length autobiography in Bengali. From the 1860s Kailashbashini Debi wrote about women imprisoned at home. In the 1880s in Maharashtra, Tarabai Shinde and Pandita Ramabai wrote with anger about upper-caste Hindu women, especially widows.

question_english: What were the effects of the spread of print culture for poor people in nineteenth-century India?
question_hinglish: Nineteenth century India mein print sanskriti ke failne ka gareebon pe kya asar hua?
answer_english: Very cheap small books were sold at crossroads in Madras towns so poor people going to markets could buy them, and public libraries set up from the early twentieth century expanded access, mostly in cities. Printed tracts addressed caste discrimination: Jyotiba Phule wrote Gulamgiri (1871), and Ambedkar and Periyar wrote powerfully on caste. Workers wrote too: Kanpur millworker Kashibaba published Chhote Aur Bade Ka Sawal (1938) on caste and class exploitation, and Bangalore and Bombay millworkers set up libraries.

Chhape tracts ne jaati bhed-bhaav uthaya: Jyotiba Phule ne Gulamgiri (1871) likhi, aur Ambedkar aur Periyar ne jaati pe zordaar likha. Mazdooron ne bhi likha: Kanpur ke mill mazdoor Kashibaba ne jaati aur varg shoshan pe Chhote Aur Bade Ka Sawal (1938) chhapi, aur Bangalore aur Bombay ke mill mazdooron ne libraries banayi.

question_english: What was Battala in Calcutta known for?
question_hinglish: Calcutta ka Battala kis liye jaana jaata tha?
answer_english: Battala was an area in central Calcutta devoted to printing popular books. It sold cheap editions of religious tracts and scriptures as well as literature considered obscene and scandalous, by the late nineteenth century profusely illustrated with woodcuts and coloured lithographs. Pedlars carried Battala publications to homes, letting women read them in their leisure time.

Yahan dharmik tracts aur granthon ke saste sanskaran aur ashleel aur sharmnaak maana jaane wala sahitya bhi milta tha, jo late nineteenth century tak woodcuts aur rangeen lithographs se bhara hota tha. Pheriwale Battala ki kitabein gharon tak le jaate, jisse mahilayein khaali samay mein padh sakti thi.

question_english: How did colonial press regulation change between 1798 and 1835?
question_hinglish: 1798 se 1835 ke beech colonial press niyantran kaise badla?
answer_english: Before 1798, the Company was not much concerned with censorship, and its early measures targeted Englishmen in India critical of Company misrule, fearing critics in England would attack its trade monopoly. By the 1820s, the Calcutta Supreme Court passed regulations to control press freedom and the Company encouraged newspapers celebrating British rule. In 1835, after petitions by editors, Governor-General Bentinck agreed to revise press laws, and Thomas Macaulay framed rules restoring earlier freedoms.
answer_hinglish: 1798 se pehle Company censorship ki zyada parwah nahi karti thi, aur uske shuruaati kadam Company ke kushaasan ki aalochana karne wale Englishmen ke khilaaf the, is dar se ki England mein aalochak uske vyapaar monopoly pe hamla karenge. 1820s tak Calcutta Supreme Court ne press ki azaadi pe rok ke niyam banaye aur Company ne British raaj ki tareef wale akhbaar badhaye. 1835 mein editors ki arziyon ke baad Governor-General Bentinck press laws badalne ko maane, aur Thomas Macaulay ne purani azaadi lautaane wale niyam banaye.
ncert_context: Before 1798, the colonial state under the East India Company was not too concerned with censorship. Its early measures to control printed matter were directed against Englishmen in India critical of Company misrule. The Company was worried that such criticisms might be used by its critics in England to attack its trade monopoly. By the 1820s, the Calcutta Supreme Court passed regulations to control press freedom and the Company encouraged newspapers celebrating British rule. In 1835, faced with urgent petitions by editors of English and vernacular newspapers, Governor-General Bentinck agreed to revise press laws. Thomas Macaulay, a liberal colonial official, formulated new rules that restored the earlier freedoms.

question_english: How did the colonial government control the press during the two World Wars?
question_hinglish: Dono World Wars ke dauraan colonial sarkar ne press ko kaise control kiya?
answer_english: During the First World War, under the Defence of India Rules, 22 newspapers had to furnish securities, and 18 shut down rather than comply. The Rowlatt Sedition Committee Report of 1919 strengthened controls and led to penalties on newspapers. At the start of the Second World War, the Defence of India Act allowed censoring of war-related reports, covering all reports on the Quit India movement, and in August 1942 about 90 newspapers were suppressed.

Second World War shuru hone pe Defence of India Act ne yuddh se judi reports ko censor karne diya, jisme Quit India movement ki saari reports aayi, aur August 1942 mein lagbhag 90 akhbaar dabaaye gaye.

question_english: True or False: The first printed book in Europe was produced before Marco Polo returned from China.

question_english: On what bases are resources classified?
question_hinglish: Resources ko kin aadhaaron pe baanta jaata hai?
answer_english: Resources are classified on the basis of origin (biotic and abiotic), exhaustibility (renewable and non-renewable), ownership (individual, community, national and international), and status of development (potential, developed stock and reserves).
answer_hinglish: Resources ko utpatti (biotic aur abiotic), khatam hone ki sambhavna (renewable aur non-renewable), maalikana (individual, community, national aur international), aur vikaas ki sthiti (potential, developed stock aur reserves) ke aadhaar pe baanta jaata hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What problems arose from the indiscriminate use of resources?
question_hinglish: Resources ke andhadhundh use se kaun si samasyayein paida hui?
answer_english: Believing resources were free gifts of nature, humans used them indiscriminately, leading to: depletion of resources to satisfy the greed of a few; accumulation of resources in few hands, dividing society into haves and have-nots; and global ecological crises such as global warming, ozone layer depletion, environmental pollution and land degradation.
answer_hinglish: Resources ko prakriti ka muft tohfa maan kar insaan ne inka andhadhundh use kiya, jisse yeh samasyayein aayi: kuch logon ke laalach ke liye resources ka khatam hona; resources kuch haathon mein simat-na, jisse society ameer aur gareeb mein bati; aur global warming, ozone layer ka ghatna, pradooshan aur zameen ki giraavat jaise global ecological sankat.
ncert_context: Resources are vital for human survival and quality of life. It was believed that resources are free gifts of nature. As a result, human beings used them indiscriminately, leading to major problems: depletion of resources for satisfying the greed of a few individuals; accumulation of resources in few hands, dividing society into haves and have nots, or rich and poor; and indiscriminate exploitation leading to global ecological crises such as global warming, ozone layer depletion, environmental pollution and land degradation.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit of 1992?
question_hinglish: 1992 ka Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit kya tha?
answer_english: In June 1992, more than 100 heads of state met in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, for the first International Earth Summit to address urgent problems of environmental protection and socio-economic development globally. The leaders signed the Declaration on Global Climatic Change and Biological Diversity. The Rio Convention endorsed the global Forest Principles and adopted Agenda 21 for achieving sustainable development in the 21st century.
answer_hinglish: June 1992 mein 100 se zyada raashtradhyaksh Brazil ke Rio de Janeiro mein pehle International Earth Summit mein mile, taaki duniya bhar mein paryavaran suraksha aur samajik-aarthik vikaas ki zaroori samasyaon pe baat ho. Leaders ne Declaration on Global Climatic Change and Biological Diversity pe sign kiye. Rio Convention ne global Forest Principles ko samarthan diya aur 21st century mein sustainable development ke liye Agenda 21 apnaya.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is Agenda 21?
question_hinglish: Agenda 21 kya hai?
answer_english: Agenda 21 is the declaration signed by world leaders in 1992 at the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) in Rio de Janeiro. It aims at global sustainable development and combating environmental damage, poverty and disease through global cooperation on common interests, mutual needs and shared responsibilities. question_english: What does resource planning in India involve?
question_hinglish: India mein resource planning mein kya-kya shaamil hai?
answer_english: Resource planning involves: (i) identification and inventory of resources across regions, through surveying, mapping and qualitative and quantitative estimation; (ii) evolving a planning structure with appropriate technology, skill and institutions to implement resource development plans; and (iii) matching resource development plans with overall national development plans. India has pursued these goals since the First Five Year Plan.
answer_hinglish: Resource planning mein shaamil hai: (i) survey, mapping aur gunatmak aur maatraatmak aakalan se desh ke ilaakon mein resources ki pehchaan aur suchi banana; (ii) resource development plans laagu karne ke liye sahi technology, hunar aur sansthaon wala planning dhaancha banana; aur (iii) resource development plans ko poore national development plans se milaana. India First Five Year Plan se in lakshyon pe kaam kar raha hai.

India has made concerted efforts for achieving the goals of resource planning right from the First Five Year Plan launched after Independence.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why can mere availability of resources not ensure development? Use the example of colonisation.
question_hinglish: Sirf resources hone se vikaas kyun nahi hota? Colonisation ka example do.
answer_english: Availability of resources is necessary, but without corresponding changes in technology and institutions it may not lead to development; many resource-rich regions in India are economically backward, while some resource-poor regions are developed. Colonisation shows this: rich colonial resources attracted invaders, and it was the colonisers' higher technology that let them exploit those resources and dominate. So resource development depends on technology, quality of human resources and people's historical experiences too.
answer_hinglish: Resources hona zaroori hai, par technology aur institutions mein badlav ke bina isse vikaas nahi hota; India ke kai resource-sampann ilaake pichhde hain, jabki kuch kam resource wale ilaake viksit hain. Colonisation yeh dikhata hai: colonies ke samriddh resources ne hamlaawaron ko kheecha, aur colonisers ki unnat technology ne unhe un resources ka shoshan karne aur raaj karne diya. Isliye resource development technology, insaani sansaadhan ki gunvatta aur logon ke aitihasik anubhav pe bhi nirbhar hai.
ncert_context: The availability of resources is a necessary condition for development, but mere availability in the absence of corresponding changes in technology and institutions may hinder development. Many regions in India are rich in resources but economically backward; some have a poor resource base but are economically developed. The history of colonisation reveals that rich resources in colonies were the main attractions for foreign invaders. It was primarily the higher technological development of colonising countries that helped them exploit other regions' resources and establish supremacy. Resources contribute to development only when accompanied by appropriate technological development and institutional changes. In India, resource development involves not only availability but also technology, quality of human resources and the historical experiences of the people.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What were Gandhiji's views on resource conservation?
question_hinglish: Resource conservation pe Gandhiji ke kya vichaar the?
answer_english: Gandhiji said, 'There is enough for everybody's need and not for anybody's greed.' He saw greedy, selfish individuals and the exploitative nature of modern technology as the root cause of global resource depletion. He was against mass production and wanted to replace it with production by the masses.
answer_hinglish: Gandhiji ne kaha, 'Har kisi ki zaroorat ke liye kaafi hai, par kisi ke laalach ke liye nahi.' Unhone laalchi, swaarthi logon aur modern technology ke shoshak swabhaav ko duniya bhar mein resources khatam hone ki jad maana. Woh mass production ke khilaaf the aur use janta dwara utpaadan se badalna chahte the.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Trace the major international contributions to resource conservation.
question_hinglish: Resource conservation mein mukhya international yogdaan batao.
answer_english: The Club of Rome advocated resource conservation systematically for the first time in 1968. In 1974, Schumacher presented Gandhian philosophy again in his book Small is Beautiful. The Brundtland Commission Report of 1987 introduced the concept of 'Sustainable Development' as a means of conservation, published as Our Common Future. Another significant contribution was the Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro in 1992.
answer_hinglish: Club of Rome ne 1968 mein pehli baar vyavasthit tareeke se resource conservation ki baat ki. 1974 mein Schumacher ne apni kitaab Small is Beautiful mein Gandhian darshan ko phir pesh kiya. 1987 ki Brundtland Commission Report ne conservation ke tareeke ke roop mein 'Sustainable Development' ka concept diya, jo Our Common Future naam se chhapi. Ek aur bada yogdaan 1992 ka Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit tha.
ncert_context: At the international level, the Club of Rome advocated resource conservation for the first time in a more systematic way in 1968. Subsequently, in 1974, Gandhian philosophy was once again presented by Schumacher in his book Small is Beautiful. The seminal contribution with respect to resource conservation at the global level was made by the Brundtland Commission Report, 1987. This report introduced the concept of 'Sustainable Development' and advocated it as a means for resource conservation, subsequently published in a book entitled Our Common Future. Another significant contribution was made at the Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro, Brazil in 1992.

question_hinglish: India mein zameen ke upyog ki kaun-kaun si shreniyan hain?
answer_english: Land is used as: 1. forests; 2. land not available for cultivation, including barren and waste land and land put to non-agricultural uses like buildings, roads and factories; 3. other uncultivated land (excluding fallow), including permanent pastures and grazing land, land under miscellaneous tree crops and groves, and culturable waste land; 4. fallow lands, both current fallow and other than current fallow; and 5. net sown area.
answer_hinglish: Zameen ka upyog hai: 1. jungle; 2. kheti ke liye na milne wali zameen, jisme banjar aur bekaar zameen aur imaaraton, sadkon aur factories jaise gair-kheti kaamon ki zameen hai; 3. doosri bina jot wali zameen (fallow chhod kar), jisme sthaayi charaagaah, vividh ped-fasal aur baag, aur culturable waste land hain; 4. fallow zameen, current fallow aur other than current fallow dono; aur 5. net sown area.

question_english: Why is the forest area in India a concern?
question_hinglish: India mein jungle ka kshetra chinta ka vishay kyun hai?
answer_english: Forest area in India is far lower than the desired 33 per cent of geographical area outlined in the National Forest Policy (1952), which was considered essential for ecological balance. This matters because the livelihood of millions living on the fringes of forests depends on them, and low forest cover threatens ecological balance.
answer_hinglish: India mein jungle ka kshetra National Forest Policy (1952) mein tay bhaugolik kshetra ke 33 percent se kaafi kam hai, jo paryavarniya santulan ke liye zaroori maana gaya tha. Yeh isliye mahatvapurn hai kyunki jungle ke kinaare rehne wale laakhon logon ki rozi in pe nirbhar hai, aur kam jungle paryavarniya santulan ke liye khatra hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What measures can solve the problems of land degradation?
question_hinglish: Zameen ki giraavat ki samasyaon ko kaise suljhaya ja sakta hai?
answer_english: Afforestation and proper management of grazing help. In arid areas, planting shelter belts, controlling overgrazing and stabilising sand dunes with thorny bushes check degradation. In industrial and suburban areas, proper management of waste lands, control of mining, and proper treatment and disposal of industrial effluents and wastes reduce land and water degradation.
answer_hinglish: Vanikaran aur charaai ka sahi prabandhan madad karte hain.
