Industrial aur upnagariy ilaakon mein bekaar zameen ka sahi prabandhan, khanan pe niyantran, aur industrial gande paani aur kachre ka upchaar karke nikaas zameen aur paani ki giraavat kam karta hai.
ncert_context: There are many ways to solve the problems of land degradation. Afforestation and proper management of grazing can help to some extent. Planting of shelter belts of plants, control on over grazing, stabilisation of sand dunes by growing thorny bushes are some of the methods to check land degradation in arid areas. Proper management of waste lands, control of mining activities, proper discharge and disposal of industrial effluents and wastes after treatment can reduce land and water degradation in industrial and suburban areas.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe alluvial soil and where it is found in India.
question_hinglish: Alluvial mitti ka varnan karo aur batao yeh India mein kahan milti hai.
answer_english: Alluvial soil is the most widespread and important soil. The entire northern plains are made of it, deposited by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems; it also extends into Rajasthan and Gujarat and is found in the eastern coastal deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri. It has sand, silt and clay in varying proportions, with coarser soils near the break of slope in piedmont plains like Duars, Chos and Terai.
answer_hinglish: Alluvial mitti sabse vyapak aur important mitti hai. Poore northern plains isi se bane hain, jo Indus, Ganga aur Brahmaputra nadi systems ne jamaayi; yeh Rajasthan aur Gujarat tak bhi faili hai aur Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna aur Kaveri ke poorvi tatiya delta mein milti hai. Isme ret, gaad aur chikni mitti alag anupaat mein hoti hai, aur Duars, Chos aur Terai jaise piedmont maidaanon mein dhalaan ke paas mitti mo-ti hoti hai.

question_english: What type of soil is found in the river deltas of the eastern coast? Give three features.
question_hinglish: Poorvi tat ke nadi deltaon mein kaun si mitti milti hai? Iski teen khaasiyatein batao.
answer_english: Alluvial soil is found in the deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri. subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the features of black soil, and where is it found?
question_hinglish: Kaali mitti ki khaasiyatein kya hain, aur yeh kahan milti hai?
answer_english: Black soil, also called regur or black cotton soil, is ideal for cotton. It forms from climate and parent rock, typical of the Deccan trap (basalt) region made of lava flows. It covers the plateaus of Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Malwa, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh and extends along the Godavari and Krishna valleys. It is clayey, holds moisture well, is rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash and lime but poor in phosphorus, develops deep cracks in hot weather for aeration, and is sticky when wet.
answer_hinglish: Kaali mitti, jise regur ya black cotton soil bhi kehte hain, cotton ke liye sabse achhi hai. Yeh jalvaayu aur mool chattaan se banti hai aur lava se bane Deccan trap (basalt) ilaake ki khaas mitti hai. Yeh Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Malwa, Madhya Pradesh aur Chhattisgarh ke pathaaron mein aur Godavari aur Krishna ghaatiyon mein milti hai. Yeh chikni hai, nami achhi rokti hai, calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash aur chune se bharpoor par phosphorus mein kam hai, garmi mein gehri daraarein padti hain jo hawa jaane deti hain, aur geeli hone pe chipchipi hoti hai.
ncert_context: These soils are black in colour and are also known as regur soils. Black soil is ideal for growing cotton and is also known as black cotton soil. Climatic condition along with parent rock material are important factors for its formation. It is typical of the Deccan trap (Basalt) region spread over northwest Deccan plateau, made up of lava flows. It covers the plateaus of Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Malwa, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh and extends along the Godavari and Krishna valleys. Black soils are made up of extremely fine clayey material, known for their capacity to hold moisture, rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash and lime, but generally poor in phosphoric contents. They develop deep cracks during hot weather, helping aeration, and are sticky when wet.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the features and uses of laterite soil?
question_hinglish: Laterite mitti ki khaasiyatein aur upyog kya hain?
answer_english: Laterite comes from the Latin 'later', meaning brick. It develops in tropical and subtropical climates with alternate wet and dry seasons through intense leaching by heavy rain. It is mostly deep, acidic (pH below 6.0) and deficient in nutrients, found in southern states, the Western Ghats of Maharashtra, Odisha, parts of West Bengal and the North-east. It is humus-rich under forests but humus-poor under sparse vegetation. With conservation, it grows tea and coffee in Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, and red laterite suits cashew nut.
answer_hinglish: Laterite Latin shabd 'later', yaani eent, se bana hai. Yeh baari-baari geele aur sookhe mausam wale tropical aur subtropical jalvaayu mein bhaari baarish se tez leaching se banti hai. Yeh zyadatar gehri, amliya (pH 6.0 se kam) aur poshak tatvon mein kam hoti hai, aur dakshini states, Maharashtra ke Western Ghats, Odisha, West Bengal ke kuch hisson aur North-east mein milti hai. Jungle ke neeche yeh humus se bharpoor, par kam vanaspati mein humus mein kam hoti hai. Sanrakshan ke baad Karnataka, Kerala aur Tamil Nadu mein isme chaay aur coffee ugti hai, aur laal laterite kaaju ke liye achhi hai.
ncert_context: Laterite has been derived from the Latin word 'later' which means brick. The laterite soil develops under tropical and subtropical climate with alternate wet and dry season. This soil is the result of intense leaching due to heavy rain. Lateritic soils are mostly deep to very deep, acidic (pH<6.0), generally deficient in plant nutrients and occur mostly in southern states, Western Ghats region of Maharashtra, Odisha, some parts of West Bengal and North-east regions. Where they support deciduous and evergreen forests, they are humus rich, but under sparse vegetation in semi-arid environments, humus poor. After soil conservation techniques in the hilly areas of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, this soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee. Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala suit cashew nut.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the characteristics of arid soils?
question_hinglish: Sookhi (arid) mitti ki khaasiyatein kya hain?
answer_english: Arid soils range from red to brown, are generally sandy and saline; in some areas salt content is so high that common salt is obtained by evaporating water. The dry climate and high temperature cause fast evaporation, so they lack humus and moisture. Lower horizons have kankar due to increasing calcium content downwards, which restricts water infiltration. After proper irrigation, they become cultivable, as in western Rajasthan.
answer_hinglish: Arid mitti laal se bhoore rang ki, aam taur pe retili aur khaari hoti hai; kuch jagah namak itna zyada hai ki paani bhaap bana kar namak nikaala jaata hai. Sookhi jalvaayu aur oonche taapmaan se bhaap tez banti hai, isliye isme humus aur nami nahi hoti. Neeche calcium badhne se kankar ki parat hoti hai jo paani ko andar jaane se rokti hai. Sahi sinchaai ke baad yeh kheti layak ho jaati hai, jaise western Rajasthan mein.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe forest soils.
question_hinglish: Forest mitti ka varnan karo.
answer_english: Forest soils are found in hilly and mountainous areas with sufficient rain forests. Their texture varies with the mountain environment: loamy and silty on valley sides and coarse-grained on upper slopes. In snow-covered Himalayan areas they experience denudation and are acidic with low humus, while soils in lower valleys, river terraces and alluvial fans are fertile.
answer_hinglish: Forest mitti pahaadi ilaakon mein milti hai jahan kaafi rain forests hain. Iski banaavat pahaadi maahaul ke hisaab se badalti hai: ghaati ki dhalaan pe domat aur gaad wali, aur oopri dhalaanon pe mote daane wali. Himalaya ke barf wale ilaakon mein iska kshaya hota hai aur yeh amliya aur kam humus wali hoti hai, jabki ghaatiyon ke neeche, nadi chabootron aur alluvial fans ki mitti upjaau hoti hai.
ncert_context: Forest soils are found in the hilly and mountainous areas where sufficient rain forests are available. The soil texture varies according to the mountain environment where they are formed. They are loamy and silty in valley sides and coarse grained in the upper slopes. In the snow covered areas of the Himalayas, these soils experience denudation and are acidic with low humus content. The soils found in the lower parts of the valleys, particularly on the river terraces and alluvial fans, are fertile.

question_english: Differentiate between gully erosion, sheet erosion and wind erosion.
question_hinglish: Gully erosion, sheet erosion aur wind erosion mein fark batao.
answer_english: In gully erosion, running water cuts through clayey soils to form deep channels called gullies, making land unfit for cultivation (bad land), called ravines in the Chambal basin. In sheet erosion, water flows as a sheet over large areas down a slope, washing away the top soil. In wind erosion, wind blows loose soil off flat or sloping land.
answer_hinglish: Gully erosion mein behta paani chikni mitti ko kaat kar gehri naaliyan (gullies) banata hai, jisse zameen kheti ke layak nahi rehti (bad land), aur Chambal basin mein inhe ravines kehte hain. Sheet erosion mein paani dhalaan pe bade kshetra mein chaadar ki tarah bahta hai aur oopri mitti baha le jaata hai. Wind erosion mein hawa samtal ya dhalaan wali zameen se dheeli mitti uda le jaati hai.

Wind blows loose soil off flat or sloping land known as wind erosion.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What steps can be taken to control soil erosion, especially in hilly areas?
question_hinglish: Soil erosion rokne ke liye, khaas kar pahaadi ilaakon mein, kya kadam uthaye ja sakte hain?
answer_english: Contour ploughing, ploughing along contour lines, slows water flow down slopes. Terrace cultivation, cutting steps on slopes, restricts erosion and is well developed in the western and central Himalayas. Strip cropping divides large fields into strips with grass strips between crops to break wind force. Shelter belts, rows of trees, work similarly and have helped stabilise sand dunes and the desert in western India.
answer_hinglish: Contour ploughing, yaani contour rekhaon ke saath hal chalana, dhalaan pe paani ka bahaav dheema karta hai. Terrace cultivation, yaani dhalaan pe seedhiyan kaatna, katav rokta hai aur western aur central Himalaya mein khoob viksit hai. Strip cropping mein bade khet ko pattiyon mein baant kar fasalon ke beech ghaas ki pattiyan chhodi jaati hain jo hawa ki taakat todti hain. Shelter belts, yaani pedon ki kataarein, bhi aisa hi karti hain aur western India mein ret ke teele aur registan sthir karne mein madad ki hai.
ncert_context: Ploughing along the contour lines can decelerate the flow of water down the slopes; this is called contour ploughing. Steps can be cut out on the slopes making terraces. Terrace cultivation restricts erosion. Western and central Himalayas have well developed terrace farming. Large fields can be divided into strips, with strips of grass left to grow between the crops; this breaks up the force of the wind and is known as strip cropping. Planting lines of trees to create shelter works similarly; rows of such trees are called shelter belts. These have contributed significantly to stabilising sand dunes and the desert in western India.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How have technical and economic development led to more consumption of resources?
question_hinglish: Technology aur economic vikaas ne resources ki khapat kaise badhayi?
answer_english: Humans interact with nature through technology and create institutions to accelerate economic development, so technological advances make more materials accessible and economically feasible as resources. Colonisers used superior technology to exploit colonies' resources. As resources were treated as free gifts, they were used indiscriminately, causing depletion for the greed of a few, accumulation in few hands, and ecological crises like global warming and pollution. This is why sustainable development and conservation are needed.
answer_hinglish: Insaan technology se nature ke saath kaam karta hai aur economic vikaas tez karne ke liye institutions banata hai, isliye technology badhne se zyada cheezein pahunch mein aur aarthik roop se sambhav resource ban jaati hain. Colonisers ne behtar technology se colonies ke resources ka shoshan kiya. Resources ko muft tohfa maan kar andhadhundh use kiya gaya, jisse kuch logon ke laalach mein resources khatam hue, kuch haathon mein simte, aur global warming aur pradooshan jaise sankat aaye. Isiliye sustainable development aur conservation zaroori hain.
ncert_context: A resource must be technologically accessible, economically feasible and culturally acceptable. Human beings interact with nature through technology and create institutions to accelerate economic development. It was primarily the higher technological development of colonising countries that helped them exploit resources of other regions. Resources were believed to be free gifts of nature and used indiscriminately, leading to depletion for the greed of a few, accumulation in few hands, and global ecological crises such as global warming, ozone depletion, pollution and land degradation. Gandhiji blamed the exploitative nature of modern technology and opposed mass production.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is biodiversity?
question_hinglish: Biodiversity kya hai?
answer_english: Biodiversity or biological diversity is immensely rich in wildlife and cultivated species, diverse in form and function but closely integrated in a system through multiple networks of interdependencies. We share the planet with millions of living beings, from micro-organisms and lichens to banyan trees, elephants and blue whales.
answer_hinglish: Biodiversity yaani biological diversity vanya jeevon aur ugaayi jaane wali prajaatiyon se bharpoor hai, jo roop aur kaam mein alag par aapsi nirbharta ke kai jaalon se ek system mein judi hoti hain. Hum is grah ko sookshm jeevon aur lichens se lekar bargad, haathi aur blue whale tak laakhon jeevon ke saath baant-te hain.

question_english: Why do we need to conserve our forests and wildlife?
question_hinglish: Hume apne jungal aur vanya jeevon ko kyun bachana chahiye?
answer_english: With the rapid decline of wildlife and forests, conservation has become essential. It preserves ecological diversity and our life support systems of water, air and soil. It also preserves the genetic diversity of plants and animals for better growth and breeding of species; for example, agriculture still depends on traditional crop varieties, and fisheries depend on maintaining aquatic biodiversity.

Yeh paryavarniya vividhata aur paani, hawa aur mitti jaise jeevan-sahayak systems ko bachata hai. Yeh paudhon aur jaanwaron ki genetic vividhata bhi bachata hai taaki prajaatiyon ki behtar vriddhi aur breeding ho; jaise kheti ab bhi paramparik fasal kismon pe nirbhar hai, aur machhli palan jal biodiversity pe.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act of 1972?
question_hinglish: 1972 ka Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act kya tha?
answer_english: In the 1960s and 1970s, conservationists demanded a national wildlife protection programme, and the Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act was implemented in 1972 with provisions for protecting habitats. An all-India list of protected species was published. Its thrust was to protect the remaining populations of endangered species by banning hunting, giving legal protection to their habitats and restricting wildlife trade, after which governments set up national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
answer_hinglish: 1960s aur 1970s mein sanrakshanvaadiyon ne national wildlife suraksha programme ki maang ki, aur 1972 mein Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act laagu hua jisme aavaas bachane ke provisions the. Surakshit prajaatiyon ki all-India suchi chhapi. Iska zor shikaar pe rok, aavaas ko kanooni suraksha aur vanya jeev vyapaar pe rok lagaa kar khatre wali prajaatiyon ki bachi aabaadi ko bachana tha, jiske baad sarkaron ne national parks aur wildlife sanctuaries banaye.
ncert_context: In the 1960s and 1970s, conservationists demanded a national wildlife protection programme. The Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act was implemented in 1972, with various provisions for protecting habitats. An all-India list of protected species was also published. The thrust of the programme was towards protecting the remaining population of certain endangered species by banning hunting, giving legal protection to their habitats, and restricting trade in wildlife. Subsequently, central and many state governments established national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.

question_english: Which animals have been given special protection through central government projects?
question_hinglish: Central sarkar ke projects se kin jaanwaron ko khaas suraksha di gayi hai?

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why was Project Tiger launched, and what were the threats to tigers?
question_hinglish: Project Tiger kyun shuru kiya gaya, aur tigers ko kya khatre the?
answer_english: By 1973, the tiger population had dwindled to 1,827 from an estimated 55,000 at the turn of the century. Threats included poaching for trade, shrinking habitat, depletion of prey species and growing human population; trade in tiger skins and use of bones in traditional medicines, especially in Asian countries, pushed tigers to the verge of extinction. As India and Nepal host about two-thirds of the world's surviving tigers, they were prime poaching targets. Project Tiger was launched in 1973, one of the world's best-publicised wildlife campaigns.
answer_hinglish: 1973 tak tigers ki aabaadi sadi ki shuruaat ke anumaanit 55,000 se ghat kar 1,827 reh gayi thi. Khatron mein vyapaar ke liye shikaar, sikud-te aavaas, shikaar prajaatiyon ki kami aur badhti insaani aabaadi the; khaas kar Asian deshon mein tiger ki khaal ke vyapaar aur haddiyon ke paramparik dawaon mein use ne tiger ko vilupti ke kagaar pe la diya. India aur Nepal duniya ke lagbhag do-tihaai tigers ka ghar hain, isliye shikaariyon ke mukhya nishaane bane. 1973 mein Project Tiger shuru hua, jo duniya ke sabse mashhoor wildlife campaigns mein se hai.
ncert_context: Tiger is one of the key wildlife species in the faunal web. question_english: What are permanent forest estates, and how are forest types distributed across Indian states?
question_hinglish: Permanent forest estates kya hain, aur Indian states mein jungle ke prakaar kaise bate hain?
answer_english: Reserved and protected forests are called permanent forest estates, maintained for producing timber and other forest produce and for protective reasons. Madhya Pradesh has the largest area under permanent forests, 75 per cent of its forest area. North-eastern states and parts of Gujarat have high shares of unclassed forests managed by local communities.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are sacred groves, and how do they help conservation?
question_hinglish: Sacred groves kya hain, aur yeh sanrakshan mein kaise madad karte hain?
answer_english: Nature worship is an age-old tribal belief that all creations of nature must be protected. Such beliefs have preserved virgin forests in pristine form called sacred groves, the forests of gods and goddesses, which local people leave untouched and where interference is banned. Some societies revere particular trees: the Mundas and Santhal of Chota Nagpur worship mahua and kadamba, and tribals of Odisha and Bihar worship tamarind and mango trees during weddings.
answer_hinglish: Prakriti pooja ek purani adivaasi aastha hai ki prakriti ki har rachna ki raksha honi chahiye. Is aastha ne kuwaare jungalon ko asli roop mein bachaya jinhe sacred groves, yaani devi-devtaon ke jungle, kehte hain, jinhe local log chhoote nahi aur jinme dakhal mana hai. Kuch samaaj khaas pedon ki pooja karte hain: Chota Nagpur ke Munda aur Santhal mahua aur kadamba ki, aur Odisha aur Bihar ke adivaasi shaadiyon mein imli aur aam ki pooja karte hain.
ncert_context: Nature worship is an age-old tribal belief based on the premise that all creations of nature have to be protected. Such beliefs have preserved several virgin forests in pristine form called Sacred Groves (the forests of God and Goddesses). These patches of forest have been left untouched by local people and any interference is banned. Certain societies revere a particular tree. The Mundas and the Santhal of Chota Nagpur region worship mahua (Bassia latifolia) and kadamba (Anthocaphalus cadamba) trees, and the tribals of Odisha and Bihar worship the tamarind (Tamarindus indica) and mango (Mangifera indica) trees during weddings. To many of us, peepal and banyan trees are sacred.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is Joint Forest Management (JFM)?
question_hinglish: Joint Forest Management (JFM) kya hai?
answer_english: Joint Forest Management involves local communities in managing and restoring degraded forests. It formally began in 1988 when Odisha passed the first JFM resolution. It depends on local village institutions that undertake protection activities, mostly on degraded forest land managed by the forest department. In return, community members get intermediary benefits like non-timber forest produce and a share in timber harvested through 'successful protection'.
answer_hinglish: Joint Forest Management mein local samudaayon ko kharab jungalon ke prabandhan aur sudhaar mein shaamil kiya jaata hai. Yeh 1988 mein aupchaarik roop se shuru hua jab Odisha ne JFM ka pehla prastaav pass kiya. Yeh local gaon sansthaon pe nirbhar hai jo zyadatar forest department ki kharab jungle zameen ki raksha karti hain. Badle mein samudaay ke logon ko gair-lakdi van utpaad jaise fayde aur 'safal suraksha' se kaati gayi lakdi mein hissa milta hai.
ncert_context: In India the joint forest management (JFM) programme furnishes a good example for involving local communities in the management and restoration of degraded forests. The programme has been in formal existence since 1988 when the state of Odisha passed the first resolution for joint forest management. JFM depends on the formation of local (village) institutions that undertake protection activities mostly on degraded forest land managed by the forest department. In return, the members of these communities are entitled to intermediary benefits like non-timber forest produces and share in the timber harvested by 'successful protection'.

question_english: How have human activities affected the depletion of flora and fauna?
question_hinglish: Insaani gatividhiyon ne flora aur fauna ki kami ko kaise prabhavit kiya hai?
answer_english: Human insensitivity to the environment has put India's flora and fauna under great stress. Poaching for trade, shrinking habitats, depletion of prey species and growing human population threatened animals like the tiger, whose numbers fell from about 55,000 to 1,827 by 1973. Mining and deforestation also damage habitats, as villagers fighting mining in Sariska show, so laws like the Wildlife Protection Act and community efforts became necessary.
answer_hinglish: Environment ke prati insaan ki asamvedansheelta ne India ke flora aur fauna ko bahut dabaav mein daala hai. Khanan aur jungle katna bhi aavaas bigaadte hain, jaise Sariska mein khanan ke khilaaf gaon waalon ki ladai dikhati hai, isliye Wildlife Protection Act jaise kanoon aur samudaayik prayaas zaroori hue.

question_english: How does water become a renewable resource?
question_hinglish: Paani renewable resource kaise banta hai?

subject: Social Science
question_english: How have agriculture, industrialisation and urbanisation increased pressure on water resources?
question_hinglish: Kheti, industrialisation aur shehrikaran ne paani ke resources pe dabaav kaise badhaya?
answer_english: To produce more food, water is over-exploited to expand irrigation for dry-season farming; irrigated agriculture is the largest water consumer, and farmers' own wells and tube-wells may lower groundwater and threaten food security. Industries use a lot of water and need power, much of it hydroelectric. Growing urban centres with dense populations and urban lifestyles add to water and energy needs, and housing societies pump their own groundwater, depleting resources in many cities.
answer_hinglish: Zyada anaaj ugaane ke liye sookhe mausam ki kheti ke liye sinchaai badhakar paani ka zyada shoshan hota hai; sinchaai wali kheti sabse zyada paani leti hai, aur kisaanon ke apne kuen aur tube-wells bhoojal giraa kar khaadya suraksha ko khatre mein daal sakte hain. Udyog bahut paani use karte hain aur unhe bijli chahiye, jiska bada hissa hydroelectric hai. Ghani aabaadi aur shehri jeevanshaili wale badhte shehar paani aur urja ki zaroorat badhate hain, aur housing societies apna bhoojal kheench kar kai shehron mein paani khatam kar rahi hain.

Multiplying urban centres with dense populations and urban lifestyles have added to water and energy requirements. Most housing societies in cities have their own groundwater pumping devices, causing depletion.

question_english: What is the Jal Jeevan Mission?
question_hinglish: Jal Jeevan Mission kya hai?

question_english: What is the Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal)?
question_hinglish: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal) kya hai?

subject: Social Science
question_english: Give examples of hydraulic structures in ancient and medieval India.
question_hinglish: Praacheen aur madhyakaaleen India ke hydraulic structures ke examples do.
answer_english: In the first century BC, Sringaverapura near Allahabad had a sophisticated system channelling Ganga floodwater. Under Chandragupta Maurya, dams, lakes and irrigation systems were extensively built. Irrigation works existed in Kalinga, Nagarjunakonda, Bennur and Kolhapur. In the 11th century, Bhopal Lake, one of the largest artificial lakes of its time, was built, and in the 13th-14th century, Allauddin Khilji built the Hauz Khas tank in Delhi to supply water to the Siri Fort area.
answer_hinglish: First century BC mein Allahabad ke paas Sringaverapura mein Ganga ke baadh ke paani ko modne ka unnat system tha. Chandragupta Maurya ke samay mein bahut bandh, jheelein aur sinchaai systems bane. Kalinga, Nagarjunakonda, Bennur aur Kolhapur mein sinchaai ke kaam mile hain. 11th century mein Bhopal Lake bani, jo apne samay ki sabse badi kritrim jheelon mein thi, aur 13th-14th century mein Allauddin Khilji ne Siri Fort ilaake ko paani dene ke liye Delhi mein Hauz Khas ka talaab banaya.
ncert_context: Archaeological and historical records show that from ancient times we have been constructing sophisticated hydraulic structures like dams of stone rubble, reservoirs or lakes, embankments and canals for irrigation. In the first century B.C., Sringaverapura near Allahabad had a sophisticated water harvesting system channelling the flood water of the river Ganga. During the time of Chandragupta Maurya, dams, lakes and irrigation systems were extensively built. Evidence of irrigation works has been found in Kalinga (Odisha), Nagarjunakonda (Andhra Pradesh), Bennur (Karnataka) and Kolhapur (Maharashtra). In the 11th century, Bhopal Lake, one of the largest artificial lakes of its time, was built. In the 13th–14th century, the tank in Hauz Khas, Delhi was constructed by Allauddin Khilji for supplying water to Siri Fort area.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is a dam, and how are dams classified?
question_hinglish: Dam kya hai, aur dams ko kaise baanta jaata hai?
answer_english: A dam is a barrier across flowing water that obstructs, directs or retards the flow, often creating a reservoir, lake or impoundment; 'dam' refers to the reservoir rather than the structure. Most dams have a spillway or weir for water to flow over or through. By structure and materials, dams are timber, embankment or masonry dams; by height, they are large and major dams, or low, medium height and high dams.
answer_hinglish: Dam behte paani ke aar-paar ek rukawat hai jo bahaav ko rokti, modti ya dheema karti hai, aksar ek jalaashay, jheel ya bandh banati hai; 'dam' shabd dhaanche ki jagah jalaashay ko kehta hai. Zyadatar dams mein spillway ya weir hota hai jisse paani upar se ya andar se bahta hai. Dhaanche aur saamaan ke hisaab se dams lakdi ke, embankment ya masonry hote hain; oonchaai ke hisaab se large aur major, ya low, medium aur high dams.
ncert_context: A dam is a barrier across flowing water that obstructs, directs or retards the flow, often creating a reservoir, lake or impoundment. 'Dam' refers to the reservoir rather than the structure. Most dams have a section called a spillway or weir over which or through which water flows intermittently or continuously. Dams are classified according to structure, intended purpose or height. Based on structure and materials, dams are timber dams, embankment dams or masonry dams, with subtypes. According to height, dams can be large dams and major dams, or low dams, medium height dams and high dams.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are multi-purpose river projects? Give examples.
question_hinglish: Multi-purpose river projects kya hain? Examples do.
answer_english: Dams were traditionally built to store river and rainwater for irrigation, but today they serve irrigation, electricity generation, domestic and industrial water supply, flood control, recreation, inland navigation and fish breeding, so they are called multi-purpose projects that integrate many uses of stored water. For example, the Bhakra-Nangal project in the Sutlej-Beas basin provides hydel power and irrigation, and the Hirakud project in the Mahanadi basin combines water conservation with flood control.
answer_hinglish: Pehle dams nadi aur baarish ka paani sinchaai ke liye rokne ko bante the, par aaj woh sinchaai, bijli utpaadan, ghar aur udyog ki paani supply, baadh niyantran, manoranjan, aantarik jal parivahan aur machhli palan ke kaam aate hain, isliye inhe multi-purpose projects kehte hain jo roke gaye paani ke kai upyog jodte hain. Jaise Sutlej-Beas basin ka Bhakra-Nangal project bijli aur sinchaai deta hai, aur Mahanadi basin ka Hirakud project paani bachane ko baadh niyantran se jodta hai.
ncert_context: Dams were traditionally built to impound rivers and rainwater that could be used later to irrigate agricultural fields. Today, dams are built not just for irrigation but for electricity generation, water supply for domestic and industrial uses, flood control, recreation, inland navigation and fish breeding. Hence, dams are now referred to as multi-purpose projects where the many uses of the impounded water are integrated with one another. For example, in the Sutluj-Beas river basin, the Bhakra–Nangal project water is being used both for hydel power production and irrigation. Similarly, the Hirakud project in the Mahanadi basin integrates conservation of water with flood control.

question_english: Why did Jawaharlal Nehru call dams the 'temples of modern India'?
question_hinglish: Jawaharlal Nehru ne dams ko 'aadhunik Bharat ke mandir' kyun kaha?

question_english: What are the benefits of the Sardar Sarovar Project?
question_hinglish: Sardar Sarovar Project ke kya fayde hain?
answer_english: The Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada in Gujarat is one of India's largest water projects, covering Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan. It will meet water needs of drought-prone and desert areas, irrigating 18.45 lakh hectares in 3,112 villages of 15 Gujarat districts, 2,46,000 hectares in the desert districts of Barmer and Jalore in Rajasthan, and 37,500 hectares in Maharashtra's tribal hills through lift. About 75 per cent of its Gujarat command area and all of Rajasthan's are drought-prone, which assured water should make drought-proof.

Yeh sookhe aur registani ilaakon ki paani ki zaroorat poori karega, Gujarat ke 15 districts ke 3,112 gaon ki 18.45 lakh hectare zameen, Rajasthan ke registani Barmer aur Jalore ki 2,46,000 hectare, aur Maharashtra ke adivaasi pahaadi ilaake ki 37,500 hectare zameen lift se seenchega. Gujarat ke command area ka lagbhag 75 percent aur Rajasthan ka poora sookha-prabhavit hai, jise pakka paani sookha-mukt bana dega.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Name traditional water harvesting methods used in different regions of India.
question_hinglish: India ke alag ilaakon mein use hone wale paramparik water harvesting tareekon ke naam batao.
answer_english: In the Western Himalayas, people built diversion channels called 'guls' or 'kuls' for agriculture. In Rajasthan, rooftop rainwater harvesting stored drinking water in underground tankas. In the floodplains of Bengal, inundation channels irrigated fields. In arid and semi-arid regions, fields were turned into rain-fed storage structures like the 'khadins' of Jaisalmer and 'johads' in other parts of Rajasthan. In Meghalaya, bamboo drip irrigation taps stream and spring water.
answer_hinglish: Western Himalaya mein log kheti ke liye 'guls' ya 'kuls' naam ki naaliyan banate the. Rajasthan mein rooftop rainwater harvesting se peene ka paani zameen ke neeche tankas mein jamaa hota tha. Bengal ke baadh maidaanon mein inundation channels se khet seenche jaate the. Sookhe ilaakon mein kheton ko baarish ka paani rokne wale dhaanchon mein badla gaya, jaise Jaisalmer ke 'khadins' aur Rajasthan ke 'johads'. Meghalaya mein bamboo drip irrigation se jharnon aur naalon ka paani liya jaata hai.
ncert_context: In hill and mountainous regions, people built diversion channels like the 'guls' or 'kuls' of the Western Himalayas for agriculture. In Meghalaya, a 200-year-old system of tapping stream and spring water using bamboo pipes is prevalent.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How was rainwater harvesting carried out in the semi-arid regions of Rajasthan?
question_hinglish: Rajasthan ke ardh-sookhe ilaakon mein rainwater harvesting kaise hoti thi?
answer_english: In Bikaner, Phalodi and Barmer, almost all houses had underground tanks or tankas for drinking water, some as large as a room, built inside the house or courtyard and connected to sloping roofs by a pipe. Rain from the rooftops flowed down into the tankas; the first spell was not collected because it cleaned the roofs and pipes. Stored rainwater, called palar pani and considered the purest natural water, lasted till the next rain, and underground rooms beside tankas kept houses cool in summer.
answer_hinglish: Bikaner, Phalodi aur Barmer mein lagbhag har ghar mein peene ke paani ke liye zameen ke neeche tankas the, kuch ek kamre jitne bade, jo ghar ya aangan mein bante aur dhalaan wali chhat se pipe se jude hote the. Chhat ka baarish ka paani tankas mein jaata; pehli baarish nahi rakhi jaati kyunki usse chhat aur pipe saaf hote the. Jamaa paani, jise palar pani kehte the aur sabse shuddh prakritik paani maana jaata tha, agli baarish tak chalta, aur tankas ke paas zameen ke neeche ke kamre garmi mein ghar ko thanda rakhte the.
ncert_context: In the semi-arid and arid regions of Rajasthan, particularly in Bikaner, Phalodi and Barmer, almost all houses traditionally had underground tanks or tankas for storing drinking water. The tanks could be as large as a big room. The tankas were part of the rooftop rainwater harvesting system, built inside the main house or courtyard and connected to the sloping roofs through a pipe. Rain falling on rooftops travelled down the pipe and was stored in the underground tankas. The first spell of rain was usually not collected as it would clean the roofs and pipes. Rainwater could be stored till the next rainfall, making it a reliable source of drinking water. Rainwater, or palar pani, is considered the purest form of natural water. Many houses built underground rooms adjoining the tanka to keep cool.

question_english: How are modern adaptations of traditional rainwater harvesting being used to conserve water?
question_hinglish: Paramparik rainwater harvesting ke aadhunik roop paani bachane mein kaise use ho rahe hain?
answer_english: In many parts of rural and urban India, rooftop rainwater harvesting is being successfully adapted. In Gendathur, a remote village in Mysuru, Karnataka, about 200 households installed rooftop systems, making the village rich in rainwater. Rooftop water is collected in PVC pipes, filtered through sand and bricks, stored in a sump for use, and the excess recharges groundwater through hand pumps or abandoned dugwells. Tamil Nadu was the first state to make rooftop harvesting compulsory for all houses.
answer_hinglish: Gaon aur shehron mein kai jagah rooftop rainwater harvesting ko safalta se apnaya ja raha hai. Chhat ka paani PVC pipe se ikattha, ret aur eenton se chhaan kar sump mein use ke liye rakha jaata hai, aur bacha paani hand pump ya purane kuon se bhoojal recharge karta hai. Tamil Nadu pehla state tha jisne har ghar ke liye rooftop harvesting zaroori kiya.

Rooftop rainwater is collected using a PVC pipe, filtered using sand and bricks; an underground pipe takes water to a sump for immediate use; excess water is taken to a well, recharging groundwater. Recharge can be through a hand pump or an abandoned dugwell. Tamil Nadu is the first state in India which has made rooftop rainwater harvesting structure compulsory to all houses, with legal provisions to punish defaulters.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How does the bamboo drip irrigation system of Meghalaya work?
question_hinglish: Meghalaya ka bamboo drip irrigation system kaise kaam karta hai?
answer_english: In Meghalaya, a 200-year-old system uses bamboo pipes to tap stream and spring water. Bamboo pipes divert perennial springs on hilltops to lower areas by gravity, channel sections take water to the plant site where it is distributed into branches, and pipes crossing roads are raised high. The flow is controlled by adjusting pipe positions. About 18 to 20 litres of water entering the system is reduced to 20 to 80 drops per minute near the plant roots.
answer_hinglish: Meghalaya mein 200 saal purana system bamboo ke pipes se jharnon aur naalon ka paani leta hai. Bamboo pipes pahaadi ki choti ke saal bhar chalne wale jharnon ka paani gurutvaakarshan se neeche laate hain, naaliyan paani paudhon tak le jaakar shaakhaon mein baant-ti hain, aur sadak paar karne wale pipes ooncha uthaye jaate hain. Pipes ki jagah badal kar bahaav control hota hai. System mein aane wala 18 se 20 litre paani paudhon ki jadon ke paas 20 se 80 boond per minute reh jaata hai.
ncert_context: In Meghalaya, a 200-year-old system of tapping stream and spring water by using bamboo pipes is prevalent. About 18-20 litres of water enters the bamboo pipe system, gets transported over hundreds of metres, and finally reduces to 20-80 drops per minute at the site of the plant. Bamboo pipes divert perennial springs on the hilltops to the lower reaches by gravity. Channel sections made of bamboo divert water to the plant site where it is distributed into branches. If the pipes pass a road, they are taken high above the land. The flow is controlled by manipulating pipe positions. The last channel section drops water near the roots of the plant.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is primitive subsistence farming?
question_hinglish: Primitive subsistence farming kya hai?
answer_english: Primitive subsistence farming is practised in a few pockets of India on small patches of land, using primitive tools like hoe, dao and digging sticks and family or community labour. It depends on the monsoon, natural soil fertility and suitable environmental conditions. It is 'slash and burn' agriculture: farmers clear a patch, grow cereals and food crops for their family, and shift to a fresh patch when fertility declines, letting nature restore it. Productivity is low as no fertilisers or modern inputs are used.
answer_hinglish: Primitive subsistence farming India ke kuch hisson mein zameen ke chhote tukdon pe kudaal, dao aur khodne ki lakdi jaise purane auzaaron aur parivaar ya samudaay ki mehnat se hoti hai. Yeh monsoon, mitti ki prakritik upjaau shakti aur anukool maahaul pe nirbhar hai. Yeh 'slash and burn' kheti hai: kisan zameen saaf karke parivaar ke liye anaaj ugaata hai, aur upjaau shakti ghatne pe nayi zameen pe chala jaata hai, taaki prakriti use phir upjaau banaye. Fertilisers ya modern saamaan na hone se utpaadakta kam hoti hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is intensive subsistence farming?
question_hinglish: Intensive subsistence farming kya hai?
answer_english: Intensive subsistence farming is practised where there is high population pressure on land. It is labour-intensive, using high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation for higher production. The right of inheritance has divided land into uneconomical holdings, but with no alternative livelihood, farmers try to take maximum output from limited land, creating enormous pressure on agricultural land.
answer_hinglish: Intensive subsistence farming wahan hoti hai jahan zameen pe aabaadi ka bahut dabaav hai. Yeh mehnat wali kheti hai jisme zyada utpaadan ke liye bahut biochemical saamaan aur sinchaai use hoti hai. Virasat ke haq se zameen chhote, ghaate wale tukdon mein bat gayi, par rozi ka koi aur zariya na hone se kisan seemit zameen se zyada se zyada utpaadan lene ki koshish karte hain, jisse kheti ki zameen pe bahut dabaav hai.
ncert_context: Intensive subsistence farming is practised in areas of high population pressure on land. It is labour-intensive farming, where high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation are used for obtaining higher production. Though the 'right of inheritance' leading to division of land among successive generations has rendered land-holding size uneconomical, farmers continue to take maximum output from the limited land in the absence of alternative sources of livelihood. Thus, there is enormous pressure on agricultural land.

Intent Type: explain_concept
Answer the question in English using only the given context.

Intensive subsistence farming is practised where there is high population pressure on land. It is labour-intensive, using high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation for higher production. The right of inheritance has divided land into uneconomical holdings, but with no alternative livelihood, farmers try to take maximum output from limited land, creating enormous pressure on agricultural land.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is plantation agriculture, and why is transport important for it?
question_hinglish: Plantation kheti kya hai, aur iske liye transport kyun zaroori hai?
answer_english: Plantation is a type of commercial farming in which a single crop is grown on a large area. It is an interface of agriculture and industry, covering large tracts using capital-intensive inputs and migrant labour, and all produce is used as raw material in industries. In India, tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane and banana are important plantation crops, like tea in Assam and North Bengal and coffee in Karnataka. Since production is for the market, a good transport and communication network linking plantations, processing industries and markets is essential.

India mein chaay, coffee, rubber, ganna aur kela mukhya plantation fasalein hain, jaise Assam aur North Bengal mein chaay aur Karnataka mein coffee. Utpaadan market ke liye hone se plantations, processing udyogon aur markets ko jodne wala achha transport aur sanchaar network zaroori hai.

question_english: Differentiate between rabi, kharif and zaid crops.

answer_english: Rabi crops are sown in winter (October to December) and harvested in summer (April to June), such as wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard. Kharif crops are grown with the onset of monsoon and harvested in September-October, such as paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, tur, moong, urad, cotton, jute, groundnut and soyabean. subject: Social Science
question_english: What are millets, and where are jowar, bajra and ragi grown?
question_hinglish: Millets kya hain, aur jowar, bajra aur ragi kahan ugte hain?
answer_english: Jowar, bajra and ragi are important millets; though called coarse grains, they are highly nutritious, and ragi is rich in iron, calcium, micronutrients and roughage. Jowar, the third most important food crop by area and production, is rain-fed and grown mainly in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. Bajra grows on sandy and shallow black soils in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Haryana. Ragi, a dry-region crop, grows in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Jharkhand and Arunachal Pradesh.
answer_hinglish: Jowar, bajra aur ragi mukhya millets hain; inhe mota anaaj kehte hain par yeh bahut poshtik hain, aur ragi iron, calcium, sookshm poshak tatvon aur fibre se bharpoor hai. Jowar, kshetra aur utpaadan mein teesri sabse important khaadya fasal, baarish pe nirbhar hai aur mukhya roop se Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh aur Madhya Pradesh mein ugta hai. Bajra retili aur patli kaali mitti pe Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat aur Haryana mein ugta hai. Sookhe ilaakon ki fasal ragi Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Jharkhand aur Arunachal Pradesh mein ugti hai.
ncert_context: Jowar, bajra and ragi are the important millets grown in India. Though known as coarse grains, they have very high nutritional value; ragi is very rich in iron, calcium, other micro nutrients and roughage. Jowar is the third most important food crop with respect to area and production. It is a rain-fed crop mostly grown in moist areas which hardly needs irrigation. Major jowar producing states are Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. Bajra grows well on sandy soils and shallow black soil; major states are Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Haryana. Ragi is a crop of dry regions growing on red, black, sandy, loamy and shallow black soils; major states are Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Jharkhand and Arunachal Pradesh.

question_english: What are the growing conditions for sugarcane, and where is it produced?
question_hinglish: Ganne ki ugne ki paristhitiyan kya hain, aur yeh kahan paida hota hai?
answer_english: Sugarcane is a tropical and subtropical crop needing hot, humid climate with 21°C to 27°C and 75 to 100 cm of annual rainfall, with irrigation in low-rainfall areas. It grows on many soils, needs manual labour from sowing to harvesting and takes almost a year to grow. India is the second largest producer after Brazil; it is the main source of sugar, gur, khandsari and molasses. Major producers are Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Punjab and Haryana.

India Brazil ke baad doosra sabse bada utpaadak hai; yeh cheeni, gur, khandsari aur sheere ka mukhya srot hai. question_english: Which oilseeds are grown in India, and what are their seasons and uses?
question_hinglish: India mein kaun se tilhan ugte hain, aur unke season aur upyog kya hain?
answer_english: Oilseeds cover about 12 per cent of India's total cropped area. Main ones are groundnut, mustard, coconut, sesamum (til), soyabean, castor seeds, cotton seeds, linseed and sunflower; most are edible cooking mediums, and some are used for soap, cosmetics and ointments. Linseed and mustard are rabi crops, sesamum is kharif in the north and rabi in the south, and castor is grown in both.

question_english: Why were technological and institutional reforms needed in Indian agriculture?

question_english: Enlist the institutional reform programmes introduced by the government in the interest of farmers.
question_hinglish: Kisaanon ke hit mein sarkar ke laaye institutional sudhaar programmes ki list banao.
answer_english: After Independence, priority was given to collectivisation, consolidation of holdings, cooperation and abolition of zamindari, with land reform the main focus of the First Five Year Plan. In the 1960s-70s came the Green Revolution and White Revolution (Operation Flood). The 1980s-90s land development programme included crop insurance against drought, flood, cyclone, fire and disease, Grameen banks, cooperative societies and banks offering low-interest loans. Other schemes include the Kisan Credit Card, Personal Accident Insurance Scheme, weather bulletins and farm programmes on radio and TV, and minimum support prices.
answer_hinglish: Azaadi ke baad samoohikaran, zameen ki chakbandi, sahkaarita aur zamindari khatam karne ko praathmikta di gayi, aur First Five Year Plan ka mukhya focus land reform tha. 1960s-70s mein Green Revolution aur White Revolution (Operation Flood) aaye. 1980s-90s ke land development programme mein sookha, baadh, toofaan, aag aur bimaari ke khilaaf fasal beema, Grameen banks, sahkaari samitiyan aur kam byaaj pe karz dene wale banks the. Kisan Credit Card, Personal Accident Insurance Scheme, radio aur TV pe mausam bulletins aur kheti programmes, aur minimum support price bhi hain.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the Bhoodan-Gramdan movement?
question_hinglish: Bhoodan-Gramdan andolan kya tha?
answer_english: Vinoba Bhave, whom Gandhi declared his spiritual heir, undertook a padyatra across India after Gandhi's death. At Pochampally in Telangana, landless villagers asked for land; when he promised to talk to the government if they farmed cooperatively, Shri Ram Chandra Reddy offered 80 acres to be distributed among 80 landless villagers, an act called 'Bhoodan'. Later some zamindars offered whole villages to the landless, called 'Gramdan'. Some landowners gave land fearing the land ceiling act. It is also called the Bloodless Revolution.
answer_hinglish: Gandhi ne Vinoba Bhave ko apna aadhyatmik uttaradhikaari kaha tha, aur Gandhi ki maut ke baad Vinoba ne desh bhar mein padyatra ki. Telangana ke Pochampally mein bhoomiheen gaon waalon ne zameen maangi; jab Vinoba ne kaha ki agar woh sahkaari kheti karein toh woh sarkar se baat karenge, toh Shri Ram Chandra Reddy ne 80 bhoomiheenon mein baantne ke liye 80 acre zameen di, jise 'Bhoodan' kaha gaya. Baad mein kuch zamindaron ne poore gaon bhoomiheenon ko diye, jise 'Gramdan' kaha gaya. Kuch zameendaaron ne land ceiling act ke dar se zameen di. Ise Bloodless Revolution bhi kehte hain.
ncert_context: Mahatma Gandhi declared Vinoba Bhave as his spiritual heir. He participated in Satyagraha and was a votary of Gandhi's concept of gram swarajya. After Gandhiji's martyrdom, Vinoba Bhave undertook padyatra across almost the entire country. At Pochampally in Telangana, poor landless villagers demanded land. Vinoba assured them he would talk to the Government if they undertook cooperative farming. Shri Ram Chandra Reddy offered 80 acres of land to be distributed among 80 landless villagers; this was known as 'Bhoodan'. Some zamindars, owners of many villages, offered to distribute some villages among the landless, known as Gramdan. Many land-owners gave part of their land due to fear of the land ceiling act. The Bhoodan-Gramdan movement is also known as the Blood-less Revolution.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why are minerals important in our lives?
question_hinglish: Hamari zindagi mein minerals important kyun hain?
answer_english: Almost everything we use, from a pin to a building or ship, is made from minerals, including railway lines, road tarmac, implements and machinery. Cars, buses, trains and aeroplanes are made from minerals and run on power from the earth, and even our food contains minerals. Life processes cannot occur without minerals: though they are only about 0.3 per cent of our nutrient intake, without them we could not use the other 99.7 per cent of food.

Minerals ke bina jeevan prakriyayein nahi chal sakti: yeh hamare poshak tatvon ka sirf lagbhag 0.3 percent hain, par inke bina hum baaki 99.7 percent khaana use nahi kar paate.

question_english: Which minerals are used in making toothpaste?

question_english: What is an ore, and what determines the cost of mining it?
question_hinglish: Ore kya hai, aur use nikaalne ki laagat kis pe nirbhar karti hai?

subject: Social Science
question_english: How are minerals formed in igneous and metamorphic rocks?
question_hinglish: Igneous aur metamorphic chattaanon mein minerals kaise bante hain?
answer_english: In igneous and metamorphic rocks, minerals occur in cracks, crevices, faults or joints. Smaller occurrences are called veins and larger ones lodes. They usually form when minerals in liquid, molten or gaseous form are forced upward through cavities towards the earth's surface, cooling and solidifying as they rise. Major metallic minerals like tin, copper, zinc and lead come from veins and lodes.

Tin, copper, zinc aur lead jaise mukhya dhaatu minerals veins aur lodes se milte hain.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the different modes of occurrence of minerals?
question_hinglish: Minerals ke milne ke alag-alag tareeke kaun se hain?
answer_english: (i) In igneous and metamorphic rocks, in veins and lodes, like tin, copper, zinc and lead. (ii) In sedimentary rocks, in beds or layers, like coal and some iron ore formed under heat and pressure, and gypsum, potash salt and sodium salt formed by evaporation in arid regions. (iii) By decomposition of surface rocks leaving residual ores, like bauxite. (iv) As placer deposits in valley sands, like gold, silver, tin and platinum. (v) In ocean waters and beds, like common salt, magnesium, bromine and manganese nodules.
answer_hinglish: (i) Igneous aur metamorphic chattaanon mein veins aur lodes mein, jaise tin, copper, zinc aur lead. (ii) Sedimentary chattaanon mein parton mein, jaise garmi aur dabaav se bane koyla aur kuch iron ore, aur sookhe ilaakon mein bhaap banne se bane gypsum, potash aur sodium namak. (iii) Sataha ki chattaanon ke tootne se bache ores, jaise bauxite. (iv) Ghaati ki ret mein placer deposits, jaise sona, chaandi, tin aur platinum. (v) Samudr ke paani aur tal mein, jaise namak, magnesium, bromine aur manganese nodules.
ncert_context: Minerals generally occur in these forms: (i) In igneous and metamorphic rocks in cracks, crevices, faults or joints, as veins and lodes; tin, copper, zinc and lead come from these. (ii) In sedimentary rocks minerals occur in beds or layers; coal and some iron ore concentrated under great heat and pressure; gypsum, potash salt and sodium salt formed by evaporation especially in arid regions. (iii) Decomposition of surface rocks and removal of soluble constituents leaves a residual mass containing ores; bauxite is formed this way. (iv) Alluvial deposits in sands of valley floors and the base of hills, called placer deposits, with gold, silver, tin and platinum. (v) Ocean waters provide common salt, magnesium and bromine; ocean beds are rich in manganese nodules.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How are mineral resources distributed in India?
question_hinglish: India mein mineral resources kaise faile hain?
answer_english: India has fairly rich and varied mineral resources, but they are unevenly distributed. Peninsular rocks contain most reserves of coal, metallic minerals, mica and other non-metallic minerals. Sedimentary rocks on the western and eastern flanks of the peninsula, in Gujarat and Assam, have most petroleum deposits. Rajasthan has many non-ferrous minerals, while the alluvial plains of north India are almost devoid of economic minerals, due to differences in geological structure, processes and time.
answer_hinglish: India mein kaafi samriddh aur vividh minerals hain, par yeh asamaan roop se faile hain. Prayadweepiya chattaanon mein koyla, dhaatu minerals, mica aur doosre adhaatu minerals ke zyadatar bhandaar hain. Prayadweep ke pashchimi aur poorvi kinaaron ki sedimentary chattaanon, Gujarat aur Assam mein, zyadatar petroleum hai. Rajasthan mein kai non-ferrous minerals hain, jabki north India ke alluvial maidaanon mein lagbhag koi aarthik mineral nahi, kyunki bhaugolik banaavat, prakriyaon aur samay mein fark hai.

These variations exist because of differences in geological structure, processes and time involved in mineral formation.

subject: Social Science
question_english: When does a mineral deposit or reserve turn into a mine?
question_hinglish: Mineral deposit ya reserve kab khadaan banta hai?
answer_english: The concentration of mineral in the ore, the ease of extraction and closeness to the market affect the economic viability of a reserve. When a choice is made among possible options to meet demand, a mineral deposit or reserve turns into a mine.
answer_hinglish: Ore mein mineral ki saandrata, nikaalne ki aasaani aur market se nazdeeki kisi reserve ki aarthik vyavaharyata tay karti hain. Jab demand poori karne ke liye vikalpon mein se chunaav kiya jaata hai, tab mineral deposit ya reserve khadaan ban jaata hai.
ncert_context: Always remember that the concentration of mineral in the ore, the ease of extraction and closeness to the market play an important role in affecting the economic viability of a reserve. question_english: Distinguish between ferrous and non-ferrous minerals.
question_hinglish: Ferrous aur non-ferrous minerals mein fark batao.
answer_english: Ferrous minerals contain iron, such as iron ore and manganese; they account for about three-fourths of the value of metallic mineral production and support metallurgical industries, and India exports substantial quantities. Non-ferrous minerals do not contain iron, such as copper, bauxite, lead, zinc and gold; India's reserves and production of these are not very satisfactory, though they are vital for metallurgical, engineering and electrical industries.

Non-ferrous minerals mein iron nahi hota, jaise copper, bauxite, lead, zinc aur sona; India ke paas inke bhandaar aur utpaadan santoshjanak nahi, par yeh metallurgical, engineering aur electrical udyogon ke liye zaroori hain.

question_english: Compare magnetite and hematite iron ores.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the major iron ore belts of India.
question_hinglish: India ke mukhya iron ore belts ka varnan karo.
answer_english: (1) Odisha-Jharkhand belt: high-grade hematite at Badampahar in Mayurbhanj and Kendujhar, Odisha, and at Gua and Noamundi in Singhbhum, Jharkhand. (2) Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt in Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra: super high-grade hematite in the Bailadila hills of Bastar, exported to Japan and South Korea via Visakhapatnam. (3) Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt in Karnataka, including the 100 per cent export Kudremukh mines, whose ore goes as slurry by pipeline to a port near Mangaluru. (4) Maharashtra-Goa belt, whose ore is exported through Marmagao.
answer_hinglish: (1) Odisha-Jharkhand belt: Odisha ke Mayurbhanj aur Kendujhar ke Badampahar mein aur Jharkhand ke Singhbhum ke Gua aur Noamundi mein badhiya hematite. (2) Chhattisgarh aur Maharashtra ka Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt: Bastar ki Bailadila pahaadiyon mein bahut badhiya hematite, jo Visakhapatnam se Japan aur South Korea export hota hai. (3) Karnataka ka Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt, jisme 100 percent export wali Kudremukh khadaanein hain, jinka ore slurry ke roop mein pipeline se Mangaluru ke paas port jaata hai. (4) Maharashtra-Goa belt, jiska ore Marmagao se export hota hai.
ncert_context: Major iron ore belts: Odisha-Jharkhand belt: high grade hematite in Badampahar mines in Mayurbhanj and Kendujhar districts of Odisha; in Singbhum district of Jharkhand haematite is mined in Gua and Noamundi. Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt in Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra: very high grade hematites in the Bailadila range of Bastar, 14 deposits of super high grade ore, exported to Japan and South Korea via Vishakhapatnam port. Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt in Karnataka: the Kudremukh mines in the Western Ghats are a 100 per cent export unit, among the largest in the world; ore is transported as slurry through a pipeline to a port near Mangaluru. Maharashtra-Goa belt includes Goa and Ratnagiri district; ores are not very high quality but efficiently exploited and exported through Marmagao port.

question_english: Why is aluminium important, and where are India's bauxite deposits found?
question_hinglish: Aluminium important kyun hai, aur India ke bauxite bhandaar kahan hain?
answer_english: Aluminium is obtained from bauxite, a clay-like substance formed by decomposition of rocks rich in aluminium silicates, from which alumina and then aluminium is made. Aluminium is important because it combines the strength of metals like iron with extreme lightness, good conductivity and great malleability. India's bauxite deposits are mainly in the Amarkantak plateau, Maikal hills and the Bilaspur-Katni plateau. Odisha was the largest producer in 2018-19, and the Panchpatmali deposits in Koraput are the most important.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the properties and uses of mica, and where is it found?
question_hinglish: Mica ke gun aur upyog kya hain, aur yeh kahan milta hai?
answer_english: Mica is made of plates or leaves and splits easily into very thin sheets, so thin that a thousand can form a sheet a few centimetres high; it can be clear, black, green, red, yellow or brown. subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the impacts of mining on miners' health and the environment?
question_hinglish: Khanan ka khaniko ki sehat aur paryavaran pe kya asar hota hai?
answer_english: Miners inhale dust and noxious fumes, making them vulnerable to pulmonary diseases, and face constant risks of collapsing mine roofs, inundation and fires in coal mines. Mining contaminates water sources in the region, and dumping of waste and slurry degrades land and soil and increases stream and river pollution. Stricter safety regulations and environmental laws are needed to stop mining becoming a 'killer industry'.
answer_hinglish: Khanik dhool aur zehreeli gas saans mein lete hain, jisse unhe phephdon ki bimaariyan hoti hain, aur koyla khadaanon mein chhat girne, paani bharne aur aag ka khatra hamesha rehta hai. Khanan ilaake ke paani ke srot doshit karta hai, aur kachre aur slurry ko phenkne se zameen aur mitti kharab hoti hai aur naalon aur nadiyon ka pradooshan badhta hai. Khanan ko 'killer industry' banne se rokne ke liye kade suraksha niyam aur paryavaran kanoon zaroori hain.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why do we need to conserve mineral resources, and how can we do it?
question_hinglish: Hume mineral resources kyun bachane chahiye, aur kaise?
answer_english: Workable mineral deposits are only about one per cent of the earth's crust, and they took millions of years to form; replenishment is infinitely slow compared to present consumption, so minerals are finite and non-renewable. Continued extraction raises costs as mining goes deeper and quality falls. Conservation needs planned, sustainable use, improved technologies to use low-grade ores cheaply, recycling of metals, use of scrap metals and substitutes.
answer_hinglish: Kaam layak mineral bhandaar dharti ki parat ka sirf lagbhag ek percent hain aur inhe banne mein laakhon saal lage; inka dobara banna aaj ki khapat ke mukable behad dheema hai, isliye minerals seemit aur non-renewable hain. Lagaataar nikaalne se kharch badhta hai kyunki khanan gehra hota jaata hai aur gunvatta ghat-ti hai. Sanrakshan ke liye yojnaabaddh, sthaayi upyog, kam gunvatta wale ores ko saste mein use karne ki behtar technology, dhaatuon ki recycling, scrap dhaatu aur vikalpon ka use zaroori hai.
ncert_context: The total volume of workable mineral deposits is an insignificant fraction, one per cent of the earth's crust. We are rapidly consuming mineral resources that required millions of years to be created and concentrated. Geological processes of mineral formation are so slow that rates of replenishment are infinitely small compared to present rates of consumption. Mineral resources are therefore finite and non-renewable. Continued extraction of ores leads to increasing costs as extraction comes from greater depths along with decrease in quality. A concerted effort is needed to use mineral resources in a planned and sustainable manner. Improved technologies need to be evolved to allow use of low grade ores at low costs. Recycling of metals, using scrap metals and other substitutes are steps in conserving minerals.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is the use of firewood and cattle dung cake in rural India becoming difficult and discouraged?
question_hinglish: Gaon mein lakdi aur gobar ke uplon ka use mushkil aur hatotsahit kyun ho raha hai?
answer_english: Firewood and cattle dung cake meet more than 70 per cent of the energy needs of rural households. But continuing this is increasingly difficult because forest area is decreasing, and using dung cake is discouraged because it burns valuable manure that could be used in agriculture.

ncert_context: Firewood and cattle dung cake are most common in rural India. According to one estimate more than 70 per cent energy requirement in rural households is met by these two; continuation of these is increasingly becoming difficult due to decreasing forest area. Moreover, using dung cake too is being discouraged because it consumes most valuable manure which could be used in agriculture.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the distribution of coal in India.
question_hinglish: India mein koyle ke failaav ka varnan karo.
answer_english: Coal is India's most abundant fossil fuel. It occurs in two geological ages: Gondwana, a little over 200 million years old, and tertiary deposits about 55 million years old. Major Gondwana metallurgical coal is in the Damodar valley (West Bengal-Jharkhand), with Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro the important coalfields; the Godavari, Mahanadi, Son and Wardha valleys also have coal. Tertiary coal occurs in Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland. Since coal is bulky and loses weight on use, heavy industries and thermal power stations are located on or near coalfields.

Tertiary koyla Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh aur Nagaland mein hai. Koyla bhaari hota hai aur use pe raakh bankar wazan khota hai, isliye bhaari udyog aur thermal power stations koyla kshetron ke paas lagte hain.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How does petroleum occur, and where is it produced in India?
question_hinglish: Petroleum kaise milta hai, aur India mein yeh kahan paida hota hai?
answer_english: Petroleum, India's next major energy source after coal, provides fuel, lubricants and raw materials, and refineries are a 'nodal industry' for synthetic textiles, fertilisers and chemicals. Most Indian petroleum is associated with anticlines and fault traps in tertiary rocks: oil is trapped in the crest of upfolds in porous limestone or sandstone, held by non-porous layers, with gas above the oil. Major areas are Mumbai High, Gujarat and Assam; Ankeleshwar is Gujarat's key field, and Assam, the oldest oil state, has Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran-Hugrijan.
answer_hinglish: Petroleum, koyle ke baad India ka doosra bada urja srot, indhan, chikanai aur kachcha maal deta hai, aur refineries synthetic kapde, fertiliser aur chemicals ke liye 'nodal industry' hain. India ka zyadatar petroleum tertiary chattaanon ke anticlines aur fault traps se juda hai: tel upar mude hisse ki choti mein chhed wale limestone ya sandstone mein phansa hota hai, bina chhed wali parton se ruka hota hai, aur gas tel ke upar hoti hai. Mukhya ilaake Mumbai High, Gujarat aur Assam hain; Ankeleshwar Gujarat ka mukhya kshetra hai, aur sabse purane tel state Assam mein Digboi, Naharkatiya aur Moran-Hugrijan hain.
ncert_context: Petroleum or mineral oil is the next major energy source in India after coal. It provides fuel for heat and lighting, lubricants for machinery and raw materials for manufacturing industries. Refineries act as a 'nodal industry' for synthetic textile, fertiliser and chemical industries. Most petroleum occurrences in India are associated with anticlines and fault traps in rock formations of the tertiary age. In regions of folding, oil is trapped in the crest of the upfold. The oil bearing layer is porous limestone or sandstone; non-porous layers prevent oil rising or sinking. Gas, being lighter, usually occurs above the oil. Mumbai High, Gujarat and Assam are major petroleum production areas. Ankeleshwar is the most important field of Gujarat. Assam is the oldest oil producing state; Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran-Hugrijan are important fields.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the uses of natural gas, and how has India's gas infrastructure expanded?
question_hinglish: Natural gas ke upyog kya hain, aur India ka gas infrastructure kaise badha?
answer_english: Natural gas, found with petroleum, is used as domestic and industrial fuel, in power generation, industrial heating, as raw material for chemical, petrochemical and fertiliser industries, as transport fuel (CNG) and cooking fuel (PNG). Major reserves are in Mumbai High and the west coast, the Cambay basin, and the Krishna-Godavari basin on the east coast. GAIL's 1,700 km Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur pipeline linked Mumbai High and Bassein fields to industries in western and northern India, and pipelines have expanded to 18,500 km and are expected to exceed 34,000 km as a national Gas Grid.
answer_hinglish: Petroleum ke saath milne wali natural gas ghar aur udyog ke indhan, bijli banane, udyogon mein garmi, chemical, petrochemical aur fertiliser udyogon ke kachche maal, transport indhan (CNG) aur khaana pakane ke indhan (PNG) mein use hoti hai. Mukhya bhandaar Mumbai High aur pashchimi tat, Cambay basin, aur poorvi tat ke Krishna-Godavari basin mein hain. GAIL ki 1,700 km Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur pipeline ne Mumbai High aur Bassein ko western aur northern India ke udyogon se joda, aur pipelines 18,500 km tak badhi aur national Gas Grid ke roop mein 34,000 km se zyada hone ki ummeed hai.
ncert_context: Natural gas is found with petroleum deposits. It is used as a domestic and industrial fuel, as fuel in the power sector, for heating in industries, as raw material in chemical, petrochemical and fertilizer industries, as transport fuel and cooking fuel. With city gas distribution networks, natural gas is emerging as a preferred transport fuel (CNG) and cooking fuel (PNG). India's major gas reserves are in Mumbai High and allied fields along the west coast, supplemented by finds in the Cambay basin. Along the East Coast, reserves were discovered in the Krishna-Godavari basin. The first 1,700 km Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) pipeline by GAIL linked Mumbai High and Bassein gas fields with fertilizer, power and industrial complexes in western and northern India. India's gas infrastructure has expanded from 1,700 km to 18,500 km and is expected to reach over 34,000 km as Gas Grid.

question_english: Why is there a pressing need to use non-conventional energy sources in India?
question_hinglish: India mein non-conventional urja srot use karne ki tatkaal zaroorat kyun hai?
answer_english: Growing energy consumption has made India increasingly dependent on fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas. Rising prices and potential shortages of oil and gas create uncertainty about future energy security, with serious effects on economic growth, and increasing fossil fuel use causes serious environmental problems. So India needs renewable sources like solar, wind, tide, biomass and energy from waste. India is blessed with abundant sunlight, water, wind and biomass and has the largest programmes for developing renewable energy.

Isliye solar, wind, tide, biomass aur kachre se urja jaise renewable srot chahiye. India mein bharpoor dhoop, paani, hawa aur biomass hai aur renewable urja ke sabse bade programmes hain.

question_english: How is nuclear energy produced, and where are its raw materials found in India?
question_hinglish: Nuclear urja kaise banti hai, aur India mein iska kachcha maal kahan milta hai?
answer_english: Nuclear or atomic energy is obtained by altering the structure of atoms, which releases a lot of energy as heat that is used to generate electricity. question_english: Why does solar energy have a bright future in India?
question_hinglish: India mein solar urja ka bhavishya ujjwal kyun hai?
answer_english: India is a tropical country with enormous potential for tapping solar energy. Big solar plants being set up will reduce rural households' dependence on firewood and dung cakes, helping environmental conservation and saving manure for agriculture.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is biogas, and what are the benefits of gobar gas plants?
question_hinglish: Biogas kya hai, aur gobar gas plants ke kya fayde hain?
answer_english: Biogas is produced from shrubs, farm waste and animal and human waste for rural domestic use; decomposition of organic matter yields a gas with higher thermal efficiency than kerosene, dung cake and charcoal. Plants are set up at municipal, cooperative and individual levels, and those using cattle dung are called gobar gas plants. They give farmers twin benefits, energy and better-quality manure, making biogas the most efficient use of cattle dung and preventing loss of trees and manure from burning firewood and dung cakes.
answer_hinglish: Biogas jhaadiyon, khet ke kachre aur jaanwar aur insaani mal se gaon mein gharelu use ke liye banti hai; organic padarth ke sadne se nikalne wali gas kerosene, uple aur lakdi ke koyle se zyada garmi deti hai. Plants municipal, sahkaari aur vyaktigat level pe lagte hain, aur gobar wale plants gobar gas plants kehlate hain. Yeh kisaanon ko do fayde dete hain, urja aur behtar khaad, isliye biogas gobar ka sabse achha upyog hai aur lakdi aur uple jalane se pedon aur khaad ka nuksaan rokta hai.
ncert_context: Shrubs, farm waste, animal and human waste are used to produce biogas for domestic consumption in rural areas. Decomposition of organic matter yields gas, which has higher thermal efficiency in comparison to kerosene, dung cake and charcoal. Biogas plants are set up at municipal, cooperative and individual levels. The plants using cattle dung are known as 'Gobar gas plants' in rural India. These provide twin benefits to the farmer in the form of energy and improved quality of manure. Biogas is by far the most efficient use of cattle dung. It improves the quality of manure and prevents the loss of trees and manure due to burning of fuel wood and cow dung cakes.

question_english: How is tidal energy generated, and where are suitable sites in India?

question_english: What is geothermal energy, and where has India set up projects to harness it?
question_hinglish: Geothermal urja kya hai, aur India ne ise use karne ke projects kahan lagaye hain?
answer_english: Geothermal energy is heat and electricity produced from the earth's interior heat, which exists because the earth grows hotter with depth. Where the geothermal gradient is high, groundwater absorbs heat from rocks and becomes so hot that it turns into steam on rising, which drives turbines. India has several hundred hot springs, and two experimental projects are in the Parvati valley near Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh and the Puga Valley in Ladakh.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is conservation of energy resources necessary, and how can citizens help?
question_hinglish: Urja resources ka sanrakshan kyun zaroori hai, aur nagrik kaise madad kar sakte hain?
answer_english: Energy is a basic requirement for development, needed by agriculture, industry, transport, commerce and households, and consumption has been steadily rising since Independence. So a sustainable path of energy development is needed, based on promoting energy conservation and increased use of renewables. India is among the least energy-efficient countries, so citizens can use public transport, switch off electricity when not in use, use power-saving devices and non-conventional sources, because 'energy saved is energy produced'.
answer_hinglish: Urja vikaas ki mool zaroorat hai, jo kheti, udyog, transport, vyaapaar aur gharon sabko chahiye, aur azaadi ke baad se khapat lagaataar badhi hai. Isliye sthaayi urja vikaas chahiye, jiske do aadhaar hain urja sanrakshan aur renewable srot ka zyada use. India duniya ke sabse kam urja-kushal deshon mein hai, isliye nagrik public transport use kar sakte hain, zaroorat na ho toh bijli band kar sakte hain, bijli bachane wale upkaran aur non-conventional srot use kar sakte hain, kyunki 'bachaayi urja hi banaayi urja hai'.
ncert_context: Energy is a basic requirement for economic development. Every sector of the national economy—agriculture, industry, transport, commercial and domestic—needs energy. As concerned citizens we can use public transport instead of individual vehicles, switch off electricity when not in use, use power-saving devices and non-conventional sources of energy. 'Energy saved is energy produced'.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is the manufacturing sector considered the backbone of development?
question_hinglish: Manufacturing sector ko vikaas ki reedh ki haddi kyun maana jaata hai?
answer_english: Manufacturing modernises agriculture and reduces people's heavy dependence on farm income by providing jobs in secondary and tertiary sectors. Industrial development helps eradicate unemployment and poverty, which was the philosophy behind public and joint sector industries and setting up industries in tribal and backward areas to reduce regional disparities. Export of manufactured goods expands trade and earns foreign exchange, and countries that turn raw materials into higher-value finished goods are prosperous.
answer_hinglish: Manufacturing kheti ko aadhunik banata hai aur secondary aur tertiary sectors mein naukri dekar kheti ki aamdani pe logon ki bhaari nirbharta ghatata hai. Taiyaar saamaan ka export vyapaar badhata aur videshi mudra laata hai, aur jo desh kachche maal ko keemti taiyaar saamaan banate hain woh samriddh hote hain.

question_english: How do agriculture and industry move hand in hand?
question_hinglish: Kheti aur udyog saath-saath kaise chalte hain?
answer_english: Agriculture and industry are not exclusive of each other. Agro-industries have given a major boost to agriculture by raising productivity: they depend on agriculture for raw materials and sell products like irrigation pumps, fertilisers, insecticides, pesticides, plastic and PVC pipes, machines and tools to farmers.
