subject: Social Science
question_english: How are industries classified?
question_hinglish: Udyogon ko kaise baanta jaata hai?
answer_english: By source of raw material: agro-based (cotton, woollen, jute, silk, rubber, sugar, tea, coffee, edible oil) and mineral-based (iron and steel, cement, aluminium, machine tools, petrochemicals). By main role: basic or key industries (iron and steel, copper and aluminium smelting) and consumer industries (sugar, toothpaste, paper, sewing machines, fans). By capital investment: small scale industries with maximum investment of one crore rupees. By ownership: public, private, joint and cooperative sector. By bulk and weight: heavy and light industries.
answer_hinglish: Kachche maal ke srot se: agro-based (cotton, oon, jute, resham, rubber, cheeni, chaay, coffee, khaane ka tel) aur mineral-based (iron aur steel, cement, aluminium, machine tools, petrochemicals). Mukhya bhoomika se: basic ya key udyog (iron aur steel, copper aur aluminium smelting) aur consumer udyog (cheeni, toothpaste, kaagaz, silai machine, pankhe). Poonji nivesh se: ek crore rupaye tak ke nivesh wale small scale udyog. Maalikane se: public, private, joint aur cooperative sector. Wazan aur bulk se: heavy aur light udyog.
ncert_context: On the basis of source of raw materials: agro based (cotton, woollen, jute, silk textile, rubber, sugar, tea, coffee, edible oil) and mineral based (iron and steel, cement, aluminium, machine tools, petrochemicals). According to their main role: basic or key industries supply products as raw materials to manufacture other goods, e.g. iron and steel, copper smelting, aluminium smelting; consumer industries produce goods for direct use, like sugar, toothpaste, paper, sewing machines, fans. On the basis of capital investment: a small scale industry is defined by maximum investment allowed on assets, at present one crore rupees. On the basis of ownership: public, private, joint and cooperative sector. Based on bulk and weight of raw material and finished goods: heavy industries such as iron and steel, and light industries such as electrical goods.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Distinguish between public, private, joint and cooperative sector industries with examples.
question_hinglish: Public, private, joint aur cooperative sector udyogon mein examples ke saath fark batao.
answer_english: Public sector industries are owned and operated by government agencies, like BHEL and SAIL. Private sector industries are owned and run by individuals or groups, like TISCO, Bajaj Auto and Dabur. Joint sector industries are jointly run by the state and individuals, like Oil India Ltd. Cooperative sector industries are owned and run by producers or suppliers of raw materials, workers or both, who pool resources and share profits or losses, like the sugar industry in Maharashtra and coir industry in Kerala.
answer_hinglish: Public sector udyog sarkari agencies ke maalikane aur sanchaalan mein hote hain, jaise BHEL aur SAIL. Private sector udyog vyakti ya groups chalate hain, jaise TISCO, Bajaj Auto aur Dabur. Joint sector udyog sarkar aur vyakti milkar chalate hain, jaise Oil India Ltd. subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the cotton textile industry develop in India, and why was it localised in Maharashtra and Gujarat?
question_hinglish: India mein cotton kapda udyog kaise viksit hua, aur yeh Maharashtra aur Gujarat mein kyun kendrit hua?
answer_english: In ancient India cotton textiles were made by hand spinning and handloom weaving; power-looms came after the 18th century. Traditional industries suffered under colonial rule as they could not compete with English mill cloth. The first successful mill was set up in Mumbai in 1854, and the two world wars boosted the industry due to British demand. Early on it concentrated in the cotton belt of Maharashtra and Gujarat because of raw cotton, market, transport and ports, labour and moist climate.
answer_hinglish: Praacheen India mein cotton kapde haath ki kataai aur handloom bunaai se bante the; 18th century ke baad power-looms aaye. Colonial raaj mein paramparik udyog England ke mill kapde se mukabla na kar paane se toot gaye. Pehli safal mill 1854 mein Mumbai mein bani, aur do world wars mein British demand se udyog badha. Shuru mein yeh Maharashtra aur Gujarat ke cotton belt mein kendrit hua kyunki wahan raw cotton, market, transport aur port, mazdoor aur nam jalvaayu thi.

question_english: How is the cotton textile industry linked to agriculture and other industries, and how are spinning and weaving organised?
question_hinglish: Cotton kapda udyog kheti aur doosre udyogon se kaise juda hai, aur kataai aur bunaai kaise sangathit hain?

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why are jute mills concentrated in the Hugli basin?
question_hinglish: Jute mills Hugli basin mein kendrit kyun hain?
answer_english: India is the largest producer of raw jute and jute goods and the second largest exporter after Bangladesh, with most mills along the Hugli river in West Bengal. Factors include proximity to jute-producing areas, inexpensive water transport supported by railways, roads and waterways, abundant water for processing raw jute, cheap labour from West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh, and Kolkata's banking, insurance and port facilities for exporting jute goods.
answer_hinglish: India kachche jute aur jute saamaan ka sabse bada utpaadak aur Bangladesh ke baad doosra sabse bada exporter hai, aur zyadatar mills West Bengal mein Hugli nadi ke kinaare hain. Kaaranon mein jute ugaane wale ilaakon ki nazdeeki, railways, sadkon aur jalmaargon ke saath sasta jal parivahan, kachcha jute process karne ke liye bharpoor paani, West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha aur Uttar Pradesh se sasta mazdoor, aur jute saamaan export ke liye Kolkata ki banking, insurance aur port suvidhayein hain.
ncert_context: India is the largest producer of raw jute and jute goods and stands second as an exporter after Bangladesh. Most mills are located in West Bengal, mainly along the banks of the Hugli river in a narrow belt. The first jute mill was set up near Kolkata in 1855 at Rishra. After Partition in 1947, the jute mills remained in India but three-fourth of the jute producing area went to Bangladesh. Factors responsible for their location in the Hugli basin are: proximity of jute producing areas, inexpensive water transport supported by a network of railways, roadways and waterways, abundant water for processing raw jute, cheap labour from West Bengal and adjoining Bihar, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh. Kolkata as a large urban centre provides banking, insurance and port facilities for export of jute goods.

question_hinglish: Cheeni udyog cooperative sector ke liye sabse sahi kyun hai?
answer_english: The sugar industry is seasonal, working only during the crushing season, and its raw material, sugarcane, is supplied by many farmers. question_english: Why is iron and steel called a basic and a heavy industry?
question_hinglish: Iron aur steel ko basic aur heavy udyog kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: It is a basic industry because all other industries, heavy, medium and light, depend on it for machinery, and steel is needed for engineering goods, construction, defence, medical, telephonic and scientific equipment and consumer goods; steel production and consumption is regarded as an index of development. answer_hinglish: Yeh basic udyog hai kyunki saare heavy, medium aur light udyog machinery ke liye is pe nirbhar hain, aur steel engineering saamaan, nirmaan, raksha, medical, telephone aur scientific upkaran aur consumer saamaan ke liye chahiye; steel ka utpaadan aur khapat vikaas ka soochak maana jaata hai. Yeh heavy udyog hai kyunki iska saara kachcha maal aur taiyaar saamaan bhaari aur badi maatra ka hai, jisse transport kharch zyada hota hai.

question_english: Iron ore, coking coal and limestone are required in the ratio of about 4:2:1 for steel making. If a plant uses 700 tonnes of these raw materials in total, how much of each is needed?

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is aluminium smelting important, and what factors decide its location?
question_hinglish: Aluminium smelting important kyun hai, aur iski jagah kin factors se tay hoti hai?
answer_english: Aluminium smelting is India's second most important metallurgical industry. Aluminium is light, corrosion-resistant, a good heat conductor, malleable and strong when mixed with other metals, used for aircraft, utensils and wires, and it substitutes steel, copper, zinc and lead in many industries. Smelters are in Odisha, West Bengal, Kerala, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. Their location depends on regular electricity supply and an assured source of bauxite, a bulky dark reddish rock, at minimum cost.
answer_hinglish: Aluminium smelting India ka doosra sabse important metallurgical udyog hai. Aluminium halka, jang-rodhi, garmi ka achha conductor, lachila aur doosri dhaatuon ke saath milkar mazboot hota hai, jo aircraft, bartan aur taaron mein use hota hai aur kai udyogon mein steel, copper, zinc aur lead ki jagah leta hai. Smelters Odisha, West Bengal, Kerala, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra aur Tamil Nadu mein hain. Inki jagah niyamit bijli supply aur kam kharch pe pakke bauxite, ek bhaari gehre laal rang ki chattaan, pe nirbhar hai.
ncert_context: Aluminium smelting is the second most important metallurgical industry in India. It is light, resistant to corrosion, a good conductor of heat, malleable and becomes strong when mixed with other metals. It is used to manufacture aircraft, utensils and wires. It has gained popularity as a substitute of steel, copper, zinc and lead in a number of industries. Aluminium smelting plants are located in Odisha, West Bengal, Kerala, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. Bauxite, the raw material used in the smelters, is a very bulky, dark reddish coloured rock. question_english: What does the fertilizer industry produce, and where is it located?
question_hinglish: Fertilizer udyog kya banata hai, aur yeh kahan hai?
answer_english: The fertilizer industry produces nitrogenous fertilizers (mainly urea), phosphatic fertilizers, ammonium phosphate (DAP) and complex fertilizers combining nitrogen, phosphate and potash. Potash is entirely imported because India has no commercially usable reserves. The industry expanded after the Green Revolution; Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Kerala produce half of India's fertilizers, with other producers including Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Bihar, Maharashtra, Assam and others.

Green Revolution ke baad udyog faila; Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab aur Kerala aadha utpaadan karte hain, aur Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Bihar, Maharashtra, Assam jaise aur bhi utpaadak hain.

question_english: What does the cement industry need, and why are some plants located in Gujarat?
question_hinglish: Cement udyog ko kya chahiye, aur kuch plants Gujarat mein kyun hain?
answer_english: Cement is essential for building houses, factories, bridges, roads, airports and dams. subject: Social Science
question_english: How do industries pollute the environment?
question_hinglish: Udyog paryavaran ko kaise doshit karte hain?
answer_english: Industries cause air, water, land and noise pollution. Air pollution comes from gases like sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide and particulate matter like dust, mist and smoke from chemical and paper factories, brick kilns, refineries, smelters and fossil fuel burning; toxic gas leaks, like the Bhopal gas tragedy, are very hazardous. Water pollution comes from industrial wastes and effluents with dyes, detergents, acids, salts, heavy metals and chemicals, plus thermal pollution from hot water. Dumping of wastes makes soil useless and contaminates groundwater, and machinery and equipment cause noise pollution.
answer_hinglish: Udyog hawa, paani, zameen aur shor ka pradooshan karte hain. Hawa ka pradooshan sulphur dioxide aur carbon monoxide jaisi gaso aur chemical aur kaagaz factories, eent bhatton, refineries, smelters aur fossil fuel jalane se nikalne wali dhool, dhund aur dhuen se hota hai; Bhopal gas kaand jaisi zehreeli gas leak bahut khatarnaak hain. Paani ka pradooshan rang, detergent, acid, namak, bhaari dhaatu aur chemicals wale industrial kachre aur garm paani ke thermal pradooshan se hota hai. Kachra phenkne se mitti bekaar hoti aur bhoojal doshit hota hai, aur machines shor pradooshan karti hain.
ncert_context: Industries are responsible for four types of pollution: air, water, land and noise. Air pollution is caused by undesirable gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide, and airborne particulate materials like dust, sprays, mist and smoke emitted by chemical and paper factories, brick kilns, refineries, smelting plants and burning of fossil fuels. Toxic gas leaks can be very hazardous, as in the Bhopal Gas tragedy. Water pollution is caused by organic and inorganic industrial wastes and effluents discharged into rivers by paper, pulp, chemical, textile and dyeing industries, refineries, tanneries and electroplating, releasing dyes, detergents, acids, salts and heavy metals like lead and mercury. Thermal pollution occurs when hot water is drained into rivers before cooling. Dumping of wastes renders soil useless and contaminates groundwater. Industrial and construction machinery cause noise pollution.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What steps can be taken to minimise environmental degradation by industry?
question_hinglish: Udyog se paryavaran ki giraavat kam karne ke liye kya kadam uthaye ja sakte hain?
answer_english: For water: minimise process water by reusing and recycling it, harvest rainwater, treat hot water before releasing it, treat effluents in primary (mechanical: screening, grinding, flocculation, sedimentation), secondary (biological) and tertiary (biological, chemical and physical, including recycling) phases, and legally regulate groundwater overdrawing. For air: fit smoke stacks with electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers and inertial separators, and use oil or gas instead of coal. For noise: fit generators with silencers, redesign machinery and use noise-absorbing material and earplugs.
answer_hinglish: Paani ke liye: paani ko dobara use aur recycle karke kam lena, baarish ka paani ikattha karna, garm paani chhodne se pehle upchaar karna, gande paani ka primary (mechanical: chhaanna, peesna, flocculation, sedimentation), secondary (biological) aur tertiary (biological, chemical aur physical, recycling samet) upchaar, aur bhoojal ke zyada nikaas pe kanooni rok. Hawa ke liye: chimneys mein electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers aur inertial separators lagaana, aur koyle ki jagah tel ya gas. Shor ke liye: generators mein silencer, machines ka naya design, aur shor sokhne wala material aur earplugs.
ncert_context: Every litre of waste water discharged by industry pollutes eight times the quantity of freshwater. Suggestions: minimising use of water for processing by reusing and recycling it; harvesting rainwater; treating hot water and effluents before releasing them. Treatment of industrial effluents can be done in three phases: primary treatment by mechanical means, involving screening, grinding, flocculation and sedimentation; secondary treatment by biological process; tertiary treatment by biological, chemical and physical processes, involving recycling of wastewater. Overdrawing of ground water by industry needs to be regulated legally. Particulate matter can be reduced by fitting smoke stacks with electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers and inertial separators. Smoke can be reduced by using oil or gas instead of coal. Generators should be fitted with silencers; machinery can be redesigned to reduce noise; noise absorbing material and earplugs may be used.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why are efficient means of transport prerequisites for fast development?
question_hinglish: Tez vikaas ke liye kushal transport kyun zaroori hai?
answer_english: Goods and services do not move from supply locations to demand locations on their own; their movement needs transport, facilitated by traders who bring products to consumers. So a country's pace of development depends on both the production of goods and services and their movement over space. Transport can be over land, water and air.
answer_hinglish: Saamaan aur sevayein supply ki jagah se demand ki jagah apne aap nahi jaati; inke liye transport chahiye, jise vyapaari sambhav karte hain jo utpaad upbhoktaon tak pahunchate hain. Isliye kisi desh ke vikaas ki raftaar saamaan aur sevaon ke utpaadan aur unki aavajahi dono pe nirbhar hai. Transport zameen, paani aur hawa se ho sakta hai.
ncert_context: Goods and services do not move from supply locales to demand locales on their own. The movement of goods and services from supply locations to demand locations necessitates the need for transport. Traders make products come to consumers by transportation. Thus, the pace of development of a country depends upon the production of goods and services as well as their movement over space. Therefore, efficient means of transport are prerequisites for fast development. Movement can be over three domains: land, water and air.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why are transport and communication called the lifelines of a nation and its economy?
question_hinglish: Transport aur communication ko desh aur uski economy ki jeevan-rekha kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: With science and technology, efficient transport has turned the world into a large village, supported by equally developed communication, so transport, communication and trade complement each other. Despite India's size and diversity, railways, airways, waterways, newspapers, radio, TV, cinema and internet have linked it with the world and aided socio-economic progress. Trade from local to international levels adds vitality to the economy, so a dense, efficient transport and communication network is a prerequisite for local, national and global trade.
answer_hinglish: Science aur technology ke saath kushal transport ne, utne hi viksit communication ki madad se, duniya ko ek bada gaon bana diya hai, isliye transport, communication aur vyapaar ek-doosre ke poorak hain. India ke vishaal aakaar aur vividhata ke bawajood railways, airways, waterways, akhbaar, radio, TV, cinema aur internet ne use duniya se joda aur samajik-aarthik pragati mein madad ki. Local se international vyapaar economy ko jaan deta hai, isliye ghana, kushal transport aur communication network local, national aur global vyapaar ke liye zaroori hai.
ncert_context: With development in science and technology, the area of influence of trade and transport expanded far and wide. Today, the world has been converted into a large village with efficient and fast moving transport, with the help of an equally developed communication system. Therefore, transport, communication and trade are complementary to each other. India is well-linked with the world despite its vast size, diversity and plurality. Railways, airways, waterways, newspapers, radio, television, cinema and internet have contributed to its socio-economic progress. Trade from local to international levels has added to the vitality of its economy. Modern means of transport and communication serve as lifelines of our nation and its modern economy. answer_english: India has the second largest road network in the world, about 62.16 lakh km (2020-21). question_english: What is the Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways project?
question_hinglish: Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways project kya hai?
answer_english: It is a major road development project linking Delhi-Kolkata-Chennai-Mumbai and Delhi by six-lane super highways. The North-South corridor linking Srinagar and Kanniyakumari and the East-West corridor connecting Silchar and Porbandar are part of it. Its main objective is to reduce time and distance between India's mega cities, and it is implemented by the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI).

question_english: What is the Atal Tunnel, and why is it important?
question_hinglish: Atal Tunnel kya hai, aur yeh important kyun hai?

subject: Social Science
question_english: Where and why is rail transport most convenient, and where is it difficult?
question_hinglish: Rail transport kahan aur kyun sabse suvidhajanak hai, aur kahan mushkil hai?
answer_english: The railway network is shaped by physiographic, economic and administrative factors. The northern plains, with level land, high population density and rich agriculture, are most favourable, though wide rivers needed bridges. In the peninsular hills, tracks run through low hills, gaps or tunnels. The Himalayas are unfavourable due to high relief, sparse population and few economic opportunities, and it was also difficult to lay lines on the sandy plains of western Rajasthan, swamps of Gujarat, and forests of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand; the Sahyadri could be crossed only through passes.
answer_hinglish: Railway network bhaugolik, aarthik aur prashaasnik factors se bana hai. Northern maidaan, jahan samtal zameen, ghani aabaadi aur samriddh kheti hai, sabse anukool hain, halaanki chaudi nadiyon pe pul banane pade. Prayadweep ki pahaadiyon mein patri neechi pahaadiyon, darron ya surangon se guzarti hai. Himalaya oonchaai, kam aabaadi aur kam aarthik avsaron se pratikool hai, aur western Rajasthan ki ret, Gujarat ke daldal, aur Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha aur Jharkhand ke jungalon mein bhi line bichhaana mushkil tha; Sahyadri sirf ghaaton se paar ho saki.

It was difficult to lay railway lines on the sandy plain of western Rajasthan, swamps of Gujarat, forested tracts of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand. The Sahyadri could be crossed only through gaps or passes (Ghats).

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the advantages of pipeline transport?
question_hinglish: Pipeline transport ke kya fayde hain?
answer_english: Pipelines, once used to carry water to cities and industries, now carry crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas from fields to refineries, fertiliser factories and thermal power plants; solids can also be carried as slurry. Inland refineries like Barauni, Mathura and Panipat and gas-based fertiliser plants became possible only because of pipelines. Though the initial cost is high, running costs are minimal and there are no trans-shipment losses or delays.
answer_hinglish: Pehle shehron aur udyogon tak paani le jaane wali pipelines ab kachcha tel, petroleum utpaad aur natural gas ko kshetron se refineries, fertiliser factories aur thermal power plants tak le jaati hain; thos cheezein bhi slurry banakar bheji ja sakti hain. Barauni, Mathura aur Panipat jaisi door andar ki refineries aur gas-based fertiliser plants pipelines ki wajah se hi sambhav hue. Shuru ka kharch zyada hai par chalane ka kharch bahut kam, aur beech mein maal badalne ka nuksaan ya deri nahi hoti.

Context:
Pipeline transport network is a new arrival on the transportation map of India. In the past, these were used to transport water to cities and industries. Now they transport crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas from oil and gas fields to refineries, fertilizer factories and big thermal power plants. Solids can also be transported through a pipeline when converted into slurry. The far inland locations of refineries like Barauni, Mathura, Panipat and gas based fertilizer plants could be thought of only because of pipelines. Initial cost of laying pipelines is high but subsequent running costs are minimal. It rules out trans-shipment losses or delays.

Question:
Pipeline transport ke kya fayde hain?

Answer the question in Hinglish using only the given context.<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
Pehle shehron aur udyogon tak paani le jaane wali pipelines ab kachcha tel, petroleum utpaad aur natural gas ko kshetron se refineries, fertiliser factories aur thermal power plants tak le jaati hain; thos cheezein bhi slurry banakar bheji ja sakti hain. Barauni, Mathura aur Panipat jaisi door andar ki refineries aur gas-based fertiliser plants pipelines ki wajah se hi sambhav hue. Shuru ka kharch zyada hai par chalane ka kharch bahut kam, aur beech mein maal badalne ka nuksaan ya deri nahi hoti.<end_of_turn>

question_english: What are the three important pipeline networks in India?
question_hinglish: India ke teen mukhya pipeline networks kaun se hain?
answer_english: (1) From the oil field in upper Assam to Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh) via Guwahati, Barauni and Prayagraj, with branches from Barauni to Haldia via Rajbandh, Rajbandh to Maurigram and Guwahati to Siliguri. (2) From Salaya in Gujarat to Jalandhar in Punjab via Viramgam, Mathura, Delhi and Sonipat, with branches to Koyali near Vadodara and Chakshu. (3) The 1,700 km Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline linking Mumbai High and Bassein gas fields with fertiliser, power and industrial complexes in western and northern India.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why was Deendayal Port (Kandla) developed, and what does it serve?
question_hinglish: Deendayal Port (Kandla) kyun viksit kiya gaya, aur yeh kise seva deta hai?
answer_english: Deendayal Port in Kuchchh was the first port developed after Independence to ease the volume of trade on Mumbai port after Karachi port went to Pakistan in Partition. It is a tidal port that handles exports and imports of the productive granary and industrial belt across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Gujarat.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe India's postal network and its mail channels.
question_hinglish: India ke postal network aur uske mail channels ka varnan karo.
answer_english: The Indian postal network is the largest in the world, handling parcels and personal written communication. Cards and envelopes are first-class mail, airlifted between stations over land and air. Second-class mail, like book packets, registered newspapers and periodicals, goes by surface mail over land and water. To speed delivery in large towns and cities, six mail channels have been introduced: Rajdhani, Metro, Green, Business, Bulk Mail and Periodical Channels.
answer_hinglish: India ka postal network duniya mein sabse bada hai, jo parcels aur niji likhit sandesh sambhalta hai. Card aur lifaafe first-class mail hain, jo stations ke beech hawai jahaz se zameen aur hawa dono se jaate hain. Second-class mail, jaise book packets, registered akhbaar aur patrikayein, zameen aur paani ke surface mail se jaati hai. Bade shehron mein jaldi delivery ke liye chhe mail channels shuru hue: Rajdhani, Metro, Green, Business, Bulk Mail aur Periodical Channel.

question_english: What role does mass communication play in India?

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is trade, and how does international trade differ from local trade?
question_hinglish: Vyapaar kya hai, aur international vyapaar local vyapaar se kaise alag hai?
answer_english: Trade is the exchange of goods among people, states and countries, and the market is where it takes place. Local trade is carried on within cities, towns and villages, state-level trade between two or more states, while international trade is trade between two countries through sea, air or land routes. Since resources are space-bound, no country can survive without international trade, and its advancement is an economic barometer of a country.
answer_hinglish: Logon, states aur deshon ke beech saamaan ka lena-dena vyapaar hai, aur market woh jagah hai jahan yeh hota hai. Local vyapaar shehron, kasbon aur gaon ke andar hota hai, state level vyapaar do ya zyada states ke beech, jabki international vyapaar do deshon ke beech samudr, hawa ya zameen ke raaston se hota hai. Kyunki resources jagah se bandhe hain, koi desh international vyapaar ke bina nahi chal sakta, aur iska vikaas desh ki aarthik sthiti ka barometer hai.

Advancement of international trade of a country is an index to its economic prosperity. It is therefore considered the economic barometer for a country. As resources are space bound, no country can survive without international trade.

question_english: What is the balance of trade, and when is it favourable or unfavourable?
question_hinglish: Balance of trade kya hai, aur yeh kab favourable ya unfavourable hota hai?

subject: Social Science
question_english: How does tourism contribute to India, and what schemes promote it?
question_hinglish: Tourism India mein kya yogdaan deta hai, aur kaun si schemes ise badhati hain?
answer_english: Tourism has grown remarkably in two decades through government initiatives, infrastructure and global branding. Schemes like Swadesh Darshan 2.0, the Vibrant Village Programme, PRASHAD and Paryatan Mitra boost it. Tourism promotes national integration, supports local handicrafts and cultural pursuits, and builds international understanding of our culture and heritage. Foreign tourists come for heritage, eco, adventure, cultural, medical and business tourism.
answer_hinglish: Sarkari pahal, infrastructure aur global branding se do dashakon mein tourism bahut badha hai. Swadesh Darshan 2.0, Vibrant Village Programme, PRASHAD aur Paryatan Mitra jaisi schemes ise badhati hain. Tourism national ekta badhata hai, local hastshilp aur saanskritik gatividhiyon ko sahara deta hai, aur hamari sanskriti aur virasat ki international samajh banata hai. Videshi paryatak heritage, eco, adventure, cultural, medical aur business tourism ke liye aate hain.
ncert_context: Tourism in India has grown remarkably over the past two decades, with government initiatives, infrastructure development and global branding contributing. To boost tourism, schemes like Swadesh Darshan 2.0, Vibrant Village Programme, PRASHAD (Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive), Paryatan Mitra, etc. have been started. Tourism also promotes national integration, provides support to local handicrafts and cultural pursuits, and helps in the development of international understanding about our culture and heritage. Foreign tourists visit India for heritage tourism, eco tourism, adventure tourism, cultural tourism, medical tourism and business tourism.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What led to tensions between the Dutch-speaking and French-speaking communities in Belgium?
question_hinglish: Belgium mein Dutch aur French bolne wale samudaayon ke beech tanaav kyun bana?
answer_english: The minority French-speaking community was relatively rich and powerful, which the Dutch-speaking community resented because it got the benefits of economic development and education much later. This led to tensions in the 1950s and 1960s, more acute in Brussels, where Dutch speakers were a majority in the country but a minority in the capital.
answer_hinglish: Alpsankhyak French bolne wala samudaay apekshaakrit ameer aur taakatwar tha, jisse Dutch bolne wala samudaay naraz tha kyunki use economic vikaas aur shiksha ka fayda bahut der se mila. Isse 1950s aur 1960s mein tanaav bana, jo Brussels mein zyada tez tha, kyunki Dutch bolne wale desh mein bahusankhyak par rajdhani mein alpsankhyak the.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the social composition of Sri Lanka.
question_hinglish: Sri Lanka ki samajik banaavat batao.
answer_english: Sri Lanka, an island nation a few kilometres off Tamil Nadu, has about two crore people. The major groups are Sinhala-speakers (74 per cent) and Tamil-speakers (18 per cent). Tamils include Sri Lankan Tamils (13 per cent), natives concentrated in the north and east, and Indian Tamils, whose forefathers came as plantation workers in colonial times. Most Sinhalas are Buddhists, most Tamils are Hindus or Muslims, and about 7 per cent are Christians, both Tamil and Sinhala.
answer_hinglish: Tamil Nadu se kuch kilometre door dweep desh Sri Lanka ki aabaadi lagbhag do crore hai. Mukhya groups Sinhala bolne wale (74 percent) aur Tamil bolne wale (18 percent) hain. Tamilon mein Sri Lankan Tamils (13 percent), jo desh ke mool nivaasi hain aur north aur east mein kendrit hain, aur Indian Tamils hain, jinke purvaj colonial daur mein plantation mazdoor bankar aaye. Zyadatar Sinhala Buddhist, zyadatar Tamil Hindu ya Muslim hain, aur lagbhag 7 percent Christian hain jo Tamil aur Sinhala dono hain.
ncert_context: Sri Lanka is an island nation, just a few kilometres off the southern coast of Tamil Nadu. It has about two crore people. It has a diverse population. The major social groups are the Sinhala-speakers (74 per cent) and the Tamil-speakers (18 per cent). Among Tamils there are two sub-groups. question_english: How did majoritarian policies lead to civil war in Sri Lanka?
question_hinglish: Bahusankhyakvaadi policies se Sri Lanka mein civil war kaise hua?
answer_english: These measures increased the Sri Lankan Tamils' feeling of alienation; they felt the constitution and policies denied them equal political rights, discriminated in jobs and opportunities, and ignored their interests. Tamil parties struggled for recognition of Tamil as an official language, regional autonomy and equal opportunity in education and jobs, but demands for autonomy were repeatedly denied. By the 1980s, organisations demanded an independent Tamil Eelam in the north and east, and the distrust turned into a civil war that killed thousands, created refugees, destroyed livelihoods and ended in 2009.
answer_hinglish: In kadamon se Sri Lankan Tamilon mein alagaav ki bhavna badhi; unhe laga ki constitution aur policies unhe barabar political haq nahi deti, naukriyon aur avsaron mein bhed-bhaav karti hain aur unke hiton ko nazarandaaz karti hain. Tamil parties ne Tamil ko official bhasha, kshetriya swaayattata aur shiksha aur naukri mein barabar avsar ke liye sangharsh kiya, par swaayattata ki maang baar-baar thukrayi gayi. 1980s tak sangathan north aur east mein azaad Tamil Eelam maangne lage, aur avishwaas civil war mein badla jisme hazaaron mare, log sharnaarthi bane, rozi gayi, aur yeh 2009 mein khatam hua.
ncert_context: These government measures gradually increased the feeling of alienation among Sri Lankan Tamils. They felt that none of the major political parties led by Buddhist Sinhala leaders was sensitive to their language and culture, that the constitution and policies denied them equal political rights, discriminated against them in jobs and opportunities and ignored their interests. Relations between Sinhala and Tamil communities strained. Sri Lankan Tamils launched parties and struggles for recognition of Tamil as an official language, regional autonomy and equality of opportunity in education and jobs. Their demand for more autonomy was repeatedly denied. By the 1980s, several organisations demanded an independent Tamil Eelam (state) in northern and eastern Sri Lanka. The distrust turned into widespread conflict and civil war. Thousands were killed, many families became refugees and many lost livelihoods. The civil war ended in 2009.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the main elements of the Belgian model of power sharing?
question_hinglish: Belgium ke power sharing model ke mukhya tatva kya hain?
answer_english: Between 1970 and 1993, Belgium amended its constitution four times. The constitution requires equal numbers of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central government, and some laws need majority support from each language group. Many central powers were given to state governments of the two regions, which are not subordinate to the centre. Brussels has a separate government with equal representation of both communities. A third 'community government', elected by each language community wherever they live, handles cultural, educational and language issues.
answer_hinglish: 1970 aur 1993 ke beech Belgium ne apna constitution chaar baar badla. Constitution central sarkar mein Dutch aur French bolne wale mantriyon ki barabar sankhya zaroori karta hai, aur kuch kanoonon ke liye har bhasha group ke bahumat ka samarthan chahiye. Kendra ki kai shaktiyan dono regions ki state sarkaron ko di gayi, jo kendra ke adheen nahi hain. Brussels ki alag sarkar hai jisme dono samudaayon ko barabar pratinidhitva hai. Teesri 'community government', jise har bhasha samudaay chunta hai chahe woh kahin bhi rahe, saanskritik, shaikshik aur bhasha ke mudde sambhalti hai.
ncert_context: Belgian leaders recognised regional differences and cultural diversities. Between 1970 and 1993, they amended their constitution four times. Constitution prescribes that the number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers shall be equal in the central government. Some special laws require the support of majority of members from each linguistic group, so no single community can make decisions unilaterally. Many powers of the Central Government have been given to State Governments of the two regions, which are not subordinate to the Central Government. Brussels has a separate government in which both communities have equal representation. French-speaking people accepted equal representation in Brussels because the Dutch-speaking community accepted equal representation in the Central Government. A third kind of government, the 'community government', is elected by people belonging to one language community – Dutch, French and German-speaking – no matter where they live, with power regarding cultural, educational and language-related issues.

question_english: What do we learn from the stories of Belgium and Sri Lanka?
question_hinglish: Belgium aur Sri Lanka ki kahaniyon se hum kya seekhte hain?

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the prudential and moral reasons for power sharing?
question_hinglish: Power sharing ke prudential aur moral kaaran kya hain?
answer_english: Prudential reasons stress better outcomes: power sharing reduces the possibility of conflict between social groups, and since social conflict leads to violence and instability, it ensures a stable political order; imposing the majority's will may look attractive in the short run but undermines national unity in the long run. Moral reasons stress power sharing as valuable in itself: it is the very spirit of democracy, as people affected by power have a right to be consulted, and a legitimate government is one where citizens acquire a stake through participation.
answer_hinglish: Prudential kaaran behtar nateejon pe zor dete hain: power sharing samajik groups ke beech sangharsh ki sambhavna ghatata hai, aur kyunki samajik sangharsh se hinsa aur asthirta aati hai, yeh sthir political vyavastha banata hai; bahumat ki marzi thopna thodi der achha lag sakta hai par lambe samay mein desh ki ekta kamzor karta hai. Moral kaaran power sharing ko apne aap mein keemti maante hain: yeh democracy ki aatma hai, kyunki power se prabhavit logon ko salah ka haq hai, aur vaidh sarkar woh hai jisme citizens bhagidaari se system mein hissa paate hain.
ncert_context: Two sets of reasons can be given in favour of power sharing. Firstly, power sharing is good because it helps to reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups. Since social conflict often leads to violence and political instability, power sharing ensures stability of political order. Imposing the will of majority may look attractive in the short run, but in the long run it undermines the unity of the nation. Secondly, power sharing is the very spirit of democracy. Democratic rule involves sharing power with those affected by its exercise. People have a right to be consulted on how they are to be governed. A legitimate government is one where citizens, through participation, acquire a stake in the system. Prudential reasons stress that power sharing brings better outcomes; moral reasons emphasise the act of power sharing as valuable.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did ideas about political power change with the emergence of democracy?
question_hinglish: Democracy ke aane se political power ke baare mein vichaar kaise badle?
answer_english: For a long time it was believed that all government power must reside in one person or group at one place, since dispersed power would prevent quick decisions. With democracy, this changed: people are the source of all political power and rule themselves through institutions of self-government, diverse groups and views are respected, and everyone has a voice in public policy. So political power should be distributed among as many citizens as possible.
answer_hinglish: Lambe samay tak maana gaya ki sarkar ki saari power ek vyakti ya group ke paas ek jagah honi chahiye, kyunki bikhri power se jaldi faisle nahi ho paate. Isliye political power jitne zyada nagrikon mein ho sake utni baanti jaani chahiye.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the different forms of power sharing in modern democracies? Give an example of each.
question_hinglish: Aadhunik democracies mein power sharing ke alag roop kaun se hain? Har ek ka example do.
answer_english: (1) Horizontal distribution among organs of government, legislature, executive and judiciary, creating checks and balances; for example, judges appointed by the executive can check the executive and legislature. (2) Vertical division among governments at different levels, such as the Union and State governments and municipalities and panchayats in India. (3) Sharing among social groups, like Belgium's community government or reserved constituencies in India. (4) Sharing among political parties, pressure groups and movements, as in coalition governments and interest groups influencing decisions.
answer_hinglish: (1) Sarkar ke angon, legislature, executive aur judiciary, mein horizontal bantwara, jisse checks and balances bante hain; jaise executive ke appoint kiye judges executive aur legislature ko jaanch sakte hain. (2) Alag staron ki sarkaron mein vertical bantwara, jaise India mein Union aur State sarkarein aur municipalities aur panchayatein. (3) Samajik groups ke beech, jaise Belgium ki community government ya India ke reserved constituencies. (4) Political parties, pressure groups aur andolanon ke beech, jaise coalition sarkarein aur faislon ko prabhavit karne wale interest groups.
ncert_context: In modern democracies, power sharing arrangements take many forms. 1. Power is shared among different organs of government, such as legislature, executive and judiciary: horizontal distribution of power, a system of checks and balances; although judges are appointed by the executive, they can check the executive or laws made by legislatures. 2. Power can be shared among governments at different levels, a federal government and provincial governments, and lower levels like municipality and panchayat: vertical division of power. 3. Power may be shared among social groups, such as religious and linguistic groups; 'community government' in Belgium and 'reserved constituencies' in India are examples. 4. Power sharing in the way political parties, pressure groups and movements control or influence those in power; coalition governments and interest groups such as traders, farmers and workers share power.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is horizontal distribution of power, and what are checks and balances?
question_hinglish: Horizontal distribution of power kya hai, aur checks and balances kya hain?
answer_english: Horizontal distribution of power is sharing power among organs of government at the same level, the legislature, executive and judiciary, each exercising different powers. This separation ensures no organ has unlimited power and each checks the others, creating a balance of power. For example, ministers are responsible to Parliament or State Assemblies, and judges, though appointed by the executive, can check the executive and laws made by legislatures; this is called checks and balances.
answer_hinglish: Horizontal distribution of power ek hi star pe sarkar ke angon, legislature, executive aur judiciary, mein power baantna hai, jisme har ek alag shaktiyan rakhta hai. Isse koi ang asseem power nahi rakhta aur har ek doosre ko jaanchta hai, jisse power ka santulan banta hai. Jaise mantri Parliament ya State Assemblies ke prati zimmedar hain, aur executive ke appoint kiye judges bhi executive aur legislatures ke kanoonon ko jaanch sakte hain; ise checks and balances kehte hain.
ncert_context: Power is shared among different organs of government, such as the legislature, executive and judiciary. This is horizontal distribution of power because it allows different organs placed at the same level to exercise different powers. Such separation ensures that none of the organs can exercise unlimited power. Each organ checks the others, resulting in a balance of power. In a democracy, even though ministers and officials exercise power, they are responsible to Parliament or State Assemblies. Although judges are appointed by the executive, they can check the functioning of the executive or laws made by legislatures. This arrangement is called a system of checks and balances.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is vertical division of power, or federal division of power?
question_hinglish: Vertical division of power, yaani federal division of power, kya hai?
answer_english: Vertical division of power is sharing power among governments at different levels: a general government for the whole country, called the federal government (in India, the Central or Union Government), and governments at the provincial or regional level (in India, State Governments). Where such levels exist, the constitution clearly lays down their powers; this is federal division of power, used in Belgium but refused in Sri Lanka. It extends to lower levels like municipalities and panchayats.
answer_hinglish: Vertical division of power alag staron ki sarkaron mein power baantna hai: poore desh ki ek general sarkar, jise federal sarkar kehte hain (India mein Central ya Union Government), aur pradeshik ya kshetriya sarkarein (India mein State Governments). Jahan aise star hain, constitution unki shaktiyan saaf tay karta hai; ise federal division of power kehte hain, jo Belgium ne kiya par Sri Lanka ne nahi. Yeh municipalities aur panchayaton jaise neeche ke staron tak jaata hai.
ncert_context: Power can be shared among governments at different levels – a general government for the entire country and governments at the provincial or regional level. The general government is usually called the federal government; in India, the Central or Union Government. Provincial governments in India are called State Governments. Not all countries have them. In countries like ours with different levels, the constitution clearly lays down the powers of different levels. This was done in Belgium but refused in Sri Lanka. This is called federal division of power. The principle extends to levels lower than the State, such as the municipality and panchayat. Division of powers involving higher and lower levels of government is called vertical division of power.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Annette, in a Dutch-medium school in northern Belgium, and Selvi, in a school in northern Sri Lanka, want instruction in French and Tamil respectively. Whose parents are more likely to succeed with their government, and why?
question_hinglish: Northern Belgium ke Dutch-medium school mein Annette aur northern Sri Lanka ke school mein Selvi kramash French aur Tamil mein padhai chahti hain. Kiske maata-pita ki sarkar se maang poori hone ki zyada sambhavna hai, aur kyun?
answer_english: Annette's parents are more likely to succeed. Belgium has community governments, elected by each language community, with power over cultural, educational and language issues, so a French-speaking community's needs can be accommodated. Sri Lanka followed majoritarian policies, making Sinhala the only official language and ignoring Tamil interests, so Selvi's demand is less likely to be met.
answer_hinglish: Annette ke maata-pita ki sambhavna zyada hai. Belgium mein har bhasha samudaay ki chuni community governments hain jinke paas saanskritik, shaikshik aur bhasha muddon ki shakti hai, isliye French bolne walon ki zaroorat poori ho sakti hai. Sri Lanka ne bahusankhyakvaadi policies apnayi, sirf Sinhala ko official bhasha banaya aur Tamil hiton ko nazarandaaz kiya, isliye Selvi ki maang poori hone ki sambhavna kam hai.
ncert_context: In Belgium, the 'community government' is elected by people of one language community—Dutch, French and German-speaking—no matter where they live, with power over cultural, educational and language-related issues. In Sri Lanka, a 1956 Act recognised Sinhala as the only official language, disregarding Tamil, and Tamils felt government policies ignored their interests and denied them equal rights.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Sri Lanka has about two crore people, of whom 74 per cent are Sinhala-speakers and 18 per cent Tamil-speakers, including 13 per cent Sri Lankan Tamils. Roughly how many people are Sinhala-speakers, and how many are Indian Tamils?
question_hinglish: Sri Lanka ki lagbhag do crore aabaadi mein 74 percent Sinhala bolne wale aur 18 percent Tamil bolne wale hain, jinme 13 percent Sri Lankan Tamils hain. Lagbhag kitne log Sinhala bolte hain, aur kitne Indian Tamils hain?
answer_english: Sinhala-speakers = 74% of 2 crore = 1.48 crore. Indian Tamils = Tamil-speakers minus Sri Lankan Tamils = 18% − 13% = 5%, and 5% of 2 crore = 10 lakh.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is federalism?
question_hinglish: Federalism kya hai?
answer_english: Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country. Usually there are two levels: a government for the entire country responsible for a few subjects of common national interest, and governments at the level of provinces or states that look after much of the day-to-day administration. Both levels enjoy their power independently of each other.
answer_hinglish: Federalism sarkar ka aisa system hai jisme power ek central authority aur desh ki alag ghatak ikaiyon mein baanti jaati hai. Aam taur pe do star hote hain: poore desh ki sarkar jo kuch rashtriya hit ke vishayon ki zimmedar hoti hai, aur provinces ya states ki sarkarein jo roz ka zyadatar prashaasan sambhalti hain. Dono star apni power ek-doosre se swatantra roop se rakhte hain.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the main difference between a federal and a unitary form of government? Give an example.
question_hinglish: Federal aur unitary sarkar mein mukhya fark kya hai? Example do.
answer_english: In a unitary system, there is either only one level of government or the sub-units are subordinate to the central government, which can pass orders to provincial or local governments; Sri Lanka is practically unitary. In a federal system, the central government cannot order a state government, which has its own powers for which it is not answerable to the centre, and both are separately answerable to the people. Belgium shifted from unitary to federal in 1993 by giving regional governments constitutional powers.
answer_hinglish: Unitary system mein ya toh sarkar ka ek hi star hota hai ya chhoti ikaiyan central sarkar ke adheen hoti hain, jo provincial ya local sarkaron ko aadesh de sakti hai; Sri Lanka asal mein unitary hai. Federal system mein central sarkar state sarkar ko aadesh nahi de sakti, state ki apni shaktiyan hain jinke liye woh kendra ko jawabdeh nahi, aur dono alag-alag janta ko jawabdeh hain. Belgium 1993 mein regional sarkaron ko constitutional shaktiyan dekar unitary se federal bana.
ncert_context: Under the unitary system, either there is only one level of government or the sub-units are subordinate to the central government. The central government can pass on orders to the provincial or the local government. But in a federal system, the central government cannot order the state government to do something. State government has powers of its own for which it is not answerable to the central government. Both governments are separately answerable to the people. In 1993, Belgium's regional governments were given constitutional powers no longer dependent on the central government; thus Belgium shifted from a unitary to a federal form. Sri Lanka continues to be, for all practical purposes, a unitary system where the national government has all the powers.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the key features of federalism?
question_hinglish: Federalism ki mukhya khaasiyatein kya hain?
answer_english: (1) There are two or more levels of government. (2) Different tiers govern the same citizens, but each has its own jurisdiction in legislation, taxation and administration. (3) Each tier's jurisdiction is specified in the constitution, so its existence and authority are guaranteed. (4) Fundamental provisions cannot be changed unilaterally by one level; changes need both levels' consent. (5) Courts interpret the constitution and act as umpire in disputes between levels. (6) Sources of revenue for each level are clearly specified for financial autonomy. (7) It aims to safeguard national unity while accommodating regional diversity.
answer_hinglish: (1) Sarkar ke do ya zyada star hote hain. (2) Alag star ek hi nagrikon pe shaasan karte hain, par har ek ka kanoon, tax aur prashaasan mein apna adhikaar-kshetra hota hai. (3) Har star ka adhikaar-kshetra constitution mein likha hota hai, isliye uska astitva aur adhikaar surakshit hai. (4) Ek star akele mool provisions nahi badal sakta; dono ki sahmati chahiye. (5) Courts constitution ki vyakhya karti hain aur staron ke vivaad mein umpire banti hain. (6) Har star ki aamdani ke srot saaf tay hain taaki aarthik swaayattata rahe. (7) Iska lakshya desh ki ekta banaye rakhte hue kshetriya vividhata ko jagah dena hai.
ncert_context: Key features of federalism: 1. There are two or more levels (tiers) of government. 2. Different tiers govern the same citizens, but each tier has its own jurisdiction in specific matters of legislation, taxation and administration. 3. The jurisdictions of the respective levels are specified in the constitution, so the existence and authority of each tier is constitutionally guaranteed. 4. Fundamental provisions of the constitution cannot be unilaterally changed by one level; changes require the consent of both levels. 5. Courts have the power to interpret the constitution and the powers of different levels; the highest court acts as an umpire in disputes. 6. Sources of revenue for each level are clearly specified to ensure financial autonomy. 7. The federal system has dual objectives: to safeguard and promote unity of the country while accommodating regional diversity.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Distinguish between 'coming together' and 'holding together' federations.
question_hinglish: 'Coming together' aur 'holding together' federations mein fark batao.
answer_english: In 'coming together' federations, independent States come together on their own to form a bigger unit, pooling sovereignty while retaining identity to increase security; examples are the USA, Switzerland and Australia, where constituent States usually have equal power and are strong relative to the federal government. In 'holding together' federations, a large country divides its power between the constituent States and the national government; examples are India, Spain and Belgium, where the Central Government tends to be more powerful and units may have unequal powers, some with special powers.
answer_hinglish: 'Coming together' federations mein swatantra States apni marzi se milkar bada unit banate hain, suraksha badhane ke liye sampraabhuta jodte hue pehchaan banaye rakhte hain; jaise USA, Switzerland aur Australia, jahan States ki power aam taur pe barabar aur federal sarkar ke mukable mazboot hoti hai. 'Holding together' federations mein ek bada desh apni power States aur rashtriya sarkar mein baant-ta hai; jaise India, Spain aur Belgium, jahan Central Government zyada taakatwar hoti hai aur ikaiyon ki power asamaan ho sakti hai, kuch ko khaas shaktiyan milti hain.
ncert_context: There are two routes through which federations have been formed. The first route involves independent States coming together on their own to form a bigger unit, so that by pooling sovereignty and retaining identity, they can increase their security. These 'coming together' federations include the USA, Switzerland and Australia; all constituent States usually have equal power and are strong vis-à-vis the federal government. The second route is where a large country decides to divide its power between the constituent States and the national government. India, Spain and Belgium are examples of 'holding together' federations. In this category, the Central Government tends to be more powerful vis-à-vis the States. Very often different constituent units have unequal powers; some units are granted special powers.

question_english: What makes India a federal country?
question_hinglish: India ko federal desh kya banata hai?
answer_english: Although the Constitution declared India a 'Union of States' without using the word federation, it is based on federal principles. It originally created two tiers, the Union and State governments, and a third tier of Panchayats and Municipalities was added later, each with separate jurisdiction. It provides a three-fold distribution of legislative powers through the Union, State and Concurrent Lists. The power-sharing arrangement cannot be changed by Parliament alone, courts settle disputes over division of powers, and both levels can raise taxes.

Isne pehle do star banaye, Union aur State sarkarein, aur baad mein Panchayaton aur Municipalities ka teesra star joda, har ek ka alag adhikaar-kshetra hai. Yeh Union, State aur Concurrent Lists se kanoon banane ki shaktiyan teen hisson mein baant-ta hai. Power sharing ko akeli Parliament nahi badal sakti, shaktiyon ke bantwaare ke vivaad courts suljhaati hain, aur dono star tax laga sakte hain.

The sharing of power is basic to the structure of the Constitution and is not easy to change. In case of disputes about division of powers, the High Courts and Supreme Court decide. The Union and State Governments have the power to raise resources by levying taxes.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the Union List, State List and Concurrent List?
question_hinglish: Union List, State List aur Concurrent List kya hain?
answer_english: The Union List has subjects of national importance needing a uniform policy, such as defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency; only the Union Government can legislate on them. The State List has subjects of state and local importance, like police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation; only State Governments can legislate on them. The Concurrent List has subjects of common interest, like education, forest, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession; both can legislate, but if laws conflict, the Union law prevails.
answer_hinglish: Union List mein rashtriya mahatva ke vishay hain jinpe ek jaisi policy chahiye, jaise raksha, videsh maamle, banking, sanchaar aur mudra; inpe sirf Union Government kanoon bana sakti hai. State List mein state aur local mahatva ke vishay hain, jaise police, vyapaar, vaanijya, kheti aur sinchaai; inpe sirf State Governments kanoon bana sakti hain. Concurrent List mein dono ke hit ke vishay hain, jaise shiksha, jungle, trade unions, vivaah, god lena aur uttaradhikaar; dono kanoon bana sakte hain, par takraav mein Union ka kanoon maana jaata hai.
ncert_context: The Constitution provided a three-fold distribution of legislative powers. Union List includes subjects of national importance such as defence of the country, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency, included because we need a uniform policy throughout the country. The Union Government alone can make laws on these. State List contains subjects of State and local importance, such as police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation; the State Governments alone can make laws on these. Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest to both, such as education, forest, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession. Both can make laws on these; if their laws conflict, the law made by the Union Government will prevail.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why do all States in India not have identical powers?
question_hinglish: India mein saare States ki shaktiyan ek jaisi kyun nahi hain?
answer_english: Most 'holding together' federations do not give equal power to their units. In India, States like Assam, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram enjoy special powers under Article 371 due to their peculiar social and historical circumstances, especially for protecting indigenous peoples' land rights, culture and preferential government employment; Indians who are not permanent residents cannot buy land or houses there. Union Territories like Chandigarh, Lakshadweep and Delhi have very little power and are run with special powers of the Central Government.
answer_hinglish: Zyadatar 'holding together' federations apni ikaiyon ko barabar power nahi dete. India mein Assam, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh aur Mizoram jaise States ko unki khaas samajik aur aitihasik paristhitiyon ki wajah se Article 371 ke under khaas shaktiyan hain, khaas kar mool nivaasiyon ke zameen ke haq, sanskriti aur sarkari naukriyon mein tarjeeh ki raksha ke liye; jo Indians wahan ke sthaayi nivaasi nahi woh zameen ya ghar nahi khareed sakte. Chandigarh, Lakshadweep aur Delhi jaise Union Territories ke paas bahut kam power hai aur Central Government khaas shaktiyon se inhe chalati hai.

question_english: How can the power-sharing arrangement between the Union and States be changed?
question_hinglish: Union aur States ke beech power sharing ka intezaam kaise badla ja sakta hai?
answer_english: The sharing of power between the Union and State Governments is basic to the structure of the Constitution and is not easy to change. subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe India's language policy and how it strengthened federalism.
question_hinglish: India ki bhasha neeti batao aur isne federalism ko kaise mazboot kiya.
answer_english: The Constitution gave no language the status of national language. Hindi was identified as the official language, but it is the mother tongue of only a minority of Indians, so there were safeguards for other languages: besides Hindi, 21 other languages are Scheduled Languages, candidates for Central Government exams can use any of them, and States have their own official languages. English for official purposes was to stop in 1965, but after non-Hindi States, especially Tamil Nadu, protested, the Centre agreed to continue English with Hindi. Promoting Hindi does not mean imposing it, and this flexibility helped India avoid Sri Lanka's situation.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How have Centre-State relations changed since 1990?
question_hinglish: 1990 ke baad Kendra-Rajya rishte kaise badle?
answer_english: For a long time, the same party ruled at the Centre and in most States, so States did not exercise their rights as autonomous units, and when a rival party ruled a State, the Centre tried to undermine it, often misusing the Constitution to dismiss State governments. After 1990, regional parties rose in many States and coalition governments began at the Centre, as no single party won a clear Lok Sabha majority. This created a new culture of power sharing and respect for State autonomy, supported by a Supreme Court judgement that made arbitrary dismissal of State governments difficult.
answer_hinglish: Lambe samay tak Kendra aur zyadatar States mein ek hi party ka raaj tha, isliye States ne swaayatt ikaiyon ki tarah apne haq nahi use kiye, aur jab kisi State mein virodhi party aati, Kendra use kamzor karta, aksar constitution ka galat use karke State sarkarein barkhaast karta. 1990 ke baad kai States mein kshetriya parties ubhri aur Kendra mein coalition sarkarein bani, kyunki kisi party ko Lok Sabha mein saaf bahumat nahi mila. Isse power sharing aur State swaayattata ke samman ki nayi sanskriti bani, jise ek bade Supreme Court faisle ne sahara diya jisne State sarkaron ki manmaani barkhaastgi mushkil kar di.
ncert_context: How constitutional arrangements for sharing power work in reality depends on how ruling parties and leaders follow them. For a long time, the same party ruled both at the Centre and in most States, so State Governments did not exercise their rights as autonomous federal units. When the ruling party at the State level was different, the parties at the Centre tried to undermine the States. The Central Government would often misuse the Constitution to dismiss State Governments controlled by rival parties, undermining federalism. This changed significantly after 1990, with the rise of regional parties in many States and the era of coalition governments at the Centre, since no single party got a clear Lok Sabha majority. This led to a new culture of power sharing and respect for State autonomy, supported by a major Supreme Court judgement that made it difficult to dismiss state governments arbitrarily.

question_english: What is decentralisation, and why is it needed in India?
question_hinglish: Vikendrikaran kya hai, aur India mein iski zaroorat kyun hai?
answer_english: Decentralisation is when power is taken from Central and State governments and given to local government. India needs it because a vast country cannot be run through only two tiers: States are as large as European countries (Uttar Pradesh is bigger than Russia in population, Maharashtra about as big as Germany) and internally diverse. Many problems are best settled locally, where people know their problems, have better ideas on spending and management, and can participate directly, building democratic habits and local self-government.

Kai samasyayein local level pe sabse achhe se suljhati hain, jahan log apni samasyayein jaante hain, kharch aur prabandhan ke behtar vichaar rakhte hain aur seedhe hissa le sakte hain, jisse democratic aadatein aur local swashaasan banta hai.

question_english: State the differences between local government before and after the constitutional amendment of 1992.
question_hinglish: 1992 ke constitutional amendment se pehle aur baad local government mein kya fark aaya?

subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the structure of rural local government (panchayati raj).
question_hinglish: Grameen local government (panchayati raj) ka dhaancha batao.
answer_english: Each village or group of villages has a gram panchayat, a council of ward members (panch) and a president (sarpanch) directly elected by the adult population; it is the village's decision-making body and works under the gram sabha, made of all village voters, which meets two or three times a year to approve the budget and review performance. A few gram panchayats form a panchayat samiti, block or mandal, whose members are elected by panchayat members. All panchayat samitis in a district form the zilla parishad, mostly elected, including the district's Lok Sabha members and MLAs, headed by the zilla parishad chairperson.
answer_hinglish: Har gaon ya gaon ke samooh ki gram panchayat hoti hai, jo ward members (panch) aur pradhan (sarpanch) ki parishad hai jinhe saare adult seedhe chunte hain; yeh gaon ki faisla lene wali body hai aur gram sabha ke under kaam karti hai, jisme gaon ke saare voters hain aur jo saal mein do-teen baar budget manzoor karne aur kaam jaanchne milti hai. Kuch gram panchayatein milkar panchayat samiti, block ya mandal banati hain, jiske members panchayat members chunte hain. District ki saari panchayat samitiyan zilla parishad banati hain, jiske zyadatar members chune hote hain, district ke Lok Sabha members aur MLAs bhi shaamil hain, aur iska mukhiya zilla parishad chairperson hai.
ncert_context: Rural local government is popularly known as panchayati raj. Each village, or group of villages, has a gram panchayat, a council of several ward members (panch) and a president (sarpanch), directly elected by all the adult population of that ward or village. It is the decision-making body for the village. The panchayat works under the overall supervision of the gram sabha; all voters in the village are its members. It meets at least twice or thrice a year to approve the annual budget and review the gram panchayat's performance. A few gram panchayats form a panchayat samiti or block or mandal, whose members are elected by all panchayat members in that area. All panchayat samitis in a district constitute the zilla (district) parishad. Most members are elected; Lok Sabha members and MLAs of that district and some officials are also members. The zilla parishad chairperson is its political head.

question_english: What have been the achievements and difficulties of local government in India?
question_hinglish: India mein local government ki uplabdhiyan aur kathinaiyan kya rahi hain?
answer_english: Local government is the largest experiment in democracy anywhere, with about 36 lakh elected representatives in panchayats and municipalities, more than many countries' populations. Constitutional status has deepened democracy and increased women's representation and voice. But difficulties remain: gram sabhas are not held regularly, and most State governments have not transferred significant powers or adequate resources to local governments, so the ideal of self-government is still far away.
answer_hinglish: Local government duniya mein democracy ka sabse bada prayog hai, jisme panchayaton aur municipalities mein lagbhag 36 lakh chune pratinidhi hain, jo kai deshon ki aabaadi se zyada hai. Constitutional darje ne democracy gehri ki aur mahilaon ka pratinidhitva aur awaaz badhayi. Par kathinaiyan hain: gram sabhayein niyamit nahi hoti, aur zyadatar State sarkaron ne local sarkaron ko badi shaktiyan ya kaafi sansaadhan nahi diye, isliye swashaasan ka aadarsh abhi door hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What was the Porto Alegre experiment in Brazil?
question_hinglish: Brazil ka Porto Alegre prayog kya tha?
answer_english: Porto Alegre, a city in Brazil with nearly 13 lakh people, combined decentralisation with participative democracy by setting up a parallel organisation alongside the municipal council. The city is divided into sectors whose meetings, like a gram sabha, any citizen can attend to discuss the city budget, and about 20,000 people take part each year. This ensured money is spent for the benefit of poor colonies. A similar experiment took place in parts of Kerala, where ordinary people helped plan their locality's development.
answer_hinglish: Lagbhag 13 lakh aabaadi wale Brazil ke shehar Porto Alegre ne municipal council ke saath ek samaanantar sangathan banakar vikendrikaran ko bhagidaari wali democracy se joda. Shehar sectors mein bata hai jinki gram sabha jaisi meetings mein koi bhi nagrik shehar ke budget pe charcha kar sakta hai, aur har saal lagbhag 20,000 log hissa lete hain. Isse paisa gareeb bastiyon ke fayde mein kharch hona ensure hua. Kerala ke kuch hisson mein bhi aisa prayog hua, jahan aam logon ne apne ilaake ke vikaas ki yojana banayi.
ncert_context: A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil carried out an extraordinary experiment combining decentralisation with participative democracy. The city set up a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions. Nearly 13 lakh people in this city get to participate in making the budget for their own city. The city is divided into many sectors or wards, each with a meeting like a gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate. About 20,000 people participate every year. This method has ensured that money is spent for the benefit of the poor colonies. In India, a similar experiment has taken place in some areas of Kerala, where ordinary people participated in making a plan for their locality.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Point out one feature of federalism in India that is similar to and one that is different from Belgium.
question_hinglish: India ke federalism ki ek khaasiyat batao jo Belgium jaisi hai aur ek jo alag hai.
answer_english: Similar: both India and Belgium are 'holding together' federations, where power was divided between the national government and constituent units, and both changed state or regional boundaries and powers to accommodate linguistic diversity. Different: Belgium has a third 'community government' elected by each language community wherever they live, which India does not have; India's third tier is local government (panchayats and municipalities).
answer_hinglish: Jaisi: India aur Belgium dono 'holding together' federations hain, jahan power rashtriya sarkar aur ghatak ikaiyon mein baanti gayi, aur dono ne bhaashaai vividhata ko jagah dene ke liye states ya regions ki seemayein aur shaktiyan badli. Alag: Belgium mein teesri 'community government' hai jise har bhasha samudaay kahin bhi rehkar chunta hai, jo India mein nahi; India ka teesra star local government (panchayatein aur municipalities) hai.
ncert_context: India, Spain and Belgium are examples of 'holding together' federations where a large country divides its power between constituent States and the national government. In Belgium, a third kind of government, the 'community government', is elected by people of one language community no matter where they live, with power over cultural, educational and language issues. In India, a third tier of federalism was added in the form of Panchayats and Municipalities. India created linguistic States so that people speaking the same language lived in the same State.

subject: Social Science
question_english: The distinguishing feature of a federal government is: (a) National government gives some powers to provincial governments (b) Power is distributed among legislature, executive and judiciary (c) Elected officials exercise supreme power (d) Governmental power is divided between different levels of government
question_hinglish: Federal sarkar ki pehchaan wali khaasiyat kya hai? answer_english: (d) Governmental power is divided between different levels of government. In a federation, power is divided between a central authority and constituent units, each with constitutionally guaranteed jurisdiction.

In a unitary system, the centre can pass on orders to provincial governments.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why did Belgium adopt federalism even though it is a small country?
question_hinglish: Chhota desh hote hue bhi Belgium ne federalism kyun apnaya?
answer_english: Federalism is not only for big countries; it accommodates regional and linguistic diversity. Belgium, though small, has deep divisions between Dutch, French and German-speaking communities. To avoid conflict and a possible split, it gave regional governments constitutional powers no longer dependent on the centre in 1993, shifting from unitary to federal, which helped keep the country united.

Sangharsh aur sambhavit bantwaare se bachne ke liye isne 1993 mein regional sarkaron ko kendra pe nirbhar na rehne wali constitutional shaktiyan di aur unitary se federal bana, jisse desh ekjut raha.
ncert_context: One of the key changes made in the Constitution of Belgium was to reduce the power of the Central Government and give these powers to regional governments. Regional governments existed earlier, but their powers could be withdrawn by the Central Government. In 1993, regional governments were given constitutional powers no longer dependent on the central government. Thus, Belgium shifted from a unitary to a federal form of government. The federal system safeguards unity while accommodating regional diversity.

question_english: Mention different aspects of life in which women are discriminated against or disadvantaged in India.

answer_english: India is still male-dominated and patriarchal. subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the status of women's representation in India's legislative bodies?
question_hinglish: India ki legislative bodies mein mahilaon ke pratinidhitva ki sthiti kya hai?
answer_english: Women's share in Indian legislatures has been very low: elected women in the Lok Sabha touched 14.36 per cent of its strength for the first time in 2019, and their share in state assemblies is less than 5 per cent. India is among the bottom group of nations, behind several developing countries of Africa and Latin America, and cabinets are largely all-male. Local bodies, however, reserve one-third seats for women, giving over 10 lakh women representatives, and the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023 will give 33 per cent reservation in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Delhi Assembly.
answer_hinglish: Indian legislatures mein mahilaon ka hissa bahut kam raha hai: 2019 mein pehli baar Lok Sabha mein chuni mahilayein 14.36 percent pahunchi, aur state assemblies mein yeh 5 percent se kam hai. India duniya ke sabse neeche ke deshon mein hai, Africa aur Latin America ke kai developing deshon se peeche, aur cabinets zyadatar purushon ki hain. Par local bodies mein ek-tihaai seatein mahilaon ke liye reserve hain, jisse 10 lakh se zyada mahila pratinidhi hain, aur Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023 Lok Sabha, State Assemblies aur Delhi Assembly mein 33 percent reservation dega.
ncert_context: In India, the proportion of women in legislature has been very low. Cabinets are largely all-male even when a woman becomes Chief Minister or Prime Minister. One-third of seats in local government bodies are reserved for women; there are more than 10 lakh elected women representatives in rural and urban local bodies. In 2023, the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Act, 2023) was passed, giving 33 percent reservation for women in Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and Delhi Assembly.

subject: Social Science
question_english: In what ways can religion legitimately play a role in politics?
question_hinglish: Dharm politics mein kin tareekon se sahi bhoomika nibha sakta hai?
answer_english: Ideas, ideals and values from different religions can play a role in politics, and people should be able to express their needs and demands as members of a religious community. Gandhiji said religion can never be separated from politics, meaning moral values common to all religions should guide politics. Human rights groups demand government protection of religious minorities from communal riots, and the women's movement demands changes in family laws that discriminate against women. Such acts are not wrong as long as they treat every religion equally.
answer_hinglish: Alag dharmon ke vichaar, aadarsh aur mulya politics mein bhoomika nibha sakte hain, aur log dharmik samudaay ke sadasya ke roop mein apni zaroortein aur maangein rakh sakte hain. Gandhiji kehte the ki dharm ko politics se alag nahi kiya ja sakta, matlab saare dharmon ke naitik mulya politics ko disha dein. Human rights groups sarkar se dharmik alpsankhyakon ko dangon se bachane ki maang karte hain, aur mahila andolan mahilaon se bhed-bhaav karne wale family laws badalne ki maang karta hai. Yeh kaam tab tak galat nahi jab tak har dharm se barabar vyavhaar ho.
