subject: Social Science
question_english: What is communal politics, and when does religion in politics become a problem?
question_hinglish: Communal politics kya hai, aur politics mein dharm kab samasya ban jaata hai?
answer_english: The problem begins when religion is seen as the basis of the nation and is expressed in politics in exclusive, partisan terms: when one religion's beliefs are presented as superior, one group's demands are formed in opposition to another's, and state power is used to establish one group's domination. Communal politics is based on the idea that religion is the principal basis of social community, that followers of one religion form one community with the same fundamental interests, and that followers of different religions cannot belong to the same community.
answer_hinglish: Samasya tab shuru hoti hai jab dharm ko rashtra ka aadhaar maana jaaye aur politics mein ek-tarfa, pakshpaati tareeke se rakha jaaye: jab ek dharm ke vishwaas ko shreshth bataya jaaye, ek group ki maangein doosre ke virodh mein bane, aur state power se ek group ka dabdaba banaya jaaye. Communal politics is soch pe tiki hai ki dharm samajik samudaay ka mukhya aadhaar hai, ek dharm ke log ek samudaay hain jinke mool hit ek jaise hain, aur alag dharmon ke log ek samudaay nahi ho sakte.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is the belief underlying communalism fundamentally flawed?
question_hinglish: Communalism ke peeche ka vishwaas mool roop se galat kyun hai?
answer_english: In its extreme form, communalism holds that people of different religions cannot live as equal citizens in one nation, so one must dominate or they must form separate nations. This is flawed because people of one religion do not share the same interests and aspirations in every context; everyone has several other roles, positions and identities, and there are many voices inside every community, all with a right to be heard. So bringing all followers of a religion together in a non-religious context suppresses many voices.
answer_hinglish: Apne ugr roop mein communalism maanta hai ki alag dharmon ke log ek rashtra mein barabar nagrik nahi reh sakte, isliye ek ko haavi hona hoga ya alag rashtra banane honge. Yeh galat hai kyunki ek dharm ke logon ke har sandarbh mein hit aur ichchhayein ek jaisi nahi hoti; har kisi ki kai aur bhoomikayein, sthitiyan aur pehchaan hoti hain, aur har samudaay mein kai awaazein hoti hain jinhe sune jaane ka haq hai. Isliye dharm se alag sandarbh mein ek dharm ke sab logon ko ekjut karna kai awaazein dabaata hai.

question_english: What constitutional provisions make India a secular state?
question_hinglish: Kaun se constitutional provisions India ko secular state banate hain?
answer_english: There is no official religion for the Indian state; unlike Buddhism in Sri Lanka, Islam in Pakistan or Christianity in England, no religion has special status. The Constitution gives all individuals and communities freedom to profess, practise and propagate any religion, or none, prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, and allows the state to intervene in religious matters to ensure equality within religious communities, for example by banning untouchability.
answer_hinglish: Indian state ka koi official dharm nahi; Sri Lanka mein Buddhism, Pakistan mein Islam ya England mein Christianity ki tarah kisi dharm ko khaas darja nahi. Constitution har vyakti aur samudaay ko koi bhi dharm maanne, palan karne aur prachaar karne, ya koi na maanne, ki azaadi deta hai, dharm ke aadhaar pe bhed-bhaav rokta hai, aur dharmik samudaayon ke andar barabari ke liye state ko dharmik maamlon mein dakhal dene deta hai, jaise chhua-chhoot pe rok.
ncert_context: Communalism was and continues to be a major challenge to democracy. The makers of our Constitution chose the model of a secular state, reflected in several constitutional provisions. There is no official religion for the Indian state. Unlike the status of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, Islam in Pakistan and Christianity in England, our Constitution does not give a special status to any religion. The Constitution provides to all individuals and communities freedom to profess, practice and propagate any religion, or not to follow any. The Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion. At the same time, it allows the state to intervene in matters of religion to ensure equality within religious communities; for example, it bans untouchability.

question_english: What was the religious composition of India in 2011, and is any community likely to overtake others?
question_hinglish: 2011 mein India ki dharmik banaavat kya thi, aur kya koi samudaay doosron se aage nikal jaayega?
answer_english: In 2011, Hindus were 79.8 per cent, Muslims 14.2 per cent, Christians 2.3 per cent, Sikhs 1.7 per cent, Buddhists 0.7 per cent and Jains 0.4 per cent. Since Independence, each community's population grew but proportions changed little. The impression that Muslims will overtake others is mistaken; the Sachar Committee estimated their share may rise only about 3 to 4 per cent in 50 years, so the population balance will not change much.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What makes the caste system in India different from other forms of social inequality?
question_hinglish: India ki jaati vyavastha samajik asamanta ke doosre roopon se alag kya banati hai?
answer_english: All societies have some social inequality and division of labour, with occupations often passed down generations. The caste system is an extreme form, unique to India, because hereditary occupational division was sanctioned by rituals. Members of a caste formed a community practising the same occupation, married within the caste and did not eat with other castes. It was based on exclusion of and discrimination against 'outcaste' groups through untouchability, which reformers like Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B. R. Ambedkar and Periyar fought against.
answer_hinglish: Har samaaj mein kuch samajik asamanta aur kaam ka bantwara hota hai, aur aksar peshe peedhi-dar-peedhi chalte hain. Jaati vyavastha iska ugr roop hai, jo India mein hi hai, kyunki isme vanshaanugat pesha bantwara rituals se manzoor tha. Ek jaati ke log ek jaisa pesha karne wala samudaay the, jaati ke andar shaadi karte aur doosri jaatiyon ke saath nahi khaate the. Yeh 'outcaste' groups ko chhua-chhoot se bahar rakhne aur bhed-bhaav pe tiki thi, jiske khilaaf Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B. R. Ambedkar aur Periyar jaise sudhaarakon ne kaam kiya.
ncert_context: Unlike gender and religion, caste division is special to India. All societies have some social inequality and some division of labour; in most, occupations are passed on from one generation to another. Caste system is an extreme form of this. What makes it different is that hereditary occupational division was sanctioned by rituals. Members of the same caste formed a social community that practiced the same or similar occupation, married within the caste and did not eat with members from other caste groups. The caste system was based on exclusion of and discrimination against 'outcaste' groups, subjected to untouchability. Political leaders and social reformers like Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker worked for a society without caste inequalities.

question_english: What are the various forms caste takes in politics?
question_hinglish: Politics mein jaati kaun-kaun se roop leti hai?
answer_english: When choosing election candidates, parties keep the electorate's caste composition in mind and nominate candidates from different castes to win support. When governments are formed, parties ensure representatives of different castes and tribes find a place. Parties and candidates appeal to caste sentiment for support, and some parties are known to favour certain castes. Universal adult franchise and one-person-one-vote made leaders mobilise political support and brought new consciousness among castes earlier treated as inferior.

subject: Social Science
question_english: State reasons why caste alone cannot determine election results in India.
question_hinglish: Kaaran batao ki India mein sirf jaati chunaav ke nateeje tay kyun nahi kar sakti.
answer_english: No parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one caste, so every candidate must win the confidence of more than one caste and community. No party wins all the votes of a caste; a 'vote bank' only means a large share votes for that party. Many parties may field candidates from the same caste, while many voters have no candidate from their caste. Ruling parties and sitting MPs and MLAs often lose, which could not happen if castes were frozen in preferences. Voters' attachment to parties, differing economic interests within a caste, and assessment of government performance and leaders' popularity also matter.
answer_hinglish: Kisi bhi parliamentary constituency mein ek jaati ka saaf bahumat nahi, isliye har ummeedwaar ko ek se zyada jaati aur samudaay ka bharosa jeetna padta hai. Koi party kisi jaati ke saare vote nahi paati; 'vote bank' ka matlab bas itna hai ki bada hissa us party ko vote deta hai. Kai parties ek hi jaati ke ummeedwaar khade karti hain, jabki kai voters ki jaati ka koi ummeedwaar nahi hota. Ruling parties aur maujooda MPs aur MLAs aksar haarte hain, jo tab na hota agar jaatiyan apni pasand mein jami hoti. Parties se lagaav, jaati ke andar alag aarthik hit, aur sarkar ke kaam aur netaon ki lokpriyata bhi mayne rakhti hai.
ncert_context: The focus on caste in politics can give an impression that elections are all about caste. That is far from true. No parliamentary constituency in the country has a clear majority of one single caste, so every candidate and party needs to win the confidence of more than one caste. No party wins the votes of all voters of a caste; a 'vote bank' means a large proportion of that caste votes for the party. Many parties may put up candidates from the same caste, while many voters have no candidate from their caste. The ruling party and sitting MP or MLA frequently lose elections, which could not happen if castes were frozen in preferences. Voters have strong attachment to parties, often stronger than to caste. People within the same caste have different interests depending on economic condition; rich and poor or men and women often vote differently. People's assessment of government performance and popularity of leaders are often decisive.

The focus on caste in politics can give an impression that elections are all about caste. That is far from true. No parliamentary constituency in the country has a clear majority of one single caste, so every candidate and party needs to win the confidence of more than one caste. No party wins the votes of all voters of a caste; a 'vote bank' means a large proportion of that caste votes for the party. Many parties may put up candidates from the same caste, while many voters have no candidate from their caste. The ruling party and sitting MP or MLA frequently lose elections, which could not happen if castes were frozen in preferences. Voters have strong attachment to parties, often stronger than to caste. People within the same caste have different interests depending on economic condition; rich and poor or men and women often vote differently. People's assessment of government performance and popularity of leaders are often decisive.

Question:
Kaaran batao ki India mein sirf jaati chunaav ke nateeje tay kyun nahi kar sakti.

Intent Type: analytical
Answer the question in Hinglish using only the given context.

Kisi bhi parliamentary constituency mein ek jaati ka saaf bahumat nahi, isliye har ummeedwaar ko ek se zyada jaati aur samudaay ka bharosa jeetna padta hai. Koi party kisi jaati ke saare vote nahi paati; 'vote bank' ka matlab bas itna hai ki bada hissa us party ko vote deta hai. Kai parties ek hi jaati ke ummeedwaar khade karti hain, jabki kai voters ki jaati ka koi ummeedwaar nahi hota. Ruling parties aur maujooda MPs aur MLAs aksar haarte hain, jo tab na hota agar jaatiyan apni pasand mein jami hoti. Parties se lagaav, jaati ke andar alag aarthik hit, aur sarkar ke kaam aur netaon ki lokpriyata bhi mayne rakhti hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How does politics influence caste, and what are the positive and negative effects of caste in politics?
question_hinglish: Politics jaati ko kaise prabhavit karti hai, aur politics mein jaati ke achhe aur bure asar kya hain?
answer_english: Politics influences caste by bringing it into the political arena: caste gets politicised rather than politics becoming caste-ridden. Caste groups grow by incorporating neighbouring sub-castes, enter coalitions and negotiations with other castes, and new groups like 'backward' and 'forward' castes emerge. Positively, it gives disadvantaged communities like Dalits and OBCs space to demand their share of power and better access to decision-making. Negatively, politics based only on caste can divert attention from issues like poverty, development and corruption, and can cause tension, conflict and violence.
answer_hinglish: Politics jaati ko political maidaan mein laakar prabhavit karti hai: politics jaativaadi nahi hoti, jaati ka rajneetikaran hota hai. Jaati groups aas-paas ki up-jaatiyon ko jodkar bade bante hain, doosri jaatiyon se gathbandhan aur baatcheet karte hain, aur 'backward' aur 'forward' jaise naye groups bante hain. Achha asar: Dalits aur OBCs jaise pichhde samudaayon ko power mein hissa maangne aur faislon tak behtar pahunch ki jagah milti hai. Bura asar: sirf jaati pe based politics gareebi, vikaas aur bhrashtachaar jaise muddon se dhyaan hata sakti hai aur tanaav, sangharsh aur hinsa la sakti hai.
ncert_context: Politics too influences the caste system and caste identities by bringing them into the political arena. It is not politics that gets caste-ridden, it is caste that gets politicised. Each caste group tries to become bigger by incorporating neighbouring castes or sub-castes. Various caste groups enter into a coalition with other castes and enter into dialogue and negotiation. New kinds of caste groups have come up like 'backward' and 'forward' caste groups. In some situations, expression of caste differences in politics gives disadvantaged communities space to demand their share of power, helping Dalits and OBCs gain better access to decision making. At the same time, politics based on caste identity alone is not healthy; it can divert attention from pressing issues like poverty, development and corruption, and in some cases leads to tensions, conflict and violence.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How is caste still linked to economic inequality in India?
question_hinglish: India mein jaati ab bhi aarthik asamanta se kaise judi hai?
answer_english: Caste regulated access to resources: in the past, 'untouchable' castes were denied the right to own land, while only 'twice born' castes could get education. Though such explicit inequality is outlawed, centuries of accumulated advantages and disadvantages persist, and new inequalities have developed. Every caste has some poor members, but the proportion living in extreme poverty is much higher for the lowest castes, Dalits and Adivasis, and much lower for upper castes, with backward classes in between.
answer_hinglish: Jaati sansaadhanon tak pahunch tay karti thi: pehle 'achhoot' jaatiyon ko zameen rakhne ka haq nahi tha, jabki sirf 'dwij' jaatiyon ko shiksha ka haq tha. Aisi khuli asamanta ab gair-kanooni hai, par sadiyon ke jama fayde-nuksaan ka asar ab bhi hai aur nayi asamantayein bhi bani hain. Har jaati mein kuch gareeb hain, par atyant gareebi mein rehne walon ka anupaat sabse neechi jaatiyon, Dalits aur Adivasis, mein bahut zyada aur oonchi jaatiyon mein bahut kam hai, aur pichhde varg beech mein hain.
ncert_context: Caste is an important source of economic inequality because it regulates access to resources. In the past, the so-called 'untouchable' castes were denied the right to own land, while only the so-called 'twice born' castes had the right to education. Although this explicit inequality is now outlawed, the effects of centuries of accumulated advantages and disadvantages continue. New kinds of inequalities have also developed. Although every caste has some poor members, the proportion living in extreme poverty (below the official poverty line) is much higher for the lowest castes and much lower for the upper castes, with the backward classes in between.

question_english: Which statement about India's Constitution is wrong? It (a) prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion (b) gives official status to one religion (c) provides freedom to profess any religion (d) ensures equality of citizens within religious communities

answer_english: (b) gives official status to one religion. This is wrong because India has no official religion; the Constitution gives no special status to any religion.

subject: Social Science
question_english: State the various functions political parties perform in a democracy.
question_hinglish: Democracy mein political parties kaun-kaun se kaam karti hain?
answer_english: Parties (1) contest elections, putting up candidates; (2) put forward different policies and programmes for voters to choose from, reducing many opinions to a few basic positions; (3) play a decisive role in making laws, as legislators follow party direction; (4) form and run governments, recruiting and training leaders as ministers; (5) act as opposition when they lose, criticising the government and mobilising opposition; (6) shape public opinion by raising issues and launching movements; and (7) provide people access to government machinery and welfare schemes, since a local party leader is easier to approach than an officer.
answer_hinglish: Parties (1) ummeedwaar khade karke chunaav ladti hain; (2) voters ke liye alag policies aur programmes rakhti hain, kai raayon ko kuch mool sthitiyon mein badalti hain; (3) kanoon banane mein nirnaayak bhoomika nibhaati hain, kyunki vidhaayak party ki disha maante hain; (4) sarkar banati aur chalati hain, netaon ko bharti aur train karke mantri banati hain; (5) haarne pe opposition banti hain, sarkar ki aalochana aur virodh lamband karti hain; (6) mudde uthakar aur andolan chalakar janmat banati hain; aur (7) logon ko sarkari machinery aur welfare schemes tak pahunch deti hain, kyunki local party neta officer se zyada aasaani se milta hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why do modern democracies need political parties?
question_hinglish: Aadhunik democracies ko political parties ki zaroorat kyun hai?
answer_english: Without parties, every candidate would be independent, so no one could promise major policy changes, and governments would be formed but remain uncertain in utility; representatives would answer only to their localities, and no one would be responsible for running the country. Non-party panchayat elections show villages still split into factions with 'panels', which is what parties do. As societies grew large and complex, they needed an agency to gather views, bring representatives together to form responsible governments, and support or restrain the government. Parties fulfil these needs, so they are a necessary condition for democracy.
answer_hinglish: Parties ke bina har ummeedwaar independent hoga, isliye koi bade policy badlav ka vaada nahi kar paayega, aur sarkar ban toh jaayegi par uska upyog anishchit rahega; pratinidhi sirf apne ilaake ko jawabdeh honge aur desh chalane ki zimmedari kisi ki nahi hogi. Bina party ke panchayat chunaav mein bhi gaon guton mein bat-kar 'panel' khade karte hain, jo parties hi karti hain. Bade aur jatil samaajon ko vichaar ikatthe karne, pratinidhiyon ko jodkar zimmedar sarkar banane, aur sarkar ko samarthan ya rok lagaane ka zariya chahiye. Parties yeh zaroortein poori karti hain, isliye woh democracy ki zaroori shart hain.
ncert_context: We can understand the necessity of parties by imagining a situation without parties. Every candidate will be independent, so no one will be able to make promises about major policy changes. The government may be formed, but its utility will remain uncertain. subject: Social Science
question_english: Distinguish between one-party, two-party and multi-party systems with examples.
question_hinglish: One-party, two-party aur multi-party systems mein examples ke saath fark batao.
answer_english: In a one-party system, only one party is allowed to control and run the government, as in China with the Communist Party; it is not a democratic option because there is no free competition for power. In a two-party system, power usually alternates between two main parties, though others may exist and win a few seats, as in the USA and the UK. In a multi-party system, several parties compete and more than two have a reasonable chance of coming to power alone or in alliance, as in India.
answer_hinglish: One-party system mein sirf ek party ko sarkar chalane ki ijaazat hoti hai, jaise China mein Communist Party; yeh democratic vikalp nahi kyunki power ke liye khula mukabla nahi hota. Two-party system mein power aam taur pe do mukhya parties ke beech badalti hai, halaanki doosri parties hokar kuch seatein jeet sakti hain, jaise USA aur UK mein. Multi-party system mein kai parties mukabla karti hain aur do se zyada ke akele ya gathbandhan mein sarkar banane ki sambhavna hoti hai, jaise India mein.
ncert_context: In some countries, only one party is allowed to control and run the government; these are one-party systems. In China, only the Communist Party is allowed to rule; the electoral system does not permit free competition. One-party system is not a good option because it is not a democratic option; any democratic system must allow at least two parties to compete and provide a fair chance to come to power. In some countries, power usually changes between two main parties; several other parties may exist but only the two main parties have a serious chance of winning majority; this is a two-party system, as in the USA and UK. If several parties compete and more than two have a reasonable chance of coming to power on their own or in alliance, it is a multiparty system. India has a multiparty system.

question_english: Why has India evolved a multi-party system, and which party system is best?
question_hinglish: India mein multi-party system kyun bana, aur kaun sa party system sabse achha hai?
answer_english: India has a multi-party system because the social and geographical diversity of such a large country cannot be easily absorbed by two or even three parties. A multi-party system often appears messy and may lead to instability, but it lets a variety of interests and opinions enjoy representation. subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
question_hinglish: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ke baare mein batao.
answer_english: The BJP was founded in 1980 by reviving the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, formed by Syama Prasad Mukherjee in 1951. It wants to build a strong, modern India inspired by ancient culture and values and Deendayal Upadhyaya's ideas of integral humanism and Antyodaya; cultural nationalism (Hindutva) is central to its idea of nationhood. It wants full integration of Jammu and Kashmir, a uniform civil code and a ban on religious conversions. Its support expanded beyond the north, west and cities in the 1990s; it came to power in 1998 leading the NDA and won 303 seats in 2019, leading the NDA government.

Yeh Jammu and Kashmir ka poora ekeekaran, uniform civil code aur dharm parivartan pe rok chahti hai. 1990s mein iska aadhaar north, west aur shehron se aage badha; 1998 mein NDA ki aguaai mein sattaa mein aayi aur 2019 mein 303 seatein jeet kar NDA sarkar chala rahi hai.

Cultural nationalism (or 'Hindutva') is an important element in its conception of Indian nationhood. Wants full territorial and political integration of Jammu and Kashmir with India, a uniform civil code for all people irrespective of religion, and ban on religious conversions. Its support base increased substantially in the 1990s; earlier limited to north, west and urban areas, it expanded to the south, east, north-east and rural areas. subject: Social Science
question_english: Describe the Indian National Congress (INC).

answer_english: The INC, popularly the Congress Party, founded in 1885, is one of the world's oldest parties and has had many splits. It ruled at the Centre till 1977 and from 1980 to 1989; after 1989 its support declined but it remains present nationwide across social divisions. Under Jawaharlal Nehru, the party sought to build a modern secular democratic republic in India. Ruling party at the centre till 1977 and from 1980 to 1989. After 1989, its support declined, but it continues to be present throughout the country, cutting across social divisions. A centrist party (neither rightist nor leftist), the party espouses secularism and welfare of weaker sections and minorities. Supports new economic reforms but with a human face. Leader of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government from 2004 to 2019. In the 2019 Lok Sabha election, it won 19.5% votes and 52 seats.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are State parties, and how have they strengthened federalism and democracy?
question_hinglish: State parties kya hain, aur inhone federalism aur democracy ko kaise mazboot kiya?
answer_english: Other than the national parties, most major parties are classified by the Election Commission as State parties, commonly called regional parties, though they need not be regional in ideology; some, like the Samajwadi Party and Rashtriya Janata Dal, have units in several states, while others like Biju Janata Dal, Sikkim Democratic Front, Mizo National Front and Telangana Rashtra Samithi are conscious of State identity. Their number and strength have grown, making Parliament more diverse; since no national party won a Lok Sabha majority on its own until 2014, national parties allied with State parties, and since 1996 nearly every State party has been part of a national coalition, strengthening federalism and democracy.
answer_hinglish: National parties ke alawa zyadatar badi parties ko Election Commission State parties, yaani regional parties, maanta hai, halaanki zaroori nahi ki unki soch kshetriya ho; Samajwadi Party aur Rashtriya Janata Dal jaisi kuch ke kai states mein units hain, jabki Biju Janata Dal, Sikkim Democratic Front, Mizo National Front aur Telangana Rashtra Samithi jaisi State pehchaan ke prati sajag hain. Inki sankhya aur taakat badhi, jisse Parliament zyada vividh hua; 2014 tak koi national party akele Lok Sabha bahumat nahi paa saki, isliye national parties ne State parties se gathbandhan kiye, aur 1996 se lagbhag har State party kisi national coalition ka hissa rahi, jisse federalism aur democracy mazboot hue.

question_english: What are the various challenges faced by political parties?
question_hinglish: Political parties ke saamne kaun si chunautiyan hain?
answer_english: (1) Lack of internal democracy: power concentrates in a few top leaders, parties do not keep membership registers or hold regular meetings and internal elections, and personal loyalty to the leader matters more than principles. question_english: Why is dynastic succession bad for democracy?
question_hinglish: Vanshvaad democracy ke liye bura kyun hai?
answer_english: Since most parties lack open and transparent procedures, ordinary workers have very few ways to rise to the top. Leaders are in a position of unfair advantage to favour people close to them or their family members, so in many parties top positions are always controlled by one family. This is unfair to other members and bad for democracy, because people without adequate experience or popular support come to occupy positions of power.
answer_hinglish: Zyadatar parties mein khule aur paardarshi tareeke nahi hote, isliye aam kaaryakarta ke upar pahunchne ke raaste bahut kam hain. question_english: How does the decline in ideological differences among parties affect voters?
question_hinglish: Parties ke beech vaichaarik fark ghatne ka voters pe kya asar hota hai?
answer_english: To offer meaningful choice, parties must be significantly different. subject: Social Science
question_english: What recent efforts have been made in India to reform political parties?
question_hinglish: India mein political parties sudhaarne ke liye haal mein kya prayaas hue hain?
answer_english: The Constitution was amended to stop elected MLAs and MPs from changing parties, since many defected for ministership or cash; now a legislator who changes parties loses the seat, which reduced defection but made dissent harder, as MPs and MLAs must accept leaders' decisions. The Supreme Court made it mandatory for every candidate to file an affidavit giving details of property and pending criminal cases, though its truth is not checked. The Election Commission ordered parties to hold organisational elections and file income tax returns, though elections are sometimes a mere formality.
answer_hinglish: MLAs aur MPs ko party badalne se rokne ke liye constitution badla gaya, kyunki kai mantri pad ya paise ke liye dal-badal karte the; ab party badalne pe seat jaati hai, jisse dal-badal ghata par asahmati mushkil hui, kyunki MPs aur MLAs ko netaon ke faisle maanne padte hain. Supreme Court ne har ummeedwaar ke liye sampatti aur lambit criminal cases ki jaankari wala affidavit dena zaroori kiya, halaanki iski sachchai jaanchi nahi jaati. Election Commission ne parties ko andar ke chunaav karne aur income tax returns bharne ka aadesh diya, par kabhi yeh sirf formality hoti hai.
ncert_context: The Constitution was amended to prevent elected MLAs and MPs from changing parties, because many were indulging in defection to become ministers or for cash rewards. Now if any MLA or MP changes parties, he or she will lose the seat. This law has helped bring defection down, but has made dissent more difficult; MPs and MLAs have to accept whatever party leaders decide. The Supreme Court passed an order to reduce the influence of money and criminals: it is mandatory for every candidate to file an affidavit giving details of property and criminal cases pending. But there is no system to check if the information is true. The Election Commission passed an order making it necessary for parties to hold organisational elections and file income tax returns. Parties have started doing so but sometimes it is mere formality.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Suggest some reforms to strengthen political parties.
question_hinglish: Political parties ko mazboot karne ke liye kuch sudhaar sujhao.
answer_english: A law could regulate parties' internal affairs, making them keep a members' register, follow their own constitution, have an independent authority to judge disputes and hold open elections to top posts. Parties could be required to give about one-third of tickets to women and have quotas for women in decision-making bodies. There could be state funding of elections, in kind (petrol, paper, telephone) or cash based on votes. Beyond laws, people can pressure parties through petitions, publicity and agitations, and those who want reform can join parties.
answer_hinglish: Ek kanoon parties ke andar ke maamle niyantrit kar sakta hai, jisme members ka register rakhna, apne constitution ka paalan, vivaad suljhaane ke liye swatantra authority aur bade padon ke khule chunaav zaroori hon. Parties ke liye lagbhag ek-tihaai tickets mahilaon ko dena aur faisla lene wali bodies mein mahilaon ka quota zaroori ho sakta hai. Chunaav ki state funding ho sakti hai, saamaan (petrol, kaagaz, telephone) ya pichhle vote ke aadhaar pe paise mein. Kanoon ke alawa log petitions, prachaar aur andolan se dabaav daal sakte hain, aur sudhaar chaahne wale parties join kar sakte hain.
ncert_context: Suggestions to reform political parties: a law should regulate the internal affairs of parties; it should be compulsory to maintain a register of members, follow its own constitution, have an independent authority to judge party disputes, and hold open elections to the highest posts. It should be mandatory to give a minimum number of tickets, about one-third, to women, with a quota for women in decision making bodies. There should be state funding of elections; the government should give parties money for election expenses in kind (petrol, paper, telephone) or in cash based on votes in the last election. Over-regulation can be counter-productive. Two other ways: people can put pressure through petitions, publicity and agitations; and parties can improve if those who want reform join them.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why must we be careful about legal solutions to reform political parties?
question_hinglish: Political parties sudhaarne ke kanooni upaayon ke baare mein saavdhaan kyun rehna chahiye?
answer_english: Over-regulation of political parties can be counter-productive, because it would force all parties to find ways to cheat the law. Besides, parties will not agree to pass a law they do not like. So public pressure through petitions, publicity and agitations, and participation of reform-minded citizens in parties, are also important; the problem of bad politics can be solved by more and better politics.
answer_hinglish: Parties pe zyada niyantran ulta asar kar sakta hai, kyunki isse saari parties kanoon ko dhokha dene ke tareeke dhundhengi. Saath hi parties aisa kanoon pass karne ko taiyaar nahi hongi jo unhe pasand na ho. Isliye petitions, prachaar aur andolanon se janta ka dabaav, aur sudhaar chaahne walon ka parties mein judna bhi zaroori hai; buri politics ka hal zyada aur behtar politics hai.
ncert_context: We must be very careful about legal solutions to political problems. Over-regulation of political parties can be counter-productive. This would force all parties to find ways to cheat the law. Besides, political parties will not agree to pass a law that they do not like. People can put pressure on political parties through petitions, publicity and agitations; ordinary citizens, pressure groups, movements and the media can play an important role. Political parties can improve if those who want this join them. The quality of democracy depends on the degree of public participation. The problem of bad politics can be solved by more and better politics.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the dilemma people face about democracy, and how should we think about its outcomes?
question_hinglish: Democracy ko lekar logon ki duvidha kya hai, aur hume iske nateejon ke baare mein kaise sochna chahiye?
answer_english: Most people support democracy against alternatives like rule by monarchs or military or religious leaders, but many are not satisfied with democracy in practice; democracy seems good in principle but not so good in practice. We tend to expect democracy to solve all socio-economic and political problems and blame it when it doesn't. The first step is to recognise that democracy is just a form of government: it can only create conditions for achieving goals, and citizens must use those conditions to achieve them.
answer_hinglish: Zyadatar log raaja, sena ya dharmik netaon ke raaj ke mukable democracy ka samarthan karte hain, par kai log asli democracy se santusht nahi; democracy siddhaant mein achhi par amal mein kam achhi lagti hai. Hum ummeed karte hain ki democracy saari samajik-aarthik aur political samasyayein suljhaayegi aur na hone pe use dosh dete hain. Pehla kadam yeh samajhna hai ki democracy sirf ek sarkar ka roop hai: yeh sirf lakshya paane ki sthitiyan bana sakti hai, aur nagrikon ko un sthitiyon ka use karke lakshya haasil karne hain.
ncert_context: Most people support democracy against other alternatives, such as rule by a monarch or military or religious leaders. But not so many would be satisfied with democracy in practice. So we face a dilemma: democracy is seen to be good in principle, but felt to be not so good in practice. Our fascination for democracy often pushes us into taking a position that democracy can address all socio-economic and political problems. If some expectations are not met, we start blaming the idea of democracy. The first step towards thinking carefully about outcomes of democracy is to recognise that democracy is just a form of government. It can only create conditions for achieving something. The citizens have to take advantage of those conditions and achieve those goals.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How does democracy produce an accountable, responsive and legitimate government?
question_hinglish: Democracy jawabdeh, sanvedansheel aur vaidh sarkar kaise banati hai?
answer_english: Democracy gives people the right to choose and control their rulers and to participate in decisions affecting them, so its most basic outcome is a government accountable and responsive to citizens. It ensures decisions follow norms and procedures, so citizens can check how decisions were taken (transparency), and develops mechanisms like regular, free and fair elections, open public debate on major policies, and citizens' right to information. Though it may be slow, less efficient and not always responsive or clean, a democratic government is legitimate because it is people's own government.
answer_hinglish: Democracy logon ko apne shaasak chunne aur unpe niyantran ka, aur apne ko prabhavit karne wale faislon mein hissa lene ka haq deti hai, isliye iska sabse mool nateeja nagrikon ke prati jawabdeh aur sanvedansheel sarkar hai. Yeh ensure karti hai ki faisle niyamon aur prakriyaon se hon, taaki nagrik jaanch sakein ki faisla kaise liya (paardarshita), aur niyamit, free aur fair chunaav, badi policies pe khuli bahas aur nagrikon ke jaankari ke haq jaise tareeke banati hai. Dheemi, kam kushal aur hamesha sanvedansheel ya saaf na hone pe bhi democratic sarkar vaidh hai kyunki woh janta ki apni sarkar hai.
ncert_context: In a democracy, people have the right to choose their rulers and control over them, and citizens should be able to participate in decision making. The most basic outcome of democracy should be a government that is accountable to citizens and responsive to their needs. Democracy ensures decision making is based on norms and procedures; a citizen who wants to know if a decision was taken through correct procedures can find this out—this is transparency. Democratic government develops mechanisms for citizens to hold it accountable: regular, free and fair elections; open public debate on major policies and legislations; and citizens' right to information about the government. A democratic government is legitimate government. It may be slow, less efficient, not always very responsive or clean, but it is people's own government.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Is democratic government inefficient because it delays decisions?
question_hinglish: Kya faislon mein deri ki wajah se democratic sarkar akushal hai?
answer_english: Non-democratic rulers need not bother with deliberation, majorities or public opinion, so they can decide quickly, but their decisions may not be accepted by people and may face problems. Democracy is based on deliberation and negotiation, so some delay is bound to happen, but because it follows procedures, its decisions are more acceptable and more effective. So the cost of time democracy pays is perhaps worth it.
answer_hinglish: Gair-democratic shaasakon ko bahas, bahumat ya janmat ki parwah nahi karni padti, isliye woh jaldi faisle le sakte hain, par unke faisle janta maan na bhi sakti hai aur mushkilein aa sakti hain. Democracy bahas aur baatcheet pe tiki hai, isliye kuch deri hoti hai, par prakriya maanne se iske faisle zyada sweekaarya aur asardaar hote hain. Isliye democracy jo samay ki keemat chukaati hai woh shayad uchit hai.
ncert_context: Some people think democracy produces less effective government. Non-democratic rulers do not have to bother about deliberation in assemblies or worry about majorities and public opinion, so they can be very quick and efficient. Democracy is based on deliberation and negotiation, so some delay is bound to take place. Imagine a government that takes decisions very fast but they are not accepted by people and face problems. In contrast, the democratic government takes more time to follow procedures, but because it has followed procedures, its decisions may be both more acceptable to people and more effective. So, the cost of time that democracy pays is perhaps worth it.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is transparency in a democracy?
question_hinglish: Democracy mein transparency kya hai?
answer_english: Transparency means that a citizen who wants to know if a decision was taken through the correct procedures has the right and the means to examine the decision-making process. This factor is often missing from non-democratic governments.
answer_hinglish: Transparency ka matlab hai ki jo nagrik jaanna chahe ki faisla sahi prakriya se liya gaya ya nahi, uske paas faisla lene ki prakriya jaanchne ka haq aur zariya hai. Yeh gair-democratic sarkaron mein aksar nahi hota.
ncert_context: Democracy ensures that decision making will be based on norms and procedures. So, a citizen who wants to know if a decision was taken through the correct procedures can find this out. She has the right and the means to examine the process of decision making. This is known as transparency. This factor is often missing from a non-democratic government.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the actual record of democracies on accountability and responsiveness?
question_hinglish: Jawabdehi aur sanvedansheelta pe democracies ka asli record kaisa hai?
answer_english: The record is mixed. Democracies have been more successful in setting up regular, free elections and conditions for open public debate, but most fall short of elections giving everyone a fair chance and of subjecting every decision to debate, and they don't share information well. They often frustrate people's needs and ignore majority demands, and corruption persists. Still, democracies are much better than non-democracies in these respects, and nothing shows non-democracies are less corrupt or more sensitive to people.
answer_hinglish: Record mila-jula hai. Democracies niyamit, free chunaav aur khuli bahas ki sthitiyan banane mein zyada safal rahi hain, par zyadatar sabko barabar mauka dene wale chunaav aur har faisle pe public bahas mein peeche hain, aur jaankari baantne mein achhi nahi. Woh aksar logon ki zaroortein poori nahi karti aur bahumat ki maangein nazarandaaz karti hain, aur bhrashtachaar bana rehta hai. Phir bhi in maamlon mein democracies gair-democracies se kaafi behtar hain, aur koi saboot nahi ki gair-democracies kam bhrasht ya zyada sanvedansheel hain.
ncert_context: The actual performance of democracies shows a mixed record. Democracies have had greater success in setting up regular and free elections and conditions for open public debate. But most democracies fall short of elections that provide a fair chance to everyone and in subjecting every decision to public debate. Democratic governments do not have a very good record in sharing information with citizens. All one can say is that they are much better than any non-democratic regime in these respects. It is reasonable to expect a government attentive to people's needs and largely free of corruption, but the record is not impressive. Democracies often frustrate the needs of people and ignore demands of a majority. The routine tales of corruption show democracy is not free of this evil. At the same time, there is nothing to show that non-democracies are less corrupt or more sensitive to people.

question_english: Do democracies produce higher economic growth than dictatorships?
question_hinglish: Kya democracies dictatorships se zyada economic growth deti hain?
answer_english: Evidence shows many democracies did not fulfil this expectation. Between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships had a slightly higher growth rate (4.42) than democracies (3.95). But among poor countries, the difference is negligible: 4.34 under dictatorship versus 4.28 under democracy. answer_hinglish: Saboot dikhata hai ki kai democracies ne yeh ummeed poori nahi ki. 1950 se 2000 tak dictatorships ki growth rate (4.42) democracies (3.95) se thodi zyada thi. Kyunki economic vikaas aabaadi, global sthiti, sahyog aur aarthik praathmiktaon pe nirbhar hai, hum nahi keh sakte ki democracy vikaas ki guarantee hai, par yeh peeche nahi rehti, aur fark na ke barabar hone se democracy apne doosre achhe nateejon ki wajah se behtar hai.
ncert_context: If democracies are expected to produce good governments, is it fair to expect they also produce development? Evidence shows many democracies did not fulfil this expectation. Rates of economic growth 1950-2000: all democratic regimes 3.95, all dictatorial regimes 4.42, poor countries under dictatorship 4.34, poor countries under democracy 4.28. When comparing only poor countries, there is virtually no difference. Economic development depends on several factors: population size, global situation, cooperation from other countries, economic priorities. We cannot say democracy guarantees development, but we can expect it not to lag behind dictatorships. With negligible difference, it is better to prefer democracy as it has several other positive outcomes.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Have democracies been successful in reducing economic inequality and poverty?
question_hinglish: Kya democracies aarthik asamanta aur gareebi kam karne mein safal rahi hain?
answer_english: Democracies are based on political equality, as every individual has equal weight in electing representatives, but economic inequalities have grown alongside: a small number of ultra-rich enjoy a highly disproportionate and rising share of wealth, while those at the bottom have declining incomes and struggle to meet basic needs like food, clothing, housing, education and health. Although the poor form a large share of voters, democratic governments are not as keen to address poverty as expected, and in Bangladesh more than half the population lives in poverty.
answer_hinglish: Democracies political barabari pe tiki hain, kyunki pratinidhi chunne mein har vyakti ka barabar mahatva hai, par saath hi aarthik asamanta badhi hai: kuch ati-ameer daulat ka bahut bada aur badhta hissa rakhte hain, jabki neeche ke logon ki aamdani ghat rahi hai aur khaana, kapda, ghar, shiksha aur sehat jaisi mool zaroortein poori karna mushkil hai. Gareeb voters ka bada hissa hain, phir bhi chuni sarkarein gareebi pe utni gambhir nahi jitni ummeed thi, aur Bangladesh mein aadhi se zyada aabaadi gareeb hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the conditions under which democracies accommodate social diversities?
question_hinglish: Kin sharton mein democracies samajik vividhata ko jagah deti hain?
answer_english: Democracies usually develop procedures to conduct competition, reducing the chance of tensions becoming violent, and evolve mechanisms to negotiate differences, as Belgium did. But as Sri Lanka shows, two conditions are needed. First, democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion; the majority must work with the minority so the government represents the general view. Second, rule by majority must not become rule by a majority community of religion, race or language; different people and groups should be able to form a majority in each decision or election, and no one should be barred from being in the majority by birth.
answer_hinglish: Democracies aam taur pe mukabla chalane ke niyam banati hain, jisse tanaav hinsak hone ki sambhavna ghat-ti hai, aur Belgium ki tarah matbhed suljhaane ke tareeke banati hain. Par Sri Lanka dikhata hai ki do shartein zaroori hain. Pehli, democracy sirf bahumat ki raay ka raaj nahi; bahumat ko alpmat ke saath milkar kaam karna chahiye taaki sarkar samaanya raay dikhaye. Doosri, bahumat ka raaj dharm, nasl ya bhasha ke bahusankhyak samudaay ka raaj na bane; har faisle ya chunaav mein alag log aur groups bahumat bana sakein, aur kisi ko janm ke aadhaar pe bahumat mein aane se na roka jaaye.
ncert_context: Democracies usually develop a procedure to conduct their competition, reducing the possibility of tensions becoming explosive or violent. No society can fully resolve conflicts among groups, but we can learn to respect differences and evolve mechanisms to negotiate them. Democracy is best suited to this. Non-democratic regimes often suppress internal social differences. The example of Sri Lanka reminds us that democracy must fulfil two conditions. It is necessary to understand that democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion. The majority always needs to work with the minority so that governments represent the general view. It is also necessary that rule by majority does not become rule by majority community in terms of religion, race or linguistic group. Rule by majority means that in every decision or election, different persons and groups may form a majority. If someone is barred from being in majority on the basis of birth, democratic rule ceases to be accommodative for that person or group.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Is ensuring that people do not fight each other enough to call it harmony? What can democracy realistically offer?
question_hinglish: Kya logon ka aapas mein na ladna samanjasya kehne ke liye kaafi hai? Democracy asal mein kya de sakti hai?
answer_english: No society can fully and permanently resolve conflicts among groups, so democracy cannot guarantee perfect harmony. But it can help people learn to respect differences and evolve mechanisms to negotiate them, conducting competition through procedures so tensions do not become explosive or violent. Non-democratic regimes often ignore or suppress social differences, so democracy's ability to handle social divisions and conflicts is a definite plus.
answer_hinglish: Koi samaaj groups ke beech sangharsh poori tarah aur hamesha ke liye nahi suljha sakta, isliye democracy poora samanjasya guarantee nahi kar sakti. Par yeh logon ko matbhed ka samman karna aur unhe suljhaane ke tareeke banana sikha sakti hai, niyamon se mukabla chala kar taaki tanaav hinsak na ho. Gair-democratic sarkarein aksar samajik matbhedon ko nazarandaaz ya dabaati hain, isliye samajik vibhaajan aur sangharsh sambhalne ki kshamta democracy ka pakka fayda hai.
ncert_context: Do democracies lead to peaceful and harmonious life among citizens? Democracies usually develop a procedure to conduct their competition, reducing the possibility of tensions becoming explosive or violent. No society can fully and permanently resolve conflicts among different groups. But we can certainly learn to respect these differences and evolve mechanisms to negotiate them. Democracy is best suited to produce this outcome. Non-democratic regimes often turn a blind eye to or suppress internal social differences. Ability to handle social differences, divisions and conflicts is thus a definite plus point of democratic regimes.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How does democracy promote the dignity and freedom of individuals, especially women and disadvantaged castes?
question_hinglish: Democracy vyaktiyon, khaas kar mahilaon aur pichhdi jaatiyon, ki garima aur azaadi kaise badhati hai?
answer_english: Democracy is far superior to other forms of government in promoting individual dignity and freedom, since the passion for respect and freedom is its basis. Long struggles by women have created sensitivity that respect and equal treatment of women are necessary in a democratic society; though women are not always respected, once the principle is recognised, it becomes easier to fight what is legally and morally unacceptable, which would lack legal basis in a non-democracy. Similarly, Indian democracy has strengthened the claims of disadvantaged castes for equal status and opportunity, and caste atrocities now lack moral and legal foundations.
answer_hinglish: Vyakti ki garima aur azaadi badhane mein democracy doosri sarkaron se kahin behtar hai, kyunki samman aur azaadi ki chahat hi iska aadhaar hai. Mahilaon ke lambe sangharsh ne yeh samajh banayi ki democracy mein mahilaon ka samman aur barabar vyavhaar zaroori hai; mahilaon ka hamesha samman nahi hota, par siddhaant maan liye jaane se kanooni aur naitik roop se galat cheez ke khilaaf ladna aasaan hota hai, jiska gair-democracy mein kanooni aadhaar nahi hota. Isi tarah Indian democracy ne pichhdi jaatiyon ke barabar darje aur avsar ke daavon ko mazboot kiya, aur jaati atyaachaaron ka ab koi naitik ya kanooni aadhaar nahi.
ncert_context: Democracy stands much superior to any other form of government in promoting dignity and freedom of the individual. Every individual wants respect from fellow beings. The passion for respect and freedom are the basis of democracy. Most societies were historically male dominated. Long struggles by women have created sensitivity that respect to and equal treatment of women are necessary ingredients of a democratic society. That does not mean women are always treated with respect. But once the principle is recognised, it becomes easier for women to struggle against what is now unacceptable legally and morally. In a non-democratic set up, this unacceptability would not have legal basis. The same is true of caste inequalities. Democracy in India has strengthened the claims of disadvantaged and discriminated castes for equal status and equal opportunity. There are still caste-based inequalities and atrocities, but these lack moral and legal foundations.

question_english: Do people in South Asia believe their vote makes a difference?
question_hinglish: Kya South Asia ke log maante hain ki unka vote farak padta hai?
answer_english: Yes. subject: Social Science
question_english: Nannu, a daily wage earner in Delhi, could not get a duplicate ration card for months until he filed an RTI application, after which officials quickly gave him the card. What does his example show?
question_hinglish: Delhi ke dihaadi mazdoor Nannu ko mahino tak duplicate ration card nahi mila jab tak usne RTI application nahi di, jiske baad adhikaariyon ne jaldi card de diya. Uska example kya dikhata hai?
answer_english: Nannu's example shows how democratic mechanisms like the citizens' right to information make government accountable and transparent. The RTI application, asking for progress, the officials responsible and action against them, forced officials to act within a week and even treat him warmly. It shows democracy gives ordinary citizens means to examine decision-making and hold officials accountable, turning them from subjects into citizens.
answer_hinglish: Nannu ka example dikhata hai ki nagrikon ka jaankari ka haq jaise democratic tareeke sarkar ko jawabdeh aur paardarshi banate hain. Pragati, zimmedar adhikaariyon aur unpe karyavahi poochne wali RTI application ne adhikaariyon ko ek hafte mein kaam karne aur use pyaar se pesh aane pe majboor kiya. Yeh dikhata hai ki democracy aam nagrikon ko faislon ki jaanch aur adhikaariyon ko jawabdeh banane ka zariya deti hai, unhe praja se nagrik banati hai.
ncert_context: Nannu, a daily wage earner in a slum in East Delhi, lost his ration card and applied for a duplicate in January 2004. For three months, clerks and officials would not even look at him. He filed an application under the Right to Information Act asking for daily progress on his application, names of officials supposed to act and what action would be taken against them. Within a week, an inspector informed him the card was ready, and the Food and Supply Officer offered him tea and requested him to withdraw the RTI application. Democratic government develops mechanisms for citizens to hold it accountable, including citizens' right to information about the government; this is transparency.

subject: Social Science
question_english: In the context of democracies, which idea is correct? Democracies have successfully eliminated: (a) conflicts among people (b) economic inequalities (c) differences of opinion on treating marginalised sections (d) the idea of political inequality
question_hinglish: Democracies ke sandarbh mein kaun sa vichaar sahi hai? Democracies ne safalta se khatam kiya hai: (a) logon ke beech sangharsh (b) aarthik asamantayein (c) haashiye ke vargon ke saath vyavhaar pe matbhed (d) political asamanta ka vichaar

subject: Social Science
question_english: In assessing democracy, which is the odd one out? Democracies need to ensure: (a) free and fair elections (b) dignity of the individual (c) majority rule (d) equal treatment before law
question_hinglish: Democracy ko parakhne mein kaun sa alag hai? Democracies ko ensure karna chahiye: (a) free aur fair chunaav (b) vyakti ki garima (c) bahumat ka raaj (d) kanoon ke saamne barabar vyavhaar
answer_english: (c) Majority rule. Democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion; the majority must work with the minority, and rule by majority must not become rule by a majority community, while free and fair elections, dignity and equal treatment are essential outcomes.
answer_hinglish: (c) Bahumat ka raaj. Democracy sirf bahumat ki raay ka raaj nahi; bahumat ko alpmat ke saath kaam karna chahiye aur yeh bahusankhyak samudaay ka raaj nahi banna chahiye, jabki free aur fair chunaav, garima aur barabar vyavhaar zaroori nateeje hain.
ncert_context: It is necessary to understand that democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion. The majority always needs to work with the minority so that governments represent the general view. Rule by majority must not become rule by majority community in terms of religion, race or language. Democracies are expected to have regular, free and fair elections, promote dignity and freedom of the individual, and ensure equality.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Do industrialised countries afford democracy while poor countries need dictatorship to become rich?
question_hinglish: Kya viksit desh democracy afford kar sakte hain jabki gareeb deshon ko ameer banne ke liye dictatorship chahiye?
answer_english: This assertion is not supported. Evidence from 1950 to 2000 shows that among poor countries, growth under dictatorship (4.34) and democracy (4.28) was virtually the same. Economic development depends on factors like population, global situation, cooperation and economic priorities, not just regime type. Since democracy does not lag behind and offers other benefits like accountability, dignity and accommodation of diversity, poor countries have no reason to prefer dictatorship.
answer_hinglish: Is daave ka koi aadhaar nahi. 1950 se 2000 ka saboot dikhata hai ki gareeb deshon mein dictatorship (4.34) aur democracy (4.28) mein growth lagbhag barabar thi. Economic vikaas sirf sarkar ke prakaar pe nahi, balki aabaadi, global sthiti, sahyog aur aarthik praathmiktaon pe nirbhar hai. Kyunki democracy peeche nahi rehti aur jawabdehi, garima aur vividhata ko jagah dene jaise fayde deti hai, gareeb deshon ke paas dictatorship chunne ki koi wajah nahi.
ncert_context: Rates of economic growth 1950–2000: poor countries under dictatorship 4.34, poor countries under democracy 4.28; when we compare their record only in poor countries, there is virtually no difference. Economic development depends on several factors: country's population size, global situation, cooperation from other countries, economic priorities. We can expect democracy not to lag behind dictatorships. With negligible difference, it is better to prefer democracy as it has several other positive outcomes.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Does having one vote for every citizen mean there is no domination or conflict in a democracy?
question_hinglish: Kya har nagrik ka ek vote hone ka matlab hai ki democracy mein koi dabdaba ya sangharsh nahi?
answer_english: No. Equal votes give political equality, but economic inequalities have grown, with the ultra-rich holding a disproportionate share of wealth. Social conflicts continue, as no society can permanently resolve them, and majority rule can turn into domination by a majority community, as in Sri Lanka. Caste and gender inequalities and atrocities also persist, though they now lack legal and moral foundations.
answer_hinglish: Nahi. Barabar vote political barabari dete hain, par aarthik asamanta badhi hai, jahan ati-ameer daulat ka bahut bada hissa rakhte hain. Samajik sangharsh jaari hain, kyunki koi samaaj unhe hamesha ke liye nahi suljha sakta, aur bahumat ka raaj Sri Lanka ki tarah bahusankhyak samudaay ka dabdaba ban sakta hai. Jaati aur gender asamantayein aur atyaachaar bhi jaari hain, halaanki ab unka kanooni aur naitik aadhaar nahi.
ncert_context: Democracies are based on political equality; all individuals have equal weight in electing representatives. Yet we find growing economic inequalities. No society can fully and permanently resolve conflicts among different groups. The example of Sri Lanka reminds us that rule by majority must not become rule by majority community. There are still instances of caste-based inequalities and atrocities, but these lack moral and legal foundations. Women are not always treated with respect.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What does thinking about development involve?
question_hinglish: Development ke baare mein sochne mein kya-kya shaamil hai?
answer_english: Development involves thinking about our aspirations for how we want to live and what a country should be like: what essential things we need, whether life can be better for all, how people should live together and whether there can be more equality, and about ways to achieve these goals. It is influenced by the past, and these hopes can be achieved only through a democratic political process.
answer_hinglish: Development mein hum is pe sochte hain ki hum kaise jeena chahte hain aur desh kaisa ho: hume kaun si zaroori cheezein chahiye, kya sabki zindagi behtar ho sakti hai, log saath kaise rahein aur kya zyada barabari ho sakti hai, aur in lakshyon ko paane ke tareeke kya hain. Yeh ateet se prabhavit hota hai, aur yeh ummeedein sirf democratic political process se poori ho sakti hain.
ncert_context: The idea of development or progress has always been with us. We have aspirations or desires about what we would like to do and how we would like to live. Similarly, we have ideas about what a country should be like. What are the essential things that we require? Can life be better for all? How should people live together? Can there be more equality? Development involves thinking about these questions and about the ways in which we can work towards achieving these goals. The way we live today is influenced by the past. It is only through a democratic political process that these hopes and possibilities can be achieved in real life.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why do different persons have different notions of development?
question_hinglish: Alag-alag logon ki development ki soch alag kyun hoti hai?
answer_english: Different persons have different developmental goals because their life situations are different, and each seeks what is most important for fulfilling their own aspirations. For example, landless rural labourers want more days of work, better wages, quality education for children and no discrimination, while prosperous Punjab farmers want high support prices, cheap labour and to settle children abroad.
answer_hinglish: Alag logon ke development ke lakshya alag hote hain kyunki unki zindagi ki sthitiyan alag hain, aur har koi woh chahta hai jo uski apni ichchhayein poori kare. Jaise bhoomiheen grameen mazdoor zyada din ka kaam, behtar mazdoori, bachchon ke liye achhi shiksha aur bhed-bhaav ka ant chahte hain, jabki Punjab ke samriddh kisan oonche support price, sasta mazdoor aur bachchon ko videsh basana chahte hain.
ncert_context: Different persons have different aspirations. Landless rural labourers want more days of work and better wages; the local school able to provide quality education for their children; no social discrimination and they too can become leaders in the village. Prosperous farmers from Punjab want assured high family income through higher support prices for crops and through hardworking and cheap labourers; they want to settle their children abroad. A girl from a rich urban family wants as much freedom as her brother and to pursue studies abroad. Each of them seeks different things, that which can fulfil their aspirations or desires.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Can developmental goals of different people be conflicting? Give examples.
question_hinglish: Kya alag logon ke development ke lakshya ek-doosre ke virodhi ho sakte hain? Examples do.
answer_english: Yes. What may be development for one may not be development for another, and may even be destructive. A girl wants as much freedom as her brother and wants him to share household work, which he may not like. Industrialists may want more dams for electricity, but these may submerge land and displace people such as tribals, who may prefer small check dams or tanks to irrigate their land.
answer_hinglish: Haan. Jo ek ke liye development hai woh doosre ke liye nahi ho sakta, balki nuksaandeh bhi ho sakta hai. Ek ladki apne bhai jitni azaadi chahti hai aur chahti hai ki woh ghar ke kaam mein haath bataye, jo bhai ko pasand na ho. Industrialists bijli ke liye zyada dams chahte hain, par isse zameen doob sakti hai aur adivaasi jaise log visthaapit ho sakte hain, jo apni zameen seenchne ke liye chhote check dams ya talaab pasand karenge.
ncert_context: At times, two persons or groups of persons may seek things which are conflicting. A girl expects as much freedom and opportunity as her brother, and that he also shares in the household work. Her brother may not like this. Similarly, to get more electricity, industrialists may want more dams. But this may submerge the land and disrupt the lives of people who are displaced, such as tribals. They might resent this and may prefer small check dams or tanks to irrigate their land. So, two things are clear: different persons can have different developmental goals, and what may be development for one may not be development for the other; it may even be destructive.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Besides income, what other goals do people seek in development?
question_hinglish: Aamdani ke alawa log development mein aur kya lakshya chahte hain?
answer_english: People want regular work, better wages and decent prices, that is, more income. But they also seek non-material things like equal treatment, freedom, security and respect from others, and resent discrimination; sometimes these matter more than income. For example, when taking a job, people consider family facilities, working atmosphere, learning opportunities and job security, not just pay. A safe environment and respect for women can let more women take up jobs.
answer_hinglish: Log niyamit kaam, behtar mazdoori aur uchit daam, yaani zyada aamdani, chahte hain. Par woh barabar vyavhaar, azaadi, suraksha aur doosron ka samman jaisi gair-bhautik cheezein bhi chahte hain aur bhed-bhaav se naraz hote hain; kabhi yeh aamdani se zyada mayne rakhti hain. subject: Social Science
question_english: What does national development mean?
question_hinglish: National development ka kya matlab hai?
answer_english: If individuals seek different goals, their notions of national development also differ and may conflict. National development means thinking about which ideas should be considered important when there are conflicts, how to decide among them, what a fair and just path for all would be, whether there is a better way of doing things, and whether an idea would benefit a large number of people or only a small group.
answer_hinglish: Agar log alag lakshya chahte hain, toh national development ki unki soch bhi alag aur virodhi ho sakti hai. National development ka matlab hai sochna ki takraav mein kaun se vichaar important hain, unme faisla kaise ho, sabke liye nyaypoorn raasta kya hai, kya koi behtar tareeka hai, aur kya koi vichaar zyada logon ko fayda dega ya sirf chhote group ko.
ncert_context: If individuals seek different goals, their notion of national development is also likely to be different. Different persons could have different as well as conflicting notions of a country's development. Can all ideas be considered equally important? If there are conflicts, how does one decide? What would be a fair and just path for all? We also have to think whether there is a better way of doing things. Would the idea benefit a large number of people or only a small group? National development means thinking about these questions.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is per capita income used to compare countries instead of total income?
question_hinglish: Deshon ki tulna ke liye total income ki jagah per capita income kyun use hoti hai?
answer_english: Income is considered one of the most important attributes for comparing countries, since more income means more of the things people need. A country's total income is the income of all its residents, but countries have different populations, so total income does not show what an average person earns. So we compare average income, total income divided by total population, also called per capita income.
answer_hinglish: Deshon ki tulna mein aamdani sabse important gunon mein se ek maani jaati hai, kyunki zyada aamdani ka matlab logon ki zaroorat ki zyada cheezein. Desh ki total income uske saare nivaasiyon ki aamdani hai, par deshon ki aabaadi alag hai, isliye total income se pata nahi chalta ki aam vyakti kitna kamaata hai. Isliye hum average income, yaani total income ko total aabaadi se bhaag dekar, compare karte hain, jise per capita income kehte hain.
ncert_context: For comparing countries, their income is considered one of the most important attributes. Countries with higher income are more developed than others with less income, based on the understanding that more income means more of all things human beings need. Intuitively, the income of the country is the income of all residents, giving the total income. However, for comparison between countries, total income is not useful, since countries have different populations; comparing total income will not tell us what an average person is likely to earn. Hence, we compare the average income, which is the total income of the country divided by its total population. The average income is also called per capita income.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the main criterion used by the World Bank to classify countries, and what are its limitations?
question_hinglish: World Bank deshon ko baantne ke liye kaun sa mukhya maapdand use karta hai, aur iski seemayein kya hain?
answer_english: The World Bank's World Development Reports classify countries by per capita income. Countries with per capita income of US$66,500 a year and above in 2024 are called high-income or rich countries, those with about US$2,300 or less are low-income, and India, at about US$11,000 in 2024, is in the lower middle income category. Its limitations: averages hide disparities in how income is distributed, and income alone does not show health, education or other quality-of-life factors.
answer_hinglish: World Bank ki World Development Reports deshon ko per capita income se baant-ti hain. 2024 mein US$66,500 saalana ya usse zyada per capita income wale desh high-income ya ameer kehlate hain, lagbhag US$2,300 ya kam wale low-income, aur 2024 mein lagbhag US$11,000 wala India lower middle income shreni mein hai. Iski seemayein: average aamdani ke bantwaare ki asamanta chhupa deta hai, aur sirf aamdani sehat, shiksha ya jeevan ki gunvatta nahi dikhati.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Country A's five citizens earn ₹9,500, ₹10,500, ₹9,800, ₹10,000 and ₹10,200 a month; Country B's earn ₹500, ₹500, ₹500, ₹500 and ₹48,000. Calculate the average income of each, and which country would most people prefer?
question_hinglish: Country A ke paanch nagrik mahine mein ₹9,500, ₹10,500, ₹9,800, ₹10,000 aur ₹10,200 kamaate hain; Country B ke ₹500, ₹500, ₹500, ₹500 aur ₹48,000. Dono ki average income nikaalo, aur zyadatar log kaun sa desh pasand karenge?
answer_english: Country A: (9,500 + 10,500 + 9,800 + 10,000 + 10,200) ÷ 5 = 50,000 ÷ 5 = ₹10,000. Country B: (500 × 4 + 48,000) ÷ 5 = 50,000 ÷ 5 = ₹10,000. Both averages are equal, but most would prefer Country A because income is equitably distributed, whereas in B most are poor and one person is extremely rich.

Dono ka average barabar hai, par zyadatar log Country A pasand karenge kyunki wahan aamdani barabari se bati hai, jabki B mein zyadatar gareeb hain aur ek vyakti bahut ameer hai.

question_english: Why do we use averages, and what are their limitations?
question_hinglish: Hum averages kyun use karte hain, aur unki seemayein kya hain?
answer_english: Averages let us compare situations, like countries with different populations, by showing what a typical person earns. Two countries can have the same average income while one has equitable distribution and the other has most people poor and one person very rich. So a rising average income does not mean all sections have become better off.

question_english: Define infant mortality rate, literacy rate and net attendance ratio.
question_hinglish: Infant mortality rate, literacy rate aur net attendance ratio ki paribhasha do.
answer_english: Infant mortality rate (IMR) is the number of children who die before the age of one year as a proportion of 1,000 live children born in that year. Literacy rate measures the proportion of literate population in the 7-and-above age group. Net attendance ratio is the number of children aged 15-17 attending school as a percentage of all children in that age group.
answer_hinglish: Infant mortality rate (IMR) us saal paida hue har 1,000 jeevit bachchon mein se ek saal se pehle marne wale bachchon ki sankhya hai. Literacy rate 7 saal aur usse upar ki aabaadi mein saakshar logon ka anupaat hai. Net attendance ratio 15-17 saal ke school jaane wale bachchon ka us umar ke saare bachchon mein percentage hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why does Kerala, with lower per capita income than Haryana, do better on health and education?
question_hinglish: Haryana se kam per capita income hone pe bhi Kerala sehat aur shiksha mein behtar kyun hai?
answer_english: Money in your pocket cannot buy all the goods and services needed to live well, so income alone is not an adequate indicator. Many important things, like security, schools and health care, are best and most cheaply provided collectively. Kerala has a low infant mortality rate because it has adequate provision of basic health and educational facilities. Similarly, where the Public Distribution System functions well, people's health and nutrition are likely to be better.
answer_hinglish: Jeb ka paisa achhe jeevan ke liye zaroori saari cheezein nahi khareed sakta, isliye sirf aamdani kaafi soochak nahi. Suraksha, school aur sehat seva jaisi kai zaroori cheezein milkar dene se sabse achhi aur sasti milti hain. Kerala ka infant mortality rate kam hai kyunki wahan basic sehat aur shiksha ki kaafi suvidhayein hain. Isi tarah jahan Public Distribution System achha chalta hai, wahan logon ki sehat aur poshan behtar hone ki sambhavna hai.
ncert_context: How is it that the average person in Haryana has more income than the average person in Kerala but lags behind in crucial areas? Money in your pocket cannot buy all the goods and services that you may need to live well. Income by itself is not a completely adequate indicator of material goods and services citizens are able to use. For many important things in life, the best and cheapest way is to provide these goods and services collectively. Kerala has a low Infant Mortality Rate because it has adequate provision of basic health and educational facilities. Similarly, in some states, the Public Distribution System (PDS) functions well, and health and nutritional status of people of such states is likely to be better.

subject: Social Science
question_english: In what respects is the criterion used by the UNDP for measuring development different from the World Bank's?
question_hinglish: Development naapne ke liye UNDP ka maapdand World Bank se kaise alag hai?
answer_english: The World Bank classifies countries mainly by per capita income. The UNDP's Human Development Report compares countries based on the educational levels of people, their health status and per capita income, combined in the Human Development Index (HDI). By prefixing 'human' to development, it makes clear that what matters most is what happens to citizens, their health and well-being.
answer_hinglish: World Bank deshon ko mukhya roop se per capita income se baant-ta hai. subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is the issue of sustainability important for development?
question_hinglish: Development ke liye sustainability ka mudda important kyun hai?
answer_english: We want development to rise or at least be maintained for future generations, but since the second half of the twentieth century scientists have warned that present types and levels of development are not sustainable. Overuse of resources like groundwater and exhaustion of non-renewable resources like crude oil threaten future development. As the saying goes, 'we have borrowed the world from our children', and environmental degradation crosses national boundaries, so our future is linked together.
answer_hinglish: Hum chahte hain ki development badhe ya kam se kam aane wali peedhiyon ke liye bana rahe, par twentieth century ke doosre half se scientists chetavni de rahe hain ki aaj ka development sthaayi nahi hai. Bhoojal jaise resources ka zyada use aur kachche tel jaise non-renewable resources ka khatam hona bhavishya ke vikaas ke liye khatra hai. Jaise kaha gaya hai, 'humne duniya apne bachchon se udhaar li hai', aur paryavaran ka nuksaan seemaon ko nahi maanta, isliye hamara bhavishya juda hai.
ncert_context: Suppose a country is quite developed. We would like this level of development to go up further or at least be maintained for future generations. However, since the second half of the twentieth century, scientists have been warning that the present type and levels of development are not sustainable. 'We have not inherited the world from our forefathers—we have borrowed it from our children.' Groundwater is being overused and crude oil reserves may last only about 50 years. Consequences of environmental degradation do not respect national or state boundaries; our future is linked together. Sustainability of development is a new area in which scientists, economists, philosophers and other social scientists are working together.
