subject: Social Science
question_english: 'The impact of globalisation has not been uniform.' Explain this statement.
question_hinglish: 'Globalisation ka asar ek jaisa nahi raha.' Is kathan ko samjhao.
answer_english: Globalisation has benefited well-off urban consumers with more choice, better quality and lower prices, top Indian companies that upgraded technology or became MNCs, and IT service providers. People with education, skill and wealth used the new opportunities best. But many small producers, such as Ravi in capacitors and those in toys, batteries and dairy, were hit hard and units shut down, and workers like Sushila lost job security and benefits. So its benefits were not shared equally.
answer_hinglish: Globalisation se shehron ke sampann consumers ko zyada vikalp, behtar quality aur kam daam mile, badi Indian companies ne technology sudhaari ya MNC bani, aur IT sevaon ko fayda hua. Shiksha, kaushal aur daulat wale logon ne naye mauko ka sabse achha upyog kiya. Par Ravi jaise capacitor utpaadak aur khilaune, batteries aur dairy ke kai chhote utpaadak buri tarah prabhaavit hue aur units band hui, aur Sushila jaise mazdooron ki naukri ki suraksha aur fayde chale gaye. Isliye fayde barabar nahi bate.
ncert_context: In the last twenty years, globalisation of the Indian economy has come a long way. The impact of globalisation has not been uniform. Globalisation and greater competition has been of advantage to consumers, particularly the well-off sections in the urban areas. Several top Indian companies benefited, and some emerged as multinationals. Globalisation has created new opportunities for companies providing IT services. For a large number of small producers and workers globalisation has posed major challenges; small manufacturers of batteries, capacitors, plastics, toys, tyres, dairy products and vegetable oil were hit hard. Workers' jobs are no longer secure. People with education, skill and wealth have made the best use of the new opportunities. On the other hand, there are many people who have not shared the benefits.

question_english: Assertion (A): MNCs set up production in countries like India and China. question_hinglish: Assertion (A): MNCs India aur China jaise deshon mein utpaadan lagaati hain. subject: Social Science
question_english: Why are individual consumers often in a weak position in the marketplace?
question_hinglish: Bazaar mein akele consumers aksar kamzor sthiti mein kyun hote hain?
answer_english: When there is a complaint about a good or service, the seller tries to shift all responsibility to the buyer, saying 'If you didn't like what you bought, please go elsewhere', as if the seller had no responsibility after the sale. Markets do not work fairly when producers are few and powerful while consumers buy in small amounts and are scattered. Large companies with huge wealth, power and reach can manipulate the market, even passing on false information through the media.
answer_hinglish: Kisi saamaan ya seva ki shikaayat pe bechne wala saari zimmedari khareedne wale pe daal deta hai, kehta hai 'pasand nahi aaya toh kahin aur jaao', jaise bikri ke baad uski koi zimmedari nahi. Jab utpaadak kam aur taakatvar hon aur consumers thoda-thoda khareedein aur bikhre hon, toh bazaar nyaypoorn nahi chalta. Bahut daulat, taakat aur pahunch wali badi companies bazaar ko manipulate kar sakti hain, media se galat jaankari tak failaati hain.
ncert_context: Individual consumers often find themselves in a weak position. Whenever there is a complaint regarding a good or service that had been bought, the seller tries to shift all the responsibility on to the buyer. The consumer movement is an effort to change this situation. Markets do not work in a fair manner when producers are few and powerful whereas consumers purchase in small amounts and are scattered. This happens especially when large companies are producing these goods. These companies with huge wealth, power and reach can manipulate the market in various ways. At times false information is passed on through the media, and other sources to attract consumers.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the various ways in which consumers may be exploited in the market?
question_hinglish: Bazaar mein consumers ka shoshan kin-kin tareekon se ho sakta hai?
answer_english: Shopkeepers may weigh less than they should; traders may add charges not mentioned before; adulterated or defective goods may be sold; and powerful companies may pass false information through the media to attract consumers. Consumers may also be forced to buy things they do not want, for example a stove with a new gas connection.
answer_hinglish: Dukaandaar kam tol sakte hain; vyapaari pehle na bataaye gaye charges jod sakte hain; milaawati ya kharaab saamaan becha ja sakta hai; aur taakatvar companies consumers ko lubhaane ke liye media se galat jaankari failaa sakti hain. Consumers ko anchaahi cheezein khareedne pe bhi majboor kiya ja sakta hai, jaise naye gas connection ke saath stove.
ncert_context: Exploitation in the marketplace happens in various ways. For example, sometimes traders indulge in unfair trade practices such as when shopkeepers weigh less than what they should or when traders add charges that were not mentioned before, or when adulterated/defective goods are sold. At times false information is passed on through the media, and other sources to attract consumers. Sometimes gas supply dealers insist that you have to buy the stove from them when you take a new connection. In this way many a times you are forced to buy things that you may not wish to and you are left with no choice.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Give examples showing why rules and regulations are needed to protect consumers.
question_hinglish: Aise examples do jo dikhaayein ki consumers ki suraksha ke liye niyam kyun zaroori hain?
answer_english: A company sold powder milk for babies all over the world as the most scientific product, claiming it was better than mother's milk; it took years of struggle to force it to accept these were false claims. Similarly, a long battle with court cases was needed to make cigarette companies accept that their product could cause cancer. Such cases show the need for rules and regulations to protect consumers.
answer_hinglish: Ek company ne bachchon ka powder doodh duniya bhar mein sabse vaigyanik utpaad batakar becha aur daava kiya ki yeh maa ke doodh se behtar hai; use galat daave maanne pe majboor karne mein saalon ka sangharsh laga. Isi tarah cigarette companies se yeh manwaane ke liye ki unka utpaad cancer kar sakta hai, court cases ke saath lambi ladaai ladni padi. Aise maamle consumers ki suraksha ke liye niyamon ki zaroorat dikhaate hain.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why are rules and regulations required in the marketplace? Relate this to producers and workers too.
question_hinglish: Bazaar mein niyam aur kanoon kyun zaroori hain? Ise utpaadakon aur mazdooron se bhi jodo.
answer_english: Just as rules are needed to protect unorganised sector workers from low wages and unfair conditions, and borrowers from moneylenders' high interest and tricks like forcing Swapna to sell her land, rules are needed to protect consumers. Individual consumers are weak against sellers who shift responsibility, weigh less, add hidden charges, sell adulterated goods or make false claims, so rules ensure fair dealing.
answer_hinglish: Jaise unorganised sector ke mazdooron ko kam vetan aur galat shartein se aur borrowers ko moneylenders ke zyada interest aur Swapna se zameen bikwaane jaise hathkandon se bachaane ke liye niyam chahiye, waise hi consumers ke liye bhi niyam chahiye. Akela consumer un bechne walon ke saamne kamzor hai jo zimmedari taalte hain, kam tolte hain, chhupe charges jodte hain, milaawati saamaan bechte hain ya galat daave karte hain, isliye niyam nyaypoorn len-den pakka karte hain.
ncert_context: In the preceding chapters we discussed the need for rules and regulations that would promote development, for the protection of workers in the unorganised sector or to protect people from high interest rates charged by moneylenders in the informal sector. Moneylenders adopt various tricks to bind the borrower: they could make the producer sell the produce to them at a low rate in return for a timely loan; they could force a small farmer like Swapna to sell her land to pay back the loan. Many people in the unorganised sector have to work at a low wage and accept conditions that are not fair. Likewise, rules and regulations are required for the protection of consumers in the marketplace. Individual consumers often find themselves in a weak position. Hence, there is a need for rules and regulations to ensure protection for consumers.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What factors gave birth to the consumer movement in India? Trace its evolution.
question_hinglish: India mein consumer movement kin kaaranon se shuru hua? Iske vikaas ka safar batao.
answer_english: The consumer movement arose from consumers' dissatisfaction with unfair practices by sellers, with no legal system to protect them. In India, it originated as a 'social force' to protect consumers against unethical and unfair trade practices; rampant food shortages, hoarding, black marketing and adulteration of food and edible oil gave birth to it in an organised form in the 1960s. Till the 1970s, organisations mainly wrote articles, held exhibitions and formed groups to look into ration shop malpractices and overcrowded road transport. More recently, the number of consumer groups has surged, and COPRA was enacted in 1986.
answer_hinglish: Consumer movement bechne walon ki galat harkaton se consumers ki naaraazgi se shuru hua, kyunki unhe bachaane ke liye koi kanooni vyavastha nahi thi. India mein yeh anaitik aur galat vyapaar ke khilaaf consumers ke hiton ki raksha ke liye ek 'social force' ke roop mein shuru hua; khaane ki bhaari kami, jamakhori, kaala bazaar aur khaane aur tel mein milaawat ne 1960s mein ise sangathit roop diya. 1970s tak sangathan mukhya roop se lekh likhte, pradarshaniyan lagaate aur ration dukaanon ki gadbadiyon aur bhari hui sadak yaatayaat pe groups banaate the. Haal mein consumer groups ki sankhya tezi se badhi, aur 1986 mein COPRA bana.
ncert_context: The consumer movement arose out of dissatisfaction of the consumers as many unfair practices were being indulged in by the sellers. There was no legal system available to consumers to protect them from exploitation in the marketplace. In India, the consumer movement as a 'social force' originated with the necessity of protecting and promoting the interests of consumers against unethical and unfair trade practices. Rampant food shortages, hoarding, black marketing, adulteration of food and edible oil gave birth to the consumer movement in an organised form in the 1960s. Till the 1970s, consumer organisations were largely engaged in writing articles and holding exhibitions. They formed consumer groups to look into the malpractices in ration shops and overcrowding in the road passenger transport. More recently, India witnessed an upsurge in the number of consumer groups. A major step taken in 1986 by the Indian government was the enactment of the Consumer Protection Act 1986, popularly known as COPRA.

subject: Social Science
question_english: How did the consumer movement shift responsibility from consumers to sellers?
question_hinglish: Consumer movement ne zimmedari consumers se bechne walon pe kaise daali?
answer_english: Earlier, an unhappy consumer simply avoided that brand or shop, and it was presumed that consumers were responsible for being careful while buying. It took many years for organisations in India and around the world to create awareness, which shifted the responsibility of ensuring the quality of goods and services onto the sellers.
answer_hinglish: Pehle naaraaz consumer bas us brand ya dukaan se khareedna band kar deta tha, aur maana jaata tha ki khareedte waqt saavdhaan rehna consumer ki zimmedari hai. India aur duniya bhar ke sangathanon ko jaagrukta failaane mein kai saal lage, jisse saamaan aur sevaon ki quality pakki karne ki zimmedari bechne walon pe aa gayi.
ncert_context: For a long time, when a consumer was not happy with a particular brand product or shop, he or she generally avoided buying that brand product, or would stop purchasing from that shop. It was presumed that it was the responsibility of consumers to be careful while buying a commodity or service. It took many years for organisations in India, and around the world, to create awareness amongst people. This has also shifted the responsibility of ensuring quality of goods and services on the sellers.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What are the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection and Consumers International?
question_hinglish: UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection aur Consumers International kya hain?
answer_english: In 1985 the United Nations adopted the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection, a tool for nations to adopt consumer protection measures and for consumer advocacy groups to press their governments to do so; it became the foundation of the consumer movement internationally. Consumers International is an umbrella body of over 200 member organisations from over 100 countries.
answer_hinglish: 1985 mein United Nations ne UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection apnaaye, jo deshon ke liye consumers ki suraksha ke kadam uthaane aur consumer groups ke liye sarkaron pe dabaav daalne ka zariya the; yeh antarrashtriya star pe consumer movement ki neev bane. Consumers International 100 se zyada deshon ke 200 se zyada sadasya sangathanon ki umbrella body hai.
ncert_context: In 1985 United Nations adopted the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection. This was a tool for nations to adopt measures to protect consumers and for consumer advocacy groups to press their governments to do so. At the international level, this has become the foundation for consumer movement. Today, Consumers International has become an umbrella body to over 200 member organisations from over 100 countries.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the right to safety? Explain with an example.
question_hinglish: Right to safety kya hai? Example se samjhao.
answer_english: Consumers have the right to be protected against the marketing of goods and delivery of services that are hazardous to life and property, and producers must strictly follow safety rules. For example, a pressure cooker's safety valve, if defective, can cause a serious accident, so manufacturers must ensure high quality, and public or government action is needed to maintain it. Bad quality products still appear because supervision is weak and the consumer movement is not strong enough.
answer_hinglish: Consumers ko jaan aur sampatti ke liye khatarnaak saamaan aur sevaon se suraksha ka haq hai, aur utpaadakon ko suraksha niyam sakhti se maanne chahiye. Jaise pressure cooker ka safety valve kharaab ho toh gambhir durghatna ho sakti hai, isliye banane walon ko oonchi quality pakki karni chahiye, aur ise banaaye rakhne ke liye sarkari ya saarvajanik kadam chahiye. Phir bhi kharaab saamaan milta hai kyunki nigraani kamzor hai aur consumer movement utna mazboot nahi.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What happened in the case of Reji Mathew, and which consumer right does it illustrate?
question_hinglish: Reji Mathew ke maamle mein kya hua, aur yeh kaun sa consumer adhikaar dikhata hai?
answer_english: Reji Mathew, a healthy Class IX student, was admitted to a private clinic in Kerala for tonsil removal. Due to improper general anaesthesia, he developed brain abnormalities and was crippled for life. His father claimed ₹5,00,000 compensation in the State Consumer Commission, which dismissed it for insufficient evidence. On appeal, the National Commission in New Delhi held the hospital responsible for medical negligence and directed it to pay compensation. The case illustrates the right to safety and the right to seek redressal.
answer_hinglish: Class IX ka swasth chhaatra Reji Mathew tonsils nikalwaane ke liye Kerala ke ek private clinic mein bharti hua. Galat general anaesthesia ki wajah se uske dimaag mein gadbadi hui aur woh zindagi bhar ke liye apaahij ho gaya. Uske pita ne State Consumer Commission mein ₹5,00,000 muaavze ka daava kiya, jise kam saboot ki wajah se khaarij kar diya gaya. Appeal pe New Delhi ke National Commission ne hospital ko medical laaparwaahi ka zimmedar maana aur muaavza dene ka aadesh diya. Yeh right to safety aur right to seek redressal dikhata hai.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the right to information for consumers? Why must manufacturers display details on packaging?
question_hinglish: Consumers ke liye right to information kya hai? Manufacturers ko packet pe jaankari kyun deni padti hai?
answer_english: Consumers have the right to be informed about the particulars of goods and services they purchase. Packets show ingredients, price, batch number, date of manufacture, expiry date and the manufacturer's address; medicines show directions for use and side effects, and garments show washing instructions. With this information, consumers can complain and ask for compensation or replacement if a product proves defective, for example within its expiry period, and can protest if charged above the MRP.
answer_hinglish: Consumers ko khareede gaye saamaan aur sevaon ki jaankari paane ka haq hai. Packet pe saamagri, daam, batch number, banne ki taarikh, expiry date aur banane wale ka pata hota hai; dawaiyon pe istemaal ke nirdesh aur side effects, aur kapdon pe dhone ke nirdesh hote hain. Is jaankari se consumer saamaan kharaab nikalne pe, jaise expiry se pehle, shikaayat karke muaavza ya badalna maang sakta hai, aur MRP se zyada daam lene pe virodh kar sakta hai.
ncert_context: When you buy any commodity, you will find certain details given on the packing. These details are about ingredients used, price, batch number, date of manufacture, expiry date and the address of the manufacturer. When we buy medicines, on the packets, you might find 'directions for proper use' and information relating to side effects and risks. When you buy garments, you will find information on 'instructions for washing'. Rules have been made so that the manufacturer displays this information because consumers have the right to be informed about the particulars of goods and services that they purchase. Consumers can then complain and ask for compensation or replacement if the product proves to be defective in any manner. If we buy a product and find it defective well within the expiry period, we can ask for a replacement. If the expiry period was not printed, the manufacturer would blame the shopkeeper and will not accept the responsibility.

subject: Social Science
question_english: What is the right to choose? Give examples of when it is denied.
question_hinglish: Right to choose kya hai? Iske chheene jaane ke examples do.
answer_english: Any consumer who receives a service, regardless of age, gender and nature of service, has the right to choose whether to continue receiving it. The right is denied when a shop owner sells toothpaste only if you also buy a toothbrush, or when gas supply dealers insist you buy a stove from them with a new connection, forcing you to buy things you do not want.
answer_hinglish: Koi bhi consumer jo seva leta hai, umar, ling aur seva ke prakaar se pare, yeh chunne ka haq rakhta hai ki seva jaari rakhe ya nahi. Yeh haq tab chheena jaata hai jab dukaandaar toothpaste sirf toothbrush ke saath bechne ki zid kare, ya gas dealer naye connection ke saath unse hi stove khareedne ko kahe, jisse anchaahi cheezein khareedni padti hain.
ncert_context: Any consumer who receives a service in whatever capacity, regardless of age, gender and nature of service, has the right to choose whether to continue to receive the service. Suppose you want to buy toothpaste, and the shop owner says that she can sell the toothpaste only if you buy a toothbrush. If you are not interested in buying the brush, your right to choice is denied. Similarly, sometimes gas supply dealers insist that you have to buy the stove from them when you take a new connection. In this way many a times you are forced to buy things that you may not wish to and you are left with no choice.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Abirami paid ₹61,020 in advance for a two-year coaching course but left after one year due to poor teaching. What did the consumer commissions decide?
question_hinglish: Abirami ne do saal ke coaching course ke liye ₹61,020 advance diye par kharaab padhai ki wajah se ek saal baad chhod diya. Consumer commissions ne kya faisla kiya?
answer_english: When the institute refused a refund, the District Consumer Commission directed it to refund ₹28,000, saying she had the right to choose. On the institute's appeal, the State Commission upheld this, fined the institute ₹25,000 for a frivolous appeal, ordered ₹7000 as compensation and litigation cost, and restrained all educational and professional institutions in the state from charging fees for the entire course in advance at one go, with penalties and imprisonment for violation.
answer_hinglish: Institute ne refund se inkaar kiya toh District Consumer Commission ne ₹28,000 lautaane ka aadesh diya, kehte hue ki use chunne ka haq hai. Institute ki appeal pe State Commission ne yeh faisla barkaraar rakha, bekaar appeal ke liye institute pe ₹25,000 jurmaana lagaaya, ₹7000 muaavza aur mukadme ka kharch dilwaaya, aur state ke saare shiksha aur professional sansthaanon ko poore course ki fees ek saath advance lene se roka, ulanghan pe jurmaana aur jail ke saath.
ncert_context: Abirami, a student of Ansari Nagar, joined a two-year course at a local coaching institute for professional courses in New Delhi. At the time of joining, she paid the fees Rs 61,020 as lumpsum for the entire course of two years. However, she decided to opt out at the end of one year as she found that the quality of teaching was not up to the mark. When she asked for a refund of the fee for one year, it was denied. When she filed the case in the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, the Commission directed the Institute to refund Rs 28,000 saying that she had the right to choose. The Institute appealed in the State Consumer Commission. The State Commission upheld the District Commission's direction and further fined the institute Rs 25,000 for a frivolous appeal. It also directed the institute to pay Rs 7000 as compensation and litigation cost. The State Commission also restrained all the educational and professional institutions in the state from charging fees from students for the entire duration of the course in advance and that too at one go. Any violation may invite penalties and imprisonment.

question_english: What is the right to seek redressal?
question_hinglish: Right to seek redressal kya hai?
answer_english: Consumers have the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices and exploitation. If any damage is done to a consumer, she has the right to get compensation depending on the degree of damage. An easy and effective public system is needed for this, which COPRA provides through Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions.

Iske liye aasaan aur asardaar saarvajanik vyavastha chahiye, jo COPRA Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions ke zariye deta hai.

Under COPRA, a three-tier quasi-judicial machinery was set up for redressal of consumer disputes.

question_english: Prakash's money order for his daughter's marriage did not reach her in time. What steps did he take to get justice?

question_english: What is the difference between a consumer protection council and a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission?
question_hinglish: Consumer protection council aur Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission mein kya fark hai?

question_hinglish: In maamlon ko consumer adhikaaron mein baanto: (a) Lata ko nayi press se current laga; (b) Iqbal packet ki saari jaankari padhta hai; (c) tum cable operator nahi badal sakte; (d) tum kharaab camera ki baar-baar shikaayat karte ho.
answer_english: (a) Lata's electric shock from a new iron is the right to safety. (b) Iqbal reading pack details is the right to information. (c) Being unable to switch cable operators is the right to choice being denied. (d) Persistently complaining about a defective camera is the right to redressal.
answer_hinglish: (a) Nayi press se Lata ko current lagna right to safety hai. (b) Iqbal ka packet ki jaankari padhna right to information hai. (c) Cable operator na badal paana right to choice ka chheena jaana hai. (d) Kharaab camera ki lagaataar shikaayat right to redressal hai.
ncert_context: The Consumer Protection Act 1986 ensures rights: choice, information, redressal, representation, safety, consumer education. Consumers have the right to be protected against goods hazardous to life and property (safety); the right to be informed about the particulars of goods (information); the right to choose whether to continue to receive a service (choice); and the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices and get compensation (redressal).

subject: Social Science
question_english: What do logos like ISI, Agmark, Hallmark and +F indicate? Is certification compulsory for all products?
question_hinglish: ISI, Agmark, Hallmark aur +F jaise logo kya batate hain? Kya sabhi utpaadon ke liye certification zaroori hai?
answer_english: These logos and certifications assure consumers of quality. The organisations that issue them allow producers to use their logos only if they follow certain quality standards. Certification is not compulsory for all producers, but for products affecting health and safety or of mass consumption, like LPG cylinders, food colours and additives, cement and packaged drinking water, producers must get certified.
answer_hinglish: Yeh logo aur certification consumers ko quality ka bharosa dete hain. Inhe jaari karne wali sansthayein utpaadakon ko logo tabhi use karne deti hain jab woh tay quality standards maanein. Sab utpaadakon ke liye certification zaroori nahi, par sehat aur suraksha ko prabhaavit karne wale ya aam upyog ke utpaad, jaise LPG cylinders, food colours aur additives, cement aur packaged peene ka paani, ke liye certification anivaarya hai.
ncert_context: While buying many commodities, on the cover, you might have seen a logo with the letters ISI, Agmark, Hallmark or +F. These logos and certification help consumers get assured of quality while purchasing the goods and services. The organisations that monitor and issue these certificates allow producers to use their logos provided they follow certain quality standards. Though these organisations develop quality standards for many products, it is not compulsory for all the producers to follow standards. However, for some products that affect the health and safety of consumers or of products of mass consumption like LPG cylinders, food colours and additives, cement, packaged drinking water, it is mandatory on the part of the producers to get certified by these organisations.

question_english: How does the government spread awareness about consumer rights?
question_hinglish: Sarkar consumer adhikaaron ke baare mein jaagrukta kaise failaati hai?
answer_english: The enactment of COPRA led to separate Departments of Consumer Affairs in central and state governments. They spread information about the legal process people can use through posters and advertisements, including on television, helping consumers become conscious of their rights and make informed choices.
answer_hinglish: COPRA banne se central aur state sarkaron mein alag Departments of Consumer Affairs bane. Yeh posters aur television sameth vigyaapanon se logon ko kanooni prakriya ki jaankari dete hain, jisse consumers apne adhikaaron ke prati jaagruk hote hain aur soch-samajh kar chunaav karte hain.
ncert_context: When we as consumers become conscious of our rights, while purchasing various goods and services, we will be able to distinguish and make informed choices. This calls for acquiring the knowledge and skill to become a well-informed consumer. The enactment of COPRA has led to the setting up of separate Departments of Consumer Affairs in central and state governments. The posters are one example through which government spread information about legal process which people can use. You might also be seeing such advertisements on television channels.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Critically examine the progress of the consumer movement in India.
question_hinglish: India mein consumer movement ki pragati ki aalochnaatmak jaanch karo.
answer_english: Progress: India observes 24 December as National Consumers' Day, has exclusive authority for consumer redressal, and has over 2000 consumer groups, though only about 50-60 are well organised and recognised. COPRA was amended in 2019 to include internet buying and mediation. Problems: redressal is becoming cumbersome, expensive and time-consuming, often needing lawyers; cash memos are often not issued, so evidence is hard to gather; most purchases are small retail sales; awareness spreads slowly after 30 years; and laws and market rules are poorly enforced.
answer_hinglish: Pragati: India 24 December ko National Consumers' Day manaata hai, uske paas consumer nivaaran ki alag vyavastha hai, aur 2000 se zyada consumer groups hain, jinme sirf lagbhag 50-60 achhe se sangathit aur maanyata praapt hain. COPRA 2019 mein sudhaara gaya, internet khareedari aur mediation jode gaye. Samasyayein: nivaaran prakriya pecheeda, mehengi aur samay lene wali ho rahi hai, aksar vakeel chahiye; cash memo nahi milta isliye saboot mushkil; zyadatar khareedari chhoti retail hai; 30 saal baad bhi jaagrukta dheere fail rahi hai; aur kanoon aur bazaar ke niyam theek se laagu nahi hote.
ncert_context: India has been observing 24 December as the National Consumers' Day. India is one of the countries that have exclusive authority for consumer redressal. The consumer movement in India has made some progress in terms of numbers of organised groups and their activities. There are today more than 2000 consumer groups in the country of which only about 50-60 are well organised and recognised for their work. However, the consumer redressal process is becoming cumbersome, expensive and time consuming. Many a time, consumers are required to engage lawyers. These cases require time for filing and attending the commission proceedings. In most purchases cash memos are not issued hence evidence is not easy to gather. Moreover most purchases in the market are small retail sales. After more than 30 years of the enactment of COPRA, consumer awareness in India is spreading but slowly. Besides this the enforcement of laws that protect workers, especially in the unorganised sectors is weak. Similarly, rules and regulations for working of markets are often not followed.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Why is it said that consumer movements can be effective only with consumers' active involvement?
question_hinglish: Kyun kaha jaata hai ki consumer movement sirf consumers ki sakriya bhaagidaari se hi asardaar ho sakta hai?
answer_english: Laws like COPRA exist, but enforcement is weak, market rules are often not followed, and redressal is slow and costly. Awareness is spreading only slowly. So the movement needs voluntary effort and struggle involving everyone: consumers must know their rights, insist on bills, look for certification marks, and complain and seek redressal when exploited.
answer_hinglish: COPRA jaise kanoon hain, par unka paalan kamzor hai, bazaar ke niyam aksar nahi maane jaate, aur nivaaran dheema aur mehenga hai. Jaagrukta bhi dheere fail rahi hai. Isliye movement ko sabki swaichchhik koshish aur sangharsh chahiye: consumers ko apne adhikaar jaanne, bill maangne, certification marks dekhne, aur shoshan hone pe shikaayat aur nivaaran maangne chahiye.
ncert_context: After more than 30 years of the enactment of COPRA, consumer awareness in India is spreading but slowly. Besides this the enforcement of laws that protect workers, especially in the unorganised sectors is weak. Similarly, rules and regulations for working of markets are often not followed. Nevertheless, there is scope for consumers to realise their role and importance. It is often said that consumer movements can be effective only with the consumers' active involvement. It requires a voluntary effort and struggle involving the participation of one and all.

Nevertheless, there is scope for consumers to realise their role and importance. It is often said that consumer movements can be effective only with the consumers' active involvement. It requires a voluntary effort and struggle involving the participation of one and all.

subject: Social Science
question_english: Which of these offers would really benefit consumers: '15 gm more in every 500 gm pack' or 'Scratch and win gifts worth ₹10 lakhs'?
question_hinglish: Inme se kaun sa offer sach mein consumers ke kaam ka hai: 'Har 500 gm pack mein 15 gm zyada' ya 'Scratch karo aur ₹10 lakh ke inaam jeeto'?
answer_english: '15 gm more in every 500 gm pack' gives every buyer a definite 3 per cent extra quantity (15 ÷ 500), so it really benefits consumers. 'Scratch and win gifts worth ₹10 lakhs' is a catchy offer where only a few may win, so most buyers gain nothing; alert consumers should not respond unhesitatingly to such offers.
answer_hinglish: 'Har 500 gm pack mein 15 gm zyada' har khareedaar ko pakka 3 percent zyada maal deta hai (15 ÷ 500), isliye yeh sach mein faydemand hai. 'Scratch karo aur ₹10 lakh ke inaam jeeto' lubhaavna offer hai jisme kuch hi log jeet sakte hain, isliye zyadatar khareedaaron ko kuch nahi milta; jaagruk consumers ko aise offers pe bina soche pratikriya nahi deni chahiye.
